-- ⚠️ The `setRef r v` -> `r := v` migration DELIBERATELY SKIPS this file (#1746).
-- `test/wasm/diff_wasm_typed.sh` pins ~60 of this file's `setRef` call sites as
-- LITERAL SOURCE TEXT (the leaf-demand carrier ratchets), including NEGATIVE regex
-- checks asserting a given writer does NOT exist — and a negative check that is not
-- taught the `:=` spelling stops seeing a rogue writer, i.e. fails OPEN. Migrating
-- the calls without rewriting that suite in lockstep would silently weaken a
-- soundness ratchet for a purely stylistic gain, so the two move together or not at
-- all. #1746 does both.
--
-- WasmGC backend emitter — WASMGC-DESIGN.md §7.  Peer of `backend.llvm_emit`:
-- consumes the SAME backend-neutral Core IR (`ir.core_ir`) the LLVM emitter
-- consumes (lowered by the SAME `core_ir_lower.lowerProgramEmitWith`) and produces a
-- complete WAT text module (assembled by `wasm-tools parse`, run under a WasmGC
-- engine).  `emitProgram : WasmEmitInput -> CProgram -> String`.
--
-- ── W2 SCOPE (immediates + arithmetic) ─────────────────────────────
-- Scalar / arithmetic subset on raw i32: CLit Int/Bool/Unit, CVar (fn/global/
-- local), CBinPrim int arith+cmp, CUnOp `-`, CIf, CLet/CSLet/CBlock via
-- locals, top-level fns (incl recursion), value-bindings→globals, value-main
-- auto-print.
--
-- ── W3 SCOPE (ADTs + match) ────────────────────────────────────────
-- User `data` types + `match` (CDecision/CTree), incl the reserved Option/Result/
-- Ordering ADTs.  W3 adds:
--   * a §3.4 dynamic type section: per payload-ctor `struct` (discriminant field 0
--     + one `(ref eq)` per field) under a per-datatype root struct, plus the
--     reserved Option/Result/Ordering roots/structs.
--   * construction: `CApp (CVar ctor) args` → `struct.new` (payload) / `ref.i31
--     globalNullaryTag` (nullary); a nullary `CVar ctor` likewise.
--   * match: `CDecision`/`CTree` → discriminant extraction (i31 nullary vs struct
--     payload) feeding a `br_table` on the dense per-type ordinal, then field
--     extraction via `ref.cast` + `struct.get`, leaf re-match for var bindings.
--
-- ── W4 SCOPE (closures + call_ref + guaranteed TCO) ────────────────
-- Higher-order code + tail-call optimization (WASMGC-DESIGN §4).  W4 adds:
--   * Closure ABI (§4.1): a CLam is lambda-lifted to a top-level $codety function;
--     the closure is a `$clos` struct `{ code:(ref $codety); arity:i32; env:$argarr }`
--     under the (ref eq) unitype.  ARITY LIVES IN THE STRUCT (§11) — every apply
--     site reads it from the value, never a name-keyed table, which kills the native
--     backend's table-miss miscompile class by construction.  Captures live in the
--     `env` array; a lifted fn reads captures from `self`'s env and params from the
--     args array.  A capture-free top-level fn used as a VALUE gets a wrapper closure
--     (`$mdk_w_<name>`, env = []).
--   * Application (§4.1): a saturated direct call to a known top-level fn → `call`
--     (the fast path, unchanged).  Anything else (partial / over application; an
--     indirect call to a closure value) → pack args into a $argarr + `call $__mdk_apply`
--     (the universal apply, in wasm_preamble): EXACT → call_ref; UNDER → build a PAP
--     closure (code = $mdk_pap, remaining arity); OVER → saturate `arity` args, then
--     re-apply the surplus to the result.
--   * TCO (§4.2): at TAIL positions (descending if/let/block/decision-arm tails) a
--     saturated direct call → `return_call`; an indirect / non-saturated call →
--     `return_call $__mdk_apply` (which itself `return_call_ref`s the exact case).
--     Guaranteed constant-stack (Wasm 3.0 / Node 24).  The common emitRefTail
--     dispatcher handles raw i64 direct calls and boxed ref calls.
--   * Multi-clause / pattern-param top-level fns: coalesced into one wasm func that
--     dispatches over its synthetic positional params (a fallthrough clause chain
--     testing literal/ctor params + binding PVar params), reusing the W3 match
--     machinery.  A program using any of {CLam, indirect/HOF application, multi-
--     clause-or-pattern-param fn, a top-level fn referenced as a value} forces the
--     uniform (ref eq) rep (`useClos`), since a closure captures heterogeneous values.
--
-- ── W6 SCOPE (strings + the byte-level IO path) ────────────────────
-- The temporary W2 IO scaffold (JS-side decimal/bool/newline formatting via
-- mdk_write_int/mdk_write_bool) is COLLAPSED: the module produces its own output
-- bytes through real codegen + ONE byte-level host import `env.mdk_write_byte(i32)`
-- (§6 / §10 fork e).  W6 adds:
--   * §3.3 String rep: `(type $str (sub (struct $cp_count i32 $bytes (ref $u8arr))))`
--     + `(type $u8arr (array (mut i8)))` — UTF-8 bytes + cached codepoint count, so
--     stringLength is O(1) (mirrors the locked native rep, RUNTIME-DESIGN §7 dec 2).
--     Emitted into the rec group only when the program uses strings (`useStr`).
--   * String literals (`CLit (LString _)`): bytes in a passive data segment, built at
--     run time by `array.new_data` (the §11-preferred non-const-array init); cp_count
--     computed at emit time (UTF-8 codec, peer to llvm_emit.strBytes/utf8Bytes).
--   * Char literals (`CLit (LChar _)`): the codepoint as an i31 immediate.
--   * Externs: `intToString` (decimal → $str, byte-matches medaka_rt.c incl. neg/zero),
--     `stringLength` (O(1) cp_count), `putStr`/`putStrLn` (byte-write), `flushStdout`
--     (no-op).  Value-main auto-print routes Int→$mdk_print_int / Bool→$mdk_print_bool
--     / String→$mdk_print_strln; a Unit main (putStrLn …) auto-prints nothing.
--   * A program using strings forces ref-mode (a String is a boxed (ref eq) value).
--
-- ── W6b RESIDUAL GAPS AS OF THIS SLICE (#383: verify against CURRENT source, not
--    this snapshot — every one of these except the pattern-guard row has since
--    closed; grep the extern name to see its real implementation) ─────────────
--   * charToStr (needs a codepoint→$str runtime) — CLOSED, the `WasmStr` family.
--     stringConcat (`List String` → W7 list support) — CLOSED, the `WasmStr` family +
--     `strConcatRuntimeLines`.  `++` String concat — CLOSED (`op == "++"`).
--     floatToString (Float → W6b) — CLOSED, W8b (below).  The remaining string
--     externs (stringSlice/stringIndexOf/stringCompare/toUpper/…) — CLOSED,
--     the `WasmStr` family.  ePutStr/ePutStrLn (stderr byte-write import) — CLOSED
--     (`WasmEmit.useEPut`).  RNG + remaining externs → W8, CLOSED there.
--   * Refutable pattern guards (`p <- e`) in a match arm — STILL a gap (both
--     tail and non-tail arms `gapL`, ~line 6494/7310/7318; ledgered live as
--     `llvm/guard_refut_ctor` in test/engine_divergence.txt).
--   * A CLetGroup — CLOSED, W9 (`emitLetGroupWith`).
--
-- ── W7 SCOPE (collections) ─────────────────────────────────────────
-- List / Tuple / Array / Record / Ref, ranges, index/slice (§3.3 heap aggregates +
-- §8.6 (ref eq) unitype).  KEY DESIGN: List/Tuple/Record reuse the W3 ctor machinery
-- via SYNTHETIC ctors so construction + the discriminant br_table + field extraction
-- stay uniform (peer to the LLVM backend's Cons/Nil/$tuple synthetic names):
--   * List: ctors Cons (ord 0, struct $C_Cons {tag,head,tail}) / Nil (ord 1, an i31).
--     `CList` = right-nested struct.new spine; `CRangeList` = a back-to-front counted
--     cons loop; the HCons/HNil match heads map through `conHeadInfo`→("Cons",2)/
--     ("Nil",0), so the §3.4 i31-vs-struct discriminant read selects Nil vs Cons.
--   * Tuple n: a per-arity synthetic ctor "Tup<n>" (type "$Tuple<n>", single-ctor),
--     struct $C_Tup<n> {tag + n (ref eq)}.  `CTuple` = struct.new; HTuple n drives the
--     same (single-slot) br_table; tuple-pattern fields extract via struct.get i+1.
--   * Array: $arr = (array (mut (ref eq))).  `CArray` = array.new_fixed; `CRangeArray`
--     = a counted fill loop; `CIndex` = a bounds-checked array.get (i<0 || i>=len →
--     `unreachable`, matching native @mdk_oob's abort — both abort with empty stdout);
--     `CSlice` = array.new + array.copy.  Array temps are (ref null $arr) scratch
--     locals (`ref.as_non_null` before array ops).
--   * Record: a named-field ctor is ALREADY a W3 user ctor (its $C_<name> struct is
--     declared), so `CRecord` = positional struct.new in declared field order;
--     `CFieldAccess` = struct.get at 1+field-index (from WasmEmitInput's declared
--     record order, then this Prog's immutable construction fallback); `CRecordUpdate`/`CVariantUpdate` = struct.new
--     copying the unchanged fields (struct.get of a stashed base) + the overrides.
--   * Ref: $refbox = a 1-field mutable struct (declared on use; the Ref/setRef
--     externs' full lowering rides on W8's extern surface — the type is reserved).
-- The range/index/slice/record-update codegen uses depth-keyed typed scratch locals
-- ($__rli<d>/$__raarr<d>/…); a function declares the ones its body references (w7Local).
--
-- ── W8b SCOPE (Float + the last externs; MVP-completing) ──────────
-- Float is now a boxed (struct $float (f64)) (ref eq).  CLOSED this slice:
--   * Float LITERALS — `f64.const <floatToString-text>` + `struct.new $float` (the same
--     rendering the LLVM oracle bakes into its const — shortest-round-trip since #57,
--     NOT `%.12g`, see wasm_preamble.mdk's W8b Float section — so the parsed double is
--     byte-identical across clang and wasm-tools).  pi/e likewise.
--   * Float ARITHMETIC / COMPARISON — read off the binder stamps (Core carries each
--     binder's runtime type) via `cexprIsFloat`: a Float lit / pi/e / Float-returning
--     extern or function / Float binop / a variable stamped Float.  Unbox→f64 op→rebox
--     (arith) or →i31 Bool (compare).  Unary `-` → f64.neg.
--   * Float EXTERNS — intToFloat/floatToInt/hashFloat/randomFloat are pure WAT (the
--     boxed-Float conversions; hashFloat = reinterpret+mix64; randomFloat = SplitMix64
--     → f64 in [-1,1), the medaka_rt.c offset).  floatToString is a HOST IMPORT (the
--     shortest-round-trip formatter, #57; the JS host reproduces it byte-for-byte via
--     `toExponential()` reformatted through the same exponent threshold —
--     the ONE host-dependent formatter, a clean parallel to the deferred IO/WASI seam).
--   * stringIndexOf / stringCompare — pure WAT building the Option Int / Ordering result
--     directly (byte search → Some/None; memcmp+length → Lt/Eq/Gt).
--   * Float value-main auto-print → WFloat → unbox → $mdk_float_to_str → print + '\n'.
-- This CLOSED the previously-gapped real-prelude `impl Num/Debug/Display/Hash Float`
-- validation (those impls are retained whole by DCE in every real-prelude program; the
-- modules gate went 0/9-gap → 9/9-ok).
-- REMAINING DEFERRED after W8b, AS OF THIS SLICE (#383: all three below are now
-- CLOSED — see WASMGC-DESIGN.md's "IMPLEMENTATION STATUS" note for the authoritative
-- current summary; this comment is the historical W8b-era snapshot, kept for the
-- narrative, not a live status):
--   * stringToFloat — CLOSED (layer-6): a real host import (`mdk_str_to_float`, the
--     host's strtod), not a trap stub — no deferred-Float trap path
--     remains; see ~line 1005 / 2143 / 2216.
--   * The IO/WASI surface (readFile/args/getEnv/fileExists/exit) — CLOSED (W12): real
--     host imports (the plan's host keys) and `ioHostRuntimeLines`.
--     The file externs are all lowered since; `runCommand` (explicitly named in this
--     bullet's original scope) has no wasm equivalent at all (no wasm profile grants
--     Exec). Its row in `backend.extern_catalog` is the source of truth, `PERMANENT`;
--     don't infer "IO is done" from this comment.
--   * self-host-on-WasmGC — CLOSED (layers 12/16): `wasm_emit_modules_main` compiles
--     Medaka programs to working WasmGC modules end-to-end; the in-browser playground
--     (`playground/dist/playground.wasm`) is live. Detail: `WASM-SELFHOST-ROADMAP.md`.
--

-- ── VALUE-REP DECISION (resolve per the slice guardrail) ─────────────────────
-- W2 used raw i32 for every value.  ADT values force a uniform §8.6 rep.  CHOICE:
-- **per-PROGRAM split.**  A program with NO ADTs (no `data` decl, no CDecision)
-- emits the W2 raw-i32 shape VERBATIM (the 15 W2 fixtures stay byte-identical — the
-- gate is output-diff, so this is the safe-and-simple half).  A program that uses
-- ANY ADT switches WHOLESALE to the §8.6 uniform `(ref eq)` rep: every value slot
-- (param / local / global / fn result) is `(ref eq)`; Int/Bool/Unit/nullary-ctors
-- are `i31ref` immediates (`ref.i31`); payload ctors are typed structs.  Arithmetic
-- unboxes its operands (`i31.get_s`) and re-boxes the result.  WHY per-program (not
-- per-function): a per-function split needs the callee's signature to agree at each
-- call site, i.e. real cross-fn rep inference; the gate is output-diff so the extra
-- boxing in ref-mode is invisible, and per-program keeps the two reps from ever
-- meeting inside one module — strictly simpler to keep CORRECT, which is the
-- guardrail's tie-breaker.  (Perf — the monomorphic-i32 fast path — is a later
-- slice.)  The mode is computed once in `emitProgram` (`programUsesAdt`) and
-- threaded as `Prog.useRef`.
--
-- ── WAT lowering strategy ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- A wasm function body is an INSTRUCTION SEQUENCE leaving its result on the stack.
-- `emitExpr` returns a flat list of instruction lines.  In ref-mode the value left
-- on the stack is always `(ref eq)`; in scalar-mode it is i32.

-- ── static value kind (scalar-mode only; for the auto-print routing) ─────────
data WTy = WInt | WBool | WUnit | WStr | WRef | WChar | WFloat

-- Per-emission gap lifecycle. Strict is the normal public path; record mode
-- continues with placeholders while preserving first-observed event order.
data WGapMode = WGapStrict | WGapRecord

-- Destination-passing TMC context. It is owned by a fresh WasmEmit so nested
-- and independent emission routes cannot leak loop-local authority.
data WTrmcCtx =
  | WTrmcOff
  | WTrmcOn SelfRef Int (List String) (List (String, Int)) Bool String String

-- the active dispatch-group context during a group member's body emit.  `WDispOn root
-- loopLbl rootArity members` ⇒ redirect SPINE cons leaves (a peeled cons chain
-- bottoming in a saturated call to a group member) to the dest-passing emit +
-- `return_call` (the root's inner loop for the root, the member fn itself otherwise),
-- and base leaves to the dest-close.  WDispOff ⇒ ordinary emit.  Owned by a fresh
-- WasmEmit (peer of WTrmcCtx) so one emission's group authority cannot reach another.
data WDispCtx = WDispOff | WDispOn String String Int (List String)

data WasmEmit = WasmEmit {
  physical : Option WasmDemandPlan,
  externFacts : OrdMap ExternDeclFact,
  gapMode : WGapMode,
  gapLog : Ref (List String),
  curGapBind : Ref String,
  stringSegments : Ref (List (Int, List Int)),
  nextStringSegmentId : Ref Int,
  -- the segment of each distinct literal payload, keyed by `strSegKey` (an OrdMap,
  -- so a lookup is O(log n)).  `freshStrSeg` consults it before allocating.
  strSegIds : Ref (OrdMap Int),
  nextLambdaId : Ref Int,
  liftedDefinitions : Ref (List (List String)),
  liftedDefinitionNames : Ref (OrdMap Unit),
  -- S-4: the capture-free closure globals this emission hoisted.  `constClosIdx`
  -- maps an initializer's TEXT to its global name (the dedup key — an OrdMap, not
  -- a List-as-map, so N distinct cells cost N log N and not N²); `constClosCells`
  -- keeps them in emission order for the module's global section.  See
  -- `wConstClos` for the mechanism.
  constClosIdx : Ref (OrdMap String),
  constClosCells : Ref (List (String, String)),
  nextConstClosId : Ref Int,
  -- the module's physical identities so far and the defects found against them,
  -- latest first (backend/wasm_symbols.mdk).  `closureChecked` is False for the
  -- gap census, which writes no module: there a use need not find its identity.
  -- `completionChecked` is False for the input-isolation harness
  -- (`emitProgramUnchecked`): its mismatched inputs can plan a call whose helper
  -- the plan leaves out, and its module is never assembled, so only the uses
  -- still waiting once it is complete go unjudged.
  symbols : Ref SymbolRegistry,
  symbolDefects : Ref (List SymbolDefect),
  closureChecked : Bool,
  completionChecked : Bool,
  trapImportNeeded : Ref Bool,
  trapIntNeeded : Ref Bool,
  -- located traps: the files a trap site names, in reverse number order, and
  -- their 1-based numbers; whether the located-trap runtime and the shared
  -- non-exhaustive-match trap are called.
  siteFiles : Ref (List String),
  siteFileNums : Ref (OrdMap Int),
  siteRtUsed : Ref Bool,
  siteNonexhUsed : Ref Bool,
  -- coded trap texts: one `$trapmsg_K` helper per DISTINCT text, numbered in
  -- first-use order.  `trapMsgIds` maps a text to its number (an OrdMap, so a
  -- lookup is O(log n)); `trapMsgFns` holds the helper definitions latest-first.
  -- See `trapMsgCall`.
  trapMsgIds : Ref (OrdMap Int),
  trapMsgFns : Ref (List String),
  -- the checked `Int` operators and `Int` shifts this emission called, by helper
  -- name (`add`, `left`, ...), for `intRuntimeLines` (wasm_preamble.mdk).
  intRtUsed : Ref (List String),
  useEPut : Ref Bool,
  useDivGuard : Ref Bool,
  useRng : Ref Bool,
  useHash : Ref Bool,
  useFloatHash : Ref Bool,
  useFloatRng : Ref Bool,
  useFileBytes : Ref Bool,
  useStrCodec : Ref Bool,
  useByteBlock : Ref Bool,
  useValueCmp : Ref Bool,
  useCharFromCode : Ref Bool,
  useCharClass : Ref Bool,
  -- ── lifted from module-level ambient cells (X-W.H) ─────────────────────
  -- PROGRAM-lifetime: the representation / runtime demand the plan's
  -- `wasmDemand` seeds (`seedDemandW`), plus the tuple arities and the
  -- statically-Float top-level globals.  Body emission may turn more on; the
  -- type / import / runtime sections read them.
  useStr : Ref Bool,
  useList : Ref Bool,
  useArray : Ref Bool,
  useRefBox : Ref Bool,
  useStrLeaf : Ref Bool,
  useFloat : Ref Bool,
  useU64 : Ref Bool,
  useI64 : Ref Bool,
  useStrSearch : Ref Bool,
  useValueAdd : Ref Bool,
  useValueSub : Ref Bool,
  useValueMul : Ref Bool,
  useValueDiv : Ref Bool,
  useValueMod : Ref Bool,
  useValueCmpNum : Ref Bool,
  useStrToInt : Ref Bool,
  useStrReverse : Ref Bool,
  useStrJoin : Ref Bool,
  tupleArities : Ref (List Int),
  wDispGroups : Ref (List DispGroup),
  -- the W7 scratch locals (`__rli2`, ...) the function being emitted references;
  -- see w7ScopeOpen.
  w7Used : Ref (OrdMap Unit),
}

freshWasmEmit : WGapMode -> WasmEmit
freshWasmEmit mode = WasmEmit {
  physical = None,
  externFacts = omEmpty,
  gapMode = mode,
  gapLog = Ref [],
  curGapBind = Ref "?",
  stringSegments = Ref [],
  nextStringSegmentId = Ref 0,
  strSegIds = Ref omEmpty,
  nextLambdaId = Ref 0,
  liftedDefinitions = Ref [],
  liftedDefinitionNames = Ref omEmpty,
  constClosIdx = Ref omEmpty,
  constClosCells = Ref [],
  nextConstClosId = Ref 0,
  symbols = Ref emptyRegistry,
  symbolDefects = Ref [],
  closureChecked = True,
  completionChecked = True,
  trapImportNeeded = Ref False,
  trapIntNeeded = Ref False,
  siteFiles = Ref [],
  siteFileNums = Ref omEmpty,
  siteRtUsed = Ref False,
  siteNonexhUsed = Ref False,
  trapMsgIds = Ref omEmpty,
  trapMsgFns = Ref [],
  intRtUsed = Ref [],
  useEPut = Ref False,
  useDivGuard = Ref False,
  useRng = Ref False,
  useHash = Ref False,
  useFloatHash = Ref False,
  useFloatRng = Ref False,
  useFileBytes = Ref False,
  useStrCodec = Ref False,
  useByteBlock = Ref False,
  useValueCmp = Ref False,
  useCharFromCode = Ref False,
  useCharClass = Ref False,
  useStr = Ref False,
  useList = Ref False,
  useArray = Ref False,
  useRefBox = Ref False,
  useStrLeaf = Ref False,
  useFloat = Ref False,
  useU64 = Ref False,
  useI64 = Ref False,
  useStrSearch = Ref False,
  useValueAdd = Ref False,
  useValueSub = Ref False,
  useValueMul = Ref False,
  useValueDiv = Ref False,
  useValueMod = Ref False,
  useValueCmpNum = Ref False,
  useStrToInt = Ref False,
  useStrReverse = Ref False,
  useStrJoin = Ref False,
  tupleArities = Ref [],
  wDispGroups = Ref [],
  w7Used = Ref omEmpty,
}

-- Declaration-derived facts are indexed once for each emission.
import types.capability_manifest.{ManifestRequirement}

data WasmEmitInputData =
  WasmEmitInputData (OrdMap (List Int)) RuntimeExternDomain ManifestRequirement

export type WasmEmitInput = WasmEmitInputData

export
makeWasmEmitInput : ManifestRequirement ->
  RuntimeExternDomain ->
  List (String, List String) ->
  WasmEmitInput
makeWasmEmitInput requirement domain ctorFieldTypes =
  WasmEmitInputData (ctorFloatFieldIndex ctorFieldTypes) domain requirement

export
inputRuntimeExternsW : WasmEmitInput -> RuntimeExternDomain
inputRuntimeExternsW (WasmEmitInputData _ names _) = names

export
inputCtorFloatFieldsW : WasmEmitInput -> OrdMap (List Int)
inputCtorFloatFieldsW (WasmEmitInputData fields _ _) = fields

inputManifestRequirementW : WasmEmitInput -> ManifestRequirement
inputManifestRequirementW (WasmEmitInputData _ _ requirement) = requirement

physicalPlanW : EmitPlan -> WasmDemandPlan
physicalPlanW plan = match plan.wasmPhysical
  Some p => p
  None => panic "internal error: missing-wasm-demand-plan"

emitDemandW : WasmEmit -> WasmDemandPlan
emitDemandW emit = match emit.physical
  Some p => p
  None => panic "internal error: missing-wasm-demand-plan"

seedPhysicalW : WasmEmit -> WasmDemandPlan -> Unit
seedPhysicalW emit physical =
  let _ = seedDemandW emit physical.representation
  let _ =
    forEachU
      ((name, cell) => setRef cell (hasWasmHelper physical name))
      [
        ("strLeafRuntimeLines", emit.useStrLeaf),
        ("strSearchRuntimeLines", emit.useStrSearch),
        ("valueEqRuntimeLines", emit.useValueCmp),
        ("valueCmpNumRuntimeLines", emit.useValueCmpNum),
        ("valueAddRuntimeLines", emit.useValueAdd),
        ("valueSubRuntimeLines", emit.useValueSub),
        ("valueMulRuntimeLines", emit.useValueMul),
        ("valueDivRuntimeLines", emit.useValueDiv),
        ("valueModRuntimeLines", emit.useValueMod),
        ("floatRuntimeLines", emit.useFloat),
        ("stderrByteImportLines", emit.trapImportNeeded),
        ("trapIntRuntimeLines", emit.trapIntNeeded),
      ]
  let _ = setRef emit.intRtUsed physical.intHelpers
  let _ = setRef emit.siteRtUsed physical.siteRuntime
  setRef emit.siteNonexhUsed physical.nonexhaustiveRuntime

-- ── program info threaded through the ref-mode emitter ───────────────────────
-- WasmProgramIndex owns the declaration-derived function, value, constructor,
-- record-fallback, lazy-global, and per-method-impl lookup tables for this emission.
-- Prog retains only the remaining ordered carriers: user type names, value-global
-- names, closure-use flag, impl entries, and declaration-derived input.
data WasmFnImplIndex = WasmFnImplIndex {
  fnNames : OrdMap Unit,
  valNames : OrdMap Unit,
  -- the defined arity of every top-level binding, constructor and impl entry
  -- (`core_ir_lower.programArities`)
  arities : ArityEnv,
  implBuckets : OrdMap (List CImplEntry),
  lazyGlobals : OrdMap Unit,
  -- the super count of each interface word (`DeclFacts.factSupers`); a word
  -- absent from it has no supers
  superCounts : OrdMap Int,
  -- the plan's self-recursive TRMC verdict (`EmitPlan.trmc`)
  trmc : TrmcVerdicts,
}

data WasmRecordValueIndex = WasmRecordValueIndex { fnValues : OrdMap Unit }

data WasmCtorIndex = WasmCtorIndex {
  arities : OrdMap Int,
  types : OrdMap String,
  ordinals : OrdMap Int,
  typeCtors : OrdMap (List String),
}

-- The program's binder table (`DeclFacts.factBinders`): every row by the
-- ordinal of its id (printed, so an env entry can name a row without parsing),
-- and the row of each top-level binding by its name.
data WasmStamps = WasmStamps {
  rows : OrdMap BinderRow,
  tops : OrdMap BinderRow,
}

data WasmProgramIndex = WasmProgramIndex {
  fnImpl : WasmFnImplIndex,
  recordValue : WasmRecordValueIndex,
  ctor : WasmCtorIndex,
  stamps : WasmStamps,
  typeContext : WasmTypeContext,
}

makeWasmStamps : List CBind -> List BinderRow -> WasmStamps
makeWasmStamps groups binderRows =
  let rows =
    omFromPairs
      (reverseL (map (r => (intToString (binderOrdinal r.brId), r)) binderRows))
      omEmpty
  WasmStamps {
    rows = rows,
    tops = omFromPairs (reverseL (flatMap (topRow rows) groups)) omEmpty,
  }

topRow : OrdMap BinderRow -> CBind -> List (String, BinderRow)
topRow rows (CBind name _ _ bid) =
  match omLookup (intToString (binderOrdinal bid)) rows
    Some row => [(name, row)]
    None => []

data Prog =
  Prog WasmProgramIndex (List String) (List String) Bool (List CImplEntry) WasmEmitInput WasmEmit FnCtx

-- What is true of the ONE function whose body is being emitted: the TMC loop
-- or dispatch-group context its tail leaves redirect to, its first-clause site
-- (packed by `sitePackedW`, 0 for none), and the binding name its gap messages
-- cite.  It is a value of the `Prog` the body is emitted with, never a cell: a
-- function that needs a different context emits its body with a derived `Prog`
-- (`progInFn`, `progForBinding`, `progWithTrmc`, `progWithDisp`), so there is no
-- state to restore, and a lifted lambda or let-group member starts without its
-- encloser's TMC loop, dispatch group or clause site however it was reached.  A
-- lifted lambda keeps citing its encloser's binding name.
data FnCtx = FnCtx {
  trmc : WTrmcCtx,
  disp : WDispCtx,
  site : Int,
  binding : String,
  origin : SymbolOrigin,
  localSlots : Ref (OrdMap LocalSlot),
  localTypes : Ref (List WasmRepr),
  nextLocal : Ref Int,
}

freshFnCtx : Unit -> FnCtx
freshFnCtx () = FnCtx {
  trmc = WTrmcOff,
  disp = WDispOff,
  site = 0,
  binding = "?",
  origin = SymbolOrigin "?" "" 0 0,
  localSlots = Ref omEmpty,
  localTypes = Ref [],
  nextLocal = Ref 0,
}

progValNames : Prog -> List String
progValNames (Prog _ _ vals _ _ _ _ _) = vals

progUseClos : Prog -> Bool
progUseClos (Prog _ _ _ uc _ _ _ _) = uc

-- W5: the lowered typeclass impl entries (CProgram's 4th field).
progImpls : Prog -> List CImplEntry
progImpls (Prog _ _ _ _ impls _ _ _) = impls

progIndex : Prog -> WasmProgramIndex
progIndex (Prog index _ _ _ _ _ _ _) = index

progEmit : Prog -> WasmEmit
progEmit (Prog _ _ _ _ _ _ emit _) = emit

progFnCtx : Prog -> FnCtx
progFnCtx (Prog _ _ _ _ _ _ _ fn) = fn

-- [prog] for emitting the body of another function: no TMC loop, no dispatch
-- group, no clause site; the binding name is inherited.
progInFn : Prog -> Prog
progInFn prog = progWithFnCtx prog { freshFnCtx () |
  binding = (progFnCtx prog).binding,
  origin = (progFnCtx prog).origin,
}

-- [progInFn prog] for the binding [name] at [loc], whose first clause is at [site].
progForBinding : String -> Loc -> Int -> Prog -> Prog
progForBinding name loc site prog = progWithFnCtx prog { freshFnCtx () |
  site = site,
  binding = name,
  origin = bindingOrigin name loc,
}

-- [prog] with its physical definitions and uses attributed to [label], for a
-- body that has no source binding of its own (an impl method, `main`, a value).
progWithOrigin : String -> Prog -> Prog
progWithOrigin label prog =
  progWithFnCtx prog { progFnCtx prog | origin = SymbolOrigin label "" 0 0 }

-- The binding name the body being emitted with [prog] cites in a gap message.
progBinding : Prog -> String
progBinding prog = (progFnCtx prog).binding

-- [prog] with [ctx] as the Stage-1 TMC loop context of the body about to be emitted.
progWithTrmc : WTrmcCtx -> Prog -> Prog
progWithTrmc ctx prog = progWithFnCtx prog { progFnCtx prog | trmc = ctx }

-- [prog] with [ctx] as the dispatch-group context of the body about to be emitted.
progWithDisp : WDispCtx -> Prog -> Prog
progWithDisp ctx prog = progWithFnCtx prog { progFnCtx prog | disp = ctx }

progWithFnCtx : Prog -> FnCtx -> Prog
progWithFnCtx (Prog index types vals uc impls input emit _) fn =
  Prog index types vals uc impls input emit fn

indexFnNamesW : WasmProgramIndex -> OrdMap Unit
indexFnNamesW index = index.fnImpl.fnNames

indexValNamesW : WasmProgramIndex -> OrdMap Unit
indexValNamesW index = index.fnImpl.valNames

indexAritiesW : WasmProgramIndex -> ArityEnv
indexAritiesW index = index.fnImpl.arities

indexImplsByMethodW : WasmProgramIndex -> OrdMap (List CImplEntry)
indexImplsByMethodW index = index.fnImpl.implBuckets

indexLazyGlobalsW : WasmProgramIndex -> OrdMap Unit
indexLazyGlobalsW index = index.fnImpl.lazyGlobals

progTrmcW : Prog -> TrmcVerdicts
progTrmcW prog = (progIndex prog).fnImpl.trmc

indexFnsUsedAsValuesW : WasmProgramIndex -> OrdMap Unit
indexFnsUsedAsValuesW index = index.recordValue.fnValues

indexCtorAritiesW : WasmProgramIndex -> OrdMap Int
indexCtorAritiesW index = index.ctor.arities

indexCtorTypesW : WasmProgramIndex -> OrdMap String
indexCtorTypesW index = index.ctor.types

indexCtorOrdinalsW : WasmProgramIndex -> OrdMap Int
indexCtorOrdinalsW index = index.ctor.ordinals

indexTypeCtorsW : WasmProgramIndex -> OrdMap (List String)
indexTypeCtorsW index = index.ctor.typeCtors

-- ── declaration-derived semantic input readers ────────────────────────────────
-- the DECLARATION word of the interface an impl entry implements (mirror of
-- llvm_emit's `implEntryIfaceWord`): a supplied method carries it as the first field
-- of its route key, an inherited default directly as `CImplDefault`'s first field —
-- the same `ifaceWordOf` word a `CMethod` occurrence carries (`narrowByIfaceW`).
implEntryIfaceWordW : CImplEntry -> String
implEntryIfaceWordW (CImplEntry _ _ _ (CImplTagged _ _ iface _ _ _ _)) = iface
implEntryIfaceWordW (CImplEntry _ _ _ (CImplDefault ifaceWord _ _ _ _ _ _)) =
  ifaceWord

-- the head tag / canonical key / clause of any per-instance entry
implEntryTagW : CImplEntry -> String
implEntryTagW (CImplEntry _ _ _ (CImplTagged t _ _ _ _ _ _)) = t
implEntryTagW (CImplEntry _ _ _ (CImplDefault _ t _ _ _ _ _)) = t

implEntryKeyW : CImplEntry -> String
implEntryKeyW (CImplEntry _ _ _ (CImplTagged _ k _ _ _ _ _)) = k
implEntryKeyW (CImplEntry _ _ _ (CImplDefault _ _ k _ _ _ _)) = k

implEntryPatsW : CImplEntry -> List Pat
implEntryPatsW (CImplEntry _ _ _ (CImplTagged _ _ _ _ _ pats _)) = pats
implEntryPatsW (CImplEntry _ _ _ (CImplDefault _ _ _ _ _ pats _)) = pats

implEntryMethodW : CImplEntry -> String
implEntryMethodW (CImplEntry m _ _ _) = m

-- does [entry] answer to the route word [word]?  A word names exactly one instance.
implEntryAnswersW : String -> CImplEntry -> Bool
implEntryAnswersW word entry = implEntryKeyW entry == word

-- the entries of the interface an occurrence resolved to (`""`: none recorded, and
-- nothing is narrowed), so two interfaces' same-spelled methods are never candidates
-- for one another (#1265, #1619)
narrowByIfaceW : String -> List CImplEntry -> List CImplEntry
narrowByIfaceW "" entries = entries
narrowByIfaceW iface entries =
  filterList (ent => implEntryIfaceWordW ent == iface) entries

-- #2076: the wasm peer of `llvm_emit.mdk`'s `ffiSigOf`/`isFfiExtern` — the host
-- bindings of `name` when it is a USER-declared FFI extern.  Built from
-- `makeWasmEmitInput`'s rows (empty for every caller of `makeWasmEmitInput`).
-- Consulted by `emitAppRef`/`emitTailCallW`/`emitVarRefPlain` ahead of the
-- runtime extern families, as `DemandScope` resolves a name.
ffiBindsOfW : Prog -> String -> Option (List (String, String))
ffiBindsOfW prog name = match omLookup name (progEmit prog).externFacts
  Some fact if fact.bindingKind == ForeignBinding => Some fact.hostBindings
  _ => None

isFfiExternW : Prog -> String -> Bool
isFfiExternW prog name = isSome (ffiBindsOfW prog name)

-- The plan's `jsffi` import for the user extern `name`, or the gap its
-- reference is.  `check --target` refuses a reached extern with no `js`
-- binding (T-TARGET-NO-BINDING), so only a lowering that skipped the target
-- check meets the last gap.  An `Array Int` result has no channel on either target
-- (compiler/FFI-ABI.md section 2.4), so wasm refuses it as native does.
jsImportForW : Prog -> String -> Result (List String) JsImport
jsImportForW prog name = match selectedJsImport prog name
  Some imp =>
    if not (allList jsCrossableHead (imp.result :: imp.params)) then
      Err
        (gapLP
          prog
          "wasm: a non-crossable type reached the lowering of foreign call '\{externDisplayW (progEmit prog) name}' (compiler/FFI-ABI.md section 1)")
    else if imp.result == "Array" then
      Err
        (gapLP
          prog
          "wasm: foreign call '\{externDisplayW (progEmit prog) name}' returns 'Array Int', which no FFI target can return (compiler/FFI-ABI.md section 2.4, docs/spec/WASM-SEMANTICS.md section 3.1). Declare the array as a parameter instead and have the binding fill it in place: its elements are copied back after the call returns")
    else
      Ok imp
  None => match ffiBindsOfW prog name
    Some binds if isSome (hostSymbol "js" binds) =>
      Err
        (gapLP
          prog
          "internal error: the emit plan has no `jsffi` import for the reached extern '\{externDisplayW (progEmit prog) name}'")
    _ =>
      Err
        (gapLP
          prog
          "wasm: the extern '\{externDisplayW (progEmit prog) name}' has no `js` binding, so the module has nothing to import for it; `check --target` refuses a reached extern with no binding for its target's host (T-TARGET-NO-BINDING)")

selectedJsImport : Prog -> String -> Option JsImport
selectedJsImport prog name = match omLookup name (progEmit prog).externFacts
  Some fact if fact.bindingKind
    == ForeignBinding => match hostSymbol "js" fact.hostBindings
    Some host =>
      map
        (shape => JsImport {
          medakaName = name,
          jsName = host,
          params = shape.parameterHeads,
          result = shape.resultHead,
        })
        fact.callableShape
    None => None
  _ => None

-- A user extern applied: with all its arguments, the arguments and then its
-- wrapper (`jsffiWrapperLines`); otherwise its eta closure, applied.
emitFfiAppW : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  CExpr ->
  String ->
  List CExpr ->
  CallEndW ->
  List String
emitFfiAppW prog env d hd name args end = match jsImportForW prog name
  Err gap => gap
  Ok imp =>
    if listLen args == listLen imp.params then
      flatMap (a => emitRefExpr prog env d a) args
        ++ [callFnW prog end (jsffiWrapperW prog imp) (listLen args)]
    else
      emitIndirectApp prog env d hd args end

-- A user extern named as a value: a captureless closure whose code unpacks its
-- arguments and calls the wrapper (the native peer is `emitFfiEtaClosure`).
emitFfiEtaW : Prog -> String -> List String
emitFfiEtaW prog name = match jsImportForW prog name
  Err gap => gap
  Ok imp =>
    let arity = listLen imp.params
    let lamName = "$mdk_ffi_" ++ injectiveIdent name
    let params = synthParams arity
    let body =
      flatMap argLoadAt (zipIdx params 0)
        ++ map (p => "local.get $" ++ gname p) params
        ++ [callFnW prog CallValueW (jsffiWrapperW prog imp) arity, "return"]
    let _ = noteFuncRef prog lamName
    let _ =
      addLiftedNamed
        prog
        lamName
        codeShapeW
        ([
            "  (func "
              ++ lamName
              ++ " (type $codety) (param $self (ref eq)) (param $args (ref $argarr)) (result (ref eq))",
          ]
          ++ map ("    " ++ _) (map localDeclRef params)
          ++ indent body
          ++ ["  )"])
    wConstClos prog lamName arity

-- The binding's wrapper, lifted once; its name without the `$`.  Its traps are
-- the native boundary's (compiler/FFI-ABI.md section 2.1a, 2.4).
jsffiWrapperW : Prog -> JsImport -> String
jsffiWrapperW prog imp =
  let emit = progEmit prog
  let name = jsffiWrapperId imp.medakaName
  let call = "foreign call '\{imp.jsName}'"
  let intTrap =
    if imp.result == "Int" then
      wasmTrap
        emit
        "E-PANIC"
        "\{call} returned a value outside Int's range -4611686018427387904..4611686018427387903 (docs/spec/WASM-SEMANTICS.md section 3.1); declare the result I64 to receive the full 64-bit range"
    else
      []
  let charTrap =
    if imp.result == "Char" then
      wasmTrap
        emit
        "E-PANIC"
        "\{call} returned a value that is not a valid Char: a Char must be a Unicode scalar, i.e. in 0..1114111 excluding the UTF-16 surrogates 55296..57343 (docs/spec/WASM-SEMANTICS.md section 3.1)"
    else
      []
  let copyTrap =
    if contains "Array" imp.params then
      wasmTrap
        emit
        "E-PANIC"
        "\{call} wrote a value outside Int's range -4611686018427387904..4611686018427387903 into an Array Int argument (docs/spec/WASM-SEMANTICS.md section 3.1)"
    else
      []
  let _ =
    addLiftedNamed
      prog
      ("$" ++ name)
      (FuncParams (listLen imp.params))
      (jsffiWrapperLines imp intTrap charTrap copyTrap)
  name

progFnMemberW : Prog -> String -> Bool
progFnMemberW prog n = omHasKey n (indexFnNamesW (progIndex prog))

-- val-name membership is served by this Prog's immutable index.
progValMemberW : Prog -> String -> Bool
progValMemberW prog x = omHasKey x (indexValNamesW (progIndex prog))

-- Pre-Prog scans receive this invocation's locally-built fn index directly.
fnMemberIndexW : OrdMap Unit -> String -> Bool
fnMemberIndexW fnNames n = omHasKey n fnNames

-- ── impl INDEX by method name (perf #382 — the #350/#349 twins) ───────────────
-- The `Prog` carries every impl clause as one flat `List CImplEntry` (`progImpls`),
-- and the emitter scans the WHOLE list per RKey/RDict dispatch site: `implForW`,
-- `methodImpls`,
-- `methodReturnsBoolW`, and the `emitImplFns`/`gatherImplGroup` group builder all do
-- `findByKeyArityW`/`flatMap implClauseFor`/`flatMap methodImplKey` over one method bucket.
-- EVERY one of those first filters by the METHOD name (`n == method`) — so restricting
-- the scan to just that method's entries yields the IDENTICAL first-match/flat-map
-- result, only faster.  Wasm inlines a dispatch chain PER call site (llvm outlines one
-- dispatcher), so these per-site scans multiply → O(sites · impls) on dispatch-heavy
-- code (#382). The private immutable index groups the entries by method name once per
-- invocation into per-method lists in ORIGINAL ORDER, so a multi-clause impl's first
-- clause still wins findByKeyArityW. Every per-method scan below routes through it.
-- method name of an impl entry (field 1 — the interface method it implements).
implEntryMethod : CImplEntry -> String
implEntryMethod (CImplEntry n _ _ _) = n

orEmptyEntriesW : Option (List CImplEntry) -> List CImplEntry
orEmptyEntriesW (Some xs) = xs
orEmptyEntriesW None = []

-- one LEFT fold prepending each entry to its method's bucket (O(1) per entry), then
-- `omMapValues reverseL` restores original order in each bucket — total O(entries).
-- (A right-append build would be O(bucket²) on a many-impl method; prepend+reverse is
-- linear, the same discipline the fn-index / ctor tables use.)
groupImplsByMethodW : List CImplEntry -> OrdMap (List CImplEntry)
groupImplsByMethodW entries =
  omMapValues reverseL (foldImplsByMethodW entries omEmpty)

makeWasmProgramIndex : EmitPlan ->
  DeclFacts ->
  List CBind ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  List (String, String) ->
  List CImplEntry ->
  List String ->
  List String ->
  WasmProgramIndex
makeWasmProgramIndex plan facts groups ctorArs ctorTypes impls fnNames valNames =
  makeWasmProgramIndexWithLazy
    plan.wasmInputs.ctorFloatFields
    facts
    groups
    ctorArs
    ctorTypes
    impls
    fnNames
    valNames
    plan.lazyGlobals
    plan.trmc

makeWasmProgramIndexGaps : OrdMap (List Int) ->
  TrmcVerdicts ->
  DeclFacts ->
  List CBind ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  List (String, String) ->
  List CImplEntry ->
  List String ->
  List String ->
  WasmProgramIndex
makeWasmProgramIndexGaps ctorFields trmc facts groups ctorArs ctorTypes impls fnNames valNames =
  makeWasmProgramIndexWithLazy
    ctorFields
    facts
    groups
    ctorArs
    ctorTypes
    impls
    fnNames
    valNames
    []
    trmc

makeWasmProgramIndexWithLazy : OrdMap (List Int) ->
  DeclFacts ->
  List CBind ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  List (String, String) ->
  List CImplEntry ->
  List String ->
  List String ->
  List String ->
  TrmcVerdicts ->
  WasmProgramIndex
makeWasmProgramIndexWithLazy ctorFields facts groups ctorArs ctorTypes impls fnNames valNames lazyNames trmc =
  let fnIndex = omFromNames fnNames omEmpty
  let valIndex = omFromNames valNames omEmpty
  let ctorArIndex = omFromPairs (reverseL ctorArs) omEmpty
  let ctorTyIndex = omFromPairs (reverseL ctorTypes) omEmpty
  let typeCtors = typeCtorsOfW (reverseL ctorTypes) omEmpty
  let ctorOrds =
    ctorOrdsOfW (distinctTypeNames ctorTypes) ctorTyIndex typeCtors omEmpty
  let usedFns =
    scanFnValueUses fnIndex ctorArs groups
      ++ scanImplValueUses fnIndex ctorArs impls
  WasmProgramIndex {
    fnImpl = WasmFnImplIndex {
      fnNames = fnIndex,
      valNames = valIndex,
      arities =
        programArities (CProgram groups ctorArs ctorTypes impls [] noDeclFacts),
      implBuckets = groupImplsByMethodW impls,
      lazyGlobals = omFromNames lazyNames omEmpty,
      superCounts = omFromPairs facts.factSupers omEmpty,
      trmc = trmc,
    },
    recordValue = WasmRecordValueIndex {
      fnValues = omFromNames usedFns omEmpty,
    },
    ctor = WasmCtorIndex {
      arities = ctorArIndex,
      types = ctorTyIndex,
      ordinals = ctorOrds,
      typeCtors = typeCtors,
    },
    stamps = makeWasmStamps groups facts.factBinders,
    typeContext =
      wasmTypeContext
        ctorFields
        (CProgram groups ctorArs ctorTypes impls [] facts),
  }

foldImplsByMethodW : List CImplEntry ->
  OrdMap (List CImplEntry) ->
  OrdMap (List CImplEntry)
foldImplsByMethodW [] m = m
foldImplsByMethodW (e :: rest) m =
  let k = implEntryMethod e
  foldImplsByMethodW rest (omInsert k (e :: orEmptyEntriesW (omLookup k m)) m)

-- [method]'s impl entries from this Prog's immutable bucket, in original order.
-- Every whole-`progImpls` per-site scan routes through this lookup.
methodEntriesW : Prog -> String -> List CImplEntry
methodEntriesW prog method =
  orEmptyEntriesW (omLookup method (indexImplsByMethodW (progIndex prog)))

-- The defined arity of a callee reached outside an application (a value-position
-- occurrence, a dispatch-group member), read from the program as
-- `core_ir_lower.stampCallModes` reads it for an application.
definedArityW : Prog -> CExpr -> Option Int
definedArityW prog hd =
  definedArityOf (indexAritiesW (progIndex prog)) omEmpty hd

-- a top-level function's parameter count, or -1 when [n] names no function (the
-- contract the shared dispatch-group detection takes)
fnParamCountW : Prog -> String -> Int
fnParamCountW prog n =
  if progFnMemberW prog n then
    optionOr (-1) (definedArityW prog (CVar n AGlobal))
  else
    -1

-- W9: canonicalize a referenced fn name against the defined-fn set, mirroring DCE's
-- canonRef + the LLVM emitter's canonFnName.  Mangling renames prelude defs to
-- `core__<name>` AND rewrites the uses it can see; under the old mangle-first order it
-- ran before the passes that SYNTHESIZE bare prelude references (notably string-interp
-- `\{e}` → `debug`/`debugStringLit`/`displayListItems`, and `/=` → `not`), so such a
-- bare ref did not match its `core__`-mangled def by string equality.  The repair: if
-- the bare name isn't a defined fn but its `core__` form is, use the mangled name.
-- Since #2809 the emit drivers elaborate FIRST and mangle after, so those synthesized
-- references are renamed too.  Accommodation 12 of the census in
-- `compiler/TYPECHECK-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md` SA-10a item 20, and it retires with it —
-- each of the four mirrored copies on its own measurement.
canonFn : Prog -> String -> String
canonFn prog n =
  if progFnMemberW prog n then
    n
  else if progFnMemberW prog ("core__" ++ n) then
    "core__" ++ n
  else
    n

-- ── program entry ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Names of lifted defines whose body is fully determined by the name (the eta-wrap
-- ctor `$mdk_wctor_<C>` and extern `$mdk_ext_<name>` closures) — used to dedup so a
-- ctor/extern referenced point-free at MORE THAN ONE site emits its lifted (func …)
-- ONCE.  `noteFuncRef` already deduped the matching `(elem declare)`, but `addLifted`
-- did not dedup the define, so a second use-site duplicated the func → "duplicate func
-- identifier" at wasm-tools assembly (`$mdk_lamN` names are unique, so they still route
-- through the plain `addLifted`).  Per-emission `WasmEmit` state owns its dedup set.
-- perf #382: both named-lift and function-reference sets preserve O(log n) membership;
-- companion lists retain insertion order for their module-end drains.

-- ── W6 string state ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- `useStr` records whether the program uses any String/Char literal, the
-- byte-level IO externs (putStr/putStrLn/…), or a String-returning extern
-- (intToString/charToStr/stringConcat/…) — any of which forces the §3.3 `$str`
-- aggregate + the byte-write runtime into the module (and ref-mode, since a String
-- is a boxed (ref eq) value).  `WasmEmit.stringSegments` accumulates the passive data
-- segments for string literals: one `(data $strseg_N "…")` per DISTINCT byte payload
-- (`freshStrSeg` interns by content), init'd via `array.new_data`, the
-- §11-preferred non-const-array scheme. Both segment state and `useStr` itself belong
-- to each fresh `WasmEmit` record (a `Ref Bool` field, not an ambient cell).
-- ── gap census (mirrors LLVM's per-emission gap recording) ───────────────────
-- The WasmGC emitter normally `panic`s at the first node it can't lower (`gap`).
-- In CENSUS mode the gap helpers instead RECORD the reason and return a
-- type-appropriate placeholder so emission CONTINUES, surfacing EVERY gap over the
-- whole compiler graph in one run (the LLVM-self-hosting playbook).  Default
-- (record OFF) is behaviourally identical to today — every gap still `panic`s the
-- same message, so the existing gates stay green.
-- The event log and its attribution travel only in `WasmEmit`; no gap state is
-- shared between public emission calls.
gapEventsOfW : WasmEmit -> List String
gapEventsOfW emit = reverseL !emit.gapLog

setGapBindingOfW : WasmEmit -> String -> Unit
setGapBindingOfW emit name = setRef emit.curGapBind name

noteGapW : WasmEmit -> String -> Unit
noteGapW emit reason = noteGapAtW emit !emit.curGapBind reason

noteGapAtW : WasmEmit -> String -> String -> Unit
noteGapAtW emit binding reason =
  setRef emit.gapLog ("\{binding}\t\{reason}" :: !emit.gapLog)

-- typed gap-tolerant variants, one per return shape the `gap` call sites need.
-- Each records (census mode) or panics (default), returning a placeholder.
gapL : WasmEmit -> String -> List String
gapL emit reason = match emit.gapMode
  WGapRecord => let _ = noteGapW emit reason in []
  WGapStrict => gap reason

gapLTy : WasmEmit -> String -> (List String, WTy)
gapLTy emit reason = match emit.gapMode
  WGapRecord => let _ = noteGapW emit reason in ([], WInt)
  WGapStrict => gap reason

-- an unresolved name is an OBSERVATION ("this lookup found nothing"), not a
-- claim that wasm codegen lacks coverage for it — `gap`'s "wasm_emit gap — "
-- prefix asserts the latter, and asserting a category the emitter cannot
-- verify is exactly what T-22 (AGENTS.md) is about: on the untypechecked,
-- prelude-free probe path an interface method occurrence (e.g. `.[i]`'s
-- `index`) NEVER resolves to anything but a bare unbound name — not because
-- wasm codegen is missing it, but because the probe skipped typecheck/marker,
-- the pass that would have turned it into a dispatchable `CMethod`.  Twelve+
-- fixtures sat ledgered as "wasm gaps" for weeks on exactly this laundered
-- claim (test/engine_divergence.txt).  So an unbound-name lookup miss is
-- reported plainly — no "gap" wording, let the reader diagnose the cause —
-- while every OTHER gap call site here is a genuine, verified codegen-coverage
-- gap (an exhaustive match with no arm for the node/op/extern shape) and keeps
-- the `gap` wording, which is accurate for that case.
gapUnboundL : WasmEmit -> String -> List String
gapUnboundL emit reason = match emit.gapMode
  WGapRecord => let _ = noteGapW emit reason in []
  WGapStrict => panic reason

gapUnboundLTy : WasmEmit -> String -> (List String, WTy)
gapUnboundLTy emit reason = match emit.gapMode
  WGapRecord => let _ = noteGapW emit reason in ([], WInt)
  WGapStrict => panic reason

gapS : WasmEmit -> String -> String
gapS emit reason = match emit.gapMode
  WGapRecord => let _ = noteGapW emit reason in "0"
  WGapStrict => gap reason

gapSInt : WasmEmit -> String -> (String, Int)
gapSInt emit reason = match emit.gapMode
  WGapRecord => let _ = noteGapW emit reason in ("0", 0)
  WGapStrict => gap reason

gapOptE : WasmEmit -> String -> Option CExpr
gapOptE emit reason = match emit.gapMode
  WGapRecord => let _ = noteGapW emit reason in None
  WGapStrict => gap reason

gapL2 : WasmEmit -> String -> (List String, Env)
gapL2 emit reason = match emit.gapMode
  WGapRecord => let _ = noteGapW emit reason in ([], envEmpty)
  WGapStrict => gap reason

gapL3 : WasmEmit -> String -> (List String, List String, Env)
gapL3 emit reason = match emit.gapMode
  WGapRecord => let _ = noteGapW emit reason in ([], [], envEmpty)
  WGapStrict => gap reason

gapLP : Prog -> String -> List String
gapLP prog reason = gapL (progEmit prog) reason

gapUnboundLP : Prog -> String -> List String
gapUnboundLP prog reason = gapUnboundL (progEmit prog) reason

-- The fallthrough for a runtime extern wasm does not lower.  The extern check
-- (`refuseUnprovidedExternsW`) has already refused it in strict mode and
-- recorded it in record mode, so record mode adds no second event, and strict
-- mode reaching here means the two disagree about which references are free.
unprovidedExternW : WasmEmit -> String -> List String
unprovidedExternW emit name = match emit.gapMode
  WGapRecord => []
  WGapStrict => panic (unrefusedExternMessage WasmBackend name)

gapSP : Prog -> String -> String
gapSP prog reason = gapS (progEmit prog) reason

gapSIntP : Prog -> String -> (String, Int)
gapSIntP prog reason = gapSInt (progEmit prog) reason

gapL2P : Prog -> String -> (List String, Env)
gapL2P prog reason = gapL2 (progEmit prog) reason

gapL3P : Prog -> String -> (List String, List String, Env)
gapL3P prog reason = gapL3 (progEmit prog) reason

-- ── W7 collection state ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Which collection reps the program actually uses (gates their type-section decls,
-- peer to `useStr`).  `useList`: any CList/CRangeList or a HCons/HNil match
-- head → the cons-cell `$C_Cons` + root `$T_List` (Nil is an i31).  `useArray`:
-- any CArray/CRangeArray/CIndex/CSlice → the `$arr` (array (mut (ref eq))) type.
-- `useRefBox`: any Ref/setRef/.value → the `$refbox` 1-field mutable struct.
-- `tupleArities`: the distinct tuple arities present (CTuple / HTuple) → one
-- per-arity struct `$C_TupN`.  Records reuse the EXISTING per-ctor struct ($C_<ctor>,
-- already declared by the W3 ctor type section since a named-field ctor is in the
-- ctor table) — they need no new type, only the field-order table below.
-- ── W8 extern-use state ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Which W8 LEAF runtime groups the program reaches (gates their preamble
-- emission, peer to useStr).  useStrLeaf: any pure-WAT string leaf op
-- (++/charToStr/stringConcat/stringSlice/toUpper/toLower) → the strLeafRuntime.
-- The per-emission RNG/hash observations live in WasmEmit; `WasmEmit.useEPut` gates the
-- stderr import + runtime.
-- B5 (RUNTIME-TRAP-UNIFY §3 (5)): per-emission event set while a coded runtime trap
-- writes stderr bytes. Body emission precedes late scalar/ref import bindings, so strict
-- lets expose this physical fact without ambient authority.

isLazyGlobalW : Prog -> String -> Bool
isLazyGlobalW prog x = omHasKey x (indexLazyGlobalsW (progIndex prog))

-- W8b: the program uses Float (a Float literal, a Float extern, or a Float arith op).
-- Forces ref-mode (a Float is a boxed (ref eq) $float struct) + gates the Float runtime
-- (floatRuntimeLines + the floatToString host import).  WasmEmit.useFloatHash / useFloatRng
-- gate the hashFloat / randomFloat runtimes (which need the shared mix64 / next_u64).

-- W8b: the program uses stringIndexOf / stringCompare (the strSearchRuntime).
-- WasmEmit.useValueCmp records layer-9 per-emission demand from a ref-mode
-- `==`/`/=`/ordering binop in a string-using program for the runtime-shape-dispatched
-- $mdk_value_eq / $mdk_value_cmp
-- (Core IR is type-erased, so a String `==` cannot be told from an Int `==` statically;
-- the old i31-only lowering trapped `illegal cast` on a String operand).  Its producer
-- also forces useStrSearch so $mdk_str_compare (the byte comparator) is in scope.

-- A0/A1 (poly-`Num`-on-Float): the program routes an arithmetic binop through the
-- runtime value-tag-dispatched $mdk_value_add/sub/mul/div/mod helpers (a polymorphic
-- `Num a` operand — see isPolyNumOperand).  Gates valueArithRuntimeLines.
-- A1 (poly-`Num`-on-Float): the pattern-var names bound at the CURRENT function's
-- POLYMORPHIC `Num`/`Ord` param positions — a param whose declared type head is a type
-- VARIABLE (lowercase-initial) used arithmetically, OR (no declared sig) any param used
-- arithmetically.  The wasm peer of native's `isNumPolyParam`/LTNum seed.  A binop with
-- such an operand routes to the runtime value-dispatch helper instead of the trapping
-- inline int primitive; the static Int/Float fast paths (declared `Int`/`Float`, literals,
-- structural Float) are unchanged.  Seeded (and reset to []) per fn in emitRefFnBind.
-- W12: the program uses any IO host-surface extern (readFile / fileExists / args /
-- getEnv / exit).  Gates the IO host imports + the byte-channel marshaling runtime.
-- All of these touch a $str (path/result), so they also force useStr.
-- W8b: the names KNOWN to hold a Float in the CURRENT function/impl body — set while
-- emitting an `impl Num Float` (etc.) method, whose params are Float but appear as bare
-- CVars the structural detector can't otherwise see.  `cexprIsFloat` consults this so
-- `add a b = a + b` lowers to f64 ops.  Reset to [] before every non-Float-impl body.
-- #288: top-level nullary value bindings whose RHS is statically Float (e.g.
-- `nan = 0.0 / 0.0`).  A `global.get` of such a binding carries no static Float
-- tag at the USE site, so a `nan <= nan` comparison would fall to the poly
-- runtime-dispatched path.  Seeding these names (in emitRefProgram, before any body
-- emission) lets `cexprIsFloat` recognize the operand as Float so the comparison
-- lowers to inline `f64.le`/`f64.ge` (IEEE-correct, NaN → False), mirroring native's
-- fcmp on a global whose stamp is Float.
-- (#305: the poly path is IEEE-correct at NaN too now — ordering there calls the
-- per-op $mdk_value_lt/le/gt/ge rather than comparing a 3-way against 0 — so this
-- seeding is a code-quality win (inline f64, no call), no longer a correctness fix.)
-- convert one ctorFieldTypeNames entry to (ctorName, [floatFieldIndex, …]).
freshStrSeg : Prog -> List Int -> Int
freshStrSeg prog bytes =
  let emit = progEmit prog
  let key = strSegKey bytes
  match omLookup key !emit.strSegIds
    Some i => i
    None =>
      let i = !emit.nextStringSegmentId
      let _ = setRef emit.nextStringSegmentId (i + 1)
      let _ = setRef emit.stringSegments ((i, bytes) :: !emit.stringSegments)
      let _ = setRef emit.strSegIds (omInsert key i !emit.strSegIds)
      let _ =
        registerW
          emit
          (declareSymbol
            (WasmData (strSegNameW i))
            DataDecl
            (progFnCtx prog).origin)
      i

-- the name of string segment [i], without its `$`
strSegNameW : Int -> String
strSegNameW i = "strseg_" ++ intToString i

-- `$strseg_<i>` read by a body
strSegRefW : Prog -> Int -> String
strSegRefW prog i =
  let _ =
    registerW
      (progEmit prog)
      (checkRef (WasmData (strSegNameW i)) (progFnCtx prog).origin)
  "$" ++ strSegNameW i

-- the `strSegIds` key of a payload: its byte values, comma-separated.  Distinct byte
-- lists give distinct keys (a comma follows every value but the last, and only the
-- empty list spells as "").
strSegKey : List Int -> String
strSegKey bytes = joinWith "," (map intToString bytes)

freshLamId : WasmEmit -> Int
freshLamId emit =
  let n = !emit.nextLambdaId
  let _ = setRef emit.nextLambdaId (n + 1)
  n

-- Lift the definition [def] of function [name], whose shape is [shape].  The
-- lifted section is written only for a module with closures, so only there does
-- the registry learn of the definition.
addLifted : Prog -> String -> WasmShape -> List String -> Unit
addLifted prog name shape def =
  let emit = progEmit prog
  let _ = if progUseClos prog then defineFnW prog name shape
  setRef emit.liftedDefinitions (def :: !emit.liftedDefinitions)

-- addLifted, but keyed by a unique define name: a second call
-- with an already-seen name is a no-op, so a point-free ctor/extern used at N sites
-- lifts its (func …) exactly once.
addLiftedNamed : Prog -> String -> WasmShape -> List String -> Unit
addLiftedNamed prog name shape def =
  let emit = progEmit prog
  if omHasKey name !emit.liftedDefinitionNames then
    ()
  else
    let _ =
      setRef
        emit.liftedDefinitionNames
        (omInsert name () !emit.liftedDefinitionNames)
    addLifted prog name shape def

-- the shape of a `$codety` function: its self and its argument array
codeShapeW : WasmShape
codeShapeW = FuncOfType "codety" 2

-- ── the physical-identity registry (backend/wasm_symbols.mdk) ─────────────────

-- Apply one registry step for [emit]: keep the registry it returns, or keep the
-- defect it found.
registerW : WasmEmit ->
  (SymbolRegistry -> Result SymbolDefect SymbolRegistry) ->
  Unit
registerW emit step = match step !emit.symbols
  Ok reg => setRef emit.symbols reg
  Err d => setRef emit.symbolDefects (d :: !emit.symbolDefects)

-- a physical name as the registry keys it: without its `$`
symNameW : String -> String
symNameW n = if startsWith "$" n then stringSlice 1 (stringLength n) n else n

-- [prog] defines function [name] with [shape]; a function declared through a
-- type uses that type, which the type section must declare.
defineFnW : Prog -> String -> WasmShape -> Unit
defineFnW prog name shape =
  let emit = progEmit prog
  let origin = (progFnCtx prog).origin
  let _ = match shape
    FuncOfType t _ =>
      if emit.closureChecked then
        registerW emit (checkTypeUse t (symNameW name) origin)
    _ => ()
  registerW emit (defineSymbol (WasmFunc (symNameW name)) shape origin)

-- the instruction that calls `$<target>` with [operands] operands
callFnW : Prog -> CallEndW -> String -> Int -> String
callFnW prog end target operands =
  callFnAtW (progEmit prog) (progFnCtx prog).origin end target operands

-- `callFnW` for code no binding's body owns, its uses attributed to [origin]
callFnAtW : WasmEmit -> SymbolOrigin -> CallEndW -> String -> Int -> String
callFnAtW emit origin end target operands =
  let _ = registerW emit (checkCall (WasmFunc target) operands origin)
  callInstrW end target

-- `call $<name>` of a runtime helper or host import, with [operands] operands
rtCallW : Prog -> String -> Int -> String
rtCallW prog name operands = callFnW prog CallValueW name operands

-- the Int box seam's two calls
unboxIntW : Prog -> String
unboxIntW prog = rtCallW prog "mdk_unbox_int" 1

boxIntW : Prog -> String
boxIntW prog = rtCallW prog "mdk_box_int" 1

-- the uses of code emitted outside any binding: coded traps and their helpers
trapOriginW : SymbolOrigin
trapOriginW = SymbolOrigin "coded trap" "" 0 0

-- `<op> <name>` for the access [op] (`global.get`, `global.set`) of the global
-- [name].  The gap census declares no globals, so it checks no access.
globalW : Prog -> String -> String -> String
globalW prog op name =
  let emit = progEmit prog
  let _ =
    if emit.closureChecked then
      registerW
        emit
        (checkRef (WasmGlobal (symNameW name)) (progFnCtx prog).origin)
  "\{op} \{name}"

-- the SplitMix64 state global `rngStateGlobalLines` declares
rngStateW : String
rngStateW = "$mdk_rng_state"

-- `ref.func` of [name] in a body: the function must exist and an element
-- declaration must list it.
refFuncW : Prog -> String -> String
refFuncW prog name =
  let origin = (progFnCtx prog).origin
  let _ = registerW (progEmit prog) (checkRef (WasmFunc (symNameW name)) origin)
  let _ = registerW (progEmit prog) (checkRef (WasmElem (symNameW name)) origin)
  "ref.func " ++ name

-- the module-level identities, declared before any body is emitted: the type
-- section, the host imports, the planned runtime helpers, the globals and the
-- closure-apply element entry, whose function the closure helpers define
seedSymbolsW : Prog -> WasmDemandPlan -> List String -> Unit
seedSymbolsW prog physical globals =
  let emit = progEmit prog
  let origin = SymbolOrigin "module" "" 0 0
  let declare = sym shape => registerW emit (declareSymbol sym shape origin)
  let _ =
    forEachU (t => declare (WasmType t) TypeDecl) physical.representationTypes
  let _ =
    forEachU
      (imp => declare (WasmFunc imp.watSymbol) FuncImported)
      physical.imports
  let _ = forEachU (registerW emit) (declarePlannedHelpers physical)
  let _ = forEachU (g => declare (WasmGlobal g) GlobalDecl) globals
  if progUseClos prog then
    let _ = declare (WasmElem "mdk_pap") ElemDecl
    registerW emit (checkRef (WasmFunc "mdk_pap") origin)

-- every defect this emission found: those found as it went, then (unless it is
-- the census or the input-isolation harness) one for each identity a use still
-- waits for
symbolDefectsW : WasmEmit -> List SymbolDefect
symbolDefectsW emit =
  reverseL !emit.symbolDefects
    ++ (if emit.closureChecked && emit.completionChecked then
      unresolved !emit.symbols
    else
      [])

-- ── S-4: capture-free closure hoisting (the WasmGC peer of S-1/S-2's LLVM cells) ──
-- A `$clos` struct whose capture set is EMPTY has fields that are ALL constant: the
-- code pointer is `ref.func $lam`, the arity is an `i32.const`, and the env is a
-- zero-length `array.new_fixed $argarr 0`.  Such a struct is identical at every entry
-- to the enclosing function, so it need not be rebuilt per entry: emit it ONCE as an
-- IMMUTABLE module global and read it with a single `global.get`.
--
-- This is NOT a port of the LLVM mechanism — that one hoists a flat `[2 x i64]`
-- `internal constant` cell and hands back a `ptrtoint` constant-expression (F8).  The
-- WasmGC representation is a GC struct, so the analogue is a global whose INITIALIZER
-- is a `struct.new`, which needs wasm-GC constant expressions.  Confirmed accepted by
-- this project's whole toolchain before the mechanism was written: `wasm-tools parse`,
-- `wasm-tools validate --features=all`, and the Node engine `test/wasm/run.js` uses
-- all accept `(global $g (ref $clos) (struct.new $clos (ref.func $l) (i32.const N)
-- (array.new_fixed $argarr 0)))` and read back field `$arity` correctly.  There is no
-- prior const-initialized global in this file (every other one is `mut` + a runtime
-- store), so that probe — not precedent — is what licenses this.
--
-- `ref.func` inside a global initializer self-declares the function reference (the
-- validator's `refs` set is collected from module fields OUTSIDE function bodies,
-- globals included), so no `(elem declare)` entry is required for validity — but the
-- call sites keep their existing `noteFuncRef` anyway, since the lifted code function
-- is also reachable through ordinary code paths.
--
-- SOUND because a `$clos` struct is never mutated after construction on any path: its
-- three fields are IMMUTABLE in the type (`$clos` declares no `mut` field), so unlike
-- LLVM there is not even a back-patch to reason about.  The knot for a mutually- or
-- self-recursive let-group is tied by RECONSTRUCTION inside each lifted member's
-- prologue (`emitLgLifted`'s `memberRebuilds`), which this does not touch.
--
-- Deduped by initializer TEXT: two references to the same capture-free closure share
-- one global.  That is observationally safe here for the same reason it is in LLVM —
-- a closure value has no identity in this language (no reference equality on
-- functions), and `$mdk_apply`/`$mdk_pap` only READ the struct, allocating any partial
-- application into a fresh cell.
wConstClos : Prog -> String -> Int -> List String
wConstClos prog lamName arity =
  let emit = progEmit prog
  let origin = (progFnCtx prog).origin
  -- a global's initializer declares its own function reference, so only the
  -- function and the `$clos` type have to exist
  let _ = registerW emit (checkRef (WasmFunc (symNameW lamName)) origin)
  let _ =
    if emit.closureChecked then
      registerW emit (checkTypeUse "clos" (symNameW lamName) origin)
  let initBody =
    "(struct.new $clos (ref.func \{lamName}) (i32.const \{intToString arity}) (array.new_fixed $argarr 0))"
  match omLookup initBody !emit.constClosIdx
    Some g => [globalW prog "global.get" g]
    None =>
      let g = "$mdk_cc_" ++ intToString !emit.nextConstClosId
      let _ =
        registerW
          emit
          (declareSymbol (WasmGlobal (symNameW g)) GlobalDecl origin)
      let _ = setRef emit.nextConstClosId (!emit.nextConstClosId + 1)
      let _ = setRef emit.constClosIdx (omInsert initBody g !emit.constClosIdx)
      let _ = setRef emit.constClosCells ((g, initBody) :: !emit.constClosCells)
      [globalW prog "global.get" g]

-- the hoisted globals, in emission order.  Drained by emitRefProgram AFTER every body
-- has been emitted (the same after-body discipline `dataSegs` / `trapImport` use), so
-- this must be bound late even though the lines are placed with the other globals.
wConstClosGlobalLines : WasmEmit -> List String
wConstClosGlobalLines emit =
  map oneConstClosGlobal (reverseL !emit.constClosCells)

oneConstClosGlobal : (String, String) -> String
oneConstClosGlobal (g, initBody) = "  (global \{g} (ref $clos) \{initBody})"

-- [nm] is taken by `ref.func`, so the element declaration lists it.  That
-- declaration is written only for a module with closures.
noteFuncRef : Prog -> String -> Unit
noteFuncRef prog nm =
  if progUseClos prog then
    registerW
      (progEmit prog)
      (declareSymbol (WasmElem (symNameW nm)) ElemDecl (progFnCtx prog).origin)

-- The module text, or the physical defects that keep it from being written.
export
emitProgram : WasmEmitInput ->
  EmitPlan ->
  CProgram ->
  Result (List SymbolDefect) String
emitProgram input plan cp =
  emitProgramWith (freshWasmEmit WGapStrict) input plan cp

-- The X-W.H1/H2 same-process input/state-isolation harnesses (`reemitInput` and
-- peers, compiler/entries/wasm_emit_typed_main.mdk) deliberately re-emit ONE
-- lowered `CProgram` under MISMATCHED inputs (P's real program with U's
-- ctor/method tables) specifically to prove each field
-- independently influences the physical plan (`P_NE_CTOR` etc). Such a
-- combination never occurs in a real compile (there sigs/ctors/methods are
-- always derived from the SAME decls as the program), can
-- legitimately desync a gating decision that reads the mismatched table (e.g.
-- a plan forcing a Float auto-print with no Float anywhere in the
-- program's own body), and is never assembled by wasm-tools -- so it is not
-- this check's business, same reasoning as `emitProgramGaps` below. Exported
-- for that harness ONLY; every real caller (build/run, every fixture-driven
-- gate) stays on the checked `emitProgram`.
export
emitProgramUnchecked : WasmEmitInput ->
  EmitPlan ->
  CProgram ->
  Result (List SymbolDefect) String
emitProgramUnchecked input plan cp =
  emitProgramCore
    { freshWasmEmit WGapStrict | completionChecked = False }
    input
    plan
    cp

-- Record mode is a complete ordinary emission with a fresh event lifecycle.
-- It is intentionally separate from the all-binding/no-main census below.
export
emitProgramRecord : WasmEmitInput ->
  EmitPlan ->
  CProgram ->
  Result (List SymbolDefect) (String, List String)
emitProgramRecord input plan cp =
  let emit = freshWasmEmit WGapRecord
  map (text => (text, gapEventsOfW emit)) (emitProgramWith emit input plan cp)

emitProgramWith : WasmEmit ->
  WasmEmitInput ->
  EmitPlan ->
  CProgram ->
  Result (List SymbolDefect) String
emitProgramWith emit input plan cp = match emitProgramCore emit input plan cp
  Err defects => Err defects
  Ok text =>
    -- WGapRecord is the tolerant/census mode (mirrors emitProgramGaps below): it
    -- continues past an unsupported node by RECORDING a gap event instead of
    -- aborting, so its assembled text is intentionally allowed to be incomplete/
    -- self-inconsistent -- not a real module, so not this check's business.
    -- Only WGapStrict (the real, on-by-default production path) is asserted.
    let _ = match emit.gapMode
      WGapStrict => assertEmittedClosureW text
      WGapRecord => ()
    Ok text

-- Strict and record modes share one semantic gateway; only target gaps may
-- become record events instead of a refusal.
refuseUnprovidedExternsW : WasmEmit ->
  WasmEmitInput ->
  EmitPlan ->
  CProgram ->
  Unit
refuseUnprovidedExternsW emit input plan cp =
  let validation =
    validateForEmission
      WasmBackend
      (inputRuntimeExternsW input)
      (inputManifestRequirementW input)
      plan
      cp
  match validation.defects
    bad :: _ => panic (coreDefectMessage bad)
    [] => match validation.externFindings
      [] => ()
      findings => match emit.gapMode
        WGapStrict => panic (renderExternRefusal findings)
        WGapRecord =>
          forEachU
            (f => noteGapAtW emit (findingBinding f) (renderExternFinding f))
            findings

emitProgramCore : WasmEmit ->
  WasmEmitInput ->
  EmitPlan ->
  CProgram ->
  Result (List SymbolDefect) String
emitProgramCore emit input plan cp =
  emitUniqueProgram
    { emit |
      externFacts = requirementFacts plan.externRequirements,
      physical = plan.wasmPhysical,
    }
    input
    plan
    cp

emitUniqueProgram : WasmEmit ->
  WasmEmitInput ->
  EmitPlan ->
  CProgram ->
  Result (List SymbolDefect) String
emitUniqueProgram emit input plan (cp@(CProgram groups ctorArs ctorTypes impls _ facts)) =
  let _ = refuseUnprovidedExternsW emit input plan cp
  let physical = physicalPlanW plan
  let _ = seedPhysicalW emit physical
  let fnNames = collectFnNames groups
  let valNames = collectValNames groups
  let index =
    makeWasmProgramIndex
      plan
      facts
      groups
      ctorArs
      ctorTypes
      impls
      fnNames
      valNames
  let useClos = physical.useClos
  let useRef = physical.useRef
  let typeNames = distinctTypeNames ctorTypes
  let prog =
    Prog index typeNames valNames useClos impls input emit (freshFnCtx ())
  emitRefProgram prog plan groups

-- ── emit-time closure check (#392) ──────────────────────────────────────────
-- The runtime-line gating graph (which WAT helper block a program's use-flags
-- pull in) is hand-maintained; S1-S3 each narrowed it (fewer impls, per-operator
-- splits, dropped names), and a wrongly-narrowed gate would otherwise surface only as a
-- downstream `wasm-tools validate` "unknown func $x" on whichever fixture
-- happened to exercise the gap (#388: `$mdk_value_mod` called `$mdk_float_rem`
-- with only `useValueArith` set, silently broke 21 int-only fixtures). Run on
-- every emit (not a flag) so a gate that gets narrowed wrong fails HERE, in
-- process, naming the missing symbol, instead of downstream and silently.
--
-- Operates on the FINAL assembled text, granularity-agnostic to whatever flags
-- gated what -- it only asserts every directly-named callee resolves within
-- this module, either as a `(func $name ...)` definition or an
-- `(import "env" "..." (func $name ...))` declaration (see
-- `stderrByteImportLines`, wasm_preamble.mdk, for the import text shape).
-- `call_ref`/`return_call_ref` are exempt: they dispatch dynamically through a
-- `(ref $codety)` table value, never naming a callee symbol directly, and
-- their literal text never matches the `call $` needle below (`call_ref`/
-- `return_call_ref` both have `_ref` where this needle expects a space).
--
-- NOT one call per line: wasm_emit.mdk's own call sites are each their own
-- list element (flat, unfolded -- operands already on the stack), but the
-- hand-written runtime blocks in wasm_preamble.mdk are FOLDED s-expr WAT
-- with a call site anywhere inside a line, sometimes several per line (e.g.
-- valueAddRuntimeLines' `(call $mdk_box_int (i64.add (call $mdk_unbox_int
-- ...) (call $mdk_unbox_int ...)))`) -- an earlier draft of this check that
-- assumed startsWith missed exactly this shape. So this scans every line for
-- ALL occurrences of the `call $` needle, not just a line-leading one.
-- `return_call $NAME` is caught by the SAME needle -- "return_call $NAME"
-- literally contains "call $NAME" as a substring (right after `return_`), so
-- no separate needle is needed.
-- A string literal can never spoof either needle: `escWatBytes` hex-escapes
-- EVERY byte of a data segment (`oneDataSeg`), so no literal ASCII ever
-- reaches the assembled text from user data.
assertEmittedClosureW : String -> Unit
assertEmittedClosureW text =
  let lines = splitNl text
  let defined = omFromNames (collectDefinedNamesW lines) omEmpty
  let called = collectCalledNamesW lines
  checkCalledNamesW defined called

-- ⚠️ ACCUMULATOR-PASSING, DELIBERATELY (#392 follow-up).  The three walkers
-- below (`collectCalledNamesGoW`, `collectDefinedNamesGoW`, `identsAfterAllGoW`)
-- would otherwise build their result AFTER the recursive call returns (`idents ++
-- recurse rest` / `name :: recurse ...`), i.e. one live stack frame per WAT line
-- and per `call $` occurrence within a line.  That is fine on the native path
-- (a 256 MB GC-aware worker thread, runtime/medaka_rt.c) but FATAL on the wasm
-- path: `compiler/entries/playground_main.mdk` compiles this very code to
-- WasmGC, and the guest then runs on the HOST JS engine's ~1 MB stack, so the
-- check's own depth is proportional to the emitted module's text size.  It
-- overflowed at 15,739 lines -- i.e. on `main = 42`, the smallest program there
-- is -- taking every browser compile down with `Maximum call stack size
-- exceeded`.  Threading an accumulator makes each self-call a TRUE tail call,
-- which W4's TCO (§4.2) emits as `return_call`: constant stack, any module size.
-- Keep them tail-recursive.  The `Rev` suffix marks the reversed intermediate:
-- each `xxxRevW` returns its names LAST-FIRST, and the single `reverseL` at the
-- public entry restores the exact pre-rewrite order (per line, and across
-- lines), so the collected lists are element-for-element identical to what the
-- non-tail version produced.
collectCalledNamesW : List String -> List String
collectCalledNamesW lines = reverseL (collectCalledNamesGoW lines [])

collectCalledNamesGoW : List String -> List String -> List String
collectCalledNamesGoW [] acc = acc
collectCalledNamesGoW (line :: rest) acc =
  if startsWith ";;" (stringTrimLeft line) then
    collectCalledNamesGoW rest acc
  else
    collectCalledNamesGoW rest (identsAfterAllRevW "call $" 6 line ++ acc)

-- `(func $NAME` appears exactly once per defining line -- a plain top-level
-- function's own def line AND an import's `(import "env" "..." (func $NAME
-- ...))` line alike -- so one needle covers both (a) and (b) of the closure
-- requirement.
collectDefinedNamesW : List String -> List String
collectDefinedNamesW lines = reverseL (collectDefinedNamesGoW lines [])

collectDefinedNamesGoW : List String -> List String -> List String
collectDefinedNamesGoW [] acc = acc
collectDefinedNamesGoW (line :: rest) acc =
  collectDefinedNamesGoW rest (identsAfterAllRevW "(func $" 7 line ++ acc)

-- every occurrence of `needle` in `line`, mapped to the identifier
-- immediately following it (skipping `skipLen` chars of the needle itself,
-- e.g. `call $` -> 6, so the scan resumes right after the `$`), in REVERSE
-- order of occurrence.  The callers above prepend this onto their own reversed
-- accumulator, so one `reverseL` at the public entry un-reverses both levels at
-- once: acc = revLn ++ ... ++ revL1, and `reverseL acc` = L1 ++ ... ++ Ln,
-- exactly the old `L1 ++ ... ++ Ln`.
identsAfterAllRevW : String -> Int -> String -> List String
identsAfterAllRevW needle skipLen line =
  identsAfterAllGoW needle skipLen line 0 []

identsAfterAllGoW : String -> Int -> String -> Int -> List String -> List String
identsAfterAllGoW needle skipLen line from acc =
  let n = stringLength line
  if from >= n then
    acc
  else match stringIndexOf needle (stringSlice from n line)
    None => acc
    Some rel =>
      let hit = from + rel
      let name = identAfterW line (hit + skipLen)
      identsAfterAllGoW
        needle
        skipLen
        line
        (hit + stringLength needle)
        (name :: acc)

-- read a bare identifier (word chars only -- `$` already consumed) forward
-- from `from` until a non-identifier char or end of line.
identAfterW : String -> Int -> String
identAfterW line from = identAfterGoW line from (stringLength line) from

identAfterGoW : String -> Int -> Int -> Int -> String
identAfterGoW line i n from =
  if i >= n then
    stringSlice from n line
  else if isIdentCharW (stringSlice i (i + 1) line) then
    identAfterGoW line (i + 1) n from
  else
    stringSlice from i line

isIdentCharW : String -> Bool
isIdentCharW c = c /= " " && c /= "(" && c /= ")" && c /= "\""

checkCalledNamesW : OrdMap Unit -> List String -> Unit
checkCalledNamesW _ [] = ()
checkCalledNamesW defined (name :: rest) =
  if omHasKey name defined then
    checkCalledNamesW defined rest
  else
    panic
      ("wasm emit: call to undefined/unimported $"
        ++ name
        ++ " -- a runtime-line gate is missing this helper's dependency (#392)")

-- ── gap census driver ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The WasmGC peer of llvm_emit's emitProgramGaps: emit EVERY binding (fns +
-- impls + top-level values) in record mode and return the recorded gap events,
-- WITHOUT requiring a `main`.  Mirrors emitProgram's Prog/state setup (the same
-- W7 scans + Prog build), but forces the ref path (the whole compiler graph is
-- ADT/string/closure-heavy, so ref-mode is the representative path) and never
-- calls the main-requiring emitRefMain.  Each binding is wrapped with setGapBindingOfW
-- so a recorded gap is attributed to its source binding.
export
emitProgramGaps : WasmEmitInput ->
  EmitPlan ->
  CProgram ->
  Result (List SymbolDefect) (List String)
emitProgramGaps input plan cp0 =
  let (CProgram groups ctorArs ctorTypes impls mctx facts) = cp0
  let emit = freshWasmEmit WGapRecord
  let emit = { emit |
    externFacts = requirementFacts plan.externRequirements,
    physical = plan.wasmPhysical,
    closureChecked = False,
  }
  let _ =
    refuseUnprovidedExternsW
      emit
      input
      plan
      (CProgram groups ctorArs ctorTypes impls mctx facts)
  let _ = seedPhysicalW emit (physicalPlanW plan)
  let emit =
    { emit | physical = Some (WD.censusWasmDemand (physicalPlanW plan)) }
  let fnNames = collectFnNames groups
  let valNames = collectValNames groups
  let index =
    makeWasmProgramIndexGaps
      plan.wasmInputs.ctorFloatFields
      plan.trmc
      facts
      groups
      ctorArs
      ctorTypes
      impls
      fnNames
      valNames
  let useClos = (physicalPlanW plan).useClos
