  -- force the ref path: the census measures the full (ref eq) emitter surface.
  let typeNames = distinctTypeNames ctorTypes
  let prog =
    Prog index typeNames valNames useClos impls input emit (freshFnCtx ())
  let _ = emitFnsGapsW prog (userFnBinds groups)
  let _ = emitImplsGapsW prog (implGroups prog impls)
  let _ = emitValsGapsW prog (filterList isValBind groups)
  match symbolDefectsW emit
    [] => Ok (gapEventsOfW emit)
    defects => Err defects

emitFnsGapsW : Prog -> List CBind -> Unit
emitFnsGapsW _ [] = ()
emitFnsGapsW prog ((CBind name cs site bid) :: rest) =
  let _ = setGapBindingOfW (progEmit prog) ("fn " ++ name)
  let _ = emitRefFnBind prog (CBind name cs site bid)
  emitFnsGapsW prog rest

emitImplsGapsW : Prog -> List ImplG -> Unit
emitImplsGapsW _ [] = ()
emitImplsGapsW prog ((g@(ImplG method headTag _ _ _ _)) :: rest) =
  let _ = setGapBindingOfW (progEmit prog) "impl \{method}@\{headTag}"
  let _ = emitImplGroup prog g
  emitImplsGapsW prog rest

emitValsGapsW : Prog -> List CBind -> Unit
emitValsGapsW _ [] = ()
emitValsGapsW prog (b :: rest) =
  let _ = setGapBindingOfW (progEmit prog) ("val " ++ bindName b)
  let _ = emitRefValInit prog b
  emitValsGapsW prog rest

externFamilyW : WasmEmit -> String -> Option WasmFamily
externFamilyW emit name =
  if name == siteSentinelName then
    Some WasmLeaf
  else match lookupAssoc name (emitDemandW emit).catalogFamilies
    Some f => if isWasmExternFamily f then Some f else None
    None => None

isWasmEtaExtern : WasmEmit -> String -> Bool
isWasmEtaExtern emit name = isSome (externFamilyW emit name)

-- A declared file bound's grant, thunk body and mode (1 for FileWrite): the type
-- checker writes `$withFileReadBound grant (_ => body)` around the body of a
-- binding whose row is closed and names a narrow file authority.  The body is
-- emitted inline, in the enclosing function, between entering and leaving a host
-- bound frame (`emitAppRef`, `emitAppTail`).
fileBoundW : CExpr -> Option (CExpr, CExpr, Int)
fileBoundW app = match flattenApp app []
  (CVar "$withFileReadBound" _, [g, CLam [PWild] b]) => Some (g, b, 0)
  (CVar "$withFileWriteBound" _, [g, CLam [PWild] b]) => Some (g, b, 1)
  _ => None

-- Entering a bound pushes its grant and asks the host for a frame.  Off a tail
-- position the host always keeps a record, so leaving pops one unconditionally.
-- In a tail position it pushes a frame only when no equal bound of the mode is
-- active, as medaka_rt.c mdk_with_file_bound does, and says whether it did: a
-- re-entered bound leaves the body's tail call a tail call.
fileBoundEnterW : Prog -> Env -> Int -> CExpr -> Int -> Bool -> List String
fileBoundEnterW prog env d g mode keep =
  emitRefExpr prog env d g
    ++ [
      rtCallW prog "mdk_push_grant" 1,
      "i32.const \{intToString mode}",
      "i32.const \{if keep then "1" else "0"}",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_file_bound_enter" 2,
    ]

-- ── W6: does the program use strings? ────────────────────────────────────────
-- True if any body contains a String/Char literal, or applies an extern whose
-- catalog wasm family is `WasmStr` (intToString/putStrLn/stringConcat/…).  Any of
-- these forces the §3.3 $str rep + the byte-write runtime + ref-mode.  Detected
-- structurally over every clause body.
-- Local spellings retain legacy mode eligibility; extern binding uses facts.
seedDemandW : WasmEmit -> WasmDemand -> Unit
seedDemandW emit d =
  let _ = forEachU (u => noteWasmUse emit u) d.uses
  let _ = if d.refBox then setRef emit.useRefBox True
  let _ = if d.divGuard then setRef emit.useDivGuard True
  setRef emit.tupleArities (reverseL d.tupleArities)

-- The `WasmEmit` flag that carries one catalog demand.
noteWasmUse : WasmEmit -> WasmUse -> Unit
noteWasmUse emit UseStr = setRef emit.useStr True
noteWasmUse emit UseStrLeaf = setRef emit.useStrLeaf True
noteWasmUse emit UseRng = setRef emit.useRng True
noteWasmUse emit UseHash = setRef emit.useHash True
noteWasmUse emit UseFloat = setRef emit.useFloat True
noteWasmUse emit UseU64 = setRef emit.useU64 True
noteWasmUse emit UseI64 = setRef emit.useI64 True
-- the libm and clock imports are the extern's own host keys (`EmitPlan.hostKeys`)
noteWasmUse _ UseMath = ()
noteWasmUse _ UseFloatStr = ()
noteWasmUse emit UseFloatHash = setRef emit.useFloatHash True
noteWasmUse emit UseFloatRng = setRef emit.useFloatRng True
noteWasmUse emit UseStrSearch = setRef emit.useStrSearch True
noteWasmUse emit UseStrCodec = setRef emit.useStrCodec True
noteWasmUse emit UseArray = setRef emit.useArray True
noteWasmUse emit UseList = setRef emit.useList True
noteWasmUse emit UseCharFromCode = setRef emit.useCharFromCode True
noteWasmUse emit UseCharClass = setRef emit.useCharClass True
noteWasmUse emit UseEPut = setRef emit.useEPut True
noteWasmUse emit UseByteBlock = setRef emit.useByteBlock True
noteWasmUse _ UseArgs = ()
noteWasmUse emit UseFileBytes = setRef emit.useFileBytes True
noteWasmUse _ UseClock = ()
noteWasmUse emit UseStrToInt = setRef emit.useStrToInt True
noteWasmUse emit UseStrReverse = setRef emit.useStrReverse True
noteWasmUse emit UseStrJoin = setRef emit.useStrJoin True
cFieldExpr : CField -> CExpr
cFieldExpr (CField _ _ e) = e

-- the set of top-level fn names that appear as VALUES (bare ref in a non-call
-- position, or partially / over applied) anywhere in the program — these need a
-- closure wrapper so they can flow through `(ref eq)` slots / be applied indirectly.
scanFnValueUses : OrdMap Unit -> List (String, Int) -> List CBind -> List String
scanFnValueUses fnNames ctorArs groups =
  dedupKeep (flatMap (scanBindValueUses fnNames ctorArs envEmpty) groups)

-- W9: the impl method bodies + interface defaults also use top-level fns as values
-- (e.g. `toList = identity` in `impl Foldable List`), so their fn-value uses must seed
-- the closure-wrapper set too — else `$mdk_w_<f>` is referenced but never emitted.
scanImplValueUses : OrdMap Unit ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  List CImplEntry ->
  List String
scanImplValueUses fnNames ctorArs impls =
  dedupKeep (flatMap (e => scanImplEntryValueUses fnNames ctorArs e) impls)

scanImplEntryValueUses : OrdMap Unit ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  CImplEntry ->
  List String
scanImplEntryValueUses fnNames ctorArs (ent@(CImplEntry _ _ _ body)) =
  let locals =
    envExtendUnstamped (flatMap patVars (implEntryPatsW ent)) envEmpty
  match body
    CImplTagged _ _ _ _ _ _ b => scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals b
    CImplDefault _ _ _ _ _ _ b => scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals b

-- `locals` is the scope's locally-bound names (parameters, let, lambda and
-- let-group binders): a local named like a top-level fn shadows it, so it is not a
-- value use of the fn (emitVarRef and emitAppRef consult the env first), the same
-- rule `exprUsesClosures` applies.
scanBindValueUses : OrdMap Unit ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  Env ->
  CBind ->
  List String
scanBindValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CBind _ clauses _ _) =
  flatMap
    ((CClause pats body) =>
      scanExprValueUses
        fnNames
        ctorArs
        (envExtendUnstamped (flatMap patVars pats) locals)
        body)
    clauses

scanExprValueUses : OrdMap Unit ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  Env ->
  CExpr ->
  List String
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CVar x _) =
  if envHas x locals then
    []
  else if fnMemberIndexW fnNames x then
    [x]
  else if fnMemberIndexW fnNames ("core__" ++ x) then
    ["core__" ++ x]
  else
    []
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (app@(CApp _ _ _)) =
  let (hd, args, mode) = appParts app
  let here = match hd
    CVar fn0 _ =>
      let fn =
        if fnMemberIndexW fnNames fn0 then
          fn0
        else if fnMemberIndexW fnNames ("core__" ++ fn0) then
          "core__" ++ fn0
        else
          fn0
      if not (envHas fn0 locals)
        && fnMemberIndexW fnNames fn
        && not (isExactCall mode) then
        [fn]
      else
        []
    -- P1: an RLocal method-ref head is a DIRECT call to a shadowing standalone top-level
    -- fn — the same direct call the CVar arm above describes, reached by a different
    -- route.  So it needs the SAME rule: when the call is not exact, emitMethodRef
    -- falls back to the closure/$__mdk_apply path, which references `$mdk_w_<fn>` — and
    -- that wrapper is only DEFINED for a fn this scan reports.  Missing it emitted the
    -- ref.func and never the func: "unknown func $mdk_w_…" at assemble (exactly the
    -- failure the composite-arm comment below records).  Kept in lockstep with
    -- emitMethodRef's RLocal arm, including the `sym == ""` bare-name fallback.
    CMethod mname (MethodEvidence _ _ (RLocal sym dicts) _ _) =>
      let target = if sym == "" then mname else sym
      if isEmpty dicts
        && fnMemberIndexW fnNames target
        && not (isExactCall mode) then
        [target]
      else
        []
    _ => scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals hd
  here ++ flatMap (scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals) args
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CLam pats b) =
  scanExprValueUses
    fnNames
    ctorArs
    (envExtendUnstamped (flatMap patVars pats) locals)
    b
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CBinPrim _ l r _ _) =
  scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals l
    ++ scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals r
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CUnOp _ x) =
  scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals x
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CIf c t f) =
  scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals c
    ++ scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals t
    ++ scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals f
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CLet _ pat a b) =
  scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals a
    ++ scanExprValueUses
      fnNames
      ctorArs
      (envExtendUnstamped (patVars pat) locals)
      b
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CBlock stmts) =
  scanBlockValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals stmts
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CDecision scrut arms _) =
  scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals scrut
    ++ flatMap (a => scanArmValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals a) arms
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CMatch scrut arms) =
  scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals scrut
    ++ flatMap (a => scanArmValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals a) arms
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CLetGroup binds b) =
  let inGroup = envExtendUnstamped (map bindName binds) locals
  flatMap (bd => scanBindValueUses fnNames ctorArs inGroup bd) binds
    ++ scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs inGroup b
-- Composite arms emitVarRef descends into at emit time — each can hold a fn-VALUE
-- use (`map (mapIfaceMethod f) ms` lives in a CRecordUpdate; `map (substField s) fs`
-- in a CTuple; `flatMap dataArity prog` in a CRecord field).  Missing these here
-- under-counted fn-value uses → the closure wrapper `$mdk_w_<f>` was referenced
-- (ref.func emitted) but never DEFINED → "unknown func" at assemble.
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CTuple xs) =
  flatMap (scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals) xs
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CList xs) =
  flatMap (scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals) xs
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CArray xs) =
  flatMap (scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals) xs
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CRecord _ fs) =
  flatMap (fd => scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (cFieldExpr fd)) fs
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CFieldAccess r _ _ _) =
  scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals r
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CRecordUpdate _ r fs) =
  scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals r
    ++ flatMap
      (fd => scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (cFieldExpr fd))
      fs
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CVariantUpdate _ r fs) =
  scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals r
    ++ flatMap
      (fd => scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (cFieldExpr fd))
      fs
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CRangeList lo hi _) =
  scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals lo
    ++ scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals hi
scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CRangeArray lo hi _) =
  scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals lo
    ++ scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals hi
scanExprValueUses _ _ _ _ = []

-- scan an arm's guards (refutable `Pat <- e` / boolean `if e`) AND its body — a
-- guard scrutinee can carry a fn-value use just like the body.
scanArmValueUses : OrdMap Unit ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  Env ->
  CArm ->
  List String
scanArmValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CArm _ guards body) =
  flatMap (g => scanGuardValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals g) guards
    ++ scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals body

scanGuardValueUses : OrdMap Unit ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  Env ->
  CGuard ->
  List String
scanGuardValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CGBool e) =
  scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals e
scanGuardValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (CGBind _ e) =
  scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals e

-- a block's statements, each later one seeing the names an earlier `let` bound
scanBlockValueUses : OrdMap Unit ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  Env ->
  List CStmt ->
  List String
scanBlockValueUses _ _ _ [] = []
scanBlockValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals ((CSLet _ pat e) :: rest) =
  scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals e
    ++ scanBlockValueUses
      fnNames
      ctorArs
      (envExtendUnstamped (patVars pat) locals)
      rest
scanBlockValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals ((CSExpr e) :: rest) =
  scanExprValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals e
    ++ scanBlockValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals rest
scanBlockValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals (_ :: rest) =
  scanBlockValueUses fnNames ctorArs locals rest

anyList : (a -> Bool) -> List a -> Bool
anyList _ [] = False
anyList p (x :: xs) = if p x then True else anyList p xs

-- ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- Raw physical values and function-local storage.
-- ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

oneGlobalI32 : String -> String
oneGlobalI32 n = "  (global $" ++ gname n ++ " (mut i64) (i64.const 0))"

printFor : Prog -> WTy -> List String
-- layer-17 §2.1: scalar values are uniformly i64 now.  Int prints directly; Bool is
-- an i64 0/1, so wrap to i32 for $mdk_print_bool.
printFor prog WInt = ["    " ++ rtCallW prog "mdk_print_int" 1]
printFor prog WBool =
  ["    i32.wrap_i64", "    " ++ rtCallW prog "mdk_print_bool" 1]
printFor prog WUnit =
  gapLP prog "scalar-mode: Unit main has no scalar value to print"
printFor prog WStr =
  gapLP
    prog
    "scalar-mode main produced a String — internal mode mismatch (strings force ref-mode)"
printFor prog WChar =
  gapLP
    prog
    "scalar-mode main produced a Char — internal mode mismatch (Char main forces ref-mode)"
printFor prog WRef =
  gapLP prog "scalar-mode main produced a (ref eq) — internal mode mismatch"
printFor prog WFloat =
  gapLP
    prog
    "scalar-mode main produced a Float — internal mode mismatch (Float forces ref-mode)"

emitLitI32 : WasmEmit -> Lit -> (List String, WTy)
-- layer-17 §2.1: scalar mode is now uniformly i64 (Int/Bool/Unit all i64 0/1/value)
-- so >2^30 Int arithmetic computes in i64 and never truncates.
emitLitI32 _ (LInt n) = (["i64.const " ++ intToString n], WInt)
emitLitI32 _ (LBool b) = ([if b then "i64.const 1" else "i64.const 0"], WBool)
emitLitI32 _ LUnit = (["i64.const 0"], WUnit)
emitLitI32 emit (LFloat _) =
  gapLTy
    emit
    "Float literal (boxed (struct f64)) is deferred — no scalar Float fixture"
emitLitI32 emit (LString _) =
  gapLTy emit "String literal (the (array i8) rep) is W6"
emitLitI32 emit (LChar _) =
  gapLTy emit "Char literal is W6 (string/unicode slice)"
emitLitI32 emit (LU64 _ _) =
  gapLTy emit "U64 literal (a boxed $u64 cell) needs ref-mode"
emitLitI32 emit (LI64 _ _) =
  gapLTy emit "I64 literal (a boxed $i64 cell) needs ref-mode"

rawProgramW : Prog -> Bool
rawProgramW prog = not (emitDemandW (progEmit prog)).useRef

programReprW : Prog -> WasmRepr
programReprW prog = if rawProgramW prog then WInt63 else WBoxEq

programValueW : Prog -> List String -> WasmValue
programValueW prog lines = WasmValue (programReprW prog) lines

prependValueW : List String -> WasmValue -> WasmValue
prependValueW prefix (WasmValue repr lines) = WasmValue repr (prefix ++ lines)

rawPrintKindW : WasmRepr -> WTy
rawPrintKindW WBool64 = WBool
rawPrintKindW WUnit64 = WUnit
rawPrintKindW _ = WInt

rawReprW : WTy -> WasmRepr
rawReprW WBool = WBool64
rawReprW WUnit = WUnit64
rawReprW _ = WInt63

localTargetW : Prog -> Env -> String -> String
localTargetW prog env name =
  if rawProgramW prog then match WD.envLookup name env
    WD.LocalBinder ord => match omLookup ord (progFnCtx prog).localSlots.value
      Some slot => intToString (slotIndex slot)
      None => panic ("wasm: missing numeric local for binder " ++ ord)
    _ => panic ("wasm: missing scoped binder for local " ++ name)
  else
    "$" ++ gname name

mintLocalW : Prog -> BinderId -> Unit
mintLocalW prog bid =
  if rawProgramW prog then
    let ctx = progFnCtx prog
    let ord = intToString (binderOrdinal bid)
    let index = ctx.nextLocal.value
    let _ = setRef ctx.nextLocal (index + 1)
    let _ =
      setRef
        ctx.localSlots
        (omInsert ord (LocalSlot index WInt63) ctx.localSlots.value)
    setRef ctx.localTypes (WInt63 :: ctx.localTypes.value)

installRawParamsW : Prog -> Int -> List Pat -> Unit
installRawParamsW prog index [] = setRef (progFnCtx prog).nextLocal index
installRawParamsW prog index (pat :: rest) =
  let ctx = progFnCtx prog
  let _ = match pat
    PVar _ _ bid =>
      setRef
        ctx.localSlots
        (omInsert
          (intToString (binderOrdinal bid))
          (LocalSlot index WInt63)
          ctx.localSlots.value)
    _ => ()
  installRawParamsW prog (index + 1) rest

numericDeclsW : Prog -> List String
numericDeclsW prog =
  map
    (repr => "  (local " ++ physicalType repr ++ ")")
    (reverseL (progFnCtx prog).localTypes.value)

rawScratchW : Prog -> List String
rawScratchW prog =
  if rawProgramW prog && (progEmit prog).useDivGuard.value then
    ["  (local $__sdivr i64)"]
  else
    []

conditionW : Prog -> List String
conditionW prog =
  if rawProgramW prog then
    ["i64.const 0", "i64.ne"]
  else
    ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_u"]

-- Sign-extend the i64 on the stack from bit 62 — the `(x << 1) >> 1` pair that
-- mirrors native's tag/untag shift.  Only a fixed-width (`U8`/`U16`/`U32`) scalar
-- site still emits it, ahead of its mask, where it cannot change the kept low bits;
-- an `Int` site checks instead of wrapping (`intChkCall`).
normInt64 : List String
normInt64 = ["i64.const 1", "i64.shl", "i64.const 1", "i64.shr_s"]

-- The `Int` operators whose exact result can leave the 63-bit range, given operands
-- already in it: `+ - *`, and `/` only at intMinBound / -1.  `%` and the
-- comparisons cannot.
intOpCanOverflow : String -> Bool
intOpCanOverflow op = contains op ["+", "-", "*", "/"]

-- A call to the checked `Int` operator for `op` (`$mdk_int_add`… in
-- `intRuntimeLines`): it leaves the exact result on the stack, or stops the
-- program with E-INT-OVERFLOW.  Operands and result are raw 63-bit i64s, so the
-- same call serves scalar and ref mode (ref mode reboxes after it).  The plan
-- selects the helper (`intHelpers`); the registry refuses the call otherwise.
intChkCall : Prog -> String -> Int -> List String
intChkCall prog op site = [
  "i64.const " ++ intToString site,
  rtCallW prog ("mdk_int_" ++ intChkName op) 3,
]

-- `Int` negation, checked the same way (`$mdk_int_neg`).
intChkNegCall : Prog -> List String
intChkNegCall prog = [rtCallW prog "mdk_int_neg" 1]

-- An `Int` shift (`$mdk_shift_left`/`$mdk_shift_right`, "left"/"right"): raw i64
-- value and amount in, raw i64 out.  Its negative-amount panic streams the amount
-- through the decimal trap seam.
intShiftCall : Prog -> String -> List String
intShiftCall prog dir = [rtCallW prog ("mdk_shift_" ++ dir) 2]

intChkName : String -> String
intChkName "+" = "add"
intChkName "-" = "sub"
intChkName "*" = "mul"
intChkName "/" = "div"
intChkName op = panic ("wasm: no checked Int operator '" ++ op ++ "'")

-- `uNTruncate x` in ref mode: unbox, keep the head's low bits, rebox.
emitTruncateRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> String -> CExpr -> List String
emitTruncateRef prog env d head a = match fixedWidthMask head
  Some mask =>
    emitRefExpr prog env d a
      ++ [
        unboxIntW prog,
        "i64.const " ++ intToString mask,
        "i64.and",
        boxIntW prog,
      ]
  None => gapLP prog ("wasm: '" ++ head ++ "' is not a fixed-width head")

-- A `U8`/`U16`/`U32` arithmetic site (`CBinPrim`'s tag names the head) computes the
-- Int op and then keeps the low `n` bits, so `+ - *` wrap modulo 2^n
-- (`docs/design/INTEGER-TYPES-DESIGN.md` §4).  The mask is applied to the raw i64
-- result, whose low 32 bits are exact even when the Int product overflowed 64 bits.
-- `/` and `%` of in-range operands are already in range and take the Int path as is.
-- An `I32` site sign-extends the low 32 bits instead, which also wraps
-- `minBound / -1` (2^31 in the i64) back to `minBound`; its `%` cannot leave range.
fixedWidthWrapW : String -> String -> List String
fixedWidthWrapW tag op = match fixedWidthMask tag
  Some mask =>
    if contains op ["+", "-", "*"] then
      ["i64.const " ++ intToString mask, "i64.and"]
    else
      []
  None =>
    if tag == "I32" && contains op ["+", "-", "*", "/"] then
      ["i64.extend32_s"]
    else
      []

emitRefProgram : Prog ->
  EmitPlan ->
  List CBind ->
  Result (List SymbolDefect) String
emitRefProgram prog plan groups =
  let header = preambleHeadLines
  let typeSection =
    if rawProgramW prog then
      [
        "  (rec", "    (type $boxint (sub (struct (field i64))))",
        "    (type $float (sub (struct (field f64))))", "  )"
      ]
    else
      emitTypeSection prog
  let physical = physicalPlanW plan
  let imports = plannedImportLines physical.imports
  let valNames = progValNames prog
  -- Stage-2/3 (b′) WASMGC-TRMC: the plan's dispatch-graph TMC groups (the lexer's
  -- `scan` token spine, the offside-rule `layout` family, `intersperse`), installed
  -- BEFORE emitting fns, so emitRefFnBind can route a group member to the
  -- dest-passing reset-wrapper + inner-loop emit.
  let dispGroups = plan.dispGroups
  let _ = setRef (progEmit prog).wDispGroups dispGroups
  -- W8: the SplitMix64 seed lives in a mutable i64 global (emitted before the value globals).
  let rngGlobal =
    if (progEmit prog).useRng.value then rngStateGlobalLines else []
  let dispGlobals = flatMap wDispGlobalLines dispGroups
  -- #561 PR-B: a LAZY value global ALSO carries a per-global 3-state flag $gs_<name>
  -- (0 UNFORCED / 1 FORCING / 2 FORCED); the value cell $g_<name> stays (ref null eq).
  let lazyStateGlobals =
    map oneGlobalState (filterList (isLazyGlobalW prog) valNames)
  let globals =
    rngGlobal
      ++ dispGlobals
      ++ map (if rawProgramW prog then oneGlobalI32 else oneGlobalRef) valNames
      ++ lazyStateGlobals
  let _ =
    seedSymbolsW
      prog
      physical
      ((if isEmptyL rngGlobal then [] else [symNameW rngStateW])
        ++ flatMap wDispGlobalNames dispGroups
        ++ map gname valNames
        ++ map
          (n => "gs_" ++ gname n)
          (filterList (isLazyGlobalW prog) valNames))
  -- emit user fns FIRST (this accumulates lifted lambdas into this WasmEmit).
  let fns = flatMap (emitRefFnBind prog) (userFnBinds groups)
  -- W5: the typeclass impl functions ($mdk_impl_<tag>_<method>), emitted as ordinary
  -- (ref eq) functions the RKey direct call / RDict if-chain dispatch into.
  let implFns = emitImplFns prog
  -- #561 PR-B: a `$force_<name>` func for every LAZY value global — the 3-state force
  -- (memoise-or-black-hole) that its reads `call` instead of `global.get`.  Emitted
  -- alongside initLines so its body-emit runs BEFORE the trapImport binding below reads
  -- trapImportNeeded (an E-CYCLIC-VALUE trap sets it); mirrors value-init order.
  let forceFns = emitRefForceFns prog groups
  let initLines = emitRefInit prog plan groups
  -- now drain the lifted-lambda defs + the closure-apply runtime + elem-declare.
  let lifted =
    if progUseClos prog then
      flatMap (x => x) (reverseL (progEmit prog).liftedDefinitions.value)
    else
      []
  let elemDecl =
    if progUseClos prog then [emitElemDeclare (progEmit prog)] else []
  let runtime =
    plannedHelperLines
      physical
      (map strBytesW (reverseL (progEmit prog).siteFiles.value))
  let dataSegs = emitDataSegs (progEmit prog)
  -- S-4: the capture-free closure globals (wConstClos), accumulated during fn / impl /
  -- default / init body emission.  Bound HERE, after every body-emit binding above, for
  -- the same reason `trapImport` and `dataSegs` are; their LINES are placed with the
  -- other globals below, which the text format permits independently of binding order.
  let constClosGlobals = wConstClosGlobalLines (progEmit prog)
  -- the `$trapmsg_K` helpers, bound last of all: every coded trap they hold was
  -- interned during the body emission above.
  let trapMsgRt = trapMsgRuntimeOf (progEmit prog)
  match symbolDefectsW (progEmit prog)
    [] =>
      Ok
        (joinNl
          (header
            ++ typeSection
            ++ imports
            ++ elemDecl
            ++ globals
            ++ constClosGlobals
            ++ fns
            ++ implFns
            ++ lifted
            ++ runtime
            ++ dataSegs
            ++ forceFns
            ++ initLines
            ++ trapMsgRt
            ++ [")"]))
    defects => Err defects

-- the passive data segments for string literals — one `(data $strseg_N "…")` per
-- distinct payload (`freshStrSeg`), emitted in segment-index order.  `array.new_data`
-- reads from these (the §11-preferred non-const-array init scheme; no active memory
-- needed).
emitDataSegs : WasmEmit -> List String
emitDataSegs emit =
  let segs = sortSegsByIdx (reverseL !emit.stringSegments)
  map oneDataSeg segs

oneDataSeg : (Int, List Int) -> String
oneDataSeg (i, bytes) =
  "  (data $strseg_\{intToString i} \"\{escWatBytes bytes}\")"

-- sort (idx, bytes) entries by ascending idx (insertion sort; segment counts are tiny).
sortSegsByIdx : List (Int, List Int) -> List (Int, List Int)
sortSegsByIdx [] = []
sortSegsByIdx (x :: xs) = insertSeg x (sortSegsByIdx xs)

insertSeg : (Int, List Int) -> List (Int, List Int) -> List (Int, List Int)
insertSeg x [] = [x]
insertSeg (i, b) ((j, c) :: rest) =
  if i <= j then (i, b) :: (j, c) :: rest else (j, c) :: insertSeg (i, b) rest

-- the `(elem declare func …)` line listing every fn `ref.func`'d (lifted lambdas,
-- the PAP code, and any top-level fn used as a value) — required so `ref.func`
-- validates.  Drained from WasmEmit after all bodies are emitted.
emitElemDeclare : WasmEmit -> String
emitElemDeclare emit =
  let names = map ("$" ++ _) (elemNames !emit.symbols)
  "  (elem declare func " ++ joinWith " " names ++ ")"

oneGlobalRef : String -> String
oneGlobalRef n =
  "  (global $" ++ gname n ++ " (mut (ref null eq)) (ref.null eq))"

-- ── §3.4 type section: one rec group with the universal root + per-type roots
-- + per payload-ctor structs.  Each payload struct has an explicit i32 tag field
-- (field 0 — defends against structural-subtyping collapse) then one (ref eq) per
-- payload field.  Nullary ctors need no struct (they are i31 immediates).  The
-- reserved Option/Result/Ordering types are appended (their structs only matter
-- for the payload ctors Some/Ok/Err).
emitTypeSection : Prog -> List String
emitTypeSection prog =
  let userTypes = userTypesWithCtors prog
  let userStructs = flatMap (emitTypeStructs prog) userTypes
  let reservedStructs = emitReservedStructs prog
  let closTypes =
    if contains "codety" (emitDemandW (progEmit prog)).representationTypes then
      closTypeLines
    else
      []
  let strTypes =
    if contains "str" (emitDemandW (progEmit prog)).representationTypes then
      strTypeLines
    else
      []
  let w7Types = emitW7Types (progEmit prog)
  [
      "  ;; ── §3 type section (rec group) — §3.4 ADT structs + §8.6 (ref eq)/i31 ──",
      "  (rec",
      "    ;; layer-17 §2.1: boxed Int outside ±2^30 (the $mdk_box_int/$mdk_unbox_int seam).",
      "    (type $boxint (sub (struct (field i64))))",
      "    ;; boxed Float (§3.3) — declared, unused until a Float fixture needs it.",
      "    (type $float (sub (struct (field f64))))",
      -- W5 nested requires-dict cell (mirrors llvm_emit's `[ i64 head_tag | i64 reqdict_0 | … ]`).
      -- A one-level dict stays an i31 (just the tag); a NESTED dict (`RKey k [reqs]`) is a
      -- $dictcell: field 0 = i32 hashName(head-tag), field 1 = a $dictarr of the recursively-
      -- built nested req witnesses.  Consumption (readDictParam / loadReqDicts) type-tests the
      -- witness: i31 ⇒ tag = i31.get_s, no reqs; $dictcell ⇒ tag = struct.get 0, reqs = array.
      "    (type $dictarr (array (mut (ref eq))))",
      "    (type $dictcell (sub (struct (field i32) (field (ref $dictarr)))))",
    ]
    ++ strTypes
    ++ closTypes
    ++ userStructs
    ++ reservedStructs
    ++ w7Types
    ++ ["  )"]

-- ── W7 collection types (§3.3) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Conditionally emitted by usage (peer to strTypes):
--   List: root $T_List (i32 tag) + cons struct $C_Cons (tag, head, tail); Nil is an
--     i31 immediate (ordinal 1) so it needs no struct.  Matches the §3.3 + LLVM rep.
--   Tuple n: per-arity $T_Tup<n> root + $C_Tup<n> struct (tag + n (ref eq) fields).
--     A tuple is single-shape, but it reuses the W3 ctor machinery (discrimReadOf
--     reads the struct's field-0 tag = ordinal 0), so it carries a leading i32 tag.
--   Array: $arr = (array (mut (ref eq))) — array.len carries the length (§3.3).
--   Ref:   $refbox = a 1-field MUTABLE struct (setRef overwrites the field).
emitW7Types : WasmEmit -> List String
emitW7Types emit =
  let listT =
    if contains "T_List" (emitDemandW emit).representationTypes then
      [
        "    (type $T_List (sub (struct (field i32))))",
        -- §3/Stage-0: cons TAIL field (index 2) is `mut` so TRMC destination-passing can
        -- `struct.set` a freshly-built child into the parent cell.  Head (index 1) stays
        -- immutable.  `mut` only PERMITS mutation — output is unchanged (nothing writes it yet).
        "    (type $C_Cons (sub $T_List (struct (field i32) (field (ref eq)) (field (mut (ref eq))))))",
      ]
    else
      []
  let tupTs = flatMap tupleTypeDecl (reverseL !emit.tupleArities)
  let arrT =
    if contains "arr" (emitDemandW emit).representationTypes then
      ["    (type $arr (array (mut (ref eq))))"]
    else
      []
  let refT =
    if contains "refbox" (emitDemandW emit).representationTypes then
      ["    (type $refbox (sub (struct (field (mut (ref eq))))))"]
    else
      []
  -- a `U64` is a `$u64` cell, never an i31 or a `$boxint`: the i64 payload is read
  -- unsigned, and a separate type keeps every `ref.test` on the other shapes false.
  let u64T =
    if contains "u64" (emitDemandW emit).representationTypes then
      ["    (type $u64 (sub (struct (field i64))))"]
    else
      []
  -- an `I64` is an `$i64` cell: the same payload as `$u64`, read signed, and a
  -- type of its own so a shape-dispatched helper never reads one as the other.
  let i64T =
    if contains "i64" (emitDemandW emit).representationTypes then
      ["    (type $i64 (sub (struct (field i64))))"]
    else
      []
  listT ++ tupTs ++ arrT ++ refT ++ u64T ++ i64T

tupleTypeDecl : Int -> List String
tupleTypeDecl n =
  let fields = joinWith "" (replicate n " (field (ref eq))")
  let root = typeRootName (syntheticCtorType (tupleCtorName n))
  let cs = ctorStructName (tupleCtorName n)
  [
    "    (type $" ++ root ++ " (sub (struct (field i32))))",
    "    (type $\{cs} (sub $\{root} (struct (field i32)\{fields})))",
  ]

-- distinct user type names (declaration order) that actually own ctors, paired
-- with their ctor list.  Reserved types are handled separately so they are never
-- double-declared.
userTypesWithCtors : Prog -> List String
userTypesWithCtors (Prog _ typeNames _ _ _ _ _ _) =
  filterList (t => not (isReservedType t)) typeNames

-- per-type: a root struct (just the i32 tag) + one struct per PAYLOAD ctor (tag +
-- fields), each declared `(sub $root …)`.  Nullary ctors get no struct.
emitTypeStructs : Prog -> String -> List String
emitTypeStructs prog ty =
  let ctors = ctorsOfType prog ty
  let root = "    (type $" ++ typeRootName ty ++ " (sub (struct (field i32))))"
  let payloadStructs = flatMap (emitCtorStruct prog ty) ctors
  [root] ++ payloadStructs

emitCtorStruct : Prog -> String -> String -> List String
emitCtorStruct prog ty ctor =
  let arity = ctorArity prog ctor
  if arity == 0 then
    []
  else
    -- §3/Stage-0: ctor payload fields are `mut` so a TRMC-destination recursive field
    -- can be `struct.set` after the parent cell is built.  Field types are uniform
    -- `(ref eq)` here (no per-field type), so all payload fields are made `mut`; this is
    -- output-neutral (`mut` only PERMITS mutation — nothing writes them yet), following
    -- the `$refbox`/`$arr` precedent.
    let fields = joinWith "" (replicate arity " (field (mut (ref eq)))")
    [
      "    (type $\{ctorStructName ctor} (sub $\{typeRootName ty} (struct (field i32)\{fields})))",
    ]

-- reserved Option/Result/Ordering: declare each type's root + payload structs.
-- Emitted UNCONDITIONALLY in ref-mode (they are small; unused struct types are
-- valid WasmGC).  Detecting exact usage would need to scan the whole program for
-- reserved-ctor occurrences (constructions AND match heads) — the ctor table only
-- lists USER ctors — so always-declare is the simple correct choice for this slice.
emitReservedStructs : Prog -> List String
emitReservedStructs prog =
  reservedTypeStructs prog "Option" ["Some", "None"]
    ++ reservedTypeStructs prog "Result" ["Ok", "Err"]
    ++ reservedTypeStructs prog "Ordering" ["Lt", "Eq", "Gt"]

reservedTypeStructs : Prog -> String -> List String -> List String
reservedTypeStructs prog ty ctors =
  let root = "    (type $" ++ typeRootName ty ++ " (sub (struct (field i32))))"
  let payloadStructs = flatMap (emitReservedCtorStruct ty) ctors
  [root] ++ payloadStructs

-- reserved-ctor arities are fixed: Some/Ok/Err carry 1 payload field; None/Lt/Eq/Gt
-- are nullary.
emitReservedCtorStruct : String -> String -> List String
emitReservedCtorStruct ty ctor =
  if reservedCtorArity ctor == 0 then
    []
  else
    let fields =
      joinWith "" (replicate (reservedCtorArity ctor) " (field (ref eq))")
    [
      "    (type $\{ctorStructName ctor} (sub $\{typeRootName ty} (struct (field i32)\{fields})))",
    ]

-- ── ref-mode globals init + main ─────────────────────────────────────────────

-- #561 PR-B: the (mut i32) 3-state flag for a LAZY value global (0 UNFORCED / 1 FORCING
-- / 2 FORCED).  Peer of oneGlobalRef; the value cell $g_<name> stays (mut (ref null eq)).
oneGlobalState : String -> String
oneGlobalState n = "  (global $gs_" ++ gname n ++ " (mut i32) (i32.const 0))"

-- The program entry, shared by both init shapes.  `mdk_entry_split` marks a
-- module whose `start` does not run `main`: a host that finds `mdk_main` without
-- it holds a module whose `start` already runs `main`, and calling `mdk_main`
-- would run the program twice, so the hosts refuse such a module.
entryExports : List String
entryExports = [
  "  (export \"mdk_main\" (func $__main))",
  "  (func $__entry_split)",
  "  (export \"mdk_entry_split\" (func $__entry_split))",
]

emitRefInit : Prog -> EmitPlan -> List CBind -> List String
emitRefInit prog plan groups =
  -- #561 PR-B: only SAFE (statically-orderable) value globals are eager-initialised in
  -- $__init — byte-identical to the pre-#561 emitter whenever no global is lazy.  A SAFE
  -- global's whole eager reach is SAFE (the taint is downward-closed over reads), so this
  -- prologue never calls a $force fn.  LAZY globals are initialised on first use by their
  -- $force_<name> defines (emitRefForceFns); they are excluded from the eager set here.
  let valBinds = plannedValBinds plan groups
  let initProg = progWithOrigin "value initialization" (progInFn prog)
  let mainProg = progWithOrigin "main" (progInFn prog)
  let _ =
    forEachU
      (f => defineFnW (progWithOrigin "module" prog) f (FuncParams 0))
      ["__main", "__entry_split", "__init"]
  let initW7Outer = w7ScopeOpen (progEmit prog)
  let valInit = flatMap (emitRefValInit initProg) valBinds
  let initW7Used = w7ScopeClose (progEmit prog) initW7Outer
  let mainW7Outer = w7ScopeOpen (progEmit prog)
  let mainLines = emitRefMain mainProg plan groups
  let mainW7Used = w7ScopeClose (progEmit prog) mainW7Outer
  let valLocals =
    if rawProgramW prog then [] else flatMap collectBindLocals valBinds
  let mainBodies = match findMain (progEmit prog) groups
    Some body => [body]
    None => []
  let mainLocals =
    if rawProgramW prog then [] else flatMap collectExprLocals mainBodies
  let valBodies = flatMap bindBodies valBinds
  -- scratch ($__rf<d>) locals sized to the deepest match nesting of each
  -- function's own bodies: the val inits for $__init, `main` for $__main.
  let valDepth = if rawProgramW prog then 0 else foldMaxDepth valBodies
  let mainDepth = if rawProgramW prog then 0 else foldMaxDepth mainBodies
  let initLocalDecls =
    map
      (l => "  " ++ localDeclRef l)
      (dedupKeep valLocals
        ++ (if rawProgramW prog then [] else scratchLocals valDepth))
  let mainLocalDecls =
    map
      (l => "  " ++ localDeclRef l)
      (dedupKeep mainLocals
        ++ (if rawProgramW prog then [] else scratchLocals mainDepth))
  let initW7Decls = map ("  " ++ _) (w7LocalDecls initW7Used valDepth)
  let mainW7Decls = map ("  " ++ _) (w7LocalDecls mainW7Used mainDepth)
  -- `start` runs only the eager value inits; `main` is the exported
  -- `mdk_main`, which every host calls after instantiation.  A module
  -- instantiated without that call runs no program code.  A suspending
  -- import (JSPI) cannot be reached from `start`, and a host may re-enter
  -- `mdk_main` on one instance (playground/compile.mjs keeps the compiler's
  -- top-level memo Refs alive across analyze calls that way).
  ["  (func $__main"]
    ++ numericDeclsW mainProg
    ++ rawScratchW mainProg
    ++ mainLocalDecls
    ++ mainW7Decls
    ++ mainLines
    ++ ["  )"]
    ++ entryExports
    ++ ["  (func $__init"]
    ++ numericDeclsW initProg
    ++ rawScratchW initProg
    ++ initLocalDecls
    ++ initW7Decls
    ++ valInit
    ++ ["  )", "  (start $__init)"]

bindBodies : CBind -> List CExpr
bindBodies (CBind _ clauses _ _) = flatMap clauseBody clauses

clauseBody : CClause -> List CExpr
clauseBody (CClause _ body) = [body]

foldMaxDepth : List CExpr -> Int
foldMaxDepth [] = 0
foldMaxDepth (e :: rest) = maxI (maxRefDepth e) (foldMaxDepth rest)

emitRefValInit : Prog -> CBind -> List String
emitRefValInit prog (CBind name [CClause [] body] _ _) =
  let instrs = emitRefExpr prog envEmpty 0 body
  indent instrs ++ ["    " ++ globalW prog "global.set" ("$" ++ gname name)]
emitRefValInit prog _ = gapLP prog "value binding must be a nullary clause"

-- ── #561 PR-B: lazy value-global force functions ─────────────────────────────
-- A `$force_<name>` func for every LAZY value global (dispatch-reaching / cyclic — see
-- emit_support.lazyGlobalNames).  A faithful transliteration of the reference engine's
-- forceMemo/blackholeCell (compiler/eval/eval.mdk) and the native @mdk_force_<x>:
--   state 2 FORCED   -> return the memoised $g_<name>
--   state 1 FORCING  -> re-entered mid-init => E-CYCLIC-VALUE (the black-hole), unreachable
--   state 0 UNFORCED -> mark FORCING, run the rhs, memoise the value, mark FORCED, return
-- The FORCING flag is set BEFORE the body runs (the black-hole ordering), so a re-entrant
-- read `call $force_<name>` from inside the body hits state 1 and traps.  A read of another
-- global inside the body lowers through emitVarRefPlain exactly as anywhere else (a plain
-- `global.get` for a SAFE dep — already eager-set by $__init, which runs first — or a nested
-- `call $force_` for a LAZY dep).  Result is a non-null (ref eq) via ref.as_non_null on the
-- memoised cell, the same guarantee every eager global read carries.
emitRefForceFns : Prog -> List CBind -> List String
emitRefForceFns prog groups =
  flatMap
    (b => emitRefForceFn (progWithOrigin (bindName b) prog) b)
    (filterList
      (b => isLazyGlobalW prog (bindName b))
      (filterList isValBind groups))

emitRefForceFn : Prog -> CBind -> List String
emitRefForceFn prog (CBind name [CClause [] body] _ _) =
  let g = gname name
  let _ = defineFnW prog ("force_" ++ g) (FuncParams 0)
  let w7Outer = w7ScopeOpen (progEmit prog)
  let instrs = emitRefExpr prog envEmpty 0 body
  let bodyLocals = dedupKeep (collectExprLocals body)
  let maxDepth = maxRefDepth body
  let scratch = scratchLocals maxDepth
  let localDecls = map (l => "  " ++ localDeclRef l) (bodyLocals ++ scratch)
  let w7Decls =
    map
      ("  " ++ _)
      (w7LocalDecls (w7ScopeClose (progEmit prog) w7Outer) maxDepth)
  let cyclic =
    wasmTrapNamed
      (progEmit prog)
      "E-CYCLIC-VALUE"
      name
      " refers to itself during initialization (non-productive cyclic value)\n"
  let value = "$" ++ g
  let state = "$gs_" ++ g
  let unforced =
    ["    i32.const 1", "    " ++ globalW prog "global.set" state]
      ++ indent instrs
      ++ [
        "    local.set $__frcv",
        "    local.get $__frcv",
        "    " ++ globalW prog "global.set" value,
        "    i32.const 2",
        "    " ++ globalW prog "global.set" state,
        "    local.get $__frcv",
        "    ref.as_non_null",
      ]
  [
      "  (func $force_" ++ g ++ " (result (ref eq))",
      "  (local $__frcv (ref null eq))",
    ]
    ++ localDecls
    ++ w7Decls
    ++ [
      "    " ++ globalW prog "global.get" state,
      "    i32.const 2",
      "    i32.eq",
      "    if (result (ref eq))",
      "    " ++ globalW prog "global.get" value,
      "    ref.as_non_null",
      "    else",
      "    " ++ globalW prog "global.get" state,
      "    i32.const 1",
      "    i32.eq",
      "    if (result (ref eq))",
    ]
    ++ indent cyclic
    ++ ["    else"]
    ++ unforced
    ++ ["    end", "    end", "  )"]
emitRefForceFn prog (CBind name _ _ _) =
  -- in record mode the gap stands in for this force function
  let _ =
    setRef
      (progEmit prog).symbols
      (excuseSymbol
        (WasmFunc ("force_" ++ gname name))
        !(progEmit prog).symbols)
  gapLP prog "value binding must be a nullary clause"

-- main: compute the body (a (ref eq)), then unbox to i32 and route to the print
-- import by the body's STATIC kind (Int vs Bool — the only printable scalar mains
-- in this slice).  In ref-mode an Int/Bool result is an i31 immediate, so unbox via
-- `i31.get_s` / `i31.get_u`.
emitRefMain : Prog -> EmitPlan -> List CBind -> List String
emitRefMain prog plan groups = match findMain (progEmit prog) groups
  Some body =>
    let value = emitValueW prog envEmpty 0 body
    let instrs = valueLines value
    if rawProgramW prog then
      indent instrs ++ printFor prog (rawPrintKindW (valueRepr value))
    else
      emitBoxedMainW prog plan groups body instrs
  None => gapLP prog "no `main` binding"

emitBoxedMainW : Prog ->
  EmitPlan ->
  List CBind ->
  CExpr ->
  List String ->
  List String
emitBoxedMainW prog plan groups body instrs =
  -- A main stamped `Unit` is Unit whatever its body's shape, and one stamped
  -- with a printable scalar prints as that scalar: the structural read below is
  -- only for a main with no stamp of its own (an untyped lowering stamps every
  -- binder `RTValue`).  The typechecker's Float hint overrides a body whose
  -- result is a polymorphic return (`main = fold (acc x => acc + x) 0.0 [..]`).
  let k =
    if planEntryMainIsUnit plan
      || mainStamp prog == RTUnit
      || mainBodyIsUnit prog (cafBodies groups) body then
      WUnit
    else if planEntryMainIsFloat plan then
      WFloat
    else
      stampPrintKind (mainPrintStamp prog body)
  -- a Unit main (a `putStrLn …` etc.) has already produced its IO effect; drop its
  -- i31-0 result and auto-print NOTHING (the "Unit main no auto-print" contract).
  match k
    WUnit => indent instrs ++ ["    drop"]
    _ => indent instrs ++ refPrintFor prog k

-- W9b: a value main whose head function returns Unit (`println`, `print`, any
-- user/prelude Unit-returning wrapper: the head's return stamp) is a Unit main and
-- must NOT auto-print its result, or the Unit result would go to the Int printer
-- (a trailing `0`).
-- `cafs` maps each top-level nullary value binding still in scope to its body: a
-- reference to an unannotated CAF (`go = println "x"; main = go`) is Unit iff that
-- body is.  Following a CAF removes it from the map, so a cyclic chain ends False.
mainBodyIsUnit : Prog -> OrdMap CExpr -> CExpr -> Bool
mainBodyIsUnit prog _ (CApp f _ _) = match appHead f
  CVar fn _ =>
    isUnitExtern (runtimeNameW prog fn)
      || returnStamp prog envEmpty fn == RTUnit
  -- `println`/`print` are `Display a =>` constrained → the dict-pass rewrites the
  -- head to a CDict carrying the routes; recover the bare name.
  CDict fn _ => returnStamp prog envEmpty fn == RTUnit
  _ => False
mainBodyIsUnit prog cafs (CVar fn _) =
  if returnStamp prog envEmpty fn == RTUnit then
    True
  else match omLookup fn cafs
    Some body => mainBodyIsUnit prog (omDelete fn cafs) body
    None => False
mainBodyIsUnit prog _ (CDict fn _) = returnStamp prog envEmpty fn == RTUnit
mainBodyIsUnit prog cafs (CLet _ pat _ b) =
  mainBodyIsUnit prog (shadowCafs (patVars pat) cafs) b
-- the native branch-(2) equivalent: an UNANNOTATED `main = match … { … }` whose
-- Unit-ness is only knowable from its inferred body type (e.g. check_main's
-- `match args () { [r,c,f] => withFiles … ; _ => ePutStrLn … }`).  Type-erased here,
-- so reason structurally: a match/decision body is Unit iff EVERY tail leaf is Unit
-- (an IO-extern returning Unit, a fn whose declared ret is Unit, or another all-Unit
-- match).  Conservative — a single non-Unit leaf ⇒ False, so a value main is never
-- suppressed.  Block/Let tails recurse to their final expr.
mainBodyIsUnit prog cafs (CDecision _ arms _) = allArmsUnit prog cafs arms
mainBodyIsUnit prog cafs (CMatch _ arms) = allArmsUnit prog cafs arms
mainBodyIsUnit prog cafs (CBlock stmts) = blockTailIsUnit prog cafs stmts
mainBodyIsUnit _ _ _ = False

-- True iff every match/decision arm body is itself a Unit main body.  Empty ⇒ False
-- (no leaves to prove Unit ⇒ don't suppress).
allArmsUnit : Prog -> OrdMap CExpr -> List CArm -> Bool
allArmsUnit _ _ [] = False
allArmsUnit prog cafs arms = allArmsUnitGo prog cafs arms

allArmsUnitGo : Prog -> OrdMap CExpr -> List CArm -> Bool
allArmsUnitGo _ _ [] = True
allArmsUnitGo prog cafs ((CArm pat _ body) :: rest) =
  if mainBodyIsUnit prog (shadowCafs (patVars pat) cafs) body then
    allArmsUnitGo prog cafs rest
  else
    False

blockTailIsUnit : Prog -> OrdMap CExpr -> List CStmt -> Bool
blockTailIsUnit _ _ [] = False
blockTailIsUnit prog cafs [CSExpr e] = mainBodyIsUnit prog cafs e
blockTailIsUnit prog cafs ((CSLet _ pat _) :: rest) =
  blockTailIsUnit prog (shadowCafs (patVars pat) cafs) rest
blockTailIsUnit prog cafs (_ :: rest) = blockTailIsUnit prog cafs rest

-- The top-level nullary value bindings, name -> body (`isValBind`: never `main`).
cafBodies : List CBind -> OrdMap CExpr
cafBodies groups = omFromPairs (cafBodyRows groups) omEmpty

cafBodyRows : List CBind -> List (String, CExpr)
cafBodyRows [] = []
cafBodyRows ((CBind name [CClause [] body] _ _) :: rest) =
  if name == "main" then cafBodyRows rest else (name, body) :: cafBodyRows rest
cafBodyRows (_ :: rest) = cafBodyRows rest

-- A local binder of the same name hides a top-level CAF below it.
shadowCafs : List String -> OrdMap CExpr -> OrdMap CExpr
shadowCafs [] cafs = cafs
shadowCafs (x :: xs) cafs = shadowCafs xs (omDelete x cafs)

-- The stamp of `main` itself: the type of the value it holds.
mainStamp : Prog -> RuntimeType
mainStamp prog = varStamp prog envEmpty "main"

-- What `main`'s result prints as: its own stamp where that is a printable
-- scalar, else the stamp the body states for itself.
mainPrintStamp : Prog -> CExpr -> RuntimeType
mainPrintStamp prog body =
  let own = mainStamp prog
  if isPrintableScalarStamp own then own else cexprStamp prog envEmpty body

isPrintableScalarStamp : RuntimeType -> Bool
isPrintableScalarStamp RTInt = True
isPrintableScalarStamp RTFloat = True
isPrintableScalarStamp RTBool = True
isPrintableScalarStamp RTChar = True
isPrintableScalarStamp RTString = True
isPrintableScalarStamp _ = False

-- the auto-print kind of a main whose result has stamp [t]; a stamp that names no
-- printable scalar prints as an Int
stampPrintKind : RuntimeType -> WTy
stampPrintKind RTFloat = WFloat
stampPrintKind RTBool = WBool
stampPrintKind RTString = WStr
stampPrintKind RTChar = WChar
stampPrintKind RTUnit = WUnit
stampPrintKind _ = WInt

-- the Unit-RESULT IO externs: a `main = putStrLn …` produces Unit and must NOT be
-- auto-printed (the "Unit main no auto-print" contract — the native oracle prints
-- nothing for a Unit main; the IO side effect IS the output).
isUnitExtern : String -> Bool
-- Intentional cross-file duplicate of the same helper in llvm_emit.mdk; not consolidating (tiny helper / divergent-by-design backend pair).
-- lint-disable-next-line rule-duplicate-body
isUnitExtern name =
  contains name ["putStr", "putStrLn", "ePutStr", "ePutStrLn", "flushStdout"]

refPrintFor : Prog -> WTy -> List String
refPrintFor prog WInt =
  ["    " ++ unboxIntW prog, "    " ++ rtCallW prog "mdk_print_int" 1]
refPrintFor prog WBool = [
  "    ref.cast (ref i31)",
  "    i31.get_u",
  "    " ++ rtCallW prog "mdk_print_bool" 1,
]
refPrintFor prog WStr =
  ["    ref.cast (ref $str)", "    " ++ rtCallW prog "mdk_print_strln" 1]
-- a Char main: an i31 codepoint → encode to a $str via $mdk_char_to_str → print + '\n'
-- (matches the oracle's pp_value, which renders a Char as its glyph).  Forces the
-- $str rep + the char-encode strLeaf runtime (see noteW8MainChar).
refPrintFor prog WChar = [
  "    ref.cast (ref i31)",
  "    i31.get_u",
  "    " ++ rtCallW prog "mdk_char_to_str" 1,
  "    " ++ rtCallW prog "mdk_print_strln" 1,
]
-- W8b: a Float main → unbox the $float → format ($mdk_float_to_str builds a $str)
-- → print + '\n' (matches the oracle's mdk_print_float — shortest-round-trip since #57,
-- + the .0 rule — NOT %.12g; see wasm_preamble.mdk's W8b Float section).
refPrintFor prog WFloat = [
  "    ref.cast (ref $float)",
  "    struct.get $float 0",
  "    " ++ rtCallW prog "mdk_float_to_str" 1,
  "    " ++ rtCallW prog "mdk_print_strln" 1,
]
refPrintFor prog WUnit = gapLP prog "ref-mode: Unit main has no value to print"
refPrintFor prog WRef =
  gapLP
    prog
    "ref-mode main produced a non-scalar value — printing ADTs is W6b (Debug)"

-- ── ref-mode top-level function defs ─────────────────────────────────────────
-- Every param/local/result is `(ref eq)`.  Three shapes:
--   * single clause, all-PVar params → the fast path: bind params, TAIL-emit the
--     body (self-recursion + general tail calls become return_call/return_call_ref).
--   * single clause with a non-PVar (literal/ctor) param, OR multiple clauses →
--     coalesce into a synthetic-parameter dispatch: each clause becomes a guarded
--     block testing its non-PVar params, binding its PVar params, then tail-emitting
--     its body; clauses fall through in order (W4 clause-dispatch coalescing,
--     peer to llvm_emit's emitClauseTree).
-- After the body, if `name` is used anywhere as a VALUE (passed/returned/partially
-- applied), also emit a closure wrapper `$name__clos` (a $clos with arity = param
-- count, code = a thunk that unpacks the args array + calls $name).
emitRefFnBind : Prog -> CBind -> List String
emitRefFnBind outer (CBind name clauses bindLoc _) =
  let prog =
    progForBinding name bindLoc (sitePackedW (progEmit outer) bindLoc) outer
  let arity = clauseArityOf clauses
  let params =
    if rawProgramW prog then match clauses
      [CClause pats _] => map (patName (progEmit prog) name) pats
      _ => synthParams arity
    else
      clauseParamNames clauses arity
  -- Stage-2/3 (b′): a member of a detected dispatch-TMC group emits via the dest-passing
  -- reset-wrapper (root) / inner-loop or redirected-leaf member path.  The group takes
  -- PRECEDENCE over Stage-1: a group root like the lexer's `layout` is Stage-1-eligible
  -- for its SELF-cons arm, but only the group transform linearizes the cross-member
  -- edges (`layout ↔ flushCloseGo ↔ …`) — and a Stage-1-emitted member inside a group
  -- would return its own locally-built spine instead of closing the group's shared dest
  -- globals (a miscompile).  Detection keeps a Stage-1-claimable SINGLETON out of any
  -- group (wDispValidate v5), so plain self-TMC fns still take the Stage-1 loop below.
  if rawProgramW prog then
    emitOrdinaryFnW prog name params arity clauses
  else match dispGroupOf (progEmit prog).wDispGroups.value name
    Some grp =>
      let gd =
        if wDispIsRoot grp name then
          emitWDispRoot prog grp arity clauses
        else
          emitWDispMemberFn prog grp name name arity clauses
      gd
        ++ (if needsClosWrapper prog name then
          emitFnClosWrapper prog name arity
        else
          [])
    None => match wasmTrmcTry prog name arity clauses
      -- Stage 1 (WASMGC-TRMC-DESIGN §7): a top-level self-recursive define (uniform
      -- leading-dict count; dicts ride along as loop slots) whose
      -- clauses are `trmcEligible` for the self-only cons/ctor-tail shape (a) is emitted as
      -- a destination-passing LOOP (emitWasmTrmcBind) instead of the stack-growing recursive
      -- call (emitRefTail's generic ctor arm evaluates the self-call as a struct.new ARG, so
      -- the frame stays live → deep lists overflow).  Ineligible fns fall to the normal path.

      Some tmcDef =>
        tmcDef
          ++ (if needsClosWrapper prog name then
            emitFnClosWrapper prog name arity
          else
            [])
      None => emitOrdinaryFnW prog name params arity clauses

emitOrdinaryFnW : Prog ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  Int ->
  List CClause ->
  List String
emitOrdinaryFnW prog name params arity clauses =
  let w7Outer = w7ScopeOpen (progEmit prog)
  let bodyLines =
    if rawProgramW prog then match clauses
      [CClause pats body] =>
        if allPlainParams pats then
          let _ = installRawParamsW prog 0 pats
          emitRefTail prog (paramEnv pats) arity body
        else
          gapLP
            prog
            ("scalar-mode top-level function '"
              ++ name
              ++ "' is multi-clause or pattern-matching (decision-tree match needs ADT mode)")
      _ =>
        gapLP
          prog
          ("scalar-mode top-level function '"
            ++ name
            ++ "' is multi-clause or pattern-matching (decision-tree match needs ADT mode)")
    else
      emitClausesRef prog name params arity clauses
  let extraLocals =
    if rawProgramW prog then
      []
    else
      filterList (notIn params) (dedupKeep (clauseLocals clauses))
  let depth = if rawProgramW prog then 0 else clausesMaxDepth clauses
  let scratch = if rawProgramW prog then [] else scratchLocals depth
  let paramDecls =
    if rawProgramW prog then
      map (_ => " (param i64)") params
    else
      map paramDeclRef params
  let _ = defineFnW prog (gname name) (FuncParams (listLen params))
  let sig =
    "  (func $\{gname name}\{joinWith "" paramDecls} (result \{physicalType (programReprW prog)})"
  let localDecls = map localDeclRef (extraLocals ++ scratch)
  let w7Decls = w7LocalDecls (w7ScopeClose (progEmit prog) w7Outer) depth
  let fnDef =
    [sig]
      ++ numericDeclsW prog
      ++ rawScratchW prog
      ++ map ("  " ++ _) (localDecls ++ w7Decls)
      ++ indent bodyLines
      ++ ["  )"]
  fnDef
    ++ (if needsClosWrapper prog name then
      emitFnClosWrapper prog name arity
    else
      [])

-- synthetic positional parameter names `$__wparg0 $__wparg1 …` (used for multi-clause
-- dispatch and as the uniform fn ABI param names).  The `__wparg` prefix is RESERVED:
-- a source pattern variable in a clause head (e.g. `unifyN (TFun a1 r1 b1) (TFun a2 r2
-- b2)` binds `a1`) must NOT collide with a sibling positional param's wasm local, or
-- its `local.set` clobbers a not-yet-read argument and a later field extract `ref.cast`
-- traps `illegal cast` (layer-11 bug: the second `TFun`'s value was destroyed by the
-- first clause head binding a var literally named `a1` into `$a1`).  Earlier these were
-- `$a0/$a1/…`, which a user var named `a1` aliased directly.  `gname` escapes any user
-- identifier spelled `__wparg<digits>` (mirrors the `self`/`args` reserved-name escape),
-- so the positional params are provably distinct from every clause-bound source var.
synthParams : Int -> List String
synthParams n = map (i => "__wparg" ++ intToString i) (rangeList 0 n)

-- wasm param names for a clause group.  A single clause whose params are all plain and
-- whose body has no guard fallthrough takes the fast path (emitClausesRefEnv and the
-- TRMC loop): a PVar param is named by its source variable, so the body reads the wasm
-- param directly and no `local.get $__wparg<i>; local.set $x` copy is emitted.  The
-- source name is kept only when it is not `__`-prefixed (scratch locals), is bound once
-- in the head, and is not bound again by a local of the body (a shadowing binder would
-- otherwise share the param's own wasm local).  Every other param keeps its positional
-- `__wparg<i>` name (a PWild, a shadowed name, or any param of a multi-clause group).
clauseParamNames : List CClause -> Int -> List String
clauseParamNames [CClause pats body] arity =
  if allPlainParams pats && not (exprHasFallthrough body) then
    headParamNames pats (collectExprLocals body) 0
  else
    synthParams arity
clauseParamNames _ arity = synthParams arity

headParamNames : List Pat -> List String -> Int -> List String
headParamNames [] _ _ = []
headParamNames (p :: ps) inner i =
  let name = "__wparg" ++ intToString i
  let chosen = match p
    PVar x _ _ => if startsWith "__" x || contains x inner then name else x
    _ => name
  chosen :: headParamNames ps inner (i + 1)

-- emit the clause chain.  Single all-PVar clause: rename its params to the synthetic
-- positions (so the body env binds them) and tail-emit.  Otherwise: a fallthrough
-- chain of guarded blocks.
emitClausesRef : Prog ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  Int ->
  List CClause ->
  List String
emitClausesRef prog name params arity clauses =
  emitClausesRefEnv prog envEmpty name params arity clauses

-- W9: env-seeded clause emission — `baseEnv` names (a CLetGroup's sibling closures +
-- captured outer vars, bound as locals before the body) are in scope in every clause
-- body in addition to the clause's own param bindings.  The non-letgroup path passes
-- baseEnv=[] (emitClausesRef).
emitClausesRefEnv : Prog ->
  Env ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  Int ->
  List CClause ->
  List String
-- the single-clause fast path skips the clause BLOCK (plain params need no test).
-- But a guard chain in the body desugars to `__fallthrough__`, which needs a block
-- to `br` to — so when the body contains one, fall back to the chain path (its
-- block wrapper + trailing `unreachable` give the fall-through a target).
emitClausesRefEnv prog baseEnv name params arity (clauses@[CClause pats body]) =
  if allPlainParams pats && not (exprHasFallthrough body) then
    let aliases = bindParamAliases prog pats params
    let env = paramEnvOver pats baseEnv
    aliases ++ emitRefTail prog env arity body
  else
    emitClauseChainRefEnv prog baseEnv name params arity clauses
emitClausesRefEnv prog baseEnv name params arity clauses =
  emitClauseChainRefEnv prog baseEnv name params arity clauses

-- when the single clause's params are plain PVars, alias each to its wasm param:
-- `local.get $<param>; local.set $<srcname>`.  A PVar already named by its source
-- variable (clauseParamNames) IS its own wasm param, so no copy is emitted.  (The
-- source names are declared as locals via clauseLocals.)
bindParamAliases : Prog -> List Pat -> List String -> List String
bindParamAliases prog pats params =
  flatMap (aliasOne prog) (zipPats pats params)

aliasOne : Prog -> (Pat, String) -> List String
aliasOne _ (PVar x _ _, a) =
  if x == a then [] else ["local.get $" ++ gname a, "local.set $" ++ gname x]
aliasOne _ (PWild, _) = []
aliasOne prog _ = gapLP prog "ref-mode: non-plain param in fast-path alias"

zipPats : List Pat -> List String -> List (Pat, String)
zipPats (p :: ps) (a :: bs) = (p, a) :: zipPats ps bs
zipPats _ _ = []

allPlainParams : List Pat -> Bool
allPlainParams pats = not (anyList (p => not (isPlainParam p)) pats)

-- the fallthrough clause chain.  Each clause: a block `$cl<i>` that tests its
-- non-PVar params (literal/ctor) against the synthetic positions, binds its PVar
-- params, and on full match TAIL-emits its body; a failed test `br $cl<i>` falls
-- through to the next clause.  The last clause's failure is `unreachable` (a
-- well-typed exhaustive fn won't reach it).
emitClauseChainRefEnv : Prog ->
  Env ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  Int ->
  List CClause ->
  List String
emitClauseChainRefEnv prog baseEnv name params arity clauses =
  emitClauseChainGo
    prog
    baseEnv
    name
    params
    arity
    clauses
    0
    (progFnCtx prog).site

emitClauseChainGo : Prog ->
  Env ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  Int ->
  List CClause ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List String
-- B5: the last clause fell through (non-exhaustive function) → coded trap.
emitClauseChainGo prog _ _ _ _ [] _ site = wasmNonexhTrap (progEmit prog) site
emitClauseChainGo prog baseEnv name params arity ((CClause pats body) :: rest) i site =
  let clLabel = "$cl_\{name}_\{intToString i}"
  let (tests, binds, env) = clausePatCodeEnv prog baseEnv pats params clLabel
  -- A guard chain inside this clause's body desugars to `__fallthrough__` (the
  -- "no arm matched, try the next clause" sentinel).  We REWRITE each such occurrence
  -- in the body to a label-carrying sentinel `__ft__<clLabel>` BEFORE emitting, so the
  -- emitter lowers it to `br <clLabel>` as a PURE function of the var name.  (A mutable
  -- "current label" ref does NOT work here: this emitter builds the instruction list
  -- lazily and forces the strings at final assembly, long after any setRef/restore —
  -- so the read would see a stale/default label.  Encoding the target in the node is
  -- timing-independent.)  `br <clLabel>` exits this clause's block, landing on the next
  -- clause (or the chain's trailing `unreachable` for the last clause).
  let body2 = labelFallthrough body clLabel
  ["block " ++ clLabel]
    ++ indent (tests ++ binds ++ emitRefTail prog env arity body2)
    ++ ["end"]
    ++ emitClauseChainGo prog baseEnv name params arity rest (i + 1) site

-- `ftPrefix` / `labelFallthrough` are the BACKEND-NEUTRAL sentinel-labelling pass —
-- they now live in `backend/emit_support.mdk` and are shared with the LLVM emitter,
-- which had reimplemented the same idea as a mutable "current label" Ref and
-- MISCOMPILED a refutable pattern-guard clause because of it (see the comment there).

-- generate (tests, binds, env) for a clause's parameter patterns against the
-- synthetic positional params.  A `br clLabel` on a failed test falls to the next
-- clause.  PLit param → compare the i31 against the constant.  PCon param → test
-- the discriminant + bind fields.  PVar → bind to a local.  PWild → nothing.
clausePatCodeEnv : Prog ->
  Env ->
  List Pat ->
  List String ->
  String ->
  (List String, List String, Env)
clausePatCodeEnv prog baseEnv pats params clLabel =
  clausePatGo prog (zipPats pats params) clLabel [] [] baseEnv

clausePatGo : Prog ->
  List (Pat, String) ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  List String ->
  Env ->
  (List String, List String, Env)
clausePatGo _ [] _ tAcc bAcc env = (tAcc, bAcc, env)
clausePatGo prog ((pat, a) :: rest) clLabel tAcc bAcc env =
  let occ = ["local.get $" ++ gname a]
  let (t, b, env2) = patTestBind prog pat occ clLabel env
  clausePatGo prog rest clLabel (tAcc ++ t) (bAcc ++ b) env2

-- (tests, binds, env') for matching `pat` against the value snippet `occ`.
patTestBind : Prog ->
  Pat ->
  List String ->
  String ->
  Env ->
  (List String, List String, Env)
patTestBind prog PWild occ clLabel env = ([], [], env)
patTestBind prog (PVar x _ bid) occ clLabel env =
  ([], occ ++ ["local.set $" ++ gname x], envBind x bid env)
-- #759: unbox the scrutinee through the $mdk_unbox_int seam (i31 OR $boxint) and
-- compare at full i64 width.  An `i31.get_s` + `i32.const n` path truncates to
-- 31 bits — for |n| >= 2^30 the `i32.const` overflows (wasm-tools REJECTS the module)
-- and a boxed scrutinee ref.casts to i31 and TRAPS.
patTestBind prog (PLit (LInt n)) occ clLabel env = (
  occ
    ++ [
      unboxIntW prog,
      "i64.const " ++ intToString n,
      "i64.ne",
      "br_if " ++ clLabel,
    ],
  [],
  env,
)
patTestBind prog (PLit (LBool b)) occ clLabel env = (
  occ
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref i31)",
      "i31.get_u",
      "i32.const " ++ (if b then "1" else "0"),
      "i32.ne",
      "br_if " ++ clLabel,
    ],
  [],
  env,
)
-- W9: a `()` (Unit) clause head — Unit is the i31 0 immediate, irrefutable here
-- (the type guarantees the value is Unit), so no test and no binding.
patTestBind prog (PLit LUnit) occ clLabel env = ([], [], env)
-- W9: a Char-literal clause head — a Char is an i31 codepoint immediate (same rep
-- as emitLitRef (LChar)); compare the i31 against the codepoint constant.
patTestBind prog (PLit (LChar c)) occ clLabel env = (
  occ
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref i31)",
      "i31.get_u",
      "i32.const "
        ++ intToString (charCode (arrayGetUnsafe 0 (stringToChars c))),
      "i32.ne",
      "br_if " ++ clLabel,
    ],
  [],
  env,
)
patTestBind prog (PLit (LString s)) occ clLabel env =
  let cmpSuffix = [
    rtCallW prog "mdk_str_compare" 2,
    "ref.cast (ref i31)",
    "i31.get_u",
    "i32.const 1",
    "i32.ne",
    "br_if " ++ clLabel,
  ]
  (
    occ ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)"] ++ emitLitRef prog (LString s) ++ cmpSuffix,
    [],
    env,
  )
-- W10: a constructor clause head — test the discriminant, then descend into each
-- field with patTestBind (NOT bindConFields).  A nested field pattern can itself be
-- refutable (e.g. `Variant cname (ConNamed fs)` — the inner `ConNamed` discriminates
-- against a sibling `ConPos` of the same payload type), so the field must emit its own
-- discriminant test, else its struct cast runs unconditionally and traps `illegal
-- cast` on the sibling shape.  bindConFields only binds (no tests), so it is unsound
-- for refutable nested ctors — mirror PCons/PTuple/PList, which recurse via patTestBind.
patTestBind prog (PCon c args) occ clLabel env =
  let ctest =
    discrimReadOf occ (ctorTypeName prog c)
      ++ [
        "i32.const " ++ intToString (ctorOrdinal prog c),
        "i32.ne",
        "br_if " ++ clLabel,
      ]
  let (ft, fb, env2) = patTestBindCon prog c args occ clLabel env 0
  (ctest ++ ft, fb, env2)
patTestBind prog (PAs x _ bid p) occ clLabel env =
  let setX = occ ++ ["local.set $" ++ gname x]
  let (t, b, env2) = patTestBind prog p occ clLabel (envBind x bid env)
  (t, setX ++ b, env2)
-- W9: a refutable cons-cell clause head `(h :: t)` — the focus must be a Cons
-- (ordinal 0; Nil is ordinal 1), else fall to the next clause.  Then test+bind
-- the head (field 1) and tail (field 2) recursively (nested patterns may also be
-- refutable, e.g. `[x] = (x :: [])`).
patTestBind prog (PCons h t) occ clLabel env =
  let consTest =
    discrimReadOf occ "List" ++ ["i32.const 0", "i32.ne", "br_if " ++ clLabel]
  let hSnip = occ ++ ["ref.cast (ref $C_Cons)", "struct.get $C_Cons 1"]
  let tSnip = occ ++ ["ref.cast (ref $C_Cons)", "struct.get $C_Cons 2"]
  let (ht, hb, env2) = patTestBind prog h hSnip clLabel env
  let (tt, tb, env3) = patTestBind prog t tSnip clLabel env2
  (consTest ++ ht ++ tt, hb ++ tb, env3)
-- W9: a refutable fixed-length list clause head `[p0, p1, …]` — descend the Cons
-- spine: each element's cell must be a Cons (else fall through), then the final
-- tail must be Nil (ordinal 1).
patTestBind prog (PList ps) occ clLabel env =
  patTestBindList prog ps occ clLabel env
-- W9: a tuple clause head `(p0, p1, …)` — a tuple is single-shape (irrefutable),
-- so no test; bind each field (field i+1 of $C_Tup<n>) and recurse for nested
-- refutable subpatterns.
patTestBind prog (PTuple ps) occ clLabel env =
  patTestBindTuple prog (tupleCtorName (listLen ps)) ps occ clLabel env 0
-- G6 (#379): a range pattern `lo..=hi` / `lo..hi`.  PRng canonicalizes to PWild in the
-- decision matrix (core_ir_lower's canonPat), so the tree routes to this arm
-- UNCONDITIONALLY and marks it patNeedsGuard — the actual comparison must happen here,
-- in the guarded-arm re-match.  Peer of llvm_emit's `emitRefutMatch (PRng ...)`.
-- One signed i64 test serves both Int and Char (Char = its codepoint, cf. the PLit
-- LChar arm above); rngCmpW unboxes via $mdk_unbox_int so NEGATIVE bounds (`-1..1`) and
-- Int bounds >= 2^30 are both correct.  Fail-fast, mirroring eval.mdk's inIntRange/inCharRange:
-- `v < lo` fails; then `v > hi` (incl) / `v >= hi` (exclusive `..`) fails.
patTestBind prog (PRng lo hi incl) occ clLabel env = (
  rngCmpW prog occ (rngBound lo) "i64.lt_s" clLabel
    ++ rngCmpW
      prog
      occ
      (rngBound hi)
      (if incl then "i64.gt_s" else "i64.ge_s")
      clLabel,
  [],
  env,
)
patTestBind prog other occ clLabel env =
  gapL3P prog ("ref-mode: unsupported clause parameter pattern " ++ ptag other)

-- one half of a range test: unbox `occ` to i64 and `br_if clLabel` when `cmp` against
-- `bound` holds (i.e. when the value is OUT of range).  `occ` is re-embedded per half —
-- patTestBind's contract already requires it be a cheap re-runnable read.  #759: the
-- $mdk_unbox_int seam (i31 OR $boxint) at full i64 width so an Int bound >= 2^30 neither
-- overflows `i32.const` nor traps a boxed scrutinee's i31 cast; a Char is a small i31
-- codepoint, which $mdk_unbox_int sign-extends exactly as `i31.get_s` did.  `cmp` is the
-- i64 comparator (`i64.lt_s`/`i64.gt_s`/`i64.ge_s`).
rngCmpW : Prog -> List String -> Int -> String -> String -> List String
rngCmpW prog occ bound cmp clLabel =
  occ
    ++ [
      unboxIntW prog,
      "i64.const " ++ intToString bound,
      cmp,
      "br_if " ++ clLabel,
    ]

-- (tests, binds, env') for a refutable fixed-length list clause head against `occ`.
-- Each element requires its cell be a Cons; the spine end requires Nil.
patTestBindList : Prog ->
  List Pat ->
  List String ->
  String ->
  Env ->
  (List String, List String, Env)
patTestBindList _ [] occ clLabel env = (
  discrimReadOf occ "List" ++ ["i32.const 1", "i32.ne", "br_if " ++ clLabel],
  [],
  env,
)
patTestBindList prog (p :: ps) occ clLabel env =
  let consTest =
    discrimReadOf occ "List" ++ ["i32.const 0", "i32.ne", "br_if " ++ clLabel]
  let hSnip = occ ++ ["ref.cast (ref $C_Cons)", "struct.get $C_Cons 1"]
  let tSnip = occ ++ ["ref.cast (ref $C_Cons)", "struct.get $C_Cons 2"]
  let (ht, hb, env2) = patTestBind prog p hSnip clLabel env
  let (tt, tb, env3) = patTestBindList prog ps tSnip clLabel env2
  (consTest ++ ht ++ tt, hb ++ tb, env3)

-- (tests, binds, env') for a tuple clause head: each field i+1 of $C_Tup<n> (after
-- the i32 tag), recursing into the sub-pattern (which may itself be refutable).
patTestBindTuple : Prog ->
  String ->
  List Pat ->
  List String ->
  String ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  (List String, List String, Env)
patTestBindTuple _ _ [] _ _ env _ = ([], [], env)
patTestBindTuple prog tc (p :: rest) occ clLabel env i =
  let fieldSnip =
    occ
      ++ [
        "ref.cast (ref $" ++ ctorStructName tc ++ ")",
        "struct.get $\{ctorStructName tc} \{intToString (i + 1)}",
      ]
  let (ft, fb, env2) = patTestBind prog p fieldSnip clLabel env
  let (rt, rb, env3) = patTestBindTuple prog tc rest occ clLabel env2 (i + 1)
  (ft ++ rt, fb ++ rb, env3)

-- (tests, binds, env') for a constructor clause head's fields: field i+1 of the ctor's
-- struct (after the i32 tag), recursing into each sub-pattern with patTestBind so a
-- refutable nested ctor (`ConNamed fs`) emits its own discriminant test+bind.
patTestBindCon : Prog ->
  String ->
  List Pat ->
  List String ->
  String ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  (List String, List String, Env)
patTestBindCon _ _ [] _ _ env _ = ([], [], env)
patTestBindCon prog c (p :: rest) occ clLabel env i =
  let fieldSnip =
    occ
      ++ [
        "ref.cast (ref $" ++ ctorStructName c ++ ")",
        "struct.get $\{ctorStructName c} \{intToString (i + 1)}",
      ]
  let (ft, fb, env2) = patTestBind prog p fieldSnip clLabel env
  let (rt, rb, env3) = patTestBindCon prog c rest occ clLabel env2 (i + 1)
  (ft ++ rt, fb ++ rb, env3)

-- all locals a clause group needs: every clause's param-bound vars + body locals.
clauseLocals : List CClause -> List String
clauseLocals clauses = flatMap oneClauseLocals clauses

oneClauseLocals : CClause -> List String
oneClauseLocals (CClause pats body) =
  flatMap patVars pats ++ collectExprLocals body

clausesMaxDepth : List CClause -> Int
clausesMaxDepth clauses = foldMaxDepth (flatMap clauseBody clauses)

-- whether a top-level fn needs its closure wrapper. The pre-emission program-index
-- build scans value positions once and stores the immutable membership set in this
-- Prog's invocation-private index; lookup is O(log n) with no ambient authority.
-- Never in raw mode: a raw program declares no closure types, and the demand
-- planner routes every genuine value use of a function to ref mode.  The scan
-- behind the index does not see match-arm binders, so in raw mode a hit can only
-- be such a local shadowing the function's name, whose wrapper would reference
-- the undeclared `$codety`.
needsClosWrapper : Prog -> String -> Bool
needsClosWrapper prog name =
  not (rawProgramW prog)
    && omHasKey name (indexFnsUsedAsValuesW (progIndex prog))

-- the closure wrapper for a top-level fn: `$mdk_w_<name>` is a $codety that unpacks
-- the args array and calls $name; `$name__clos` is built by `mkFnClos` at each value
-- ref.  Here we emit only the wrapper CODE function; the $clos struct is built inline
-- at the value-reference site (emitVarRef) so partial application threads its arity.
emitFnClosWrapper : Prog -> String -> Int -> List String
emitFnClosWrapper prog name arity =
  let wrapper = "$mdk_w_" ++ name
  let _ = noteFuncRef prog wrapper
  let _ = defineFnW prog wrapper codeShapeW
  closWrapperLines wrapper (callFnW prog CallTailW (gname name) arity) arity

-- A `$codety` function [wrapper] that loads [arity] arguments out of its argument
-- array and makes the tail call [call] on them.
closWrapperLines : String -> String -> Int -> List String
closWrapperLines wrapper call arity =
  let argLoads =
    flatMap
      (i => [
        "local.get $args",
        "i32.const " ++ intToString i,
        "array.get $argarr",
        "ref.as_non_null",
      ])
      (rangeList 0 arity)
  [
      "  (func "
        ++ wrapper
        ++ " (type $codety) (param $self (ref eq)) (param $args (ref $argarr)) (result (ref eq))",
    ]
    ++ indent (argLoads ++ [call])
    ++ ["  )"]

paramDeclRef : String -> String
paramDeclRef p = " (param $" ++ gname p ++ " (ref eq))"

localDeclRef : String -> String
localDeclRef l = "(local $" ++ gname l ++ " (ref eq))"

-- ── §W5 typeclass dispatch (dict-passing) ────────────────────────────────────
-- Parallels the LLVM emitter (emitMethod/emitDictApp/dictWordsOf + emitImpls).
-- STAGE2-DESIGN §2.4c policy: dispatch is RUNTIME DICT-PASSING.  The Core IR
-- carries the resolved Routes as DATA on CMethod/CDict; this section reads them.
--
-- DICT-WITNESS REPRESENTATION (the WasmGC analogue of the LLVM i64 "dict word").
-- Every value here is a (ref eq).  A dict witness is an i31 immediate carrying
-- `hashName(impl-head-tag)` — the SAME djb2 hash the LLVM emitter stores at field
-- 0 of its dict cell.  Threading it as a (ref eq) i31 rides the uniform W4 ABI for
-- free: a constrained fn's leading `$dict_*` params are ordinary (ref eq) params,
-- and at a dispatch site the witness is unboxed (`i31.get_s`) back to the i32 tag
-- word.  For minimal Eq/Ord/Num at Int/Bool/ADT the per-instance `requires` dicts
-- are empty, so a one-level witness is just `i32.const <hashName tag>; ref.i31`
-- (no heap cell needed — the LLVM emitter's nested-cell layout is W5-out-of-scope).
--
--   RKey tag   → a STATIC direct call to $mdk_impl_<tag>_<method> (llvm_emit line
--                2846: an RKey is a compile-time direct call).
--   RDict d    → the in-scope dict param $d carries hashName(tag); unbox it and
--   RDictFwd d   if-chain over the method's candidate impls (i32.eq against each
--                impl's hashName(routeKey)) → call the matching impl.  Sparse hash
--                keys ⇒ an if-chain, NOT a br_table (which is for dense ctor tags).
--   RNone      → arg-tag fallback (gap this slice; no minimal fixture needs it).

-- the method occurrence (return-/arg-position), applied to `args`.  `implRoutes`
-- (per-instance requires) + `methRoutes` (method-level constraints) are the leading
-- dict witnesses, prepended to the args (in methRoutes++implRoutes order, matching
-- llvm_emit's dictWordsOf (methRoutes ++ implRoutes)).
emitMethodRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  Route ->
  List Route ->
  List Route ->
  List CExpr ->
  CallMode ->
  CallEndW ->
  List String
-- An RKey route is a STATIC direct call, legal only when the application is exact:
-- the selected entry's define takes exactly the supplied value arguments after its
-- dicts.  Any other application builds the method's value closure (whose own body is
-- that exact call) and applies every argument through $__mdk_apply, whose
-- under-application arm makes the residual PAP and whose over-application arm applies
-- the surplus to the call's result -- after every argument is evaluated.  A dynamic
-- mode names no selected entry's arity, and keeps the direct call.
emitMethodRef prog env d name iface siteArity (route@(RKey tag _ _)) implRoutes methRoutes args mode end =
  if missesArity mode then
    emitMethodValueRef
        prog
        env
        d
        name
        iface
        siteArity
        route
        implRoutes
        methRoutes
      ++ emitArgsArray prog env d args
      ++ [callFnW prog end "__mdk_apply" 2]
  else
    emitMethodRKeyCallRef
      prog
      env
      d
      name
      iface
      siteArity
      route
      implRoutes
      methRoutes
      args
      end
-- A runtime dictionary selects the entry, so the site cannot know its arity: every
-- argument goes to the dispatch, whose arms each apply them to their own entry.
emitMethodRef prog env d name iface siteArity (RDict dpar) _ methRoutes args _ end =
  emitMethodDispatchRef prog env d name iface siteArity dpar methRoutes args end
emitMethodRef prog env d name iface siteArity (RDictFwd dpar) _ methRoutes args _ end =
  emitMethodDispatchRef prog env d name iface siteArity dpar methRoutes args end
-- A projected super dictionary is read into its own local (`projLocalName`,
