-- declared by `collectExprLocals`) and dispatched on exactly as a dict parameter.
emitMethodRef prog env d name iface siteArity (route@(RProj r path)) _ methRoutes args _ end =
  let local = projLocalName r path
  routeWitness prog env d route
    ++ ["local.set $" ++ gname local]
    ++ emitMethodDispatchRef
      prog
      (envBindUnstamped local env)
      d
      name
      iface
      siteArity
      local
      methRoutes
      args
      end
emitMethodRef prog env d name _ _ RNone implRoutes methRoutes args _ end =
  gapLP
      prog
      ("wasm W5: RNone arg-tag dispatch for '" ++ name ++ "' is out of slice")
    ++ endValueW end
-- P0-18 (wasm peer of llvm_emit's emitMethod RLocal arm): NOT a method dispatch —
-- the receiver has no impl of this interface but a local/imported standalone shadows
-- the method name.  Emit a DIRECT call to that standalone top-level fn, exactly as a
-- known-fn CApp would.  `target` is the carried MANGLED symbol `<mid>__name` when
-- non-empty (the marked EMethodAt carries the bare dispatch name), else the bare name.
-- S-1 (wasm peer of llvm_emit's emitMethod RLocal emitDictApp delegation): a
-- CONSTRAINED shadowing standalone has leading dict PARAMS, so the call must push the
-- matching dict witnesses first.  Delegate to emitDictRef — the SAME tested helper the
-- ordinary CDict path uses.  Without this the raw `call` below pushes one operand too
-- few and wasm-tools rejects the module outright ("type mismatch: expected (ref eq) but
-- nothing on stack" — that "nothing" IS the missing dict word).  `dicts == []` keeps the
-- byte-identical pre-S1 direct call.
-- P1: the direct `call` below is only legal when the application is exact, as at
-- emitAppRef's CVar arm.  `inc = add 1` is the shape: `add` shadows the prelude
-- `Num.add` method name, so the marker rewrites it to `CMethod "add" (RLocal
-- "<mid>__add")` and it arrives HERE rather than at the CVar arm.  A non-exact call
-- goes through emitIndirectApp: it builds the fn's closure and applies via
-- $__mdk_apply, whose under-app arm makes the residual PAP.
emitMethodRef prog env d name _ _ (RLocal sym dicts) implRoutes methRoutes args mode end =
  let target = if sym == "" then name else sym
  if isEmpty dicts then
    if progFnMemberW prog target && not (isExactCall mode) then
      emitIndirectApp prog env d (CVar target AGlobal) args end
    else
      let argInstrs = flatMap (a => emitRefExpr prog env d a) args
      argInstrs ++ [callFnW prog end (gname target) (listLen args)]
  else
    emitDictRef prog env d target dicts args mode end
emitMethodRef prog env d name _ _ (RScalar _) implRoutes methRoutes args _ end =
  gapLP
      prog
      ("wasm W5: RScalar route for method '" ++ name ++ "' is out of slice")
    ++ endValueW end

-- a partial or an over application: its arguments do not fill a known arity
missesArity : CallMode -> Bool
missesArity (CallPartial _) = True
missesArity (CallOver _) = True
missesArity _ = False

-- the RKey direct call itself, for a site supplying exactly the value arity.
emitMethodRKeyCallRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  Route ->
  List Route ->
  List Route ->
  List CExpr ->
  CallEndW ->
  List String
emitMethodRKeyCallRef prog env d name iface siteArity route implRoutes methRoutes args end =
  let tag = optionOr "" (instanceWord route)
  let argInstrs = flatMap (a => emitRefExpr prog env d a) args
  -- `RKey tag` selects a STATIC impl (peer of llvm_emit's emitMethod RKey arm): the
  -- entry of the occurrence's interface filed under the instance key [tag] — a
  -- supplied method, or an inherited default's per-instance body — else a gap.
  match implForWSite prog name iface tag siteArity
    -- P3 (dropped-requires-dict over-forwarding, #717): a TERMINAL impl body that IGNORES
    -- its `requires` dict (`impl S (List a) requires S a where s _ = 2`) has that dict
    -- DROPPED from the define by the dict-pass (usesImplDict false) — so `$mdk_impl_<tag>_
    -- <name>` declares FEWER leading dict params than the call-site route forwards.  A flat
    -- `dictWords ++ argInstrs ++ call` then pushes a surplus dict witness the callee never
    -- pops ("values remaining on stack at end of block").  Native gets away with it (LLVM
    -- cdecl silently ignores extra args); wasm's strict types do not.  Forward only the
    -- leading dicts the concrete define actually declares — a PREFIX of `methRoutes ++
    -- implRoutes` (method-level dicts, then kept `requires` dicts), so a define that kept
    -- all its dicts is byte-identical.
    Some entry =>
      let kept =
        staticEntryDictRoutesW
          entry
          (MethodEvidence iface siteArity route implRoutes methRoutes)
      let keptWords = flatMap (routeWitness prog env d) kept
      keptWords
        ++ argInstrs
        ++ [
          callFnW
            prog
            end
            (implEntrySymW name entry)
            (listLen kept + listLen args),
        ]
    None =>
      gapLP
          prog
          "wasm layer-15: no impl of method '\{name}' for instance '\{tag}'"
        ++ endValueW end

-- The leading dictionaries a static call to [ent] passes after its method-level
-- ones (llvm_emit's `staticEntryDictRoutes`): a supplied method's kept `requires`,
-- or an inherited default's RECEIVER, the selected instance's dictionary built from
-- the site's word, `requires` routes and the supers the route carries for this case.
staticEntryDictRoutesW : CImplEntry -> MethodEvidence -> List Route
staticEntryDictRoutesW ent ev =
  if isInheritedEntryW ent then
    ev.meContext ++ [receiverEvidence ev]
  else
    takeRoutesW
      (implLeadingDictCountOfEntryW ent)
      (ev.meContext ++ ev.mePrereqs)

-- an inherited default's per-instance entry
isInheritedEntryW : CImplEntry -> Bool
isInheritedEntryW (CImplEntry _ _ _ (CImplDefault _ _ _ _ _ _ _)) = True
isInheritedEntryW _ = False

-- A dispatch site's method-level dictionaries: the instructions that push their
-- witnesses, and how many there are.
data MethodDictsW = MethodDictsW { mdInstrs : List String, mdCount : Int }

-- The dictionaries a dispatch arm loads for its entry after the [nMeth] method-level
-- ones: an inherited default receives the dictionary that selected it; a supplied
-- method its `requires` -- the rest of the entry's own leading `$dict_*` count --
-- which follow the dictionary's super segment (llvm_emit's `emitDispatchArmBody`).
armDictLoadsW : WasmProgramIndex -> CImplEntry -> String -> Int -> List String
armDictLoadsW index ent dpar nMeth =
  if isInheritedEntryW ent then
    ["local.get $" ++ gname dpar]
  else
    let supers = entrySuperCountW index ent
    flatMap
      (loadReqDict dpar)
      (rangeList supers (supers + armDictCountW ent nMeth))

-- how many dictionaries `armDictLoadsW` loads
armDictCountW : CImplEntry -> Int -> Int
armDictCountW ent nMeth =
  if isInheritedEntryW ent then
    1
  else
    maxI 0 (implLeadingDictCountOfEntryW ent - nMeth)

-- RDict/RDictFwd: the dict param `$dpar` is an i31 carrying hashName(tag).  Unbox
-- it, then if-chain over the method's candidate impls comparing the loaded tag
-- against each impl's hashName(routeKey); on a match call $mdk_impl_<symTag>_<m>.
-- For a value the chain runs inside a result block and each arm `br`s out with its
-- value; for a tail call each arm `return_call`s and no block is needed.
emitMethodDispatchRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  List Route ->
  List CExpr ->
  CallEndW ->
  List String
emitMethodDispatchRef prog env d name iface siteArity dpar methRoutes args end =
  -- the occurrence's interface's candidates (#1265, #1619), and (#1852, LOCKSTEP with
  -- llvm_emit's `narrowImplsByArity`) only those whose own declared arity is the
  -- arity this site supplies.
  let impls = narrowImplsByArityW (methodImpls prog name iface) siteArity
  let argInstrs = flatMap (a => emitRefExpr prog env d a) args
  -- every arm passes the site's method-level dictionaries ahead of its own
  let methInstrs = flatMap (routeWitness prog env d) methRoutes
  -- the dict tag is read repeatedly; stash it in the scratch local for this depth.
  let tagRead = readDictParam prog env dpar
  let blk = "$disp_\{name}_\{intToString d}"
  -- every entry is a guarded arm, a general instance's too: its dictionary carries
  -- its own canonical key
  let chain =
    emitDispatchChain
      prog
      name
      impls
      blk
      tagRead
      dpar
      MethodDictsW { mdInstrs = methInstrs, mdCount = listLen methRoutes }
      argInstrs
      (listLen args)
      end
      0
  match end
    CallValueW =>
      ["block " ++ blk ++ " (result (ref eq))"]
        ++ indent chain
        ++ ["unreachable", "end"]
    CallTailW => chain ++ ["unreachable"]

-- #747: the call instruction(s) a matched dispatch arm emits after its dictionaries
-- and arguments.  A nullary/return-position/dictionary-free impl (nArgs == 0 and a
-- `$memo_<symTag>_<method>` LAZY value global synthesized by core_ir_lower —
-- isLazyGlobalW confirms it exists) is a per-instance CAF: FORCE its shared CAF
-- (`call $force_<memo>`, which memoises into `$<memo>` and black-holes a cyclic
-- re-force) instead of re-calling `$mdk_impl_*`, so the resolved tag's side effect
-- runs once and is shared across every occurrence at that tag (matching eval's
-- per-VTypedImpl memoThunk).  Each tag owns its own `$memo` CAF ⇒ distinct tags
-- memoise independently.  Otherwise the ordinary impl call.
dispatchCallSeqW : Prog -> ImplArmW -> String -> Int -> CallEndW -> List String
dispatchCallSeqW prog arm name nArgs end =
  let memoName = "$memo_\{armSymTagW arm}_\{name}"
  if nArgs == 0 && isLazyGlobalW prog memoName then
    [callFnW prog end ("force_" ++ gname memoName) 0]
  else
    [callFnW prog end (armFnSymW arm) (armDictCountW (armEntryW arm) 0 + nArgs)]

-- F10 (#1450/#1668 follow-on): a dispatch site pushes exactly the arguments THAT
-- SITE saw, and the entry a runtime dictionary selects need not take that many: two
-- interfaces' same-spelled methods at different arity, or an impl clause that takes
-- fewer parameters than its declaration.  An arm whose entry takes exactly the
-- site's arguments calls its define; any other pushes the define as a closure first
-- and applies it to the dictionaries and arguments together through $__mdk_apply, so
-- an under-application builds the residual PAP and an over-application applies the
-- surplus to the define's result -- after every argument is evaluated.
armIsExactW : ImplArmW -> Int -> Bool
armIsExactW arm nArgs =
  let pats = implEntryPatsW (armEntryW arm)
  listLen pats - leadingDictParams pats == nArgs

-- The define of [arm]'s entry as a closure value: a lifted `$codety` wrapper that
-- unpacks its argument array into the define's parameters, at the define's arity.
armClosureW : Prog -> ImplArmW -> List String
armClosureW prog arm =
  let arity = listLen (implEntryPatsW (armEntryW arm))
  let wrapper = "$mdk_lam" ++ intToString (freshLamId (progEmit prog))
  let _ = noteFuncRef prog wrapper
  let _ =
    addLifted
      prog
      wrapper
      codeShapeW
      (closWrapperLines
        wrapper
        (callFnW prog CallTailW (armFnSymW arm) arity)
        arity)
  wConstClos prog wrapper arity

-- one comparison + call per candidate impl group.  loaded tag (i32) == dictTag
-- routeKey?  if so: load this impl's nested requires-dicts from the dict param's
-- $dictcell (W5 — was a placeholder zero) ++ the args, call the impl, `br` out of the
-- result block carrying its (ref eq).  The `if` carries NO result type — the matched
-- branch exits via `br $blk` (which supplies the block's value), the else branch falls
-- through to the next comparison; after the whole chain an `unreachable` (a well-typed
-- dict always names a candidate) satisfies the block's (ref eq) fallthrough requirement.
-- `idt` (trailing) is the chain's own INDENT depth — see emitLitSwitchRef (#381).
emitDispatchChain : Prog ->
  String ->
  List ImplArmW ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  String ->
  MethodDictsW ->
  List String ->
  Int ->
  CallEndW ->
  Int ->
  List String
emitDispatchChain _ _ [] _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ = []
emitDispatchChain prog name (arm :: rest) blk tagRead dpar meth argInstrs nArgs end idt =
  -- W5: a `requires`-bearing impl (e.g. `Debug (a,b) requires Debug a, Debug b`) compiles
  -- to a fn whose leading params are the forwarded `requires` dicts BEFORE the method args.
  -- The dispatch site holds the dict param ($dpar): when this impl is constrained, the dict
  -- reaching this arm is a $dictcell whose field-1 $dictarr carries those nested req dicts in
  -- order (built by routeWitness).  Load field 0..reqDicts-1 and prepend them as the impl fn's
  -- leading dict args, mirroring llvm_emit's loadReqDicts (fields 1..n of the boxed cell).
  let reqLoads =
    armDictLoadsW (progIndex prog) (armEntryW arm) dpar meth.mdCount
  let pushed = meth.mdInstrs ++ reqLoads ++ argInstrs
  let armBody =
    if not (armIsExactW arm nArgs) then
      armClosureW prog arm
        ++ pushed
        ++ [
          "array.new_fixed $argarr "
            ++ intToString
              (meth.mdCount
                + armDictCountW (armEntryW arm) meth.mdCount
                + nArgs),
          callFnW prog end "__mdk_apply" 2,
        ]
    else if meth.mdCount > 0 then
      pushed
        ++ [
          callFnW
            prog
            end
            (armFnSymW arm)
            (meth.mdCount + armDictCountW (armEntryW arm) meth.mdCount + nArgs),
        ]
    else
      pushed ++ dispatchCallSeqW prog arm name nArgs end
  let armExit = match end
    CallValueW => ["br " ++ blk]
    CallTailW => []
  indentBy idt (dispatchKeyTestW arm tagRead ++ ["if"])
    ++ indentBy (idt + 1) (armBody ++ armExit)
    ++ indentBy idt ["else"]
    ++ emitDispatchChain
      prog
      name
      rest
      blk
      tagRead
      dpar
      meth
      argInstrs
      nArgs
      end
      (idt + 1)
    ++ indentBy idt ["end"]

-- The test that selects one implementation: the dictionary's word against the arm's
-- canonical key.  A word names exactly one instance, the same one in every module.
dispatchKeyTestW : ImplArmW -> List String -> List String
dispatchKeyTestW arm tagRead =
  tagRead ++ ["i32.const " ++ intToString (dictTag (armKeyW arm)), "i32.eq"]

-- load nested req dict `i` from the dict param $dpar's $dictcell (field 1 = $dictarr).
-- Only reached for a constrained impl arm, where the in-scope dict IS a $dictcell.
-- load nested req dict `i` for a matched impl arm.  The witness ($dpar) is EITHER a
-- one-level i31 (no nested reqs — the typed-entry case where the iface table is absent
-- so the req COUNT is over-counted, or any concrete-element dict) OR a $dictcell (a real
-- nested dict carrying its element witnesses in field-1's $dictarr).  Runtime-test the
-- shape: i31 ⇒ a placeholder i31(0) (mirrors the pre-W5 stub — harmless, the impl never
-- recurses into a real element dict in that case); $dictcell ⇒ load field-1 array[i] (the
-- genuine nested element witness).  Both arms leave one (ref eq) → the arg count is static.
loadReqDict : String -> Int -> List String
loadReqDict dpar i =
  ["local.get $" ++ gname dpar, "ref.test (ref i31)", "if (result (ref eq))"]
    ++ indent ["i32.const 0", "ref.i31"]
    ++ ["else"]
    ++ indent [
      "local.get $" ++ gname dpar,
      "ref.cast (ref $dictcell)",
      "struct.get $dictcell 1",
      "i32.const " ++ intToString i,
      "array.get $dictarr",
      "ref.as_non_null",
    ]
    ++ ["end"]

-- the super dictionaries a dictionary of [ent]'s interface stores ahead of its
-- `requires` dictionaries (llvm_emit's `entrySuperCount`)
entrySuperCountW : WasmProgramIndex -> CImplEntry -> Int
entrySuperCountW index ent =
  optionOr 0 (omLookup (implEntryIfaceWordW ent) index.fnImpl.superCounts)

-- the local a projected super dictionary is dispatched through
projLocalName : Route -> List Int -> String
projLocalName (RDict d) path = "\{d}$p\{projPathWord path}"
projLocalName (RDictFwd d) path = "\{d}$p\{projPathWord path}"
projLocalName (RProj r p) path = projLocalName r (p ++ path)
projLocalName _ path = "$proj$p\{projPathWord path}"

projPathWord : List Int -> String
projPathWord path = joinWith "_" (map intToString path)

implLeadingDictCountOfEntryW : CImplEntry -> Int
implLeadingDictCountOfEntryW ent = leadingDictParams (implEntryPatsW ent)

-- `take n` for a route list (no stdlib `take` in scope here).
takeRoutesW : Int -> List Route -> List Route
takeRoutesW n _
  | n <= 0 = []
takeRoutesW _ [] = []
takeRoutesW n (r :: rest) = r :: takeRoutesW (n - 1) rest

-- read a dict PARAM's HEAD TAG (an i32) into the stack.  The witness is EITHER an i31
-- (a one-level `RKey k []` dict — tag = i31.get_s) OR a $dictcell (a nested `RKey k [reqs]`
-- dict — tag = struct.get 0).  Type-test once and read the tag from the matching shape;
-- both arms leave one i32 on the stack.  The param is a leading $dict_* local, always in env.
readDictParam : Prog -> Env -> String -> List String
readDictParam prog env dpar =
  if envHas dpar env then
    ["local.get $" ++ gname dpar, "ref.test (ref i31)", "if (result i32)"]
      ++ indent ["local.get $" ++ gname dpar, "ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_s"]
      ++ ["else"]
      ++ indent [
        "local.get $" ++ gname dpar,
        "ref.cast (ref $dictcell)",
        "struct.get $dictcell 0",
      ]
      ++ ["end"]
  else
    gapLP prog ("wasm W5: dict param '" ++ dpar ++ "' not in scope")

-- materialize a Route as its leading dict witness instruction(s): a concrete RKey →
-- the i31 of hashName(tag); a forwarded RDict/RDictFwd → re-push the in-scope dict
-- param.  Nested `requires` (RKey with non-empty reqs) are out of the minimal slice.
routeWitness : Prog -> Env -> Int -> Route -> List String
routeWitness _ _ _ (RKey tag [] []) =
  ["i32.const " ++ intToString (dictTag tag), "ref.i31"]
-- W5 (nested requires-dict): build a $dictcell — push the tag, recursively build each
-- nested req witness onto the stack, pack them into a $dictarr (array.new_fixed), then
-- struct.new $dictcell.  Mirrors llvm_emit's emitDictCell (header + recursively-built
-- req fields); the recursion is dictWordsOf == flatMap routeWitness over reqs.
-- The array holds the dictionary's direct supers first, then its requires (the
-- LLVM cell's order), so a projection indexes the same slot whichever instance the
-- dictionary is.
routeWitness prog env d (RKey tag reqs sups) =
  let fieldWitnesses = flatMap (routeWitness prog env d) (sups ++ reqs)
  ["i32.const " ++ intToString (dictTag tag)]
    ++ fieldWitnesses
    ++ [
      "array.new_fixed $dictarr " ++ intToString (listLen sups + listLen reqs),
      "struct.new $dictcell",
    ]
-- a super projected out of a dictionary: a dictionary with supers is always a cell
routeWitness prog env d (RProj r path) =
  routeWitness prog env d r ++ flatMap superFieldW path
routeWitness prog env _ (RDict dpar) =
  if envHas dpar env then
    ["local.get $" ++ gname dpar]
  else
    gapLP prog ("wasm W5: forwarded dict '" ++ dpar ++ "' not in scope")
routeWitness prog env _ (RDictFwd dpar) =
  if envHas dpar env then
    ["local.get $" ++ gname dpar]
  else
    gapLP prog ("wasm W5: forwarded dict '" ++ dpar ++ "' not in scope")
-- RNone as a witness is the dictionary for an unconstrained type variable under a
-- `requires` (the element of `None : Option a`, the error of `Ok 1 : Result e Int`).
-- There is no value of that type for a method to take, so no value-position
-- dispatch goes through it: the constructor-only and Display/Eq/Ord shapes never
-- call it.  It is the no-op i31 (dict tag 0), mirroring llvm_emit's
-- `dictWordOfRoute _ _ RNone = "0"`.
routeWitness _ _ _ RNone = ["i32.const 0", "ref.i31"]
-- S-1: RLocal's own dicts are the call's leading dict ARGS (pushed by emitMethodRef's
-- RLocal arm via emitDictRef), not a dict WITNESS for this route — so as a witness it
-- stays the no-op i31 (dict tag 0), mirroring llvm_emit's
-- `dictWordOfRoute (RLocal _ _) = "0"`.  RScalar (scalar-tag) likewise.
routeWitness _ _ _ (RLocal _ _) = ["i32.const 0", "ref.i31"]
routeWitness _ _ _ (RScalar _) = ["i32.const 0", "ref.i31"]

superFieldW : Int -> List String
superFieldW i = [
  "ref.cast (ref $dictcell)",
  "struct.get $dictcell 1",
  "i32.const " ++ intToString i,
  "array.get $dictarr",
  "ref.as_non_null",
]

-- a constrained-function occurrence applied to `args`: prepend the materialized
-- dict witnesses (one per `=>` constraint, in route order) to the args, then call
-- the lifted $name (whose leading params are the $dict_* the dict-pass injected).
emitDictRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  List Route ->
  List CExpr ->
  CallMode ->
  CallEndW ->
  List String
emitDictRef prog env d name routes args mode end =
  if envHas name env then
    emitLocalDictRef prog env d name routes args end
  else if progFnMemberW prog name then
    -- P2 (over/under-application, #729): the direct `call` is only legal when the
    -- application is exact.  A point-free dict-passed fn keeps a TRAILING CLam, so its
    -- define value-arity is SHORT of the args a saturating call supplies: `clamp lo hi
    -- = min hi >> max lo` compiles to a 3-param define (dict, lo, hi) RETURNING a
    -- closure, yet `clamp 0 10 15` supplies three value args.  Mirror emitAppRef's CVar
    -- gate: any other application materializes the CDict as a closure VALUE and
    -- applies every arg through $__mdk_apply (whose over-application arm chains into
    -- the returned closure).
    if isExactCall mode then
      let dictWords = flatMap (routeWitness prog env d) routes
      let argInstrs = flatMap (a => emitRefExpr prog env d a) args
      dictWords
        ++ argInstrs
        ++ [callFnW prog end (gname name) (listLen routes + listLen args)]
    else
      emitIndirectApp prog env d (CDict name routes) args end
  else
    gapLP prog ("wasm W5: CDict over unknown function '" ++ name ++ "'")
      ++ endValueW end

-- A dictionary-abstracted LOCAL binding is a closure whose leading parameters are
-- its dictionaries: apply it to the dict witnesses, then the arguments.
emitLocalDictRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  List Route ->
  List CExpr ->
  CallEndW ->
  List String
emitLocalDictRef prog env d name routes args end =
  let dictWords = flatMap (routeWitness prog env d) routes
  let argInstrs = flatMap (a => emitRefExpr prog env d a) args
  emitVarRef prog env d name
    ++ dictWords
    ++ argInstrs
    ++ [
      "array.new_fixed $argarr " ++ intToString (listLen routes + listLen args),
      callFnW prog end "__mdk_apply" 2,
    ]

-- ── EMITTER-GAPS E23 (wasm peer): CMethod / CDict in VALUE position ───────────
-- A typeclass METHOD (`map negate xs`, `filter isEv xs`) or a `=>`-constrained NAMED
-- function (`filter myParity xs`) passed UNAPPLIED to a higher-order combinator lowers
-- to a bare CMethod/CDict in OPERAND position.  The emitRefExpr arms previously routed
-- these to emitMethodRef/emitDictRef with `[]` args → a TRUNCATED saturated dispatch
-- (`call $mdk_impl_*` / `call $fn`) carrying ONLY the dict words, no value args and no
-- closure capture → wasm stack underflow at validate (`not enough arguments on the
-- stack for call`).  (This is the wasm peer of the LLVM emitDictValue/emitMethodValue
-- fix — EMITTER-GAPS E23; distinct from #18/E18, the shadowed-local case that stays a
-- plain EVar.)
--
-- FIX: ETA-EXPAND the occurrence to a synthetic lambda `\a0..a(k-1) -> head a0..a(k-1)`
-- and lower it through emitClosure — the universal W4 closure path.  emitClosure (a)
-- captures the route's forwarded dict params (freeVarsExpr surfaces every given the
-- evidence names, `core_ir.givenNames`) into the closure $env, and (b) re-emits the SATURATED dispatch in the
-- lifted body via the CALL-position emitMethodRef/emitDictRef (correct: dicts ++ args ++
-- call).  The result is a `$clos` struct (code_ptr, arity, $env captures) with the exact
-- ABI W4 HOFs expect — the working lambda path IS the reference.

-- CMethod value: arity k = the method's declared USER arity; a nullary method (k <= 0)
-- is a plain value — keep the immediate saturated dispatch.
emitMethodValueRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  Route ->
  List Route ->
  List Route ->
  List String
emitMethodValueRef prog env d name iface siteArity route implRoutes methRoutes =
  let node =
    CMethod name (MethodEvidence iface siteArity route implRoutes methRoutes)
  let arity = methodValueArityW prog node
  if arity <= 0 then
    emitMethodRef
      prog
      env
      d
      name
      iface
      siteArity
      route
      implRoutes
      methRoutes
      []
      (callModeFor (definedArityW prog node) 0)
      CallValueW
  else
    let names = etaValNames arity
    let ps = map (n => PVar n (Loc "" 0 0 0 0) noBinderId) names
    let body = stampedAppW prog node (map (n => CVar n AGlobal) names)
    emitClosure prog env d ps body

-- the method's USER arity for an eta-value closure: the occurrence's defined arity
-- (#410: an RLocal route forwards to a STANDALONE, so the closure exposes that
-- standalone's value arity, less the dictionaries the route supplies; an RKey route
-- the selected entry's parameters).  A route with no static arity (a runtime
-- dictionary) exposes the occurrence's declared arity.
methodValueArityW : Prog -> CExpr -> Int
methodValueArityW prog (node@(CMethod _ (MethodEvidence _ siteArity _ _ _))) =
  match definedArityW prog node
    Some n => maxI 0 n
    None => siteArity
methodValueArityW _ _ = 0

-- CDict value: value arity v = the define's parameters − route count.  A nullary
-- value arity (the constrained fn takes no value args) degenerates to the saturated
-- dict call.
emitDictValueRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> String -> List Route -> List String
emitDictValueRef prog env d name routes =
  if envHas name env then
    emitLocalDictRef prog env d name routes [] CallValueW
  else if progFnMemberW prog name then
    let valArity = optionOr 0 (definedArityW prog (CDict name routes))
    if valArity <= 0 then
      emitDictRef prog env d name routes [] CallExact CallValueW
    else
      let names = etaValNames valArity
      let ps = map (n => PVar n (Loc "" 0 0 0 0) noBinderId) names
      let body =
        stampedAppW prog (CDict name routes) (map (n => CVar n AGlobal) names)
      emitClosure prog env d ps body
  else
    gapLP prog ("wasm E23: CDict value over unknown function '" ++ name ++ "'")

-- fresh eta param names `$hov0..$hov(n-1)` (`$`-prefixed, so no source name can
-- collide); each lambda owns its own param scope so fixed names never collide.
etaValNames : Int -> List String
etaValNames n = map (i => "$hov" ++ intToString i) (rangeList 0 n)

-- [hd] applied to [args], stamped with the mode `core_ir_lower.stampCallModes` would
-- give it: the application an eta-value closure's body makes.  It is that body's
-- tail call, so it is flagged as one unless it is a partial application.
stampedAppW : Prog -> CExpr -> List CExpr -> CExpr
stampedAppW prog hd args =
  let mode = callModeFor (definedArityW prog hd) (listLen args)
  CApp hd args (CallSite mode (not (isPartialMode mode)))

-- the stamped symbol tag of an entry of either kind
implEntrySymTagW : CImplEntry -> String
implEntrySymTagW (CImplEntry _ _ _ (CImplTagged _ _ _ (ImplSym tag _ _) _ _ _)) =
  tag
implEntrySymTagW (CImplEntry _ _ _ (CImplDefault _ _ _ (ImplSym tag _ _) _ _ _)) =
  tag

-- The function symbol of one exact entry, composed from its stamp
-- (`core_ir_lower.stampImplSymbols`): a supplied method's `mdk_impl_<symTag>_<method>`,
-- or an inherited default's per-instance `mdk_default_<iface>_<method>_<key>`.
implEntrySymW : String -> CImplEntry -> String
implEntrySymW method (CImplEntry _ _ _ (CImplTagged _ _ _ (ImplSym tag _ _) _ _ _)) =
  implFnSymOfTag tag method
implEntrySymW method (CImplEntry _ _ _ (CImplDefault _ _ _ (ImplSym _ ifaceTag keyTag) _ _ _)) =
  "mdk_default_\{ifaceTag}_\{gname method}_\{keyTag}"

-- build the symbol from an entry's stamped symbol tag
implFnSymOfTag : String -> String -> String
implFnSymOfTag symTag method = "mdk_impl_\{symTag}_\{gname method}"

-- the head tycon of the impl whose canonical key is [key] (mirror of llvm_emit's
-- headTagForKey) — the group's dispatch/self/Float tag, distinct from its symbol tag.
headTagForKeyW : String -> String -> List CImplEntry -> String
headTagForKeyW method key entries = match firstEntryForKeyW method key entries
  Some ent => implEntryTagW ent
  None => ""

firstEntryForKeyW : String -> String -> List CImplEntry -> Option CImplEntry
firstEntryForKeyW _ _ [] = None
firstEntryForKeyW method key (ent :: rest)
  | implEntryMethodW ent == method && implEntryKeyW ent == key = Some ent
  | otherwise = firstEntryForKeyW method key rest

-- ── §W5 impl-function emission ───────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Coalesce the CImplEntry list (one entry per clause) by (method, symTag) into
-- per-impl clause groups, then emit each as a wasm function $mdk_impl_<tag>_<m>
-- via the SAME clause machinery top-level fns use (emitClausesRef).  Multi-clause
-- impls (`eq Red Red = …; eq _ _ = …`) coalesce into a fall-through chain.
emitImplFns : Prog -> List String
emitImplFns prog =
  flatMap (emitImplGroup prog) (implGroups prog (progImpls prog))

-- (method, tag, arity, clauses) per distinct impl key, in first-seen order.
-- (method, headTag, key, arity, clauses) per distinct canonical impl key.  #324:
-- headTag drives dispatch/self-recursion/Float-param decisions (mirror of llvm_emit's
-- ImplGroup `tag`), while [key] drives the SYMBOL (via the stamp) and clause selection
-- (mirror of `symTag`/`key`).  For a sole impl per head the two coincide in effect
-- (a sole impl's symbol tag is its head tag), so existing output is byte-identical.
data ImplG = ImplG String String String Int (List CClause) String

implGroups : Prog -> List CImplEntry -> List ImplG
implGroups prog entries =
  mapGatherGroups prog entries (distinctImplKeys entries)

-- map gatherImplGroup (an effectful fn — it reads the iface-arity table) over the keys.
mapGatherGroups : Prog -> List CImplEntry -> List (String, String) -> List ImplG
mapGatherGroups _ _ [] = []
mapGatherGroups prog entries (k :: rest) =
  let g = gatherImplGroup prog entries k
  g :: mapGatherGroups prog entries rest

-- the (method, canonical-key) groups present, first-seen order.  #324: key on the
-- CANONICAL KEY (field 2), not the head tycon — so two overlapping same-head impls
-- (`Default (Box a)` / `Default (Box Int)`, both head `Box`) form DISTINCT groups
-- and get distinct $mdk_impl_* functions, instead of collapsing into one.  For a sole
-- impl per head the key↔head map is 1:1, so the group set (and its emit order) is
-- unchanged from the old head-keyed form.
distinctImplKeys : List CImplEntry -> List (String, String)
distinctImplKeys entries = dedupPairs (flatMap implKeyOf entries) []

implKeyOf : CImplEntry -> List (String, String)
implKeyOf ent = [(implEntryMethodW ent, implEntryKeyW ent)]

-- dedup a (method, tag) key list, first-seen order (dedupKeep is String-only).  perf
-- #382: the old `containsPair p acc` was O(kept) per element ⇒ O(k²) — quadratic in
-- distinct impl keys, run once per program by `distinctImplKeys` and once per RDict site
-- by `methodImpls`.  An OrdMap seen-set makes membership O(log k); `acc` still carries
-- the reversed first-seen order (identical output), and `seen` is seeded from the initial
-- `acc` so the 2-arg contract is preserved for any caller.  `pairKey` joins on a SPACE:
-- the method (field 1) is always a bare identifier — space-free — so `m ++ " " ++ tag` is
-- injective (the first space delimits method from tag), i.e. two distinct pairs never
-- collide on a key.
dedupPairs : List (String, String) ->
  List (String, String) ->
  List (String, String)
dedupPairs pairs acc = dedupPairsGo pairs (seedPairSeen acc omEmpty) acc

pairKey : (String, String) -> String
pairKey (a, b) = "\{a} \{b}"

seedPairSeen : List (String, String) -> OrdMap Unit -> OrdMap Unit
seedPairSeen [] m = m
seedPairSeen (p :: rest) m = seedPairSeen rest (omInsert (pairKey p) () m)

dedupPairsGo : List (String, String) ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List (String, String) ->
  List (String, String)
dedupPairsGo [] _ acc = reverseL acc
dedupPairsGo (p :: rest) seen acc =
  let k = pairKey p
  if omHasKey k seen then
    dedupPairsGo rest seen acc
  else
    dedupPairsGo rest (omInsert k () seen) (p :: acc)

gatherImplGroup : Prog -> List CImplEntry -> (String, String) -> ImplG
gatherImplGroup prog entries (m, key) =
  let mEntries = methodEntriesW prog m
  let headTag = headTagForKeyW m key mEntries
  let clauses = flatMap (implClauseFor m key) mEntries
  -- the define takes exactly its clauses' parameters: a call site's mode was read
  -- against that same count, so nothing here may lengthen a clause
  let fnName = match firstEntryForKeyW m key mEntries
    Some ent => implEntrySymW m ent
    None => panic "wasm: impl group without an entry (internal error)"
  ImplG m headTag key (implGroupArity clauses) clauses fnName

-- the clauses of (method, key): the def-side grouping passes a canonical key, which
-- selects exactly one impl's clauses even when it shares a head with an overlapping
-- sibling (#324).
implClauseFor : String -> String -> CImplEntry -> List CClause
implClauseFor m tag ent =
  if implEntryMethodW ent == m && implEntryAnswersW tag ent then
    [CClause (implEntryPatsW ent) (implBodyExprW (implEntryBodyW ent))]
  else
    []

implBodyExprW : CImplBody -> CExpr
implBodyExprW (CImplTagged _ _ _ _ _ _ e) = e
implBodyExprW (CImplDefault _ _ _ _ _ _ e) = e

implEntryBodyW : CImplEntry -> CImplBody
implEntryBodyW (CImplEntry _ _ _ body) = body

implGroupArity : List CClause -> Int
implGroupArity ((CClause pats _) :: _) = listLen pats
implGroupArity [] = 0

emitImplGroup : Prog -> ImplG -> List String
emitImplGroup outer (ImplG method headTag key arity clauses fnName) =
  -- an impl method has no first-clause site of its own
  let prog = progWithOrigin "impl \{method} for \{key}" (progInFn outer)
  let params = synthParams arity
  -- Phase 2 B-dispatch (TRMC-DESIGN §"Phase 2"): a DISPATCHED self-recursive cons/ctor-tail
  -- impl (the `List map`: self-call is a `CMethod method (RKey tag)`) is emitted as a
  -- destination-passing loop — the WasmGC peer of llvm_emit's trmcImplTry.  Eligibility +
  -- the safety-critical `mentionsSelfMethod` disqualification are in wTrmcImplTry; an
  -- ineligible impl (non-tail self, dict-passed, no cons-tail) returns None → ordinary body.
  match wTrmcImplTry prog method key fnName arity clauses
    Some tmcDef => tmcDef
    None =>
      let w7Outer = w7ScopeOpen (progEmit prog)
      let bodyLines = emitClausesImpl prog fnName params arity clauses
      let allLocals = clauseLocals clauses
      let extraLocals = filterList (notIn params) (dedupKeep allLocals)
      let scratch = scratchLocals (clausesMaxDepth clauses)
      let _ = defineFnW prog fnName (FuncParams arity)
      let sig =
        "  (func $\{fnName}\{joinWith "" (map paramDeclRef params)} (result (ref eq))"
      let localDecls = map localDeclRef (extraLocals ++ scratch)
      let w7Decls =
        w7LocalDecls
          (w7ScopeClose (progEmit prog) w7Outer)
          (clausesMaxDepth clauses)
      [sig]
        ++ map ("  " ++ _) (localDecls ++ w7Decls)
        ++ indent bodyLines
        ++ ["  )"]

-- impl bodies use the SAME clause emission as top-level fns; the synthetic fn
-- "name" (used only for the internal clause-block labels) is the impl symbol.
emitClausesImpl : Prog ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  Int ->
  List CClause ->
  List String
emitClausesImpl prog fnName params arity clauses =
  emitClausesRef prog fnName params arity clauses

-- One dispatch arm: the entry's symbol tag (memo naming), the function the arm
-- calls, and the entry itself, whose canonical key its dictionary carries.
data ImplArmW = ImplArmW String String CImplEntry

armSymTagW : ImplArmW -> String
armSymTagW (ImplArmW symTag _ _) = symTag

armFnSymW : ImplArmW -> String
armFnSymW (ImplArmW _ fnSym _) = fnSym

armEntryW : ImplArmW -> CImplEntry
armEntryW (ImplArmW _ _ ent) = ent

armKeyW : ImplArmW -> String
armKeyW arm = implEntryKeyW (armEntryW arm)

-- The candidate implementations of the interface a site resolved to ([iface]; `""`
-- narrows nothing), one arm per implementation, first-seen order.
methodImpls : Prog -> String -> String -> List ImplArmW
methodImpls prog method iface =
  let mEntries = methodEntriesW prog method
  dedupArmsW
    (map
      (methodImplArm method)
      (filterList
        (ent => implEntryMethodW ent == method)
        (narrowByIfaceW iface mEntries)))
    omEmpty

methodImplArm : String -> CImplEntry -> ImplArmW
methodImplArm method ent =
  ImplArmW (implEntrySymTagW ent) (implEntrySymW method ent) ent

-- one arm per called function, first-seen order
dedupArmsW : List ImplArmW -> OrdMap Unit -> List ImplArmW
dedupArmsW [] _ = []
dedupArmsW (arm :: rest) seen =
  if omHasKey (armFnSymW arm) seen then
    dedupArmsW rest seen
  else
    arm :: dedupArmsW rest (omInsert (armFnSymW arm) () seen)

-- #1852, the wasm peer of llvm_emit's `narrowImplsByArity`.  Two unrelated interfaces
-- declaring the same-spelled method at DIFFERENT arity on one receiver head put two
-- candidates of different declared arity under one bare-name dispatcher; keep only the
-- ones whose interface declaration arity matches the occurrence's carried scalar.
-- Each arm carries its entry, so declaration identity is recovered from that entry
-- rather than from the supplied argument count.  No match stays empty: restoring the whole list would make the
-- bare-name collision authoritative again.
narrowImplsByArityW : List ImplArmW -> Int -> List ImplArmW
narrowImplsByArityW impls siteArity =
  filterList (arm => implEntryDeclaredArity (armEntryW arm) == siteArity) impls

-- the entry of the occurrence's interface [iface] for (method, tag) at the site's
-- arity (mirror of llvm_emit's implForSite): a supplied method, or an inherited
-- default's per-instance body.
implForWSite : Prog -> String -> String -> String -> Int -> Option CImplEntry
implForWSite prog method iface tag siteArity =
  findByKeyArityW
    prog
    method
    tag
    siteArity
    (narrowByIfaceW iface (methodEntriesW prog method))

findByKeyArityW : Prog ->
  String ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  List CImplEntry ->
  Option CImplEntry
findByKeyArityW _ _ _ _ [] = None
findByKeyArityW prog method tag siteArity (entry :: rest) =
  if implEntryAnswersW tag entry
    && implEntryDeclaredArity entry == siteArity then
    Some entry
  else
    findByKeyArityW prog method tag siteArity rest

-- `hashName` (djb2, seed 5381) lives in `types.private_mangle`, shared verbatim
-- with the LLVM emitter so the dict-witness tag matches across backends + the
-- route-key dispatch agrees.

-- `dictTag` (the i31-safe 30-bit mask of `hashName`) and its `posMod` helper moved
-- to `types.private_mangle`, beside `hashName`, in #377/#348: the emit-time
-- collision guard (`core_validate.validateDictTags`) has to check THIS tag space
-- with the SAME expression this emitter mints, and a second copy of the mask is a
-- copy that can drift.  Imported at the top of this file; the emitted `i32.const`s
-- are unchanged.
--
-- ⚠️ The comment that used to stand here called a 30-bit tag collision
-- "astronomically unlikely for the small impl-tag alphabet" and the 64-bit LLVM
-- scheme's the "same theoretical collision shape".  Both halves were wrong:
-- colliding pre-images are CONSTRUCTIBLE in the full i64 (`hashName "Mzone" ==
-- hashName "NYone"`), the mechanism is the radix-33 polynomial versus a 74-code-
-- point alphabet rather than anything about how many tags a program has, and it
-- was a live silent-wrong-dispatch S0 on both backends until the guard landed.
-- See `private_mangle.hashName`'s note.

-- Common expression traversal; physical mode chooses i64 or (ref eq) values.
-- `d` is the current match/switch nesting DEPTH: a CDecision/CTSwitch stashes a
-- value into the scratch local `$__rf<d>` and recurses at d+1, so simultaneously-
-- live stash locals never collide.  The function header declares `$__rf0..` up to
-- the body's max depth (`maxRefDepth`).  No mutable counter needed → re-derivable.

emitRefExpr : Prog -> Env -> Int -> CExpr -> List String
emitRefExpr prog env d expr = valueLines (emitValueW prog env d expr)

refOnlyValueW : Prog -> CExpr -> (Unit -> List String) -> WasmValue
refOnlyValueW prog expr body =
  if rawProgramW prog then
    programValueW
      prog
      (gapLP prog ("scalar-mode: unsupported Core IR node " ++ ctag expr))
  else
    WasmValue WBoxEq (body ())

emitValueW : Prog -> Env -> Int -> CExpr -> WasmValue
emitValueW prog env d (CLit l) =
  if rawProgramW prog then
    let (lines, ty) = emitLitI32 (progEmit prog) l
    WasmValue (rawReprW ty) lines
  else
    WasmValue WBoxEq (emitLitRef prog l)
emitValueW prog env d (CVar x _) = programValueW prog (emitVarRef prog env d x)
emitValueW prog env d (CBinPrim op l r tag loc) =
  let code =
    if rawProgramW prog then
      emitIntBinRef prog env d op l r tag (sitePackedW (progEmit prog) loc)
    else
      emitBinRef prog env d op l r tag (sitePackedW (progEmit prog) loc)
  WasmValue (if rawProgramW prog then rawReprW (binOpTy op) else WBoxEq) code
emitValueW prog env d (CUnOp op x) =
  programValueW prog (emitUnRef prog env d op x)
emitValueW prog env d (CIf c t f) =
  let ci = emitRefExpr prog env d c ++ conditionW prog
  let tv = emitValueW prog env d t
  let fv = emitValueW prog env d f
  WasmValue
    (valueRepr tv)
    (ci
      ++ ["if (result " ++ physicalType (programReprW prog) ++ ")"]
      ++ indent (valueLines tv)
      ++ ["else"]
      ++ indent (valueLines fv)
      ++ ["end"])
emitValueW prog env d (CLet recF pat e1 e2) =
  let (prefix, env2) = emitLetBindingW prog env d recF pat e1
  prependValueW prefix (emitValueW prog env2 d e2)
emitValueW prog env d (CLetGroup binds body) = refOnlyValueW prog (CLetGroup
  binds
  body) (() =>
  emitLetGroupWith prog env d (env2 b => emitRefExpr prog env2 d b) binds body)
emitValueW prog env d (CBlock stmts) = emitBlockRef prog env d stmts
emitValueW prog env d (app@(CApp _ _ _)) =
  programValueW prog (emitAppRef prog env d app)
emitValueW prog env d (node@(CDecision scrut arms tree)) =
  refOnlyValueW prog node (() => emitDecisionRef prog env d scrut arms tree)
emitValueW prog env d (node@(CLam pats body)) =
  refOnlyValueW prog node (() => emitClosure prog env d pats body)
emitValueW prog env d (node@(CMethod name (MethodEvidence iface arity route implRoutes methRoutes))) = refOnlyValueW
  prog
  node
  (() =>
    emitMethodValueRef prog env d name iface arity route implRoutes methRoutes)
emitValueW prog env d (node@(CDict name routes)) =
  refOnlyValueW prog node (() => emitDictValueRef prog env d name routes)
emitValueW prog env d (node@(CTuple es)) =
  refOnlyValueW prog node (() => emitTupleRef prog env d es)
emitValueW prog env d (node@(CList es)) =
  refOnlyValueW prog node (() => emitListRef prog env d es)
emitValueW prog env d (node@(CRangeList lo hi incl)) =
  refOnlyValueW prog node (() => emitRangeListRef prog env d lo hi incl)
emitValueW prog env d (node@(CArray es)) =
  refOnlyValueW prog node (() => emitArrayCreateRef prog env d es)
emitValueW prog env d (node@(CRangeArray lo hi incl)) =
  refOnlyValueW prog node (() => emitRangeArrayRef prog env d lo hi incl)
emitValueW prog env d (node@(CIndex a i)) =
  refOnlyValueW prog node (() => emitIndexRef prog env d a i)
emitValueW prog env d (node@(CSlice a lo hi incl)) =
  refOnlyValueW prog node (() => emitSliceRef prog env d a lo hi incl)
emitValueW prog env d (node@(CRecord name fields)) =
  refOnlyValueW prog node (() => emitRecordRef prog env d name fields)
emitValueW prog env d (node@(CFieldAccess ex label recName ord)) = refOnlyValueW
  prog
  node
  (() => emitFieldAccessRef prog env d ex label recName ord)
emitValueW prog env d (node@(CRecordUpdate recName base fields)) = refOnlyValueW
  prog
  node
  (() => emitRecordUpdateRef prog env d recName base fields)
emitValueW prog env d (node@(CVariantUpdate con base fields)) = refOnlyValueW
  prog
  node
  (() => emitVariantUpdateRef prog env d con base fields)
emitValueW prog env d other =
  programValueW
    prog
    (gapLP prog (if rawProgramW prog then
      "scalar-mode: unsupported Core IR node " ++ ctag other
    else
      "ref-mode: unsupported Core IR node \{ctag other} [in \{progBinding prog}]"))

-- a scalar literal → an i31 immediate.  Int: ref.i31 of the value.  Bool: 1/0.
-- Unit: i31 0 (a placeholder immediate; Unit is never inspected in this slice).
emitLitRef : Prog -> Lit -> List String
emitLitRef prog (LInt n) =
  -- layer-17 §2.1: in-range Ints stay i31 immediates (byte-identical to before);
  -- literals outside ±2^30 box into $boxint via the i64 seam so they don't truncate.
  if n >= 0 - 1073741824 && n < 1073741824 then
    ["i32.const " ++ intToString n, "ref.i31"]
  else
    ["i64.const " ++ intToString n, boxIntW prog]
emitLitRef _ (LBool b) = [if b then "i32.const 1" else "i32.const 0", "ref.i31"]
emitLitRef _ LUnit = ["i32.const 0", "ref.i31"]
-- W8b: a Float literal in ref-mode boxes the double into a `(struct $float (f64))`.
-- The f64.const text is `floatToString f` — the SAME rendering (shortest-round-trip
-- since #57, NOT `%.12g`) that the LLVM oracle bakes into its IR const, so clang and
-- wasm-tools parse the identical double (verified
-- byte-identical via i64.reinterpret_f64).  `$float` is always in the rec group.  Emitted
-- as TWO FLAT instructions (not the folded `struct.new $float (f64.const …)`) so it
-- composes with the surrounding flat instruction stream (a folded form mid-stream breaks
-- wasm-tools' stack tracking).
emitLitRef _ (LFloat f) = ["f64.const " ++ floatToString f, "struct.new $float"]
-- a `U64` literal boxes its 64 bits, written in hex so a value past 2^63 needs no
-- signed spelling.
emitLitRef _ (LU64 hi lo) =
  ["i64.const 0x" ++ u64HalvesHex hi lo, "struct.new $u64"]
-- an `I64` literal's halves are its two's complement pattern, spelled the same way.
emitLitRef _ (LI64 hi lo) =
  ["i64.const 0x" ++ u64HalvesHex hi lo, "struct.new $i64"]
-- W6: a String literal is a §3.3 `$str` boxed value.  Its UTF-8 bytes go in a
-- passive data segment (the §11-preferred non-const-array init), read at run time by
-- `array.new_data`; the cached cp_count is computed at emit time (UTF-8 codepoint
-- count == source Char count).  Stack: push cp_count (i32), build the byte array via
-- array.new_data, then struct.new $str.
emitLitRef prog (LString s) =
  let bytes = strBytesW s
  let cpc = stringLength s
  let n = listLen bytes
  let seg = freshStrSeg prog bytes
  [
    "i32.const " ++ intToString cpc,
    "i32.const 0",
    "i32.const " ++ intToString n,
    "array.new_data $u8arr " ++ strSegRefW prog seg,
    "struct.new $str",
  ]
-- W6: a Char literal is its Unicode codepoint as an i31 immediate (matching the
-- native rep: a Char is a tagged codepoint, not a boxed string).  `LChar` carries a
-- one-char String, so take the codepoint of its sole char (peer to llvm_emit).
emitLitRef _ (LChar c) = [
  "i32.const " ++ intToString (charCode (arrayGetUnsafe 0 (stringToChars c))),
  "ref.i31",
]

-- ── W6 UTF-8 codec (compiler-local; mirrors llvm_emit.strBytes/utf8Bytes — the
-- no-stdlib rule forbids importing `string`, so the codec is duplicated here). ──
-- the raw UTF-8 bytes of a string, in order.
strBytesW : String -> List Int
strBytesW s = strBytesGoW (stringToChars s) 0

strBytesGoW : Array Char -> Int -> List Int
strBytesGoW cs i =
  if i >= arrayLength cs then
    []
  else
    utf8BytesW (charCode (arrayGetUnsafe i cs)) ++ strBytesGoW cs (i + 1)

-- encode one Unicode codepoint to its UTF-8 bytes (0..255).  Bit fields are disjoint,
-- so `or` is `+` and the masks are `% 64`; no bitwise primitive needed.
utf8BytesW : Int -> List Int
utf8BytesW cp =
  if cp < 128 then
    [cp]
  else if cp < 2048 then
    [192 + cp / 64, 128 + cp % 64]
  else if cp < 65536 then
    [224 + cp / 4096, 128 + cp / 64 % 64, 128 + cp % 64]
  else
    [
      240 + cp / 262144,
      128 + cp / 4096 % 64,
      128 + cp / 64 % 64,
      128 + cp % 64,
    ]

-- escape a byte list for a WAT data-string `"…"`: every byte as `\HH` (lowercase
-- hex per wasm-tools convention; uppercase also parses, lowercase keeps the emitted
-- text stable vs a `wasm-tools print` round-trip).
escWatBytes : List Int -> String
escWatBytes [] = ""
escWatBytes (b :: rest) = "\\\{hex2W b}\{escWatBytes rest}"

hex2W : Int -> String
hex2W b = hexDigitW (b / 16) ++ hexDigitW (b % 16)

hexDigitW : Int -> String
hexDigitW d =
  if d < 10 then
    intToString d
  else if d == 10 then
    "a"
  else if d == 11 then
    "b"
  else if d == 12 then
    "c"
  else if d == 13 then
    "d"
  else if d == 14 then
    "e"
  else
    "f"

-- a variable: local/global → get (already (ref eq)); a nullary ctor → its i31 tag;
-- a top-level fn used as a VALUE → build its closure wrapper struct (code =
-- $mdk_w_<f>, arity = its param count, env = []) so it can flow through a (ref eq)
-- slot / be applied indirectly.
-- a fall-through sentinel var → its lowering.  `__ft__<label>` (produced by
-- labelFallthrough in a clause body) → `br <label>`, exiting the clause block to fall
-- through to the next clause.  The bare `__fallthrough__` (NOT rewritten — appears only
-- outside a clause block, e.g. a value-binding body or a context the typechecker proved
-- exhaustive) → a trap stub `unreachable` (the WasmGC peer of llvm_emit's `call void
-- @mdk_nonexhaustive_match()`, EMITTER-GAPS.md E3; unlike that call the bare wasm trap
-- carries no coded message — a clause chain's own terminus does, at
-- emitClauseChainGo's empty-list arm).  PURE functions of the name — no mutable "current
-- label" ref, which this lazily-assembled emitter cannot thread reliably (the strings
-- are forced at final assembly, long after any setRef).
isFtSentinel : String -> Bool
isFtSentinel x = x == "__fallthrough__" || startsWith ftPrefix x

ftSentinelInstrs : String -> List String
ftSentinelInstrs x =
  if startsWith ftPrefix x then
    ["br " ++ dropPrefix x ftPrefix]
  else
    ["unreachable"]

emitFtSentinel : String -> Option (List String)
emitFtSentinel x = if isFtSentinel x then Some (ftSentinelInstrs x) else None

dropPrefix : String -> String -> String
dropPrefix s p = stringSlice (stringLength p) (stringLength s) s

-- a variable: local/global → get (already (ref eq)); a nullary ctor → its i31 tag;
emitVarRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> String -> List String
emitVarRef prog env d x =
  if rawProgramW prog then
    if envHas x env then
      ["local.get " ++ localTargetW prog env x]
    else if omHasKey x (indexValNamesW (progIndex prog)) then
      [globalW prog "global.get" ("$" ++ gname x)]
    else if progFnMemberW prog x then
      [callFnW prog CallValueW (gname x) 0]
    else if isUnprovidedOn
      WasmBackend
      (optionOr "" (externRuntimeKey (progEmit prog).externFacts x)) then
      unprovidedExternW
        (progEmit prog)
        (optionOr "" (externRuntimeKey (progEmit prog).externFacts x))
    else
      fst
        (gapUnboundLTy
          (progEmit prog)
          ("unbound variable '"
            ++ externDisplayW (progEmit prog) x
            ++ "' (scalar mode: not a local, global value, or known function)"))
  else
    emitVarRefBoxed prog env d x

emitVarRefBoxed : Prog -> Env -> Int -> String -> List String
emitVarRefBoxed prog env d x = match emitFtSentinel x
  Some instrs => instrs
  None => emitVarRefPlain prog env d x

emitVarRefPlain : Prog -> Env -> Int -> String -> List String
emitVarRefPlain prog env d x =
  if envHas x env then
    ["local.get $" ++ gname x]
  else if progValMemberW prog x then
    -- #561 PR-B: a LAZY value global (dispatch-reaching / cyclic) is forced on first use —
    -- `call $force_<x>` memoises into $<x> and black-holes a re-entrant force into
    -- E-CYCLIC-VALUE.  A LOCAL of the same name still shadows (env checked first, above).
    -- The result is a non-null (ref eq), same as the eager `global.get; ref.as_non_null`.
    -- #664: a single memo membership check (was two linear `contains … (progValNames prog)`
    -- scans on this hot path); the lazy/eager choice nests under it, byte-identical.

    if isLazyGlobalW prog x then
      [callFnW prog CallValueW ("force_" ++ gname x) 0]
    else
      [globalW prog "global.get" ("$" ++ gname x), "ref.as_non_null"]
  else if x == "True" then
    -- the Bool constructors used as VALUES (e.g. an `eq` impl body `… = True`) are
    -- i31 immediates 1/0 — the same rep as `emitLitRef (LBool _)`, so `if` reads them
    -- via `i31.get_u` uniformly.  (Surface `True`/`False` literals desugar to CLit;
    -- these reach the emitter only as bare ctor occurrences, e.g. from impl bodies.)
    ["i32.const 1", "ref.i31"]
  else if x == "False" then
    ["i32.const 0", "ref.i31"]
  else if x == "otherwise" then
    ["i32.const 1", "ref.i31"]
  else if hasFamilyW prog x "constant"
    && runtimeNameW prog x == "charMinBound" then
    -- W9: builtin Char bounds fit in an i31 → emit directly.  These are the RAW
    -- codepoints (0 / 0x10FFFF), because an i31 payload is UNTAGGED — the same rep as
    -- `emitLitRef (LChar _)` and the `True`/`False` arms above, and what `charCode`
    -- (an identity in ref mode) and every `i31.get_u` pattern test read back.
    -- ⚠️ llvm_emit's peer constants are 1 / 2228223 and are NOT wrong there — native's
    -- word is TAGGED (`2·cp+1`).  Do NOT copy that table here: pasting the tagged words
    -- into an untagged i31 leaks the tag out as a value (#373 — `charCode charMaxBound`
    -- printed 2228223, and range checks against the bounds were silently wrong).
    ["i32.const 0", "ref.i31"]
  else if hasFamilyW prog x "constant"
    && runtimeNameW prog x == "charMaxBound" then
    ["i32.const 1114111", "ref.i31"]
  else if hasFamilyW prog x "constant" && runtimeNameW prog x == "pi" then
    -- W8b: the Float math constants pi/e are boxed (struct $float) — the SAME decimal
    -- text the LLVM oracle boxes (3.141592653589793 / 2.718281828459045).
    ["f64.const 3.141592653589793", "struct.new $float"]
  else if hasFamilyW prog x "constant" && runtimeNameW prog x == "e" then
    ["f64.const 2.718281828459045", "struct.new $float"]
  else if hasFamilyW prog x "constant"
    && runtimeNameW prog x == "intMaxBound" then
    -- P1: builtin Int bounds.  These must not be a bare `unreachable` trap-stub, on the
    -- STALE grounds that a 64-bit bound "overflows i31" and so has no
    -- wasm rep: layer-17 §2.1 gave ref-mode the `$boxint` i64 box, and every int
    -- binop already round-trips through `$mdk_box_int`/`$mdk_unbox_int` (both always in
    -- scope via ioRuntimeLines).  So the bound is representable, and a stub here makes
    -- `main = intMaxBound` ASSEMBLE and VALIDATE, then trap
    -- `unreachable` at instantiate.
    --
    -- The VALUES are the language's, not the machine's.  Medaka's Int is the NATIVE
    -- rep's 63-bit tagged word, so `intMaxBound` = 2^62-1 and `intMinBound` = -2^62 —
    -- llvm_emit emits the TAGGED words (9223372036854775807 / -9223372036854775807,
    -- as literal strings: `n*2+1` would overflow the self-host's own 63-bit Int), whose
    -- untagged values are these.  Ref-mode is untagged, so it emits the values directly
    -- — again as literal STRINGS, for exactly the same self-host-overflow reason (they
    -- are 2^62-1 / -2^62, at the boundary of the Int the compiler itself computes in).
    ["i64.const 4611686018427387903", boxIntW prog]
  else if hasFamilyW prog x "constant"
    && runtimeNameW prog x == "intMinBound" then
    ["i64.const -4611686018427387904", boxIntW prog]
  else if hasFamilyW prog x "fallthrough" then
    ftSentinelInstrs (runtimeNameW prog x)
  else if isCtor prog x then
    if ctorArity prog x == 0 then
      emitCtorConstruct prog env d x []
    else
      emitCtorEtaClosure prog x
  else if progFnMemberW prog x then
    let _ = noteFuncRef prog ("$mdk_w_" ++ x)
    -- S-4: captureless by construction (a top-level fn's wrapper closes over nothing)
    -- ⇒ one hoisted module global, not a fresh `$clos` on every evaluation of `x`.
    wConstClos prog ("$mdk_w_" ++ x) (fnParamCountW prog x)
  else if canonFn prog x /= x then
    -- W9: a bare prelude reference synthesized post-mangle (string-interp / `/=`) →
    -- resolve to its `core__`-mangled def and emit the closure wrapper for it.
    emitVarRef prog env d (canonFn prog x)
  else if isWasmEtaExtern (progEmit prog) (runtimeNameW prog x) then
    -- W9: a str/leaf extern referenced as a VALUE (point-free / passed as an arg) —
    -- build an eta closure wrapping a lifted `$mdk_ext_<name>` that calls the extern
    -- (peer of the LLVM emitExternEtaClosure).  env = [] (externs capture nothing).
    emitExternEtaClosure prog x
  else if isFfiExternW prog x then
    emitFfiEtaW prog x
  else if isUnprovidedOn WasmBackend (runtimeNameW prog x) then
    unprovidedExternW (progEmit prog) (runtimeNameW prog x)
  else
    gapUnboundLP
      prog
      "unbound variable '\{x}' (not a local, global value, constructor, or known function) [in \{progBinding prog}]"

-- W9: lift `$mdk_ext_<name>` (a $codety) that unpacks its $args into synthetic CVar
-- locals and emits the extern call, then build the closure struct at the use site.
emitExternEtaClosure : Prog -> String -> List String
emitExternEtaClosure prog name =
  let arity = match omLookup name (progEmit prog).externFacts
    Some fact => match fact.callableShape
      Some shape => shape.loweredCoreArity
      None => panic ("internal error: missing-extern-abi: " ++ name)
    None => panic ("internal error: missing-extern-requirement: " ++ name)
  let lamName = "$mdk_ext_" ++ injectiveIdent name
  let _ = noteFuncRef prog lamName
  let _ =
    addLiftedNamed
      prog
      lamName
      codeShapeW
      (emitExternEtaDefine prog lamName name arity)
  -- S-4: an extern eta captures nothing (the comment above says so) ⇒ hoisted global.
  wConstClos prog lamName arity

-- The depth-0 `$__aex*`/`$__raarr*` array-intrinsic scratch locals (the array-extern
-- rows of w7LocalKinds at depth 0) that an ARRAY-extern eta (func …)
-- must declare to host emitArrayExternRef's loop counter / size / result $arr / list
-- cursor / closure-init-value cells / i64 reinterpret accumulator.
arrayEtaScratchLocals : List String
arrayEtaScratchLocals = [
  "(local $__aexi0 i32)",
  "(local $__aexn0 i32)",
  "(local $__aexarr0 (ref null $arr))",
  "(local $__aexlst0 (ref eq))",
  "(local $__aexf0 (ref eq))",
  "(local $__aexv0 (ref eq))",
  "(local $__aexbits0 i64)",
  "(local $__raarr0 (ref null $arr))",
]

emitExternEtaDefine : Prog -> String -> String -> Int -> List String
emitExternEtaDefine prog lamName name arity =
  let params = synthParams arity
  let argPrologue = flatMap argLoadAt (zipIdx params 0)
  let argVars = map (p => CVar p AGlobal) params
  -- An ARRAY extern referenced point-free (e.g. `arrayFromList` passed to the byteparser
  -- parse path) must route to emitArrayExternRef — mirroring the DIRECT-call arm at
  -- emitAppRef (a `WasmArray` family → emitArrayExternRef).  Without this it fell to
  -- emitLeafExternRef → "unsupported leaf extern".  The array externs use the depth-0
  -- `$__aex*`/`$__raarr*` scratch locals (loop counter, size, result $arr, list cursor,
  -- closure/init/value cells, i64 reinterpret accumulator), which the synthesized eta
  -- (func …) must declare itself (its localLines otherwise only cover the param locals).
  -- the eta declares its own fixed scratch set (arrayEtaScratchLocals), so its body's
  -- W7 references must not land in the function whose codegen reached it.
  let w7Outer = w7ScopeOpen (progEmit prog)
  let key = runtimeNameW prog name
  let family = externFamilyW (progEmit prog) key
  let call = match family
    Some WasmStr =>
      emitStrExternRef prog (envExtendUnstamped params envEmpty) 0 key argVars
    Some WasmArray =>
      emitArrayExternRef prog (envExtendUnstamped params envEmpty) 0 key argVars
    Some WasmByteBlock =>
      emitByteBlockExternRef
        prog
        (envExtendUnstamped params envEmpty)
        0
        key
        argVars
    _ =>
      emitLeafExternRef prog (envExtendUnstamped params envEmpty) 0 key argVars
  let _ = w7ScopeClose (progEmit prog) w7Outer
  let arrayScratch = match family
    Some WasmArray => arrayEtaScratchLocals
    _ => []
  let localLines = map (l => localDeclRef l) params ++ arrayScratch
  [
      "  (func "
        ++ lamName
        ++ " (type $codety) (param $self (ref eq)) (param $args (ref $argarr)) (result (ref eq))",
    ]
    ++ map ("  " ++ _) localLines
    ++ indent (argPrologue ++ call ++ ["return"])
    ++ ["  )"]

-- W9b: a bare/partial ADT constructor of arity > 0 used as a VALUE (`map PVar xs`)
-- — eta-wrap it into a captureless closure whose lifted code function `$mdk_wctor_
-- <Ctor>` unpacks the argarr and allocates the ctor cell.  Peer to llvm_emit's
-- emitCtorEtaClosure: an arity-0 ctor stays the immediate i31 (emitCtorConstruct
-- … []), but an arity-N ctor in value position is a FUNCTION and must be a closure,
-- not a malformed partial struct.new (the pre-W9b bug: emitCtorConstruct unpacked 0
-- args at an N-field struct → stray operands underflow at validate).
emitCtorEtaClosure : Prog -> String -> List String
emitCtorEtaClosure prog ctor =
  let arity = ctorArity prog ctor
  let lamName = "$mdk_wctor_" ++ gname ctor
  let _ = noteFuncRef prog lamName
  let _ =
    addLiftedNamed
      prog
      lamName
      codeShapeW
      (emitCtorEtaDefine prog lamName ctor arity)
  -- S-4: a ctor eta is captureless ⇒ hoisted global, not a per-reference `$clos`.
  wConstClos prog lamName arity

emitCtorEtaDefine : Prog -> String -> String -> Int -> List String
emitCtorEtaDefine prog lamName ctor arity =
  let params = synthParams arity
  let argPrologue = flatMap argLoadAt (zipIdx params 0)
  let argVars = map (p => CVar p AGlobal) params
  let body =
    emitCtorConstruct prog (envExtendUnstamped params envEmpty) 0 ctor argVars
  let localLines = map (l => localDeclRef l) params
  [
      "  (func "
        ++ lamName
        ++ " (type $codety) (param $self (ref eq)) (param $args (ref $argarr)) (result (ref eq))",
    ]
    ++ map ("  " ++ _) localLines
    ++ indent (argPrologue ++ body ++ ["return"])
    ++ ["  )"]

-- arithmetic / comparison: unbox both operands from i31 to i32, do the i32 op, then
-- re-box (arithmetic → i31 int; comparison → i31 0/1 bool).
emitBinRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  CExpr ->
  CExpr ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  List String
-- W13: `++` is runtime-dispatched (Core IR is type-erased, so we can't tell a
-- String `++` from a List `++` statically).  Both operands stay (ref eq) and
-- $mdk_append inspects the left operand's shape ($str → string concat; i31/$C_Cons
-- → list append), mirroring the LLVM backend's @mdk_append.
emitBinRef prog env d "++" l r _ _ =
  emitRefExpr prog env d l
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d r
    ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_append" 2]
-- W9: `::` is cons — build a $C_Cons cell {tag=0, head=l, tail=r} (same rep the W7
-- list-literal / Cons match machinery uses).  Reached from prelude fns that cons in
-- expression position (e.g. `gen () :: acc` in arbitraryList's where-go).
emitBinRef prog env d "::" l r _ _ =
  ["i32.const 0"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d l
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d r
    ++ ["struct.new $C_Cons"]
-- W8b: Float arithmetic / comparison.  Core IR is type-erased (CBinPrim carries no
-- LTy), so Float-ness is recovered STRUCTURALLY from the operands (a Float lit, pi/e,
-- a Float-returning extern, or a nested Float binop).  SHARED-FLOAT-RESIDUAL §6 C3:
-- the typecheck-stamped scalar-type tag (CBinPrim's 4th field, "Float" when the
-- operands ground to concrete Float) provides a direct route — additive over the
-- structural check, so an absent/non-Float tag falls back to today's path.
emitBinRef prog env d op l r tag site =
  let branch =
    selectWasmBin
      (progIndex prog).typeContext
      (emitDemandW (progEmit prog)).stringOps
      env
      op
      l
      r
      tag
  match branch
    "int-fixed" => emitIntBinRef prog env d op l r tag site
    "u64" => emitU64BinRef prog env d op l r site
    "i64" => emitI64BinRef prog env d op l r site
    "float" => emitFloatBinRef prog env d op l r
    "compare" => emitValueCmpRef prog env d op l r
    "compare-number" => emitValueCmpNumRef prog env d op l r
    _ =>
      if startsWith "value-" branch then
        emitRefExpr prog env d l
          ++ emitRefExpr prog env d r
          ++ [rtCallW prog ("mdk_value_" ++ valueArithName op) 2]
      else
        emitIntBinRef prog env d op l r tag site

-- layer-17 §2.1: Int arithmetic/comparison computes in i64 over the box/unbox
-- seam ($mdk_unbox_int / $mdk_box_int), so values outside ±2^30 no longer
-- truncate.  Arithmetic re-boxes the i64 result (a fixed-width site masks it
-- first, `fixedWidthWrapW`); comparisons yield an i31 Bool.  A `U32` above 2^30
-- boxes into `$boxint` like any other large Int.
emitIntBinRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  CExpr ->
  CExpr ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  List String
emitIntBinRef prog env d op l r tag site =
  let seamIn = if rawProgramW prog then [] else [unboxIntW prog]
  let seamOut = if rawProgramW prog then [] else [boxIntW prog]
  let li = emitRefExpr prog env d l ++ seamIn
  let ri = emitRefExpr prog env d r ++ seamIn
  -- N4 (#3377): an `Int` `+ - * /` runs its checked operator BEFORE the rebox, so an
  -- out-of-range result stops with E-INT-OVERFLOW rather than reaching
  -- `$mdk_box_int`'s sign-extend.  A fixed-width site keeps the plain i64 op and
  -- its wrap (`fixedWidthWrapW`): the fixed-width types wrap.
  let opInstrs =
    if intOpCanOverflow op && not (isTaggedFixedHead tag) then
      intChkCall prog op site
    else
      [wasmBinOp64 (progEmit prog) op]
        ++ (if rawProgramW prog
          && isTaggedFixedHead tag
          && intOpCanOverflow op then
          normInt64
        else
          [])
  -- B5: concrete-Int `/`/`%` get a divisor-zero guard emitting the coded trap line
  -- (peer of the native emitIntDivZeroChecked) before the division.
  if op == "/" || op == "%" then
    li
      ++ ri
      ++ emitDivZeroGuard
        (progEmit prog)
        op
        (if rawProgramW prog then "$__sdivr" else divrLocal prog d)
        site
      ++ opInstrs
      ++ fixedWidthWrapW tag op
      ++ seamOut
  else if isCmpOp op then
    li
      ++ ri
      ++ [wasmBinOp64 (progEmit prog) op]
      ++ (if rawProgramW prog then ["i64.extend_i32_u"] else ["ref.i31"])
  else
    li ++ ri ++ opInstrs ++ fixedWidthWrapW tag op ++ seamOut

-- A `U64` operator (the typechecker stamps both arithmetic and comparison sites
-- `U64`): unbox both i64 payloads, then the unsigned i64 op.  `+ - *` wrap modulo
-- 2^64 for free; `/`/`%` take the Int path's divisor guard; a comparison yields
-- the i31 Bool the Int path does.
emitU64BinRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  CExpr ->
  CExpr ->
  Int ->
  List String
emitU64BinRef prog env d op l r site =
  let li = emitRefExpr prog env d l ++ unboxU64W
  let ri = emitRefExpr prog env d r ++ unboxU64W
  if op == "/" || op == "%" then
    li
      ++ ri
      ++ emitDivZeroGuard (progEmit prog) op (divrLocal prog d) site
      ++ [wasmU64Op op, "struct.new $u64"]
  else if isCmpOp op then
    li ++ ri ++ [wasmU64Op op, "ref.i31"]
  else
    li ++ ri ++ [wasmU64Op op, "struct.new $u64"]

unboxU64W : List String
unboxU64W = ["ref.cast (ref $u64)", "struct.get $u64 0"]

-- An `I64` operator (stamped `I64` at arithmetic and comparison sites alike):
-- `U64`'s shape with the signed operations.  `+ - *` are the same bits either
-- way; `/` goes through `$mdk_i64_div`, since `i64.div_s` traps on
-- `minBound / -1`, and `i64.rem_s` already answers 0 there.
emitI64BinRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  CExpr ->
  CExpr ->
  Int ->
  List String
emitI64BinRef prog env d op l r site =
  let li = emitRefExpr prog env d l ++ unboxI64W
  let ri = emitRefExpr prog env d r ++ unboxI64W
  let instr =
    if op == "/" then
      rtCallW prog "mdk_i64_div" 2
    else
      wasmBinOp64 (progEmit prog) op
  if op == "/" || op == "%" then
    li
      ++ ri
      ++ emitDivZeroGuard (progEmit prog) op (divrLocal prog d) site
      ++ [instr, "struct.new $i64"]
  else if isCmpOp op then
    li ++ ri ++ [instr, "ref.i31"]
  else
    li ++ ri ++ [instr, "struct.new $i64"]

unboxI64W : List String
unboxI64W = ["ref.cast (ref $i64)", "struct.get $i64 0"]

-- a binary `U64` kernel: both payloads, one i64 instruction (or helper call), reboxed.
emitU64KernelRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> CExpr -> CExpr -> String -> List String
emitU64KernelRef prog env d a b instr =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ unboxU64W
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d b
    ++ unboxU64W
    ++ [instr, "struct.new $u64"]

-- a `U64` shift: the payload and the Int amount, through the range-checked helper.
emitU64ShiftRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> CExpr -> CExpr -> String -> List String
emitU64ShiftRef prog env d a k helper =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ unboxU64W
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d k
    ++ [unboxIntW prog, helper, "struct.new $u64"]

wasmU64Op : String -> String
wasmU64Op "+" = "i64.add"
wasmU64Op "-" = "i64.sub"
wasmU64Op "*" = "i64.mul"
wasmU64Op "/" = "i64.div_u"
wasmU64Op "%" = "i64.rem_u"
wasmU64Op "==" = "i64.eq"
wasmU64Op "/=" = "i64.ne"
wasmU64Op "<" = "i64.lt_u"
wasmU64Op ">" = "i64.gt_u"
wasmU64Op "<=" = "i64.le_u"
wasmU64Op ">=" = "i64.ge_u"
wasmU64Op op = panic ("wasm: not a U64 op '" ++ op ++ "'")

-- A0: arithmetic op → the $mdk_value_<name> helper suffix.
valueArithName : String -> String
valueArithName "+" = "add"
valueArithName "-" = "sub"
valueArithName "*" = "mul"
valueArithName "/" = "div"
valueArithName "%" = "mod"
valueArithName op = panic ("wasm A0: not a value-arith op '" ++ op ++ "'")

-- ── located traps ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- A located trap writes `<file>:<line>:<col>: ` ahead of its line, from one packed
-- i64 `(file + 1) << 44 | line << 20 | col` (the word the native backend packs),
-- where `file` numbers the program's site files in order of first use.  0 means
-- no location: the trap is the unlocated line, byte for byte.

-- The packed site of [l], 0 when [l] names no file, is the placeholder span, or
-- does not fit its fields.
sitePackedW : WasmEmit -> Loc -> Int
sitePackedW emit (Loc f sl sc el ec)
  | f == "" || sl == 1 && sc == 0 && el == 1 && ec == 0 = 0
  | sl < 0 || sl >= 16777216 || sc < 0 || sc >= 1048576 = 0
  | otherwise = match siteFileNumW emit f
    Some n => n * 17592186044416 + sl * 1048576 + sc
    None => 0

siteFileNumW : WasmEmit -> String -> Option Int
siteFileNumW emit f = match omLookup f !emit.siteFileNums
  Some n => Some n
  None =>
    let n = omSize !emit.siteFileNums + 1
    if n >= 65536 then
      None
    else
      let _ = setRef emit.siteFileNums (omInsert f n !emit.siteFileNums)
      let _ = setRef emit.siteFiles (f :: !emit.siteFiles)
      Some n

-- `<file>:<line>:<col>: ` for [site], nothing for 0.
siteLocInstrs : WasmEmit -> Int -> List String
siteLocInstrs _ 0 = []
siteLocInstrs emit site =
  ["i64.const " ++ intToString site, trapCallW emit "mdk_write_err_loc" 1]

-- the located-trap runtime of the module: the table of site files, the location
-- writer, and the shared non-exhaustive-match trap if one is called.
siteExprInstrs : Prog -> Env -> Int -> CExpr -> List String
siteExprInstrs prog env d (CLit (LInt 0)) = []
siteExprInstrs prog env d (e@(CApp _ _ _)) = match flattenApp e []
  (CVar v _, [CLit (LString f), CLit (LInt line), CLit (LInt col)]) =>
    if v == siteSentinelName then
      siteLocInstrs
        (progEmit prog)
        (sitePackedW (progEmit prog) (Loc f line col line (col + 1)))
    else
      siteDynInstrs prog env d e
  _ => siteDynInstrs prog env d e
siteExprInstrs prog env d e = siteDynInstrs prog env d e

siteDynInstrs : Prog -> Env -> Int -> CExpr -> List String
siteDynInstrs prog env d e =
  emitRefExpr prog env d e
    ++ [unboxIntW prog, rtCallW prog "mdk_write_err_loc" 1]

-- the non-exhaustive-match trap at [site]: one call of the shared helper when
-- located, today's unrolled line when not.
wasmNonexhTrap : WasmEmit -> Int -> List String
wasmNonexhTrap emit 0 =
  wasmTrap emit "E-NONEXHAUSTIVE-MATCH" "non-exhaustive match"
wasmNonexhTrap emit site = [
  "i64.const " ++ intToString site,
  trapCallW emit "mdk_trap_nonexh" 1,
  "unreachable",
]

-- the site a decision tree's miss reports.
failSiteW : WasmEmit -> FailSite -> Int
failSiteW emit (NoArm l) = sitePackedW emit l
failSiteW emit (LetRefuted l) = sitePackedW emit l

-- the trap a decision tree's miss raises: no arm matched, or a `let` pattern
-- did not match.
wasmFailTrap : WasmEmit -> FailSite -> List String
wasmFailTrap emit (LetRefuted l) =
  let site = sitePackedW emit l
  siteLocInstrs emit site
    ++ wasmTrap emit "E-LET-REFUTE" "let pattern match failed"
wasmFailTrap emit fs = wasmNonexhTrap emit (failSiteW emit fs)

-- ── B5: coded runtime-trap helpers (RUNTIME-TRAP-UNIFY-DESIGN §3 (5), §7 forks 1-2) ──
-- The WasmGC peer of the native traps: emit the same coded stderr line the interpreter
-- and medaka_rt.c produce — `runtime error [E-CODE]: <message>\n` — then `unreachable`.
-- The bytes are streamed to stderr via the mdk_write_err_byte host import, FULLY
-- UNROLLED (one i32.const/call pair per byte): no $str value, no data segment, no
-- ref-mode dependency, so the SAME helper works in scalar AND ref mode and only the
-- import (not the $str runtime) is forced.  `unreachable` is stack-polymorphic, so the
-- sequence validates as any result type (mirroring the bare `unreachable` it replaces).
-- Records this event on WasmEmit so emit{Ref,Scalar}Program declares host import.
trapByteInstr : WasmEmit -> Int -> List String
trapByteInstr emit b =
  ["i32.const " ++ intToString b, trapCallW emit "mdk_write_err_byte" 1]

-- `call $<name>` of a runtime helper or host import from a coded trap
trapCallW : WasmEmit -> String -> Int -> String
trapCallW emit name operands =
  callFnAtW emit trapOriginW CallValueW name operands

wasmTrapBytes : WasmEmit -> String -> List String
wasmTrapBytes emit text = if text == "" then [] else trapMsgCall emit text

-- Stream the coded-trap text [text] by calling its `$trapmsg_K` helper.  The
-- helper holds the unrolled byte-writes once per DISTINCT text, so a message repeated
-- at many trap sites costs one body plus a call per site.  The helper takes and
-- leaves nothing, so the `call` is stack-neutral exactly as the pairs were; the
-- caller still supplies any `unreachable`.  Helper bodies are assembled by
-- `trapMsgRuntimeOf`, after every body emission (see the module assembly).
trapMsgCall : WasmEmit -> String -> List String
trapMsgCall emit text = match omLookup text !emit.trapMsgIds
  Some k => [trapCallW emit ("trapmsg_" ++ intToString k) 0]
  None =>
    let k = omSize !emit.trapMsgIds
    let _ = setRef emit.trapMsgIds (omInsert text k !emit.trapMsgIds)
    let def =
      ["  (func $trapmsg_" ++ intToString k]
        ++ map ("    " ++ _) (flatMap (trapByteInstr emit) (strBytesW text))
        ++ ["  )"]
    let _ = setRef emit.trapMsgFns (reverseL def ++ !emit.trapMsgFns)
    let _ =
      registerW
        emit
        (defineSymbol
          (WasmFunc ("trapmsg_" ++ intToString k))
          (FuncParams 0)
          trapOriginW)
    [trapCallW emit ("trapmsg_" ++ intToString k) 0]

-- the `$trapmsg_K` helper definitions this emission made, in number order.
trapMsgRuntimeOf : WasmEmit -> List String
trapMsgRuntimeOf emit = reverseL !emit.trapMsgFns

-- a full coded trap with a compile-time-fixed message (div/mod/OOB/non-exhaustive).
wasmTrap : WasmEmit -> String -> String -> List String
wasmTrap emit code msg =
  wasmTrapBytes emit "runtime error [\{code}]: \{msg}\n" ++ ["unreachable"]

-- a coded trap whose message is the fixed prefix, then `name`, then the fixed
-- `after` (which ends in its newline).  The prefix and `after` are interned like
-- any fixed text, so sites that differ only in `name` share their two helpers and
-- only the name bytes are unrolled at the site.  `name` is an identifier known at
-- emission; the stderr bytes are the same as the whole message spelled out.  The name
-- bytes call the error-byte import themselves, so the import flag is set here rather
-- than left to the interned prefix.
wasmTrapNamed : WasmEmit -> String -> String -> String -> List String
wasmTrapNamed emit code name after =
  wasmTrapBytes emit "runtime error [\{code}]: "
    ++ flatMap (trapByteInstr emit) (strBytesW name)
    ++ wasmTrapBytes emit after
    ++ ["unreachable"]

-- #1787: a coded trap whose message carries a RUNTIME number -- the fixed bytes
-- either side of it are still streamed unrolled, and the value itself goes through
-- $mdk_write_err_int.  `valIns` must leave the number on the stack as a (ref eq)
-- Medaka Int; it is unboxed here.  Sets trapIntNeeded so the decimal runtime is
-- emitted (a fixed-text trap alone must not pull it in -- that would move every
-- existing wasm golden).
wasmTrapNum : WasmEmit ->
  String ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  String ->
  List String
wasmTrapNum emit code before valIns after =
  wasmTrapBytes emit "runtime error [\{code}]: \{before}"
    ++ valIns
    ++ [
      trapCallW emit "mdk_unbox_int" 1,
      trapCallW emit "mdk_write_err_int" 1,
    ]
    ++ wasmTrapBytes emit "\{after}\n"
    ++ ["unreachable"]

-- B5: guard a concrete-Int div/mod divisor.  Stack in `[dividend:i64, divisor:i64]`;
-- stashes the divisor in `dloc`, traps with the coded [E-DIV-ZERO]/[E-MOD-ZERO] line if
-- it is zero, then restores `[dividend, divisor]` for the following i64.div_s/rem_s.
-- (The `if` has empty block type; the dividend rests untouched beneath it, and the
-- then-branch ends in `unreachable` so the branch is stack-polymorphic.)
emitDivZeroGuard : WasmEmit -> String -> String -> Int -> List String
emitDivZeroGuard emit op dloc site =
  let code = if op == "/" then "E-DIV-ZERO" else "E-MOD-ZERO"
  let msg = if op == "/" then "division by zero" else "modulo by zero"
  ["local.set " ++ dloc, "local.get " ++ dloc, "i64.eqz", "if"]
    ++ indent (siteLocInstrs emit site ++ wasmTrap emit code msg)
    ++ ["end", "local.get " ++ dloc]

-- layer-9: emit a runtime-shape-dispatched comparison.  `==`/`/=` go through
-- $mdk_value_eq (-> i31 Bool); ordering ops call $mdk_value_cmp (-> plain i32 -1/0/1)
-- then i32-compare the result against 0 for the requested op, re-boxing the Bool i31.
emitValueCmpRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> String -> CExpr -> CExpr -> List String
emitValueCmpRef prog env d op l r =
  let lv = emitRefExpr prog env d l
  let rv = emitRefExpr prog env d r
  if op == "==" then
    lv ++ rv ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_value_eq" 2]
  else if op == "/=" then
    lv
      ++ rv
      ++ [
        rtCallW prog "mdk_value_eq" 2,
        "ref.cast (ref i31)",
        "i31.get_u",
        "i32.eqz",
        "ref.i31",
      ]
  else
    -- #305: ordering calls the per-op IEEE predicate $mdk_value_lt/le/gt/ge,
    -- which returns an i31 Bool directly.  It USED to be `$mdk_value_cmp` then
    -- `i32.const 0` + compare — but a 3-way -1/0/1 cannot express NaN's
    -- unorderedness, so `nan <= nan` read `0 <= 0` = True.
    lv ++ rv ++ [rtCallW prog ("mdk_value_" ++ valueRelName op) 2]
