-- A1 (poly-`Ord`-on-Float, string-free program): the num-only peer of emitValueCmpRef.
-- `==`/`/=` go through $mdk_value_eq_num (-> i31 Bool); ordering through $mdk_value_cmp_num
-- (-> i32 -1/0/1).  Both dispatch $float vs int (i31/$boxint) ONLY — no $str — so they
-- need no pre-scan-set type; gated by its own useValueCmpNum flag (S2/#2359 —
-- independent of the per-operator arith flags, since this branch never touches
-- $mdk_value_add/sub/mul/div/mod).
emitValueCmpNumRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  CExpr ->
  CExpr ->
  List String
emitValueCmpNumRef prog env d op l r =
  let lv = emitRefExpr prog env d l
  let rv = emitRefExpr prog env d r
  if op == "==" then
    lv ++ rv ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_value_eq_num" 2]
  else if op == "/=" then
    lv
      ++ rv
      ++ [
        rtCallW prog "mdk_value_eq_num" 2,
        "ref.cast (ref i31)",
        "i31.get_u",
        "i32.eqz",
        "ref.i31",
      ]
  else
    -- #305: per-op IEEE predicate (num-only peer), returns an i31 Bool directly
    -- — see the note at emitValueCmpRef.
    lv ++ rv ++ [rtCallW prog ("mdk_value_" ++ valueRelName op ++ "_num") 2]

-- #305: the $mdk_value_* suffix for an ordering op.  Only `<`/`>`/`<=`/`>=` reach
-- the ordering arms — `==`/`/=` are routed to $mdk_value_eq(_num) before them.
valueRelName : String -> String
valueRelName "<" = "lt"
valueRelName ">" = "gt"
valueRelName "<=" = "le"
valueRelName ">=" = "ge"
valueRelName op = panic ("wasm: unsupported value ordering op " ++ op)

-- W8b: emit a Float binop.  Arith (+,-,*,/) → unbox both, f64 op, rebox.  `%` has no
-- f64 instruction, so it calls $mdk_float_rem (exact power-of-two-reduction fmod == LLVM frem).
-- Comparison (==,/=,<,>,<=,>=) → unbox both, f64 compare → i31 Bool.
emitFloatBinRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> String -> CExpr -> CExpr -> List String
emitFloatBinRef prog env d op l r =
  let lf =
    emitRefExpr prog env d l ++ ["ref.cast (ref $float)", "struct.get $float 0"]
  let rf =
    emitRefExpr prog env d r ++ ["ref.cast (ref $float)", "struct.get $float 0"]
  if isCmpOp op then
    lf ++ rf ++ [wasmFloatCmp op, "ref.i31"]
  else if op == "%" then
    lf ++ rf ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_float_rem" 2, "struct.new $float"]
  else
    lf ++ rf ++ [wasmFloatArith op, "struct.new $float"]

wasmFloatArith : String -> String
wasmFloatArith "+" = "f64.add"
wasmFloatArith "-" = "f64.sub"
wasmFloatArith "*" = "f64.mul"
wasmFloatArith "/" = "f64.div"
wasmFloatArith op = panic ("wasm W8b: not a Float arith op '" ++ op ++ "'")

wasmFloatCmp : String -> String
wasmFloatCmp "==" = "f64.eq"
wasmFloatCmp "/=" = "f64.ne"
wasmFloatCmp "<" = "f64.lt"
wasmFloatCmp ">" = "f64.gt"
wasmFloatCmp "<=" = "f64.le"
wasmFloatCmp ">=" = "f64.ge"
wasmFloatCmp op = panic ("wasm W8b: not a Float compare op '" ++ op ++ "'")

-- ── what a name holds, read from the binder stamps ───────────────────────────
-- Every static numeric fact this emitter acts on is a binder's published
-- runtime type (`DeclFacts.factBinders`), found through the binder's `BinderId`
-- ordinal.  A reference is a name, and the names in `env` are unique only among
-- NESTED binders (`uniqueBinders`): two sibling arms may bind `x` at different
-- types.  So `env` maps each name to the binder it currently denotes
-- (`envBind`), scoped exactly as the name is: an inner binding replaces the
-- outer one in its own scope only.  A fact is never stored under a name.

-- [env] extended with the stamped binder [x]
envBind : String -> BinderId -> Env -> Env
envBind = WD.envBind

-- the env of a function's plain parameters
paramEnv : List Pat -> Env
paramEnv = WD.paramEnv

varStamp : Prog -> Env -> String -> RuntimeType
varStamp prog = WD.varStamp (progIndex prog).typeContext

returnStamp : Prog -> Env -> String -> RuntimeType
returnStamp prog = WD.returnStamp (progIndex prog).typeContext

cexprStamp : Prog -> Env -> CExpr -> RuntimeType
cexprStamp prog = WD.cexprStamp (progIndex prog).typeContext

envBindGroups : List CBind -> Env -> Env
envBindGroups = WD.envBindGroups

-- is [e] statically a Float?
cexprIsFloat : Prog -> Env -> CExpr -> Bool
cexprIsFloat prog env e = cexprStamp prog env e == RTFloat

-- A binop operand whose type is known only at run time: a variable stamped
-- `RTValue` (a `Num a` parameter, or any binder the typechecker left generic).
-- It routes to the runtime value-dispatch helpers, never the inline Int path
-- (which would trap `illegal cast` on a boxed $float).
emitUnRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> String -> CExpr -> List String
emitUnRef prog env d "-" x =
  -- W8b: unary `-` on a Float negates the f64 (f64.neg), reboxing; else integer negate.
  if not (rawProgramW prog) && cexprIsFloat prog env x then
    emitRefExpr prog env d x
      ++ [
        "ref.cast (ref $float)",
        "struct.get $float 0",
        "f64.neg",
        "struct.new $float",
      ]
  else
    -- layer-17 §2.1: integer negate over the i64 box/unbox seam, checked
    -- (intMinBound has no negation).
    let xi =
      emitRefExpr prog env d x
        ++ (if rawProgramW prog then [] else [unboxIntW prog])
    xi
      ++ intChkNegCall prog
      ++ (if rawProgramW prog then [] else [boxIntW prog])
emitUnRef prog _ _ op _ =
  gapLP
    prog
    "\{if rawProgramW prog then "scalar-mode" else "ref-mode"}: unsupported unary op '\{op}'"
-- ── W11: irrefutable destructuring let / refutable let-else / assignment ──────
-- An irrefutable `let <pat> = e` (PTuple / single-ctor PCon / PRecord / PCons /
-- PList — all single-shape here, the type proves the shape): emit the RHS once,
-- stash it into the scratch local `$__rf<de>` (de = one slot above whatever the
-- RHS uses, so it never collides), then bind each sub-pattern by field extraction
-- (reusing bindPatRef, the same machinery match-arm leaves use).  Returns the
-- stash+bind instructions and the env extended with the bound vars.
emitDestructureLet : Prog -> Env -> Int -> Pat -> CExpr -> (List String, Env)
emitDestructureLet prog env d pat e1 =
  let de = maxIndexAt e1 d + 1
  let sv = scratchLocal de
  let rhs = emitRefExpr prog env d e1 ++ ["local.set $" ++ sv]
  let (binds, env2) = bindPatRef prog env pat ["local.get $" ++ sv]
  (rhs ++ binds, env2)

-- Binding emission is shared by value and tail descent; the caller keeps the
-- body's position and passes the extended lexical environment.
emitLetBindingW : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  Bool ->
  Pat ->
  CExpr ->
  (List String, Env)
emitLetBindingW prog env d False (PVar x _ bid) e1 =
  let rhs = emitRefExpr prog env d e1
  let _ = mintLocalW prog bid
  let env2 = envBind x bid env
  (rhs ++ ["local.set " ++ localTargetW prog env2 x], env2)
emitLetBindingW prog env d False PWild e1 =
  (emitRefExpr prog env d e1 ++ ["drop"], env)
emitLetBindingW prog env d False pat e1 =
  if rawProgramW prog then
    (
      gapLP prog "scalar-mode: only non-recursive `let x = e` / `let _ = e`",
      env,
    )
  else
    emitDestructureLet prog env d pat e1
emitLetBindingW prog env _ True (PVar x _ bid) (CLam pats body) =
  if rawProgramW prog then
    (
      gapLP prog "scalar-mode: only non-recursive `let x = e` / `let _ = e`",
      env,
    )
  else
    (emitSelfRecLocalBind prog env x bid pats body, envBind x bid env)
emitLetBindingW prog env _ _ _ _ = (
  gapLP prog (if rawProgramW prog then
    "scalar-mode: only non-recursive `let x = e` / `let _ = e`"
  else
    "ref-mode: recursive non-function `let` binding (value knot)"),
  env,
)

emitBlockRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> List CStmt -> WasmValue
emitBlockRef prog env d [CSExpr ex] = emitValueW prog env d ex
emitBlockRef prog env d ((CSExpr ex) :: rest) =
  let prefix = emitRefExpr prog env d ex ++ ["drop"]
  prependValueW prefix (emitBlockRef prog env d rest)
emitBlockRef prog env d ((CSLet recF pat ex) :: rest) =
  let (prefix, env2) = emitBlockBindingW prog env d recF pat ex
  prependValueW prefix (emitBlockRef prog env2 d rest)
emitBlockRef prog env d ((CSAssign x ex) :: rest) =
  let prefix =
    emitRefExpr prog env d ex ++ ["local.set " ++ localTargetW prog env x]
  prependValueW prefix (emitBlockRef prog env d rest)
emitBlockRef prog env d [] = emitValueW prog env d (CLit LUnit)
emitBlockRef prog _ _ _ =
  programValueW
    prog
    (gapLP prog (if rawProgramW prog then
      "scalar-mode: unsupported block statement"
    else
      "ref-mode: unsupported block statement"))

emitBlockBindingW : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  Bool ->
  Pat ->
  CExpr ->
  (List String, Env)
emitBlockBindingW prog env d _ pat ex = match (pat, ex)
  (PVar x _ bid, CLam pats body) =>
    if rawProgramW prog then
      emitLetBindingW prog env d False pat ex
    else
      (emitSelfRecLocalBind prog env x bid pats body, envBind x bid env)
  _ => emitLetBindingW prog env d False pat ex

emitDirectRawCallW : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  CExpr ->
  List CExpr ->
  Bool ->
  List String
emitDirectRawCallW prog env d (CVar f _) args tail =
  if progFnMemberW prog f then
    flatMap (a => emitRefExpr prog env d a) args
      ++ [
        callFnW
          prog
          (if tail then CallTailW else CallValueW)
          (gname f)
          (listLen args),
      ]
  else
    gapLP
      prog
      ("scalar-mode: application of non-top-level head '"
        ++ f
        ++ "' (closures/HOFs are W4)")
emitDirectRawCallW prog _ _ _ _ _ =
  gapLP
    prog
    "scalar-mode: application of a non-variable head (closures/HOFs are W4)"

-- application (non-tail position).  An exact application of a known top-level fn
-- → `call`.  A ctor application → struct.new.  Anything else (a partial / over
-- application of a known fn; an indirect call whose head is a closure value: a local
-- param, a let-bound closure, a returned closure, an immediately-applied lambda) →
-- build an args array + `call $__mdk_apply` (the universal arity-dispatched apply).
emitAppRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> CExpr -> List String
emitAppRef prog env d app =
  let (hd, args, mode) = appParts app
  if rawProgramW prog then
    emitDirectRawCallW prog env d hd args False
  else match hd
    CVar f0 _ =>
      let f = canonFn prog f0
      if f0 == "$withFileReadBound"
        || f0 == "$withFileWriteBound" then match fileBoundW app
        Some (g, body, mode) =>
          fileBoundEnterW prog env d g mode True
            ++ ["drop"]
            ++ emitRefExpr prog env d body
            ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_file_bound_exit" 0]
        None => gapLP prog "wasm: a file bound requires a grant and a thunk"
      else if isFtSentinel f0 || hasFamilyW prog f0 "fallthrough" then
        -- the desugared `__fallthrough__ ()` / `__ft__<label> ()` form: ignore the (unit)
        -- arg, lower the sentinel (br to the clause label, or trap stub).  The bare-CVar
        -- form is handled by emitVarRef; this catches the applied form guard chains make.
        ftSentinelInstrs f0
      else if envHas f0 env then
        -- E24 (wasm peer): a LOCALLY-BOUND name (param / let-binding) SHADOWS any same-named
        -- ctor / known top-level fn / extern: it is a runtime closure VALUE, so applying it
        -- is an INDIRECT call, never a direct `call $fn` / ctor.new.  Without this, a HOF
        -- param named like an interface method (`pickEq eq x y = eq x y`, or `cmp`/`compare`/
        -- `map`) that ALSO collides with a top-level fn name fell to the function-name arm →
        -- a direct `call $<toplevel>` over the WRONG callee (silent miscompile: the top-level
        -- fn ran instead of the param), while `medaka run` and the LLVM build were always
        -- correct.  Mirrors emitVarRefPlain's `envHas x env`-first priority for the bare
        -- VALUE reference, and the LLVM emitApp E24 `isLocal`-first guard.
        emitIndirectApp prog env d hd args CallValueW
      else if isCtor prog f then
        emitCtorApp prog env d f args
      else if f0 == siteSentinelName then
        emitLeafExternRef prog env d siteSentinelName args
      else if hasFamilyW prog f0 "ref" && runtimeNameW prog f0 == "Ref" then
        emitRefBoxNew prog env d args
      else if hasFamilyW prog f0 "ref" && runtimeNameW prog f0 == "setRef" then
        emitRefBoxSet prog env d args
      else if isFfiExternW prog f then
        emitFfiAppW prog env d hd f args CallValueW
      else match externFamilyW (progEmit prog) (runtimeNameW prog f0)
        Some WasmStr => emitStrExternRef prog env d (runtimeNameW prog f0) args
        Some WasmLeaf =>
          emitLeafExternRef prog env d (runtimeNameW prog f0) args
        Some WasmArray =>
          emitArrayExternRef prog env d (runtimeNameW prog f0) args
        Some WasmByteBlock =>
          emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d (runtimeNameW prog f0) args
        _ =>
          if progFnMemberW prog f && isExactCall mode then
            let argInstrs = flatMap (a => emitRefExpr prog env d a) args
            argInstrs ++ [callFnW prog CallValueW (gname f) (listLen args)]
          else
            emitIndirectApp prog env d hd args CallValueW
    -- W5: a method occurrence applied to its args (the common return-/arg-position
    -- dispatch shape — a CMethod head under a CApp).  Dispatch on the route.
    CMethod name (MethodEvidence iface arity route implRoutes methRoutes) =>
      emitMethodRef
        prog
        env
        d
        name
        iface
        arity
        route
        implRoutes
        methRoutes
        args
        mode
        CallValueW
    -- W5: a constrained-function occurrence applied to its real args.  The dict
    -- witnesses (from `routes`) are PREPENDED to the args at the call.
    CDict name routes => emitDictRef prog env d name routes args mode CallValueW
    _ => emitIndirectApp prog env d hd args CallValueW

-- A string slice call: `lo`/`hi` are i31 Ints unboxed to i32, `s` a `$str`,
-- and `callee` the runtime helper (named without its `$`) taking them in that
-- order.
emitStrSliceCall : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  CExpr ->
  CExpr ->
  CExpr ->
  List String
emitStrSliceCall prog env d callee lo hi s =
  emitRefExpr prog env d lo
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_s"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d hi
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_s"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d s
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog callee 3]

-- ── W6 string / IO externs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- `intToString` : i31 Int → unbox → i64 → $mdk_int_to_str → (ref $str) (an (ref eq)).
-- `stringLength` : (ref $str) → cached cp_count (O(1), §5 INTRINSIC) → i31 Int.
-- `putStr`/`putStrLn` : (ref $str) → byte-write (no/with trailing '\n'); Unit (i31 0).
-- `flushStdout` : no-op (byte writes are unbuffered through the host import); Unit.
-- `charToStr`/`stringConcat` are W6b (charToStr needs a codepoint→$str runtime;
-- stringConcat takes a `List String`, which needs W7 list support).
emitStrExternRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> String -> List CExpr -> List String
emitStrExternRef prog env d "intToString" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a ++ [unboxIntW prog, rtCallW prog "mdk_int_to_str" 1]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "intToString" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W6: intToString takes exactly one argument"
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringLength" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", "struct.get $str $cp_count", "ref.i31"]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringLength" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W6: stringLength takes exactly one argument"
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringByteLength" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", "struct.get $str $bytes", "array.len", "ref.i31"]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringByteLength" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W6: stringByteLength takes exactly one argument"
emitStrExternRef prog env d "putStr" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref $str)",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_print_str" 1,
      "i32.const 0",
      "ref.i31",
    ]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "putStr" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W6: putStr takes exactly one argument"
emitStrExternRef prog env d "putStrLn" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref $str)",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_print_strln" 1,
      "i32.const 0",
      "ref.i31",
    ]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "putStrLn" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W6: putStrLn takes exactly one argument"
emitStrExternRef prog env d "ePutStr" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref $str)",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_eprint_str" 1,
      "i32.const 0",
      "ref.i31",
    ]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "ePutStr" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8: ePutStr takes exactly one argument"
emitStrExternRef prog env d "ePutStrLn" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref $str)",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_eprint_strln" 1,
      "i32.const 0",
      "ref.i31",
    ]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "ePutStrLn" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8: ePutStrLn takes exactly one argument"
emitStrExternRef _ _ _ "flushStdout" _ = ["i32.const 0", "ref.i31"]
-- charToStr : a Char is an i31 codepoint (ref eq) → unbox to i32 → $mdk_char_to_str.
emitStrExternRef prog env d "charToStr" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_u", rtCallW prog "mdk_char_to_str" 1]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "charToStr" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8: charToStr takes exactly one argument"
-- stringConcat : a List String (ref eq) → walk the W7 cons list → fresh $str.
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringConcat" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_str_concat" 1]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringConcat" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8: stringConcat takes exactly one argument"
-- stringSlice lo hi s : lo/hi are i31 Int codepoint indices, s a $str.
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringSlice" [lo, hi, s] =
  emitStrSliceCall prog env d "mdk_str_slice" lo hi s
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringSlice" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8: stringSlice takes exactly three arguments"
-- stringCodepointAtByte s b : s a $str, b an i31 Int byte offset; the packed
-- codepoint * 8 + width comes back as an i31 Int.
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringCodepointAtByte" [s, b] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d s
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d b
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref i31)",
      "i31.get_s",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_str_cp_at_byte" 2,
      "ref.i31",
    ]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringCodepointAtByte" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: stringCodepointAtByte takes exactly two arguments"
-- stringSliceBytes lo hi s : lo/hi are i31 Int byte offsets, s a $str.
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringSliceBytes" [lo, hi, s] =
  emitStrSliceCall prog env d "mdk_str_slice_bytes" lo hi s
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringSliceBytes" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: stringSliceBytes takes exactly three arguments"
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringToUpper" [s] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d s
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_str_upper" 1]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringToUpper" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8: stringToUpper takes exactly one argument"
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringToLower" [s] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d s
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_str_lower" 1]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringToLower" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8: stringToLower takes exactly one argument"
-- hashString : a $str → FNV-1a i32 in [0,2^30) → i31 Int.
emitStrExternRef prog env d "hashString" [s] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d s
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_hash_string" 1, "ref.i31"]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "hashString" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8: hashString takes exactly one argument"
-- W8b: floatToString : a boxed $float → unbox → $mdk_float_to_str → (ref $str).
emitStrExternRef prog env d "floatToString" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref $float)",
      "struct.get $float 0",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_float_to_str" 1,
    ]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "floatToString" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8b: floatToString takes exactly one argument"
-- W8b: stringIndexOf needle hay : two $str → Option Int (ref eq).  The runtime fn
-- builds the Some/None result directly (Some idx / None), so no inline ctor here.
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringIndexOf" [needle, hay] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d needle
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d hay
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_str_index_of" 2]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringIndexOf" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8b: stringIndexOf takes exactly two arguments"
-- W8c: byte-level searches over two $str.  Bool / Int results are i32 immediates
-- from the runtime fns; stringLastIndexOf builds its Option Int like $mdk_str_index_of.
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringStartsWith" [p, s] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d p
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d s
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_str_starts_with" 2, "ref.i31"]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringStartsWith" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8c: stringStartsWith takes exactly two arguments"
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringEndsWith" [p, s] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d p
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d s
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_str_ends_with" 2, "ref.i31"]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringEndsWith" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8c: stringEndsWith takes exactly two arguments"
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringCountOccurrences" [n, h] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d n
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d h
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_str_count_occ" 2, "ref.i31"]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringCountOccurrences" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8c: stringCountOccurrences takes exactly two arguments"
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringLastIndexOf" [n, h] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d n
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d h
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_str_last_index_of" 2]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringLastIndexOf" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8c: stringLastIndexOf takes exactly two arguments"
-- W8d: stringToInt / stringReverse take one $str; stringJoin a $str and a cons list.
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringToInt" [s] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d s
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_str_to_int" 1]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringToInt" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8d: stringToInt takes exactly one argument"
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringReverse" [s] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d s
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_str_reverse" 1]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringReverse" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8d: stringReverse takes exactly one argument"
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringJoin" [sep, parts] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d sep
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d parts
    ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_str_join" 2]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringJoin" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8d: stringJoin takes exactly two arguments"
-- W8b: stringCompare a b : two $str → Ordering (ref eq).  The runtime fn returns the
-- Lt/Eq/Gt i31 immediate directly.
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringCompare" [a, b] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d b
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_str_compare" 2]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringCompare" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8b: stringCompare takes exactly two arguments"
-- W11b: stringToChars : String -> Array Char.  Decode the $str's UTF-8 bytes into a
-- fresh $arr of `cp_count` i31 Char codepoints.  The runtime fn builds the $arr.
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringToChars" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_str_to_chars" 1]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringToChars" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W11b: stringToChars takes exactly one argument"
-- W11b: stringFromChars : Array Char -> String.  Encode an $arr of i31 Char codepoints
-- into a fresh $str (UTF-8); cp_count = array.len.  The runtime fn builds the $str.
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringFromChars" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $arr)", rtCallW prog "mdk_chars_to_str" 1]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringFromChars" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W11b: stringFromChars takes exactly one argument"
-- W11b: stringToUtf8Bytes : String -> Array Int.  Copy the $str's $u8arr backing into
-- a fresh $arr of i31 Int bytes (0..255).  stringFromUtf8Bytes : Array Int -> String —
-- blit the low 8 bits of each i31 back into a $u8arr + struct.new $str.
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringToUtf8Bytes" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_str_to_utf8_bytes" 1]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringToUtf8Bytes" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W11b: stringToUtf8Bytes takes exactly one argument"
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringFromUtf8Bytes" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $arr)", rtCallW prog "mdk_utf8_bytes_to_str" 1]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringFromUtf8Bytes" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W11b: stringFromUtf8Bytes takes exactly one argument"
-- W11b: charFromCode : Int -> Option Char.  Range-check the i31 Int (valid = 0..0x10FFFF
-- EXCLUDING surrogates 0xD800..0xDFFF, byte-identical to medaka_rt.c mdk_char_from_code)
-- → Some <char i31> (struct.new $C_Some, ordinal 0) / None (i31 ordinal 1).  Inlined
-- (peer to the runtime-built stringIndexOf Option, but small enough to emit directly).
emitStrExternRef prog env d "charFromCode" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_s", rtCallW prog "mdk_char_from_code" 1]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "charFromCode" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W11b: charFromCode takes exactly one argument"
-- W9: debugStringLit s : $str -> $str (quote+escape with double-quotes).
emitStrExternRef prog env d "debugStringLit" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_debug_string_lit" 1]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "debugStringLit" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W9: debugStringLit takes exactly one argument"
-- W9: debugCharLit c : Char (i31) -> $str (quote+escape with single-quotes).
emitStrExternRef prog env d "debugCharLit" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_u", rtCallW prog "mdk_debug_char_lit" 1]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "debugCharLit" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W9: debugCharLit takes exactly one argument"
-- layer-6: stringToFloat : String -> Option Float.
-- Push the $str's bytes via the path channel, call mdk_str_to_float -> f64, return
-- Option Float (Some(boxed $float) | None) via the WAT runtime $mdk_string_to_float.
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringToFloat" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_string_to_float" 1]
emitStrExternRef prog env d "stringToFloat" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm layer-6: stringToFloat takes exactly one argument"
emitStrExternRef prog _ _ name _ =
  gapLP prog ("wasm W6: unsupported string extern '" ++ name ++ "'")

-- ── W8 RNG + hash LEAF externs (RUNTIME-DESIGN §5 RNG / §5 hash) ─────────────
-- RNG: randomInt lo hi (i31 Int args → $mdk_random_int → i31 Int, INCLUSIVE);
-- randomBool/randomChar take a Unit arg (emitted + dropped) → i31 Bool/Char;
-- setSeed unboxes its i31 Int to i64 into the seed global.  Hash: hashInt/hashChar
-- ── Ref / setRef / .value — $refbox mutable-cell externs ───────────────────
-- `Ref x`     : allocate a fresh 1-field mutable $refbox, storing x as (ref eq).
-- `setRef r v` : overwrite field 0 of r's $refbox; result is Unit (i31 0).
-- `.value`    : struct.get the mutable field 0; handled in emitFieldAccessRef.
emitRefBoxNew : Prog -> Env -> Int -> List CExpr -> List String
emitRefBoxNew prog env d [x] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d x ++ ["struct.new $refbox"]
emitRefBoxNew prog env d _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm Ref: Ref takes exactly one argument"

-- `setRef r v` : struct.set $refbox 0 ; returns Unit.
-- WAT stack order for struct.set is [structref, value] (ref on top first).
emitRefBoxSet : Prog -> Env -> Int -> List CExpr -> List String
emitRefBoxSet prog env d [r, v] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d r
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $refbox)"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d v
    ++ ["struct.set $refbox 0", "i32.const 0", "ref.i31"]
emitRefBoxSet prog env d _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm Ref: setRef takes exactly two arguments"

-- untag the i31 value to i32 (the runtime sign-extends to i64, matching the native
-- signed `tagged>>1`); hashBool passes the 0/1 i31.  All hash results fit i31
-- (masked to 2^30-1, non-negative).  randomFloat / hashFloat are DEFERRED (W8b —
-- they need Float boxing + the float formatter (shortest-round-trip since #57, NOT
-- %.12g — see wasm_preamble.mdk's W8b Float section); see the gap arms).
emitLeafExternRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> String -> List CExpr -> List String
-- #179: randomInt lo hi — the draw (and lo/hi) can exceed ±2^30, so BOTH args unbox
-- through the i31/$boxint seam ($mdk_unbox_int → i64) and the i64 result reboxes via
-- $mdk_box_int.  Casting args + result to a bare `ref.i31` instead traps
-- `illegal cast` when lo/hi/draw fall outside i31 (e.g. `randomInt 0 1000000000000000`
-- draws 457532755261734).  $mdk_random_int is i64→i64 (mirrors native mdk_random_int:
-- inclusive, unsigned modulus of hi-lo+1).
-- lo > hi answers lo; every other span, the full Int range's 2^63 included, draws.
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "randomInt" [lo, hi] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d lo
    ++ [unboxIntW prog]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d hi
    ++ [unboxIntW prog]
    ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_random_int" 2, boxIntW prog]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "randomInt" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8: randomInt takes exactly two arguments"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "randomBool" [u] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d u
    ++ ["drop", rtCallW prog "mdk_random_bool" 0, "ref.i31"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "randomBool" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8: randomBool takes exactly one (Unit) argument"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "randomChar" [u] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d u
    ++ ["drop", rtCallW prog "mdk_random_char" 0, "ref.i31"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "randomChar" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8: randomChar takes exactly one (Unit) argument"
-- #199: the seed is a general Int; unbox the full width through $mdk_unbox_int (→ i64)
-- so `setSeed 4503599627370497` no longer traps the i31 cast.
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "setSeed" [n] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d n
    ++ [
      unboxIntW prog,
      globalW prog "global.set" rngStateW,
      "i32.const 0",
      "ref.i31",
    ]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "setSeed" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8: setSeed takes exactly one argument"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "randomState" [u] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d u
    ++ ["drop", globalW prog "global.get" rngStateW, "struct.new $u64"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "randomState" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8: randomState takes exactly one (Unit) argument"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "restoreRandomState" [state] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d state
    ++ unboxU64W
    ++ [globalW prog "global.set" rngStateW, "i32.const 0", "ref.i31"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "restoreRandomState" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8: restoreRandomState takes exactly one argument"
-- #199: hashInt unboxes the FULL-WIDTH Int (via $mdk_unbox_int → i64) so an Int key
-- outside ±2^30 (e.g. a HashMap Int) hashes correctly instead of trapping the i31 cast;
-- $mdk_hash_int now takes i64.  hashChar's codepoint fits i32 → sign-extend to i64.
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "hashInt" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [unboxIntW prog, rtCallW prog "mdk_hash_int" 1, "ref.i31"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "hashInt" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8: hashInt takes exactly one argument"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "hashChar" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref i31)",
      "i31.get_u",
      "i64.extend_i32_s",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_hash_int" 1,
      "ref.i31",
    ]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "hashChar" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8: hashChar takes exactly one argument"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "hashBool" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref i31)",
      "i31.get_u",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_hash_bool" 1,
      "ref.i31",
    ]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "hashBool" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8: hashBool takes exactly one argument"
-- W11: charCode : Char -> Int — a Char is an i31 codepoint immediate.  Cast to i31,
-- read the unsigned payload (the codepoint), wrap back as an i31 Int.  The unbox +
-- rebox is identity on the bits (both Char and Int are i31 codepoint / integer), but
-- the cast ensures Wasm's type-safe path through (ref eq).
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "charCode" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_u", "ref.i31"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "charCode" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W11: charCode takes exactly one argument"
-- W11b: char classification predicates (ASCII-only, byte-identical to medaka_rt.c).
-- Char is i31 codepoint; unbox with i31.get_u, call WAT helper, result is i32 0/1 → ref.i31.
-- charIsAlpha c → (c>='a'&&c<='z')||(c>='A'&&c<='Z')
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "charIsAlpha" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref i31)",
      "i31.get_u",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_char_is_alpha" 1,
      "ref.i31",
    ]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "charIsAlpha" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W11b: charIsAlpha takes exactly one argument"
-- charIsSpace c → c==32 || (c>=9 && c<=13)
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "charIsSpace" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref i31)",
      "i31.get_u",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_char_is_space" 1,
      "ref.i31",
    ]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "charIsSpace" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W11b: charIsSpace takes exactly one argument"
-- charIsUpper c → c>='A'&&c<='Z'
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "charIsUpper" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref i31)",
      "i31.get_u",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_char_is_upper" 1,
      "ref.i31",
    ]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "charIsUpper" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W11b: charIsUpper takes exactly one argument"
-- charIsLower c → c>='a'&&c<='z'
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "charIsLower" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref i31)",
      "i31.get_u",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_char_is_lower" 1,
      "ref.i31",
    ]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "charIsLower" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W11b: charIsLower takes exactly one argument"
-- charIsPunct: exact set from medaka_rt.c switch — Unicode Pc/Pd/Pe/Pf/Pi/Po/Ps for ASCII.
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "charIsPunct" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref i31)",
      "i31.get_u",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_char_is_punct" 1,
      "ref.i31",
    ]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "charIsPunct" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W11b: charIsPunct takes exactly one argument"
-- charToUpper c → if c>='a'&&c<='z' then c-32 else c  (result = Char i31 codepoint)
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "charToUpper" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref i31)",
      "i31.get_u",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_char_to_upper" 1,
      "ref.i31",
    ]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "charToUpper" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W11b: charToUpper takes exactly one argument"
-- charToLower c → if c>='A'&&c<='Z' then c+32 else c  (result = Char i31 codepoint)
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "charToLower" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref i31)",
      "i31.get_u",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_char_to_lower" 1,
      "ref.i31",
    ]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "charToLower" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W11b: charToLower takes exactly one argument"
-- W8b Float leaf externs.  #199: intToFloat unboxes its Int arg through the $mdk_unbox_int
-- (→ i64) seam, and floatToInt reboxes its i64 truncation via $mdk_box_int — the SAME seam
-- randomInt/bitAnd use — so full-width Ints outside ±2^30 no longer trap the i31 cast.
-- hashFloat : $float → masked i32 → i31.  randomFloat : Unit arg dropped → $mdk_random_float.
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "intToFloat" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [unboxIntW prog, rtCallW prog "mdk_int_to_float" 1]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "intToFloat" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8b: intToFloat takes exactly one argument"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "floatToInt" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref $float)",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_float_to_int" 1,
      boxIntW prog,
    ]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "floatToInt" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8b: floatToInt takes exactly one argument"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "hashFloat" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $float)", rtCallW prog "mdk_hash_float" 1, "ref.i31"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "hashFloat" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8b: hashFloat takes exactly one argument"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "randomFloat" [u] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d u ++ ["drop", rtCallW prog "mdk_random_float" 0]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "randomFloat" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W8b: randomFloat takes exactly one (Unit) argument"
-- W12 IO host-surface externs.  readFile/fileExists/getEnv take a $str path/name;
-- args takes a Unit (dropped); exit takes an i31 Int.  Each routes through the
-- byte-channel host-import runtime (ioHostRuntimeLines).  readFile returns a Result
-- (ref eq), fileExists a Bool i31, getEnv an Option (ref eq), args a List (ref eq),
-- exit traps (mdk_exit + unreachable, stack-polymorphic like panic).
-- A file extern whose path is an authority takes its grant last
-- (EFFECTS-SEMANTICS §8), and its runtime body hands both to the host, which
-- confines the path (`ioHostRuntimeLines`).
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "readFile" [p, g] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d p
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d g
    ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_read_file_io" 2]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "readFile" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W12: readFile takes exactly one argument and its grant"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "canonicalizePath" [p, g] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d p
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d g
    ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_canonicalize_path_io" 2]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "canonicalizePath" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: canonicalizePath takes exactly one argument and its grant"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "fileExists" [p, g] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d p
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d g
    ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_file_exists_io" 2]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "fileExists" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W12: fileExists takes exactly one argument and its grant"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "getEnv" [n] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d n
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_get_env_io" 1]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "getEnv" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W12: getEnv takes exactly one argument"
-- The stdin readers share one host-side buffer: a Unit argument is dropped, and
-- readExactly's Int is unboxed to the i64 the import takes.
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "readLine" [u] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d u ++ ["drop", rtCallW prog "mdk_read_line_io" 0]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "readLine" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: readLine takes exactly one (Unit) argument"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "readLineOpt" [u] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d u ++ ["drop", rtCallW prog "mdk_read_line_opt_io" 0]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "readLineOpt" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: readLineOpt takes exactly one (Unit) argument"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "readAll" [u] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d u ++ ["drop", rtCallW prog "mdk_read_all_io" 0]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "readAll" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: readAll takes exactly one (Unit) argument"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "readExactly" [n] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d n
    ++ [unboxIntW prog, rtCallW prog "mdk_read_exactly_io" 1]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "readExactly" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: readExactly takes exactly one argument"
-- osEntropyBytes unboxes its Int to the i64 the import takes and builds an Array Int;
-- executablePath takes a Unit (dropped) and answers its String through the result channel.
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "osEntropyBytes" [n] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d n
    ++ [unboxIntW prog, rtCallW prog "mdk_os_entropy_io" 1]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "osEntropyBytes" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: osEntropyBytes takes exactly one argument"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "executablePath" [u] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d u ++ ["drop", rtCallW prog "mdk_executable_path_io" 0]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "executablePath" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: executablePath takes exactly one (Unit) argument"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "args" [u] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d u ++ ["drop", rtCallW prog "mdk_args_io" 0]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "args" args =
  gapLP prog "wasm W12: args takes exactly one (Unit) argument"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "exit" [code] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d code
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref i31)",
      "i31.get_s",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_exit" 1,
      "unreachable",
    ]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "exit" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W12: exit takes exactly one argument"
-- The clock externs: the two reads box the host's f64 seconds; sleepMs unboxes its
-- Int to the i64 the import takes (a non-positive count returns at once, host-side,
-- as medaka_rt.c's mdk_sleep_ms does).
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "wallTimeSec" [u] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d u
    ++ ["drop", rtCallW prog "mdk_wall_time_sec" 0, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "wallTimeSec" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: wallTimeSec takes exactly one (Unit) argument"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "monotonicSec" [u] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d u
    ++ ["drop", rtCallW prog "mdk_monotonic_sec" 0, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "monotonicSec" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: monotonicSec takes exactly one (Unit) argument"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "sleepMs" [n] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d n

-- ioPoll: no wasm host binds descriptor readiness, so a call stops with a coded
-- runtime error.  It traps at run time, not at build time, because the async
-- scheduler (`systemPoller`) names ioPoll and calls it only when a task waits on
-- a descriptor; a clock-only async program must still build.  The arguments are
-- evaluated left to right first, as native evaluates them.
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "ioPoll" [fds, interests, timeout] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d fds
    ++ ["drop"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d interests
    ++ ["drop"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d timeout
    ++ ["drop"]
    ++ wasmTrap
      (progEmit prog)
      "E-WASM-NO-BINDING"
      "ioPoll: descriptor readiness has no wasm binding (Net and Stdin bindings: #3666); build for a native target"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "ioPoll" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: ioPoll takes exactly three arguments"

emitLeafExternRef prog env d "writeFileBytes" _ =

    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d s

-- W10/B5: `panic msg` → stream the coded line `runtime error [E-PANIC]: <msg>\n` to
-- stderr, then `unreachable` (peer of native @mdk_panic / the interp's runtimePanic).
-- The fixed prefix is unrolled to byte-writes; the user message (a $str (ref eq), any
-- expression) is streamed through $mdk_eprint_str (forced via `WasmEmit.useEPut`, which the
-- catalog demands for `panic`), then a trailing newline byte.  `unreachable` is stack-polymorphic, so it
-- validates as any result type.
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "panic" [msg] =
  wasmTrapBytes (progEmit prog) "runtime error [E-PANIC]: "
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d msg
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_eprint_str" 1]
    ++ trapByteInstr (progEmit prog) 10
    ++ ["unreachable"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "panic" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W10: panic takes exactly one argument"
-- Index-16a: `indexError msg` streams the coded line `runtime error
-- [E-INDEX-OOB]: <msg>` to stderr and traps, the same shape `panic` uses above
-- and the same line native's @mdk_oob_msg and the interpreter both print.  The
-- $str rep and $mdk_eprint_str are demanded for `indexError` in the catalog.
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "indexError" [msg] =
  wasmTrapBytes (progEmit prog) "runtime error [E-INDEX-OOB]: "
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d msg
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_eprint_str" 1]
    ++ trapByteInstr (progEmit prog) 10
    ++ ["unreachable"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "indexError" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm Index-16a: indexError takes exactly one argument"
-- #1787: `indexErrorAt idx` raises E-INDEX-OOB naming the offending index, so all
-- three engines print the SAME line.  Dropping it here instead (as sliceError's
-- bounds still are) would redden test/wasm/diff_wasm_modules.sh, which since #531
-- compares stderr and exit code as well as stdout -- w7_array_oob.mdk exists to
-- assert exactly this parity.
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "indexErrorAt" [idx] =
  wasmTrapNum
    (progEmit prog)
    "E-INDEX-OOB"
    "index "
    (emitRefExpr prog env d idx)
    " out of bounds"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "indexErrorAt" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm #1787: indexErrorAt takes exactly one argument"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "indexErrorAtSite" [site, idx] =
  siteExprInstrs prog env d site
    ++ emitLeafExternRef prog env d "indexErrorAt" [idx]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "indexErrorAtSite" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: indexErrorAtSite takes exactly two arguments"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "panicAt" [site, msg] =
  siteExprInstrs prog env d site ++ emitLeafExternRef prog env d "panic" [msg]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "__site__" [CLit (LString f), CLit (LInt line), CLit (LInt col)] =
  emitLitRef
    prog
    (LInt (sitePackedW (progEmit prog) (Loc f line col line (col + 1))))
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "__site__" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: a trap-site literal takes a file, a line and a column"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "panicAt" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: panicAt takes exactly two arguments"
-- #670: `sliceError lo hiIncl` reuses the existing coded E-SLICE-OOB trap (the
-- same fixed text the built-in slice path emits) -- both bound arguments are
-- dropped, where native's @mdk_slice_oob formats them into the line.
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "sliceError" [lo, hi] =
  wasmTrap (progEmit prog) "E-SLICE-OOB" "slice out of bounds"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "sliceError" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm #670: sliceError takes exactly two arguments"
-- The `int`-prefixed bit externs are the originals under unshadowable names.
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "intBitAnd" args =
  emitLeafExternRef prog env d "bitAnd" args
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "intBitOr" args =
  emitLeafExternRef prog env d "bitOr" args
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "intBitXor" args =
  emitLeafExternRef prog env d "bitXor" args
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "intBitNot" args =
  emitLeafExternRef prog env d "bitNot" args
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "intShiftLeft" args =
  emitLeafExternRef prog env d "shiftLeft" args
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "intShiftRight" args =
  emitLeafExternRef prog env d "shiftRight" args
-- stage-A: bitwise / shift externs (Int -> Int -> Int).  Args are (ref eq) boxed Ints;
-- unbox both to i64 via $mdk_unbox_int, apply the i64 op, rebox via $mdk_box_int.
-- The shifts call `$mdk_shift_left`/`$mdk_shift_right` (intRuntimeLines), which
-- define every amount as native's mdk_shift_left/right do: a negative amount panics,
-- 63 or more shifts every bit out, and shiftRight is arithmetic.  shiftLeft's bits
-- past bit 62 are dropped by $mdk_box_int's sign-extend, as native's retag drops them.
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "bitAnd" [a, b] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [unboxIntW prog]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d b
    ++ [unboxIntW prog]
    ++ ["i64.and", boxIntW prog]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "bitAnd" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm stage-A: bitAnd takes exactly two arguments"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "shiftLeft" [a, b] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [unboxIntW prog]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d b
    ++ [unboxIntW prog]
    ++ intShiftCall prog "left"
    ++ [boxIntW prog]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "shiftLeft" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm stage-A: shiftLeft takes exactly two arguments"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "shiftRight" [a, b] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [unboxIntW prog]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d b
    ++ [unboxIntW prog]
    ++ intShiftCall prog "right"
    ++ [boxIntW prog]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "shiftRight" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm stage-A: shiftRight takes exactly two arguments"
-- #101: bitwise completion (mirror llvm mdk_bit_or/xor/not).  bitOr/bitXor are exact
-- i64 two's-complement ops; bitNot n = n xor -1 (== ~n = -n-1, matches native mdk_bit_not
-- for all in-range Ints).  intBitsToFloat reinterprets the unboxed i64 bit pattern as f64.
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "bitOr" [a, b] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [unboxIntW prog]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d b
    ++ [unboxIntW prog]
    ++ ["i64.or", boxIntW prog]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "bitXor" [a, b] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [unboxIntW prog]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d b
    ++ [unboxIntW prog]
    ++ ["i64.xor", boxIntW prog]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "bitNot" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [unboxIntW prog, "i64.const -1", "i64.xor", boxIntW prog]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "intBitsToFloat" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ [unboxIntW prog, "f64.reinterpret_i64", "struct.new $float"]
-- `u8Truncate`/`u16Truncate`/`u32Truncate` keep the low n bits of the Int (a
-- non-negative result, so a U32 above 2^30 reboxes into `$boxint`); the `ToInt`
-- forms are the identity on the word.
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "u8Truncate" [a] =
  emitTruncateRef prog env d "U8" a
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "u16Truncate" [a] =
  emitTruncateRef prog env d "U16" a
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "u32Truncate" [a] =
  emitTruncateRef prog env d "U32" a
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "u8ToInt" [a] = emitRefExpr prog env d a
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "u16ToInt" [a] = emitRefExpr prog env d a
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "u32ToInt" [a] = emitRefExpr prog env d a
-- `i32Truncate` sign-extends the Int's low 32 bits, so a negative `I32` stays an
-- i31 or `$boxint` word like any Int; `i32ToInt` is the identity on that word.
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "i32Truncate" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a ++ [unboxIntW prog, "i64.extend32_s", boxIntW prog]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "i32ToInt" [a] = emitRefExpr prog env d a
-- the `I64` doors keep the 64 bits and change the cell they are read from.
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "i64FromBits" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a ++ unboxU64W ++ ["struct.new $i64"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "i64ToBits" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a ++ unboxI64W ++ ["struct.new $u64"]
-- `u64Truncate` boxes the Int's sign-extended i64, which is its value modulo
-- 2^64; `u64TruncateToInt` reboxes the payload as an Int, and `$mdk_box_int`'s
-- renormalization from bit 62 is exactly "the low 63 bits, bit 62 the sign".
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "u64Truncate" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a ++ [unboxIntW prog, "struct.new $u64"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "u64TruncateToInt" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a ++ unboxU64W ++ [boxIntW prog]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "u64BitAnd" [a, b] =
  emitU64KernelRef prog env d a b "i64.and"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "u64BitOr" [a, b] =
  emitU64KernelRef prog env d a b "i64.or"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "u64BitXor" [a, b] =
  emitU64KernelRef prog env d a b "i64.xor"
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "u64MulHigh" [a, b] =
  emitU64KernelRef prog env d a b (rtCallW prog "mdk_u64_mulhi" 2)
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "u64ShiftLeft" [a, k] =
  emitU64ShiftRef prog env d a k (rtCallW prog "mdk_u64_shl" 2)
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "u64ShiftRight" [a, k] =
  emitU64ShiftRef prog env d a k (rtCallW prog "mdk_u64_shr" 2)
-- #101: libm math externs.  IEEE-exact unary ops → native f64 opcodes (correctly-rounded,
-- byte-match native libm); round → $mdk_round (C round(): half away from zero);
-- transcendentals → JS Math.* host imports; binary pow/atan2/hypot → host imports;
-- floatRem → $mdk_float_rem (WAT fmod, floatRemRuntimeLines).  A $float is
-- unboxed to f64, the op runs, the f64 result reboxes into a fresh (struct $float).
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "sqrt" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ ["f64.sqrt", "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "floor" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ ["f64.floor", "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "ceil" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ ["f64.ceil", "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "trunc" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ ["f64.trunc", "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "round" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_round" 1, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "cbrt" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_cbrt" 1, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "exp" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_exp" 1, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "log" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_log" 1, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "log2" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_log2" 1, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "log10" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_log10" 1, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "sin" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_sin" 1, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "cos" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_cos" 1, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "tan" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_tan" 1, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "asin" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_asin" 1, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "acos" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_acos" 1, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "atan" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_atan" 1, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "sinh" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_sinh" 1, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "cosh" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_cosh" 1, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "tanh" [a] =
  floatArgW prog env d a ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_tanh" 1, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "pow" [a, b] =
  floatArgW prog env d a
    ++ floatArgW prog env d b
    ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_pow" 2, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "atan2" [a, b] =
  floatArgW prog env d a
    ++ floatArgW prog env d b
    ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_atan2" 2, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "hypot" [a, b] =
  floatArgW prog env d a
    ++ floatArgW prog env d b
    ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_hypot" 2, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog env d "floatRem" [a, b] =
  floatArgW prog env d a
    ++ floatArgW prog env d b
    ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_float_rem" 2, "struct.new $float"]
emitLeafExternRef prog _ _ name _ =
  gapLP prog ("wasm W8: unsupported leaf extern '" ++ name ++ "'")

-- #101: unbox a boxed $float argument to a raw f64 on the WAT stack.  Shared by every
-- libm math arm above (unary opcode, host-import transcendental, and binary).
floatArgW : Prog -> Env -> Int -> CExpr -> List String
floatArgW prog env d a =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a ++ ["ref.cast (ref $float)", "struct.get $float 0"]

-- ── W10: Array intrinsic externs ─────────────────────────────────────────────
-- All work over `$arr = (array (mut (ref eq)))`.  Index/size args are i31 Ints
-- (unboxed to i32); element args are (ref eq).  NOTE the arg orders (runtime.mdk):
--   arrayLength    arr               → array.len → i31
--   arrayGetUnsafe idx arr           → (idx FIRST) cast arr, array.get
--   arrayMake      size init         → array.new $arr (init, size)
--   arrayMakeWith  size f            → alloc size, loop i: array.set (f applied to i)
--   arrayCopy      arr               → array.new (len) + array.copy
--   arraySetUnsafe idx val arr       → array.set; result Unit (i31 0)
--   arrayFromList  list              → alloc (length list), loop-fill from cons cells
emitArrayExternRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> String -> List CExpr -> List String
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "arrayLength" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a ++ ["ref.cast (ref $arr)", "array.len", "ref.i31"]
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "arrayLength" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W10: arrayLength takes exactly one argument"
-- idx is the FIRST arg, the array the SECOND.  Cast arr, unbox idx, array.get.
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "arrayGetUnsafe" [i, a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $arr)"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d i
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_s"]
    ++ ["array.get $arr", "ref.as_non_null"]
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "arrayGetUnsafe" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W10: arrayGetUnsafe takes exactly two arguments"
-- size FIRST, init SECOND.  array.new takes (init, size) from the stack.
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "arrayMake" [n, init] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d init
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d n
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_s"]
    ++ ["array.new $arr"]
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "arrayMake" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W10: arrayMake takes exactly two arguments"
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "arrayCopy" [a] =
  let sfx = intToString d
  let srcL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexarr" sfx
  let dstL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__raarr" sfx
  let nL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexn" sfx
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $arr)", "local.set " ++ srcL]
    ++ [
      "local.get " ++ srcL,
      "ref.as_non_null",
      "array.len",
      "local.set " ++ nL,
    ]
    ++ [
      "i32.const 0",
      "ref.i31",
      "local.get " ++ nL,
      "array.new $arr",
      "local.set " ++ dstL,
    ]
    ++ [
      "local.get " ++ dstL,
      "ref.as_non_null",
      "i32.const 0",
      "local.get " ++ srcL,
      "ref.as_non_null",
      "i32.const 0",
      "local.get " ++ nL,
      "array.copy $arr $arr",
    ]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ dstL, "ref.as_non_null"]
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "arrayCopy" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W10: arrayCopy takes exactly one argument"
-- idx, val, arr.  array.set takes (arrayref, index, value); result Unit (i31 0).
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "arraySetUnsafe" [i, v, a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $arr)"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d i
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_s"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d v
    ++ ["array.set $arr", "i32.const 0", "ref.i31"]
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "arraySetUnsafe" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W10: arraySetUnsafe takes exactly three arguments"
-- size FIRST, f SECOND.  Alloc size slots (init 0), then loop i=0..n-1:
-- array.set arr i (apply f [i]).  f is applied via the universal $__mdk_apply.
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "arrayMakeWith" [n, f] =
  let sfx = intToString d
  let arrL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexarr" sfx
  let iL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexi" sfx
  let nL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexn" sfx
  let fL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexf" sfx
  emitRefExpr prog env d n
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_s", "local.set " ++ nL]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d f
    ++ ["local.set " ++ fL]
    ++ [
      "i32.const 0",
      "ref.i31",
      "local.get " ++ nL,
      "array.new $arr",
      "local.set " ++ arrL,
    ]
    ++ ["i32.const 0", "local.set " ++ iL]
    ++ ["block $aexd" ++ sfx, "loop $aexl" ++ sfx]
    ++ [
      "local.get " ++ iL,
      "local.get " ++ nL,
      "i32.ge_s",
      "br_if $aexd" ++ sfx,
    ]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ arrL, "ref.as_non_null", "local.get " ++ iL]
    -- value = f applied to (i31 i): build a 1-element $argarr, call $__mdk_apply
    ++ [
      "local.get " ++ fL,
      "local.get " ++ iL,
      "ref.i31",
      "array.new_fixed $argarr 1",
      rtCallW prog "__mdk_apply" 2,
    ]
    ++ ["array.set $arr"]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ iL, "i32.const 1", "i32.add", "local.set " ++ iL]
    ++ ["br $aexl" ++ sfx, "end", "end"]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ arrL, "ref.as_non_null"]
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "arrayMakeWith" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W10: arrayMakeWith takes exactly two arguments"
-- count the list (a $C_Cons chain ending in an i31 Nil), alloc that many slots,
-- walk the chain again filling cells in order.  Two-pass over a $C_Cons cursor.
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "arrayFromList" [lst] =
  let sfx = intToString d
  let arrL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexarr" sfx
  let iL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexi" sfx
  let nL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexn" sfx
  let curL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexlst" sfx
  -- pass 1: length.  cursor = lst; while not i31: n++, cursor = tail.
  emitRefExpr prog env d lst
    ++ ["local.set " ++ curL]
    ++ ["i32.const 0", "local.set " ++ nL]
    ++ ["block $aexcd" ++ sfx, "loop $aexcl" ++ sfx]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ curL, "ref.test (ref i31)", "br_if $aexcd" ++ sfx]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ nL, "i32.const 1", "i32.add", "local.set " ++ nL]
    ++ [
      "local.get " ++ curL,
      "ref.cast (ref $C_Cons)",
      "struct.get $C_Cons 2",
      "local.set " ++ curL,
    ]
    ++ ["br $aexcl" ++ sfx, "end", "end"]
    -- alloc n slots
    ++ [
      "i32.const 0",
      "ref.i31",
      "local.get " ++ nL,
      "array.new $arr",
      "local.set " ++ arrL,
    ]
    -- pass 2: fill.  cursor = lst; i = 0; while not i31: set arr[i]=head, i++, cursor=tail.
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d lst
    ++ ["local.set " ++ curL]
    ++ ["i32.const 0", "local.set " ++ iL]
    ++ ["block $aexfd" ++ sfx, "loop $aexfl" ++ sfx]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ curL, "ref.test (ref i31)", "br_if $aexfd" ++ sfx]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ arrL, "ref.as_non_null", "local.get " ++ iL]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ curL, "ref.cast (ref $C_Cons)", "struct.get $C_Cons 1"]
    ++ ["array.set $arr"]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ iL, "i32.const 1", "i32.add", "local.set " ++ iL]
    ++ [
      "local.get " ++ curL,
      "ref.cast (ref $C_Cons)",
      "struct.get $C_Cons 2",
      "local.set " ++ curL,
    ]
    ++ ["br $aexfl" ++ sfx, "end", "end"]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ arrL, "ref.as_non_null"]
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "arrayFromList" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm W10: arrayFromList takes exactly one argument"
-- stage-A: arrayBlit src srcOff dst dstOff len — copies `len` elements from src[srcOff..]
-- into dst[dstOff..] using `array.copy $arr $arr`.  Arg order from runtime.mdk: src, srcOff,
-- dst, dstOff, len.  Wasm array.copy takes: [dst, dstOff, src, srcOff, len] (all i32).
-- Int args (offsets/len) are i31 small ints; unbox with i31.get_s to i32.  Result = Unit.
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "arrayBlit" [src, srcOff, dst, dstOff, len] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d dst
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $arr)"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d dstOff
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_s"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d src
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $arr)"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d srcOff
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_s"]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d len
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_s"]
    ++ ["array.copy $arr $arr", "i32.const 0", "ref.i31"]
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "arrayBlit" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm stage-A: arrayBlit takes exactly five arguments"
-- stage-A: arrayFill val arr — sets every element of arr to val via a loop.
-- Uses the $__aex* W7 scratch locals (w7Local).
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "arrayFill" [val, arr] =
  let sfx = intToString d
  let arrL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexarr" sfx
  let iL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexi" sfx
  let nL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexn" sfx
  let vL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexv" sfx
  emitRefExpr prog env d arr
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $arr)", "local.set " ++ arrL]
    ++ [
      "local.get " ++ arrL,
      "ref.as_non_null",
      "array.len",
      "local.set " ++ nL,
    ]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d val
    ++ ["local.set " ++ vL]
    ++ ["i32.const 0", "local.set " ++ iL]
    ++ ["block $afld" ++ sfx, "loop $afll" ++ sfx]
    ++ [
      "local.get " ++ iL,
      "local.get " ++ nL,
      "i32.ge_s",
      "br_if $afld" ++ sfx,
    ]
    ++ [
      "local.get " ++ arrL,
      "ref.as_non_null",
      "local.get " ++ iL,
      "local.get " ++ vL,
    ]
    ++ ["array.set $arr"]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ iL, "i32.const 1", "i32.add", "local.set " ++ iL]
    ++ ["br $afll" ++ sfx, "end", "end"]
    ++ ["i32.const 0", "ref.i31"]
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "arrayFill" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm stage-A: arrayFill takes exactly two arguments"
-- stage-B: floatToBytes64 : Float -> Array Int — reinterpret the boxed $float's f64 to
-- an i64 via i64.reinterpret_f64, then extract 8 bytes BIG-ENDIAN (byte 0 = bits>>56,
-- byte 7 = bits&0xFF) into a fresh 8-element $arr, each byte a boxed Int.  Matches
-- runtime/medaka_rt.c:mdk_float_to_bytes64 exactly (cell[i+1] = byte at (bits>>(8*(7-i)))&0xFF).
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "floatToBytes64" [f] =
  let sfx = intToString d
  let arrL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexarr" sfx
  let bitsL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexbits" sfx
  emitRefExpr prog env d f
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref $float)",
      "struct.get $float 0",
      "i64.reinterpret_f64",
      "local.set " ++ bitsL,
    ]
    -- alloc 8 slots (placeholder element, overwritten below)
    ++ [
      "i32.const 0",
      "ref.i31",
      "i32.const 8",
      "array.new $arr",
      "local.set " ++ arrL,
    ]
    ++ flatMap (i => f2bByteSet prog arrL bitsL i) [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ arrL, "ref.as_non_null"]
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "floatToBytes64" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm stage-B: floatToBytes64 takes exactly one argument"
-- stage-B: bytesToFloat64 : Array Int -> Int -> Float — read 8 bytes BIG-ENDIAN from the
-- $arr starting at index `off`, assemble an i64 (byte at off+0 → bits 56..63), then
-- f64.reinterpret_i64 + box into a $float.  Matches runtime/medaka_rt.c:mdk_bytes_to_float64.
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "bytesToFloat64" [arr, off] =
  let sfx = intToString d
  let arrL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexarr" sfx
  let offL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexi" sfx
  let bitsL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__aexbits" sfx
  emitRefExpr prog env d arr
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $arr)", "local.set " ++ arrL]
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d off
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_s", "local.set " ++ offL]
    ++ ["i64.const 0", "local.set " ++ bitsL]
    ++ flatMap
      (i => b2fByteRead prog arrL offL bitsL i)
      [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ bitsL, "f64.reinterpret_i64", "struct.new $float"]
emitArrayExternRef prog env d "bytesToFloat64" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm stage-B: bytesToFloat64 takes exactly two arguments"
emitArrayExternRef prog _ _ name _ =
  gapLP prog ("wasm W10: unsupported array extern '" ++ name ++ "'")

-- ── the `ByteBlock` builtin's primitives ──────────────────────────────────
-- A block is a bare `$u8arr`; the four that loop or copy call into
-- byteBlockRuntimeLines, the four that don't are inline.  Arg orders follow
-- stdlib/runtime.mdk (index/size FIRST, block LAST), mirroring the $arr family:
--   byteBlockMake         n            → array.new $u8arr (0, n)
--   byteBlockLength       b            → array.len → i31
--   byteBlockGetUnsafe    i b          → (i FIRST) cast b, array.get_u → i31
--   byteBlockSetUnsafe    i v b        → array.set (low 8 bits of v); result Unit
--   byteBlockCopyUnsafe   n b          → $mdk_bb_copy (a COPY — freeze's engine half)
--   byteBlockBlit         s so d do n  → array.copy (memmove-equivalent; may overlap)
--   byteBlockFromIntArray a            → $mdk_bb_from_int_array
--   byteBlockToIntArray   b            → $mdk_bb_to_int_array
--   byteBlockFromString   s            → $mdk_bb_from_string
--   byteBlockToString     b            → $mdk_bb_to_string
--   byteBlockWriteStdout  b            → $mdk_bb_write_stdout
--   sha256Native          b            → $mdk_sha256
emitByteBlockExternRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  List CExpr ->
  List String
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockMake" [n] =
  ["i32.const 0"] ++ bbIntArg prog env d n ++ ["array.new $u8arr"]
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockMake" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: byteBlockMake takes exactly one argument"
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockLength" [b] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d b ++ ["ref.cast (ref $u8arr)", "array.len", "ref.i31"]
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockLength" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: byteBlockLength takes exactly one argument"
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockGetUnsafe" [i, b] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d b
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $u8arr)"]
    ++ bbIntArg prog env d i
    ++ ["array.get_u $u8arr", "ref.i31"]
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockGetUnsafe" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: byteBlockGetUnsafe takes exactly two arguments"
-- The i8 slot keeps the low eight bits of the stored i32 on its own, so the
-- explicit mask is what makes the 0..255 domain READABLE here rather than a
-- property of the array type; both agree with native's (unsigned char) cast.
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockSetUnsafe" [i, v, b] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d b
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $u8arr)"]
    ++ bbIntArg prog env d i
    ++ bbIntArg prog env d v
    ++ ["i32.const 255", "i32.and"]
    ++ ["array.set $u8arr", "i32.const 0", "ref.i31"]
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockSetUnsafe" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: byteBlockSetUnsafe takes exactly three arguments"
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockCopyUnsafe" [n, b] =
  bbIntArg prog env d n
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d b
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $u8arr)", rtCallW prog "mdk_bb_copy" 2]
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockCopyUnsafe" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: byteBlockCopyUnsafe takes exactly two arguments"
-- array.copy takes (dst, dstOff, src, srcOff, len), so the destination operands
-- are pushed before the source ones even though the extern's argument order is
-- source-first; `byteBlockSetUnsafe` above reorders for the same reason.  The
-- copy is overlap-safe by the WasmGC spec, matching native's memmove.
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockBlit" [src, srcOff, dst, dstOff, len] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d dst
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $u8arr)"]
    ++ bbIntArg prog env d dstOff
    ++ emitRefExpr prog env d src
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $u8arr)"]
    ++ bbIntArg prog env d srcOff
    ++ bbIntArg prog env d len
    ++ ["array.copy $u8arr $u8arr", "i32.const 0", "ref.i31"]
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockBlit" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: byteBlockBlit takes exactly five arguments"
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockFromIntArray" [a] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d a
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $arr)", rtCallW prog "mdk_bb_from_int_array" 1]
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockFromIntArray" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: byteBlockFromIntArray takes exactly one argument"
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockToIntArray" [b] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d b
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $u8arr)", rtCallW prog "mdk_bb_to_int_array" 1]
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockToIntArray" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: byteBlockToIntArray takes exactly one argument"
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockFromString" [sv] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d sv
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)", rtCallW prog "mdk_bb_from_string" 1]
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockFromString" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: byteBlockFromString takes exactly one argument"
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockToString" [b] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d b
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $u8arr)", rtCallW prog "mdk_bb_to_string" 1]
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockToString" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: byteBlockToString takes exactly one argument"
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "sha256Native" [b] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d b
    ++ ["ref.cast (ref $u8arr)", rtCallW prog "mdk_sha256" 1]
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "sha256Native" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: sha256Native takes exactly one argument"
-- byteBlockWriteStdout: writes the block's bytes to stdout byte-for-byte via
-- the same $mdk_write_byte host import putStr's $mdk_print_str loop uses,
-- then returns Unit -- the operand is a $u8arr, so this dispatches through
-- the byte-block family rather than the WasmStr family's $str-typed IO externs.
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockWriteStdout" [b] =
  emitRefExpr prog env d b
    ++ [
      "ref.cast (ref $u8arr)",
      rtCallW prog "mdk_bb_write_stdout" 1,
      "i32.const 0",
      "ref.i31",
    ]
emitByteBlockExternRef prog env d "byteBlockWriteStdout" _ =
  gapLP prog "wasm: byteBlockWriteStdout takes exactly one argument"
emitByteBlockExternRef prog _ _ name _ =
  gapLP prog ("wasm: unsupported byte-block extern '" ++ name ++ "'")

-- An Int argument as a raw i32.  The $arr family takes the i31 fast path, which
-- traps on an Int outside the i31 range; native has no boxed Int at all, so a
-- block index, length, or stored byte built from a large Int would diverge rather
-- than agree.  Route through $mdk_unbox_int (i31 OR $boxint) and narrow.
bbIntArg : Prog -> Env -> Int -> CExpr -> List String
bbIntArg prog env d e =
  emitRefExpr prog env d e ++ [unboxIntW prog, "i32.wrap_i64"]

-- stage-B helpers: set arr[i] = boxed byte ((bits >> (8*(7-i))) & 0xFF); big-endian.
f2bByteSet : Prog -> String -> String -> Int -> List String
f2bByteSet prog arrL bitsL i = [
  "local.get " ++ arrL,
  "ref.as_non_null",
  "i32.const " ++ intToString i,
  "local.get " ++ bitsL,
  "i64.const " ++ intToString (8 * (7 - i)),
  "i64.shr_u",
  "i64.const 255",
  "i64.and",
  boxIntW prog,
  "array.set $arr",
]
-- read arr[off+i] (a boxed Int 0..255), shift to its big-endian position, OR into bits.
b2fByteRead : Prog -> String -> String -> String -> Int -> List String
b2fByteRead prog arrL offL bitsL i = [
  "local.get " ++ arrL,
  "ref.as_non_null",
  "local.get " ++ offL,
  "i32.const " ++ intToString i,
  "i32.add",
  "array.get $arr",
  "ref.as_non_null",
  unboxIntW prog,
  "i64.const 255",
  "i64.and",
  "i64.const " ++ intToString (8 * (7 - i)),
  "i64.shl",
  "local.get " ++ bitsL,
  "i64.or",
  "local.set " ++ bitsL,
]

-- #35 (wasm peer of llvm_emit's emitCtorApp): an APPLIED constructor, dispatched on
-- SATURATION.  This arm must not call `emitCtorConstruct` unconditionally, or an
-- UNDER-applied ctor (`Bin OAdd` for arity-3 `Bin`) emits a `struct.new $S_Bin`
-- with only 1 of its 3 fields on the stack — the identical shape (and identical
-- silent wrong-value miscompile: `check` accepts, `run` is right, `build` is garbage)
-- as the LLVM bug, and the same shape as the pre-W9b bare-ctor bug that
-- emitCtorEtaClosure was introduced to fix.  The eta-wrapper IS the missing piece: an
-- under-applied ctor is just its full-arity eta CLOSURE applied to the args it does
-- have, and `$__mdk_apply` already turns that into a `$mdk_pap` (§4 universal apply:
-- exact / under→PAP / over→saturate+reapply).  So no ctor-specific PAP forwarder is
-- needed here — unlike LLVM, whose call sites take a lifted define, wasm reads arity
-- from the VALUE.  Over-application is unreachable for a well-typed program but falls
-- out of the same path safely.  SATURATED stays `emitCtorConstruct`, byte-identical.
emitCtorApp : Prog -> Env -> Int -> String -> List CExpr -> List String
emitCtorApp prog env d ctor args =
  if listLen args == ctorArity prog ctor then
    emitCtorConstruct prog env d ctor args
  else
    emitCtorEtaClosure prog ctor
      ++ emitArgsArray prog env d args
      ++ [rtCallW prog "__mdk_apply" 2]

-- an indirect application: emit the head (a (ref eq) closure value), pack the args
-- into an $argarr, and `call $__mdk_apply` — which dispatches on the closure's arity
-- (exact / under→PAP / over→saturate+reapply).  This makes over/under/exact uniform
-- and reads arity from the value (never a name-keyed table), per WASMGC-DESIGN §11.
emitIndirectApp : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  CExpr ->
  List CExpr ->
  CallEndW ->
  List String
emitIndirectApp prog env d hd args end =
  let hi = emitRefExpr prog env d hd
  let arr = emitArgsArray prog env d args
  hi ++ arr ++ [callFnW prog end "__mdk_apply" 2]

-- How an application's final call is made: for its value, which the code after it
-- consumes, or as the tail call that replaces the enclosing function's frame.
data CallEndW = CallValueW | CallTailW

-- the instruction that makes a call of `$<target>`
callInstrW : CallEndW -> String -> String
callInstrW CallValueW target = "call $" ++ target
callInstrW CallTailW target = "return_call $" ++ target

-- what follows a value an application computes without a call to end on
endValueW : CallEndW -> List String
endValueW CallValueW = []
endValueW CallTailW = ["return"]

-- build an $argarr holding the emitted args, in order.  `array.new_fixed` takes the
-- element values from the stack — so emit all args (each leaves a (ref eq)) then one
-- array.new_fixed of the right length.  Zero args → an empty array.
emitArgsArray : Prog -> Env -> Int -> List CExpr -> List String
emitArgsArray prog env d args =
  let n = listLen args
  let argInstrs = flatMap (a => emitRefExpr prog env d a) args
  argInstrs ++ ["array.new_fixed $argarr " ++ intToString n]

-- ── §4.2 tail-position emission (guaranteed TCO) ─────────────────────────────
-- ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- Stage-1 WasmGC self-recursive TMC (destination-passing loop) — WASMGC-TRMC-DESIGN §7
-- ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- When a top-level non-dict self-recursive define is `trmcEligible` for the self-only
-- cons/ctor-tail shape (a), we emit the body as a LOOP that conses into a mutable
-- destination cell instead of issuing the stack-growing recursive call.  The
-- destination-passing context (the self-ref, arity, the param locals, the loop/exit
-- labels, the uniform cell struct name + recursive-field index) is carried in a
-- `FnCtx` of the `Prog` the body is emitted with, so tail descent (emitRefTail / emitDecisionTail) can
-- redirect its cons/ctor/base leaves without threading a new argument through every arm.
-- The ENGINE never sees a recursive `call`/`return_call` to the self fn inside the loop
-- (the decisive "TMC fired" property): a cons/ctor leaf builds a cell, struct.sets it
-- into the parent's recursive slot, advances the dest, recomputes the self-call args
-- into the loop's param locals, and `br`s to the loop header.
-- WTrmcOn self arity pslots ctorSet loopLbl exitLbl — `ctorSet` is the fn's
-- distinct (ctorName, selfFieldIdx) leaf-ctor pairs in first-seen clause order.
-- A singleton set emits exactly the historical uniform-ctor code; a MIXED set
-- (P3, TMC-parity arc — LLVM always handled mixed ctors) additionally tracks
-- WHICH ctor the current dest cell is in the i32 local $__tmc_dctor (its index
-- into ctorSet) and link sites dispatch on it (ref.cast to that ctor's struct +
-- struct.set at its recursive field).
-- #712: `isBuiltinList` (the 5th field) records whether this fn's cons leaves are
-- the built-in `h :: t` (→ reserved `$C_Cons`) vs a user ctor named `Cons`
-- (→ `$CU_Cons`).  Homogeneous per fn, so the base leaf's parent-link
-- (emitWasmTrmcBase) reads it from here rather than re-deriving from the ctor name.
-- the loop-local names used by the destination-passing emit.  `$__tmc_head` holds the
-- first cell (the result returned at exit); `$__tmc_dest` holds the cell whose recursive
-- slot the NEXT leaf must fill; `$__tmc_first` is 1 until the first cell is built.
-- `$__tmc_t<k>` are arg-recompute temps (one per param) so an arg may read an old param
-- before any slot is overwritten.
wTrmcHeadL : String
wTrmcHeadL = "$__tmc_head"
wTrmcDestL : String
wTrmcDestL = "$__tmc_dest"
wTrmcFirstL : String
wTrmcFirstL = "$__tmc_first"
wTrmcTempL : Int -> String
wTrmcTempL k = "$__tmc_t" ++ intToString k
wTrmcDctorL : String
wTrmcDctorL = "$__tmc_dctor"

-- Emit `body` in TAIL position of the enclosing function.  Descends into the tails
