-- of if/let/block/decision so the syntactic tail call is found wherever it sits.
-- A tail call emits `return_call` (saturated direct call to a known top-level fn) or
-- `return_call $__mdk_apply` (indirect / non-saturated — the universal apply itself
-- tail-dispatches via return_call_ref).  These are guaranteed constant-stack by the
-- engine (Wasm 3.0 / Node 24).  A NON-call tail leaf emits its value then `return`.
-- Calls to host imports are NOT reachable as tail calls here (IO is W6), so the
-- "never tail a host import" rule is vacuously satisfied this slice.
-- `arity` = the enclosing fn's param count (unused today; kept for symmetry with
-- the LLVM self-call walk).
emitRefTail : Prog -> Env -> Int -> CExpr -> List String
emitRefTail prog env arity e = match (progFnCtx prog).trmc
  WTrmcOn self sarity pslots ctorSet _ loopLbl exitLbl =>
    -- TMC active: descend the structural tail wrappers (if/let/block/decision) with the
    -- context STILL LIVE so their inner leaves re-enter here; redirect every LEAF
    -- (cons/ctor-tail, plain self-call, or base) to the destination-passing emit.
    if isWTrmcWrapper e then
      emitRefTailWrap prog env arity e
    else
      emitWasmTrmcLeaf prog env self sarity pslots ctorSet loopLbl exitLbl e
  WTrmcOff => match (progFnCtx prog).disp
    WDispOn root loopLbl rootArity members =>
      -- Stage-2/3 (b′) active: descend the structural tail wrappers with the dispatch
      -- context LIVE; redirect SPINE cons leaves + base leaves to the dest globals.
      if isWTrmcWrapper e then
        emitRefTailWrap prog env arity e
      else
        emitWDispLeaf prog env root loopLbl rootArity members e
    WDispOff => emitRefTailWrap prog env arity e

-- a (b′) tail leaf: a peeled spine cons `<h1> :: … :: <member> <sat>` → dest-link each
-- cell + return_call the target (the root's inner loop for the root, the member fn
-- itself otherwise — only the root carries a reset wrapper); a saturated tail-call to
-- a group member → ordinary return_call (the dest threads through untouched); any
-- other leaf (base, e.g. `[]`) → close the dest + return $g_tmc_head.
emitWDispLeaf : Prog ->
  Env ->
  String ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  List String ->
  CExpr ->
  List String
emitWDispLeaf prog env root loopLbl rootArity members (e@(CBinPrim "::" _ _ _ _)) =
  match wDispSpineParts prog (f => contains f members) e
    Some (heads, f, args) =>
      emitWDispSpineCons
        prog
        env
        root
        (if f == root then loopLbl else f)
        heads
        args
    None =>
      -- a cons that does not bottom in a saturated group call (the spine terminator
      -- can be a cons onto a non-spine value): group validation guaranteed it is
      -- member-free, so it is a BASE value — close the dest + return the head global.
      emitWDispBase prog env root e
emitWDispLeaf prog env root loopLbl rootArity members other =
  if wDispIsSatRootCall prog root rootArity other then match flattenApp other []
    -- a bare saturated tail-call to root: emit the args + return_call the inner loop
    -- (skip the reset wrapper, which would re-zero the in-flight dest).

    (_, args) =>
      flatMap (a => emitRefExpr prog env 0 a) args
        ++ [callFnW prog CallTailW (gname loopLbl) (listLen args)]
  else match flattenApp other []
    (CVar f0 _, args) =>
      let f = canonFn prog f0
      if isFtSentinel f0 then
        ftSentinelInstrs f0
      else
        emitWDispTailOrBase prog env root members f other
    _ => emitWDispBase prog env root other

-- a non-cons, non-root-bare leaf: an EXACT tail-call to another group member →
-- ordinary return_call (dest untouched; the member's own redirected leaves will close
-- it); anything else → a base value — dest-close.  (An unsaturated or non-member call
-- here cannot thread the dest, so it must terminate the spine as a value.)
emitWDispTailOrBase : Prog ->
  Env ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  String ->
  CExpr ->
  List String
emitWDispTailOrBase prog env root members f e = match appParts e
  (_, _, mode) =>
    if contains f members && isExactCall mode then
      emitAppTail prog env 0 e
    else
      emitWDispBase prog env root e

-- the ordinary tail descent (TMC-inactive, or the wrapper arms while TMC is active).
emitRefTailWrap : Prog -> Env -> Int -> CExpr -> List String
emitRefTailWrap prog env arity (CIf c t f) =
  let ci = emitRefExpr prog env 0 c ++ conditionW prog
  let ti = emitRefTail prog env arity t
  let fi = emitRefTail prog env arity f
  ci ++ ["if"] ++ indent ti ++ ["else"] ++ indent fi ++ ["end", "unreachable"]
emitRefTailWrap prog env arity (CLet recF pat e1 e2) =
  let (prefix, env2) = emitLetBindingW prog env 0 recF pat e1
  prefix ++ emitRefTail prog env2 arity e2
emitRefTailWrap prog env arity (node@(CLetGroup binds body)) =
  valueLines
    (refOnlyValueW prog node (() =>
      emitLetGroupWith
        prog
        env
        0
        (env2 b => emitRefTail prog env2 arity b)
        binds
        body))
emitRefTailWrap prog env arity (CBlock stmts) =
  emitBlockTail prog env arity stmts
emitRefTailWrap prog env arity (node@(CDecision scrut arms tree)) =
  valueLines
    (refOnlyValueW prog node (() =>
      emitDecisionTail prog env arity scrut arms tree))
emitRefTailWrap prog env arity (app@(CApp _ _ _)) =
  emitAppTail prog env arity app
-- a bare fall-through sentinel in tail position lowers to its sentinel instrs (a `br`
-- to the clause label, or a trap) — NOT value+return (the generic CVar arm would
-- append a dead `return` after an unconditional branch, leaving the stack ill-typed).
emitRefTailWrap prog env arity (e@(CVar x _)) =
  if not (rawProgramW prog) && isFtSentinel x then
    ftSentinelInstrs x
  else
    emitRefExpr prog env 0 e ++ ["return"]
emitRefTailWrap prog env arity other =
  emitRefExpr prog env 0 other ++ ["return"]

-- a structural tail WRAPPER (if/let/block/decision) whose tail descends to leaves —
-- vs a LEAF (cons/ctor/self-call/base) that TMC redirects.  These are emitRefTailWrap's
-- wrapper arms less a let-group and a recursive or destructuring let, which TMC
-- takes as a base leaf: computed as a value and stored into the destination.
isWTrmcWrapper : CExpr -> Bool
isWTrmcWrapper (CIf _ _ _) = True
isWTrmcWrapper (CLet False (PVar _ _ _) _ _) = True
isWTrmcWrapper (CLet False PWild _ _) = True
isWTrmcWrapper (CBlock _) = True
isWTrmcWrapper (CDecision _ _ _) = True
isWTrmcWrapper _ = False

-- a TMC tail leaf: an eligible cons/ctor-tail conses into the destination + loops; a
-- bare saturated plain self-call recomputes its args + loops (iterate-on-shorter-list);
-- any other leaf is the BASE — store it into the current destination + exit.
emitWasmTrmcLeaf : Prog ->
  Env ->
  SelfRef ->
  Int ->
  List String ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  String ->
  String ->
  CExpr ->
  List String
emitWasmTrmcLeaf prog env self arity pslots ctorSet loopLbl exitLbl e =
  if isCtorTail (c => isCtor prog c) (c => ctorArity prog c) self arity e then
    -- #712: `ctorTailIsCons e` distinguishes the built-in `h :: t` (reserved
    -- `$C_Cons`) from a user ctor named `Cons` (remapped `$CU_Cons`); a whole TRMC
    -- function's cons-cell leaves are homogeneous (one return type), so this leaf's
    -- verdict also governs the parent link.
    emitWasmTrmcCtor
      prog
      env
      self
      arity
      pslots
      ctorSet
      (ctorTailIsCons e)
      (ctorTailName e)
      (ctorTailSelfIdx e)
      loopLbl
      (ctorTailLeadFields e)
      (consTailArgs e)
  else if isSelfSatApp self arity e then
    emitWasmTrmcTailCall prog env pslots loopLbl e
  else
    emitWasmTrmcBase prog env exitLbl e

-- cons/ctor leaf: build THIS leaf's ctor cell with its NON-recursive (leading) fields
-- + a placeholder in the recursive slot, link it into the parent's recursive slot (or
-- seed $__tmc_head on the first cell), advance the destination to this cell, recompute
-- the self-call args into the loop's param locals, and br to the loop header.  NO
-- recursive call is emitted.
--   • first cell  → $__tmc_head := cell ; $__tmc_first := 0
--   • later cells → struct.set <parent ctor's struct> $__tmc_dest <its selfIdx+1> cell
--     (the PARENT may be a different ctor than this leaf's — wTrmcLinkParent
--     dispatches on $__tmc_dctor when the fn's leaf-ctor set is mixed)
--   • always      → $__tmc_dest := cell (+ record THIS ctor's set-index in
--     $__tmc_dctor when mixed)
-- The recursive slot is `(mut (ref eq))` (Stage 0), seeded here with a safe i31 nil
-- placeholder (never dereferenced — it is overwritten by the next iteration's struct.set,
-- or stays as the cell's tail which the BASE leaf fills before exit).
emitWasmTrmcCtor : Prog ->
  Env ->
  SelfRef ->
  Int ->
  List String ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  Bool ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  List CExpr ->
  List CExpr ->
  List String
emitWasmTrmcCtor prog env self arity pslots ctorSet isBuiltinList ctorName selfIdx loopLbl leadFields args =
  let cellStruct = trmcCellStruct isBuiltinList ctorName
  -- #712/S0: a built-in `::` leaf pins the reserved Cons ordinal; a user ctor leaf
  -- keys off the table (declaration order), same split as the cell struct id above.
  let tag =
    ["i32.const " ++ intToString (trmcCellOrdinal isBuiltinList prog ctorName)]
  let leadInstrs = flatMap (a => emitRefExpr prog env 0 a) leadFields
  -- placeholder for the recursive slot (overwritten next iter / by the base leaf).
  let placeholder = ["i32.const 1", "ref.i31"]
  let buildCell =
    tag ++ leadInstrs ++ placeholder ++ ["struct.new $" ++ cellStruct]
  -- stash new cell in temp 0; link into prev dest (or seed head); advance dest := new.
  let stashNew = buildCell ++ ["local.set " ++ wTrmcTempL 0]
  let cellVal = ["local.get " ++ wTrmcTempL 0, "ref.as_non_null"]
  let linkSet = wTrmcLinkParent isBuiltinList ctorSet cellVal
  let linkSeed = [
    "local.get " ++ wTrmcTempL 0,
    "local.set " ++ wTrmcHeadL,
    "i32.const 0",
    "local.set " ++ wTrmcFirstL,
  ]
  let linkInstrs =
    ["local.get " ++ wTrmcFirstL, "if"]
      ++ indent linkSeed
      ++ ["else"]
      ++ indent linkSet
      ++ ["end"]
  let advance =
    ["local.get " ++ wTrmcTempL 0, "local.set " ++ wTrmcDestL]
      ++ wTrmcRecordDctor ctorSet ctorName
  -- recompute the self-call args into temps (an arg may read an old param), then store
  -- into the param slots, then loop.  Args occupy temps 1..arity (temp 0 = the cell).
  -- A dict-carrying (CDict-headed) self-call's args cover only the VALUE params; its
  -- leading dict slots are loop-invariant (identity-forwarded routes, trmc_analysis
  -- dictRoutesForwarded) — store into the LAST |args| slots only (non-dict drops 0).
  let argTemps = wTrmcEmitArgsToTemps prog env args 1
  let storeSlots =
    wTrmcStoreSlots (dropFirstN (listLen pslots - listLen args) pslots) args 1
  stashNew
    ++ linkInstrs
    ++ advance
    ++ argTemps
    ++ storeSlots
    ++ ["br " ++ loopLbl]

-- store `valInstrs` into the CURRENT dest cell's recursive slot.  Singleton
-- leaf-ctor set: the parent's type is static — exactly the historical uniform
-- emit.  Mixed set: dispatch on $__tmc_dctor (the parent ctor's set-index) with
-- an if/else chain; the LAST entry needs no test (the index is exhaustive).
-- #712: the cons-cell struct id for a TRMC leaf.  A built-in `::` leaf is the
-- reserved `$C_Cons`; any user ctor keys off its name via ctorStructName (so a user
-- `Cons` becomes `$CU_Cons`).  A function's TRMC leaves are homogeneous, so one
-- `isBuiltinList` flag governs both the leaf and its parent link.
trmcCellStruct : Bool -> String -> String
trmcCellStruct True _ = "C_Cons"
trmcCellStruct False ctorName = ctorStructName ctorName

-- the cons-cell tag for a TRMC leaf (#712/S0): the reserved list ordinal for a
-- built-in `::` leaf, the table (declaration-order) ordinal for a user ctor leaf.
trmcCellOrdinal : Bool -> Prog -> String -> Int
trmcCellOrdinal True _ ctorName = syntheticCtorOrdinal ctorName
trmcCellOrdinal False prog ctorName = ctorOrdinal prog ctorName

wTrmcLinkParent : Bool -> List (String, Int) -> List String -> List String
wTrmcLinkParent isBuiltinList [(ctorName, selfIdx)] valInstrs =
  wTrmcLinkOne isBuiltinList ctorName selfIdx valInstrs
wTrmcLinkParent isBuiltinList ctorSet valInstrs =
  wTrmcLinkChain isBuiltinList ctorSet 0 valInstrs

wTrmcLinkOne : Bool -> String -> Int -> List String -> List String
wTrmcLinkOne isBuiltinList ctorName selfIdx valInstrs =
  let cellStruct = trmcCellStruct isBuiltinList ctorName
  ["local.get " ++ wTrmcDestL, "ref.cast (ref $" ++ cellStruct ++ ")"]
    ++ valInstrs
    ++ ["struct.set $\{cellStruct} \{intToString (selfIdx + 1)}"]

wTrmcLinkChain : Bool -> List (String, Int) -> Int -> List String -> List String
wTrmcLinkChain _ [] _ _ = []
wTrmcLinkChain isBuiltinList [(ctorName, selfIdx)] _ valInstrs =
  wTrmcLinkOne isBuiltinList ctorName selfIdx valInstrs
wTrmcLinkChain isBuiltinList ((ctorName, selfIdx) :: rest) k valInstrs =
  ["local.get " ++ wTrmcDctorL, "i32.const " ++ intToString k, "i32.eq", "if"]
    ++ indent (wTrmcLinkOne isBuiltinList ctorName selfIdx valInstrs)
    ++ ["else"]
    ++ indent (wTrmcLinkChain isBuiltinList rest (k + 1) valInstrs)
    ++ ["end"]

-- record which ctor the NEW dest cell is (mixed sets only; a singleton set needs
-- no tracking — the parent type is static).
wTrmcRecordDctor : List (String, Int) -> String -> List String
wTrmcRecordDctor [_] _ = []
wTrmcRecordDctor ctorSet ctorName = [
  "i32.const " ++ intToString (wTrmcCtorIndex ctorSet ctorName 0),
  "local.set " ++ wTrmcDctorL,
]

wTrmcCtorIndex : List (String, Int) -> String -> Int -> Int
wTrmcCtorIndex [] _ _ = 0
wTrmcCtorIndex ((n, _) :: rest) ctorName k =
  if n == ctorName then k else wTrmcCtorIndex rest ctorName (k + 1)

-- plain saturated self-call leaf (no cell): recompute args into temps + store into the
-- param slots + br.  Leaves the destination UNCHANGED (the next iter fills the same slot).
emitWasmTrmcTailCall : Prog ->
  Env ->
  List String ->
  String ->
  CExpr ->
  List String
emitWasmTrmcTailCall prog env pslots loopLbl e =
  let (_, args) = flattenApp e []
  -- dict-carrying self-call: skip the loop-invariant leading dict slots (see
  -- emitWasmTrmcCtor); non-dict is |args| == |pslots| ⇒ drop 0.
  let argTemps = wTrmcEmitArgsToTemps prog env args 0
  let storeSlots =
    wTrmcStoreSlots (dropFirstN (listLen pslots - listLen args) pslots) args 0
  argTemps ++ storeSlots ++ ["br " ++ loopLbl]

-- base/other leaf: a value with NO self-call.  Store it into the current destination's
-- recursive slot (or directly into $__tmc_head if no cell was ever built), then br to exit
-- where the function returns $__tmc_head.  Uses $__tmc_first to choose.
emitWasmTrmcBase : Prog -> Env -> String -> CExpr -> List String
emitWasmTrmcBase prog env exitLbl e =
  let valInstrs = emitRefExpr prog env 0 e
  -- if no cell was built, the whole result IS this value → head := value.
  -- else store it into the current dest's recursive slot (the parent ctor's type
  -- is static for a singleton leaf-ctor set; a mixed set dispatches on
  -- $__tmc_dctor — wTrmcLinkParent).  Fetch the set from the ctx.
  match (progFnCtx prog).trmc
    WTrmcOn _ _ _ ctorSet isBuiltinList _ _ =>
      let storeBranch = wTrmcLinkParent isBuiltinList ctorSet valInstrs
      let seedBranch = valInstrs ++ ["local.set " ++ wTrmcHeadL]
      ["local.get " ++ wTrmcFirstL, "if"]
        ++ indent seedBranch
        ++ ["else"]
        ++ indent storeBranch
        ++ ["end", "br " ++ exitLbl]
    WTrmcOff => valInstrs ++ ["return"]

-- recompute each self-call arg into its temp local ($__tmc_t<base+k>), left-to-right.
wTrmcEmitArgsToTemps : Prog -> Env -> List CExpr -> Int -> List String
wTrmcEmitArgsToTemps prog env args base = wTrmcArgsGo prog env args base 0

wTrmcArgsGo : Prog -> Env -> List CExpr -> Int -> Int -> List String
wTrmcArgsGo _ _ [] _ _ = []
wTrmcArgsGo prog env (a :: rest) base k =
  emitRefExpr prog env 0 a
    ++ ["local.set " ++ wTrmcTempL (base + k)]
    ++ wTrmcArgsGo prog env rest base (k + 1)

-- store each recomputed temp into the matching param slot ($a<i>), left-to-right.
wTrmcStoreSlots : List String -> List CExpr -> Int -> List String
wTrmcStoreSlots pslots args base = wTrmcStoreGo pslots args base 0

wTrmcStoreGo : List String -> List CExpr -> Int -> Int -> List String
wTrmcStoreGo [] _ _ _ = []
wTrmcStoreGo _ [] _ _ = []
wTrmcStoreGo (p :: ps) (_ :: as_) base k =
  [
      "local.get " ++ wTrmcTempL (base + k),
      "ref.as_non_null",
      "local.set $" ++ gname p,
    ]
    ++ wTrmcStoreGo ps as_ base (k + 1)

-- ── the Stage-1 driver: decide eligibility + emit the destination-passing loop ──
-- Returns `Some fnDef` when the plan's verdict (`EmitPlan.trmc`) holds `name`: a
-- top-level self-recursive define that is `trmcEligible` for the self-only
-- cons/ctor-tail shape (a).  Dict-carrying defines (every unannotated polymorphic
-- builder — F2(b) shape (a)) are admitted when the leading-dict count is uniform
-- across clauses; the
-- emit is arity-keyed and types every param `(ref eq)`, so the dict is just another
-- loop slot.
-- Otherwise `None` → the caller falls back to the ordinary (stack-growing)
-- codegen (no regression).  MIXED leaf ctors are supported (P3, TMC-parity arc):
-- the emit dispatches link sites on the parent cell's ctor; the old uniform-ctor
-- gate (a wasm-only restriction the LLVM backend never had) is retired.
wasmTrmcTry : Prog -> String -> Int -> List CClause -> Option (List String)
wasmTrmcTry prog name arity clauses =
  let self = SelfByVar name
  let pairs = map clauseToPair clauses
  -- Stage-1b: a multi-clause fn whose params carry list/ctor PATTERNS (the
  -- `stripComments` {cons-tail + plain-tail-drop + base} shape) is NOW admitted —
  -- emitWasmTrmcFn routes it through the clause-dispatch chain (emitClauseChainGo)
  -- with the TMC context live, so each clause's tail leaf is TMC-aware (cons-into-dest,
  -- plain-tail-drop+loop, base+exit) instead of the stack-growing recursive call the
  -- ordinary emitClausesRef path emits.  All-PVar single/multi-clause stays the fast
  -- direct-body path.  (Mirrors llvm_emit's trmcTryFn forceSingle=False / emitClauseTree
  -- reuse.)
  if isTrmcFn (progTrmcW prog) name then
    Some
      (emitWasmTrmcFn
        prog
        name
        arity
        clauses
        (wTrmcCtorSet prog self arity pairs))
  else
    None

clauseToPair : CClause -> (List Pat, CExpr)
clauseToPair (CClause pats body) = (pats, body)

-- Phase 2 B-dispatch (mirror of llvm_emit.trmcImplTry): a DISPATCHED self-recursive
-- cons/ctor-tail IMPL method (the `List` Functor `map`: `map f (x::xs) = f x :: map f xs`,
-- recursing via a `CMethod method (RKey tag)` node) is emitted as an O(1)-stack
-- destination-passing loop, just like a top-level builder.  Without this the ordinary
-- impl-body emit lowers the self-call as a `call $mdk_impl_<tag>_<method>` inside the
-- cons args (the frame stays live → deep lists overflow V8's stack).
--
-- The self-ref is `SelfByMethod method tag` (the self-call head is `CMethod method
-- (RKey tag)`, NOT a `CVar`).  SAFETY-CRITICAL: `freeVars (CMethod …)` is BLIND to the
-- method NAME — the analysis (`trmcEligible`/`isCtorTail`/`selfFree`) routes the
-- `SelfByMethod` disqualification through `mentionsSelfMethod`, so a body that
-- self-recurses via `CMethod` in a NON-tail position is rejected (stays ordinary) rather
-- than wrongly transformed (dropped recursion → silent miscompile).
--
-- Scope = F2(a) + F2(b) shape (a): NON-eta impls, dicts admitted when the leading-dict
-- count is uniform across clauses.  Returns Some def when eligible (the whole
-- `(func …)` define via emitWasmTrmcCore with the impl symbol + SelfByMethod), else None
-- so emitImplGroup falls back to the ordinary emitClausesImpl body.
-- [key] drives the SelfByMethod self-call recognition: the in-body self route
-- carries the instance's canonical key.
wTrmcImplTry : Prog ->
  String ->
  String ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  List CClause ->
  Option (List String)
wTrmcImplTry prog method key fnName arity clauses =
  let pairs = map clauseToPair clauses
  let self = methodSelf method key (match pairs
    (ps, _) :: _ => ps
    [] => [])
  if isTrmcImpl (progTrmcW prog) method key then
    Some
      (emitWasmTrmcCore
        prog
        fnName
        self
        fnName
        arity
        clauses
        (wTrmcCtorSet prog self arity pairs))
  else
    None

-- the fn's distinct (ctorName, selfFieldIdx) leaf-ctor pairs, in first-seen
-- clause/leaf order (deterministic).  Cons-tail leaves report ("Cons", 1).
-- trmcEligible guarantees ≥1 cons/ctor-tail leaf, so the set is never empty;
-- Axis-A eligibility puts the self-call in the LAST field, so a ctor's selfIdx
-- is a function of the ctor — dedup by NAME is exact.
wTrmcCtorSet : Prog ->
  SelfRef ->
  Int ->
  List (List Pat, CExpr) ->
  List (String, Int)
wTrmcCtorSet prog self arity pairs =
  wTrmcDedupCtors
    (flatMap (pr => wTrmcCtorTailsOf prog self arity (snd pr)) pairs)
    []

wTrmcDedupCtors : List (String, Int) -> List String -> List (String, Int)
wTrmcDedupCtors [] _ = []
wTrmcDedupCtors ((n, i) :: rest) seen =
  if contains n seen then
    wTrmcDedupCtors rest seen
  else
    (n, i) :: wTrmcDedupCtors rest (n :: seen)

snd : (a, b) -> b
snd (_, b) = b

-- collect the (ctor name, selfIdx) of every cons/ctor-tail leaf reachable through
-- the tail wrappers (if/let/block/decision).  Mirrors trmcBodyHasCons's descent.
wTrmcCtorTailsOf : Prog -> SelfRef -> Int -> CExpr -> List (String, Int)
wTrmcCtorTailsOf prog self arity (CIf _ t f) =
  wTrmcCtorTailsOf prog self arity t ++ wTrmcCtorTailsOf prog self arity f
wTrmcCtorTailsOf prog self arity (CLet _ _ _ b) =
  wTrmcCtorTailsOf prog self arity b
wTrmcCtorTailsOf prog self arity (CBlock stmts) = match lastStmtExpr stmts
  Some ex => wTrmcCtorTailsOf prog self arity ex
  None => []
wTrmcCtorTailsOf prog self arity (CDecision _ arms _) =
  flatMap (a => wTrmcCtorTailsOf prog self arity (armBody a)) arms
wTrmcCtorTailsOf prog self arity ex =
  if isCtorTail (c => isCtor prog c) (c => ctorArity prog c) self arity ex then
    [(ctorTailName ex, ctorTailSelfIdx ex)]
  else
    []

-- #712: the ctor-tail LEAF exprs (same descent as wTrmcCtorTailsOf), so the caller
-- can ask `ctorTailIsCons` per leaf.  Used to decide whether a fn builds the
-- built-in list (`::` → `$C_Cons`) or a user ADT (`$C_<ctor>` / `$CU_Cons`).
wTrmcCtorTailExprs : Prog -> SelfRef -> Int -> CExpr -> List CExpr
wTrmcCtorTailExprs prog self arity (CIf _ t f) =
  wTrmcCtorTailExprs prog self arity t ++ wTrmcCtorTailExprs prog self arity f
wTrmcCtorTailExprs prog self arity (CLet _ _ _ b) =
  wTrmcCtorTailExprs prog self arity b
wTrmcCtorTailExprs prog self arity (CBlock stmts) = match lastStmtExpr stmts
  Some ex => wTrmcCtorTailExprs prog self arity ex
  None => []
wTrmcCtorTailExprs prog self arity (CDecision _ arms _) =
  flatMap (a => wTrmcCtorTailExprs prog self arity (armBody a)) arms
wTrmcCtorTailExprs prog self arity ex =
  if isCtorTail (c => isCtor prog c) (c => ctorArity prog c) self arity ex then
    [ex]
  else
    []

-- whether an eligible TRMC fn's cons leaves are the built-in `h :: t` (homogeneous
-- per fn — a fn returns one type).  Governs the cons-cell struct id (#712).
wTrmcBuildsBuiltinList : Prog -> SelfRef -> Int -> List CClause -> Bool
wTrmcBuildsBuiltinList prog self arity clauses =
  anyList
    ctorTailIsCons
    (flatMap (c => wTrmcCtorTailExprs prog self arity (clauseBodyOf c)) clauses)

-- emit the eligible function as a destination-passing loop.  Scaffold:
--   (func $name (param $a0 …) (result (ref eq))
--     <tmc locals> <clause locals> <scratch> <w7 locals>
--     i32.const 1  local.set $__tmc_first
--     block $tmcexit  loop $tmcloop  <body via emitRefTail under WTrmcOn>  end  end
--     local.get $__tmc_head)
-- Every cons/ctor leaf `br $tmcloop` (no recursive call); the base leaf `br $tmcexit`.
emitWasmTrmcFn : Prog ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  List CClause ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  List String
emitWasmTrmcFn prog name arity clauses ctorSet =
  -- top-level define: the func symbol is `gname name`, the self-ref is `SelfByVar name`,
  -- and `name` doubles as the clause-block label root.
  emitWasmTrmcCore prog (gname name) (SelfByVar name) name arity clauses ctorSet

-- the shared destination-passing-loop emitter for BOTH the top-level path (SelfByVar) and
-- the Phase-2 B-dispatch impl path (SelfByMethod).  `funcSym` is the rendered func symbol
-- (no leading `$`; `gname name` for a top-level fn, the group's symbol for an impl);
-- `self` is the SelfRef the TMC analysis + leaf-emit thread (CVar vs CMethod recognition);
-- `lblRoot` is the clause-block label root (unique per emitted define).
emitWasmTrmcCore : Prog ->
  String ->
  SelfRef ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  List CClause ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  List String
emitWasmTrmcCore prog funcSym self lblRoot arity clauses ctorSet =
  let params = clauseParamNames clauses arity
  let pslots = map gname params
  let loopLbl = "$tmcloop"
  let exitLbl = "$tmcexit"
  let isBuiltinList = wTrmcBuildsBuiltinList prog self arity clauses
  let w7Outer = w7ScopeOpen (progEmit prog)
  let tprog =
    progWithTrmc
      (WTrmcOn self arity pslots ctorSet isBuiltinList loopLbl exitLbl)
      prog
  -- Single all-PVar clause (no fallthrough): the fast path — alias params to the
  -- synthetic positions and TMC-emit the body directly.  Otherwise (multi-clause OR
  -- a clause carries a list/ctor pattern, e.g. `stripComments`/the `map` impl): route
  -- through the clause-dispatch chain (emitClauseChainGo) with the TMC context LIVE, so
  -- each clause's tail leaf is TMC-aware (cons-into-dest / plain-tail-drop+loop / base+exit).
  let bodyLines = match clauses
    [CClause ps b] =>
      if allPlainParams ps && not (exprHasFallthrough b) then
        bindParamAliases prog ps params
          ++ emitRefTail tprog (paramEnv ps) arity b
      else
        emitClauseChainGo
          tprog
          envEmpty
          lblRoot
          params
          arity
          clauses
          0
          (progFnCtx prog).site
    _ =>
      emitClauseChainGo
        tprog
        envEmpty
        lblRoot
        params
        arity
        clauses
        0
        (progFnCtx prog).site
  let loopShell =
    ["i32.const 1", "local.set " ++ wTrmcFirstL]
      ++ ["block " ++ exitLbl, "loop " ++ loopLbl]
      ++ indent bodyLines
      ++ ["end", "end"]
      ++ ["local.get " ++ wTrmcHeadL, "ref.as_non_null"]
  -- locals: the tmc bookkeeping + temps (t0..t_arity), then the ordinary clause/scratch.
  -- a MIXED leaf-ctor set additionally tracks the dest cell's ctor set-index.
  let dctorLocal = match ctorSet
    [_] => []
    _ => ["(local " ++ wTrmcDctorL ++ " i32)"]
  let tmcLocals =
    [
        "(local " ++ wTrmcHeadL ++ " (ref null eq))",
        "(local " ++ wTrmcDestL ++ " (ref null eq))",
        "(local " ++ wTrmcFirstL ++ " i32)",
      ]
      ++ dctorLocal
      ++ map
        (k => "(local " ++ wTrmcTempL k ++ " (ref null eq))")
        (rangeList 0 (arity + 1))
  let allLocals = clauseLocals clauses
  let extraLocals = filterList (notIn params) (dedupKeep allLocals)
  let scratch = scratchLocals (clausesMaxDepth clauses)
  let localDecls = map localDeclRef (extraLocals ++ scratch)
  let w7Decls =
    w7LocalDecls
      (w7ScopeClose (progEmit prog) w7Outer)
      (clausesMaxDepth clauses)
  let _ = defineFnW prog funcSym (FuncParams (listLen params))
  let sig =
    "  (func $\{funcSym}\{joinWith "" (map paramDeclRef params)} (result (ref eq))"
  wTmcMarker funcSym "trmc"
    :: [sig]
      ++ map ("  " ++ _) (tmcLocals ++ localDecls ++ w7Decls)
      ++ indent loopShell
      ++ ["  )"]

-- ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- Stage-2/3 WasmGC DISPATCH-GRAPH TMC (shape (b′)) — WASMGC-TRMC-DESIGN §7/§11,
-- BROWSER-STACK-DIAGNOSIS §7 (Stage-3 generalization: pattern-matched roots,
-- member-targeted multi-cell spine conses, external-entry root selection)
-- ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- The lexer overflows because each per-token LEAF (`scanLower`/`emit`/…) does
-- `tok :: scan …`: the cons-target is the single dispatcher `scan`, NOT the leaf
-- itself, so the LLVM/Stage-1 self-recursive analysis (`isSelfSatApp self`) never
-- fires across the dispatch boundary.  The cons `scan …` is emitted as a struct.new
-- ARG → the leaf frame stays live to EOF → V8 stack overflow.
--
-- Fix (emitter-only, reuses Stage-1's cons-cell + dest mechanism): identify a "TMC
-- group" = a set of functions tail-connected under an EXTERNAL-ENTRY root `R`
-- (`scan`, the layout family's `layout`), where every tail leaf is either
--   (1) a base case (no call to a group member), or
--   (2) a SPINE cons — a peeled chain of 1..N member-free heads bottoming in a
--       saturated call to ANY group member (the overflow site), or
--   (3) a saturated tail-call to another group member (a dispatcher OR a
--       non-spine self-accumulator like the string-interp `acc++` loops).
-- We then emit `R` as a RESET wrapper that saves and zeroes three module-level dest
-- globals ($g_tmc_head / $g_tmc_dest / $g_tmc_first), calls an inner `R__loop`, and
-- restores them,
-- and we emit every group member with its SPINE cons leaves rewritten to: build each
-- `Cons` cell with a placeholder tail, link it into $g_tmc_dest (or seed $g_tmc_head
-- on the first cell), advance the dest, then `return_call` the bottom callee (`$R__loop`
-- when it is the root — never the reset wrapper — else the member fn itself; a REAL
-- tail call — the leaf frame dies; no struct.new holds the recursion).  A member's
-- base leaf closes the dest with its real value and returns $g_tmc_head.  Dispatcher /
-- self-accumulator tails (case 3) are emitted UNCHANGED (they already `return_call`,
-- and they never touch the dest globals, which thread through transparently).
--
-- This needs NO param-slot recompute loop (unlike Stage-1): the engine's `return_call`
-- IS the loop.  Soundness rests on the root wrapper being the group's only external
-- entry (dispValidate v4): every entry, including a re-entry from inside an in-flight
-- spine, passes through the wrapper, which saves the dest globals, runs its own spine
-- from zeroed ones, and restores them before returning, so the outer spine resumes
-- linking where it left off.

-- (`WDispCtx` rides in the `FnCtx` of the `Prog` a body is emitted with, and
-- `WasmEmit.wDispGroups` carries the detected groups; both live above.)

-- PER-GROUP dest globals (Stage-3): each group root gets its own head/dest/first
-- triple, so one group's spine build cannot clobber another's — a member's helper
-- (mid-spine, non-tail) may freely call ANOTHER group's root (e.g. a lexer helper
-- reaching `join` → `intersperse`): that root resets and threads ITS OWN globals
-- and returns a closed spine, leaving the in-flight group's dest untouched.
-- SAME-group re-entry is not excluded by validation: v3 sees only named call heads,
-- so a member calling back into its own root through a function-typed argument
-- passes it.  The root wrapper's save/restore of the triple is what makes that safe.
wDispHeadL : String -> String
wDispHeadL root = "$g_tmc_head_" ++ gname root
wDispDestL : String -> String
wDispDestL root = "$g_tmc_dest_" ++ gname root
wDispFirstL : String -> String
wDispFirstL root = "$g_tmc_first_" ++ gname root

-- the inner-loop fn name for a group root `R`: `<R>__disploop`.
wDispLoopName : String -> String
wDispLoopName root = root ++ "__disploop"

-- one group's three dest globals (mutable; reset per outer entry by the wrapper).
-- the names of the globals `wDispGlobalLines` declares, without their `$`
wDispGlobalNames : DispGroup -> List String
wDispGlobalNames grp =
  let root = dispRootOf grp
  map symNameW [wDispHeadL root, wDispDestL root, wDispFirstL root]

wDispGlobalLines : DispGroup -> List String
wDispGlobalLines grp =
  let root = dispRootOf grp
  [
    "  (global " ++ wDispHeadL root ++ " (mut (ref null eq)) (ref.null eq))",
    "  (global " ++ wDispDestL root ++ " (mut (ref null eq)) (ref.null eq))",
    "  (global " ++ wDispFirstL root ++ " (mut i32) (i32.const 1))",
  ]

-- ── group detection (SHARED — backend/trmc_analysis.mdk) ─────────────────────
-- The Stage-3 dispatch-graph groups are detected once, by the plan
-- (`emit_plan.buildEmitPlan`), with the shared detection in
-- `backend/trmc_analysis.mdk`; both backends route the SAME groups.  The spine
-- classifier below closes the shared one over `prog`.

-- shared spine classifier, closed over `prog` (detection, validation, and the
-- leaf emit below all agree on what is — and is not — a spine cons).
wDispSpineParts : Prog ->
  (String -> Bool) ->
  CExpr ->
  Option (List CExpr, String, List CExpr)
wDispSpineParts prog ok e =
  dispSpineParts
    (n => canonFn prog n)
    (n => progFnMemberW prog n)
    (n => fnParamCountW prog n)
    ok
    e

-- a saturated direct call to `root` (canonicalized), via the shared classifier.
wDispIsSatRootCall : Prog -> String -> Int -> CExpr -> Bool
wDispIsSatRootCall prog root arity e =
  dispIsSatRootCall (n => canonFn prog n) root arity e

-- ── group-member emit ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- (group lookup/accessors are the shared dispGroupOf/dispRootOf/dispMembersOf.)
wDispIsRoot : DispGroup -> String -> Bool
wDispIsRoot (DispGroup root _) name = root == name

-- census marker (TMC-parity gate): one deterministic `;; tmc: <fn> <mode>`
-- comment per TMC decision; test/tmc_census.sh + diff_compiler_tmc_parity.sh
-- extract these to diff both backends' TMC'd source-function sets.  The name is
-- census-normalized (leading `mdk_` stripped, so an impl fn reads
-- `impl_<tag>_<method>` on both backends).
wTmcMarker : String -> String -> String
wTmcMarker sym mode =
  let name = if startsWith "mdk_" sym then dropPrefix sym "mdk_" else sym
  "  ;; tmc: \{name} \{mode}"

-- emit a group ROOT: the reset wrapper `$root` (save and zero the dest globals, call the
-- inner loop, restore them) + the inner `$root__disploop` (the real body, leaves redirected).
emitWDispRoot : Prog -> DispGroup -> Int -> List CClause -> List String
emitWDispRoot prog grp arity clauses =
  let name = dispRootOf grp
  let params = synthParams arity
  let loopName = wDispLoopName name
  let _ = defineFnW prog (gname name) (FuncParams arity)
  let resetWrapper = wDispResetWrapper prog name loopName params arity
  let inner = emitWDispMemberFn prog grp loopName name arity clauses
  wTmcMarker name "group-root" :: resetWrapper ++ inner

-- the reset wrapper: (func $root (param …) (result (ref eq))
--   save $g_tmc_head / $g_tmc_dest / $g_tmc_first into locals
--   i32.const 1  global.set $g_tmc_first
--   ref.null eq  global.set $g_tmc_head
--   ref.null eq  global.set $g_tmc_dest
--   local.get $a0 … call $root__disploop
--   restore the saved triple, return the result)
-- A plain `call`, not `return_call`: the restore must run after the spine closes.
wDispResetWrapper : Prog ->
  String ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  Int ->
  List String
wDispResetWrapper prog name loopName params arity =
  let sig =
    "  (func $\{gname name}\{joinWith "" (map paramDeclRef params)} (result (ref eq))"
  let locals = [
    "(local $__disp_sh (ref null eq))",
    "(local $__disp_sd (ref null eq))",
    "(local $__disp_sf i32)",
    "(local $__disp_r (ref eq))",
  ]
  let get = g => globalW prog "global.get" g
  let set = g => globalW prog "global.set" g
  let save = [
    get (wDispHeadL name),
    "local.set $__disp_sh",
    get (wDispDestL name),
    "local.set $__disp_sd",
    get (wDispFirstL name),
    "local.set $__disp_sf",
  ]
  let reset = [
    "i32.const 1",
    set (wDispFirstL name),
    "ref.null eq",
    set (wDispHeadL name),
    "ref.null eq",
    set (wDispDestL name),
  ]
  let forward =
    flatMap (p => ["local.get $" ++ gname p]) params
      ++ [callFnW prog CallValueW (gname loopName) arity, "local.set $__disp_r"]
  let restore = [
    "local.get $__disp_sh",
    set (wDispHeadL name),
    "local.get $__disp_sd",
    set (wDispDestL name),
    "local.get $__disp_sf",
    set (wDispFirstL name),
    "local.get $__disp_r",
  ]
  [sig] ++ indent (locals ++ save ++ reset ++ forward ++ restore) ++ ["  )"]

-- emit a non-root group MEMBER (or the root's inner loop): the ordinary clause machinery,
-- but with the dispatch context LIVE so spine cons leaves + the root's base redirect.
-- `emitName` is the wasm fn name to emit under (the inner loop for the root; the fn's own
-- name for a non-root member).
emitWDispMemberFn : Prog ->
  DispGroup ->
  String ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  List CClause ->
  List String
emitWDispMemberFn prog grp emitName origName arity clauses =
  let root = dispRootOf grp
  let params = synthParams arity
  let loopName = wDispLoopName root
  -- the dispatch context carries the ROOT's arity (for the bare-root-call redirect
  -- check), NOT this member's arity — a member like scanAt is arity-6 but the bare
  -- call it makes to `scan` is arity-5.  It also carries the MEMBER SET so spine
  -- cons leaves targeting a non-root member return_call that member directly.
  let rootArity = fnParamCountW prog root
  let w7Outer = w7ScopeOpen (progEmit prog)
  let dprog =
    progWithDisp (WDispOn root loopName rootArity (dispMembersOf grp)) prog
  let bodyLines = emitClausesRef dprog origName params arity clauses
  let allLocals = clauseLocals clauses
  let extraLocals = filterList (notIn params) (dedupKeep allLocals)
  let scratch = scratchLocals (clausesMaxDepth clauses)
  let _ = defineFnW prog (gname emitName) (FuncParams arity)
  let sig =
    "  (func $\{gname emitName}\{joinWith "" (map paramDeclRef params)} (result (ref eq))"
  -- census marker for a NON-root member (the root's marker is emitted by
  -- emitWDispRoot; the inner __disploop is the root's own body, not a member).
  let marker =
    if emitName == origName then
      [wTmcMarker origName ("group:" ++ root)]
    else
      []
  -- the member needs the tmc temp local ($__tmc_t0 = the fresh cell stash).
  let tmcLocal = ["(local " ++ wTrmcTempL 0 ++ " (ref null eq))"]
  let localDecls = map localDeclRef (extraLocals ++ scratch)
  let w7Decls =
    w7LocalDecls
      (w7ScopeClose (progEmit prog) w7Outer)
      (clausesMaxDepth clauses)
  marker
    ++ [sig]
    ++ map ("  " ++ _) (tmcLocal ++ localDecls ++ w7Decls)
    ++ indent bodyLines
    ++ ["  )"]

-- the spine-cons leaf rewrite (case 2), generalized to N cells + any group-member
-- target: build each peeled cell in source order (lead field + placeholder tail),
-- link it into $g_tmc_dest (or seed $g_tmc_head on the very first cell), advance the
-- dest — the second-and-later cells naturally chain through the just-advanced dest —
-- then emit the bottom call's ARGS + `return_call` the target (`$root__disploop` for
-- the root, the member fn itself otherwise).  NO struct.new holds the recursion →
-- the leaf frame dies.
emitWDispSpineCons : Prog ->
  Env ->
  String ->
  String ->
  List CExpr ->
  List CExpr ->
  List String
emitWDispSpineCons prog env root target heads args =
  flatMap (h => emitWDispCell prog env root h) heads
    ++ flatMap (a => emitRefExpr prog env 0 a) args
    ++ [callFnW prog CallTailW (gname target) (listLen args)]

-- one Cons cell of a spine-cons leaf: build, link, advance.
emitWDispCell : Prog -> Env -> String -> CExpr -> List String
emitWDispCell prog env root head =
  let cellStruct = "C_Cons"
  -- #712/S0: this is the built-in list `::` spine — pin the reserved Cons ordinal,
  -- not `ctorOrdinal "Cons"` (which a coexisting user `Cons` ctor would poison).
  let tag = ["i32.const " ++ intToString (syntheticCtorOrdinal "Cons")]
  let headInstrs = emitRefExpr prog env 0 head
  let placeholder = ["i32.const 1", "ref.i31"]
  let buildCell =
    tag ++ headInstrs ++ placeholder ++ ["struct.new $" ++ cellStruct]
  let stashNew = buildCell ++ ["local.set " ++ wTrmcTempL 0]
  -- link: first cell → head:=cell, first:=0 ; else struct.set dest.tail := cell.
  let linkSeed = [
    "local.get " ++ wTrmcTempL 0,
    globalW prog "global.set" (wDispHeadL root),
    "i32.const 0",
    globalW prog "global.set" (wDispFirstL root),
  ]
  let linkSet = [
    globalW prog "global.get" (wDispDestL root),
    "ref.cast (ref $" ++ cellStruct ++ ")",
    "local.get " ++ wTrmcTempL 0,
    "ref.as_non_null",
    "struct.set $" ++ cellStruct ++ " 2",
  ]
  let linkInstrs =
    [globalW prog "global.get" (wDispFirstL root), "if"]
      ++ indent linkSeed
      ++ ["else"]
      ++ indent linkSet
      ++ ["end"]
  let advance = [
    "local.get " ++ wTrmcTempL 0,
    globalW prog "global.set" (wDispDestL root),
  ]
  stashNew ++ linkInstrs ++ advance

-- the root's BASE leaf (case 1): close the dest with the real value of the base (the
-- spine's terminator, e.g. `[]` = Nil), then return $g_tmc_head.  If no cell was ever
-- built ($g_tmc_first still 1) the whole result IS the base value.
emitWDispBase : Prog -> Env -> String -> CExpr -> List String
emitWDispBase prog env root e =
  let valInstrs = emitRefExpr prog env 0 e
  let cellStruct = "C_Cons"
  let storeBranch =
    [
        globalW prog "global.get" (wDispDestL root),
        "ref.cast (ref $" ++ cellStruct ++ ")",
      ]
      ++ valInstrs
      ++ ["struct.set $" ++ cellStruct ++ " 2"]
  let seedBranch = valInstrs ++ [globalW prog "global.set" (wDispHeadL root)]
  [globalW prog "global.get" (wDispFirstL root), "if"]
    ++ indent seedBranch
    ++ ["else"]
    ++ indent storeBranch
    ++ ["end"]
    ++ [
      globalW prog "global.get" (wDispHeadL root),
      "ref.as_non_null",
      "return",
    ]

-- A tail-position application.  A file bound and a fall-through sentinel are
-- control, not calls, and keep their own lowering.  An application the lowering
-- flagged as the tail call (`isTailCall`) replaces this function's frame
-- (`emitTailCallW`); any other is computed and returned.
emitAppTail : Prog -> Env -> Int -> CExpr -> List String
emitAppTail prog env arity app =
  let (hd, args, _) = appParts app
  if rawProgramW prog then
    if isTailCall app then
      emitDirectRawCallW prog env 0 hd args True
    else
      emitAppRef prog env 0 app ++ ["return"]
  else match hd
    CVar f0 _ =>
      if f0 == "$withFileReadBound"
        || f0 == "$withFileWriteBound" then match fileBoundW app
        Some (g, body, mode) =>
          let pushed =
            emitRefExpr prog env 0 body
              ++ [rtCallW prog "mdk_file_bound_exit" 0, "return"]
          fileBoundEnterW prog env 0 g mode False
            ++ ["if"]
            ++ indent pushed
            ++ ["else"]
            ++ indent (emitRefTail prog env arity body)
            ++ ["end", "unreachable"]
        None => gapLP prog "wasm: a file bound requires a grant and a thunk"
      else if isFtSentinel f0 || hasFamilyW prog f0 "fallthrough" then
        -- tail-position `__fallthrough__ ()` / `__ft__<label> ()`: lower the sentinel
        -- (a `br`, NOT a `return` — control leaves the clause, not the function).
        ftSentinelInstrs f0
      else
        emitFlaggedAppW prog env app
    _ => emitFlaggedAppW prog env app

emitFlaggedAppW : Prog -> Env -> CExpr -> List String
emitFlaggedAppW prog env app =
  if isTailCall app then
    emitTailCallW prog env app
  else
    emitAppRef prog env 0 app ++ ["return"]

-- The tail call itself: the call `emitAppRef` would make, as a `return_call`.  A
-- constructor, `Ref`/`setRef` and an extern compute a value and return it.  An
-- indirect call returns through `$__mdk_apply`, which `return_call_ref`s the
-- closure's code, so every shape is constant-stack.
emitTailCallW : Prog -> Env -> CExpr -> List String
emitTailCallW prog env app =
  let (hd, args, mode) = appParts app
  match hd
    CVar f0 _ =>
      let f = canonFn prog f0
      if envHas f0 env then
        -- E24 (wasm peer): a LOCALLY-BOUND name shadows any same-named ctor / known top-level
        -- fn / extern — applying it is an INDIRECT tail call (`return_call $__mdk_apply`), never a
        -- direct `return_call $<toplevel>`.  Same guard as emitAppRef's CVar arm; without it a
        -- method-named HOF param colliding with a top-level fn (`pickEq eq x y = eq x y`) tail-
        -- called the WRONG callee.  Mirrors emitVarRefPlain's `envHas x env`-first priority.

        emitIndirectApp prog env 0 hd args CallTailW
      else if isCtor prog f then
        emitRefExpr prog env 0 app ++ ["return"]
      else if isFfiExternW prog f then
        emitFfiAppW prog env 0 hd f args CallTailW
      else if f0 == siteSentinelName
        || hasFamilyW prog f0 "ref" && runtimeNameW prog f0 == "Ref"
        || hasFamilyW prog f0 "ref" && runtimeNameW prog f0 == "setRef"
        || isSome (externFamilyW (progEmit prog) (runtimeNameW prog f0)) then
        emitAppRef prog env 0 app ++ ["return"]
      else if progFnMemberW prog f && isExactCall mode then
        flatMap (a => emitRefExpr prog env 0 a) args
          ++ [callFnW prog CallTailW (gname f) (listLen args)]
      else
        emitIndirectApp prog env 0 hd args CallTailW
    -- #1349: a dispatched method in tail position.  An RKey route return_calls the
    -- selected entry (an impl method calling itself among them); a runtime
    -- dictionary return_calls the entry each dispatch arm selects.
    CMethod name (MethodEvidence iface arity route implRoutes methRoutes) =>
      emitMethodRef
        prog
        env
        0
        name
        iface
        arity
        route
        implRoutes
        methRoutes
        args
        mode
        CallTailW
    -- P0-7 / #2577: a `=>`-constrained function in tail position.  The un-annotated
    -- `Num a` loop (`loop acc n = … loop (acc+n) (n-1)`) lowers its recursive call
    -- to a `CDict loop [<Num route>]` head: dict words + args + `return_call $loop`
    -- for a top-level one, and `return_call $__mdk_apply` for a local
    -- (`where`-bound) one.
    CDict name routes => emitDictRef prog env 0 name routes args mode CallTailW
    _ => emitIndirectApp prog env 0 hd args CallTailW

-- a block in tail position: the last CSExpr is the tail; everything before is a
-- statement (effect/let).  (W4 blocks in tail position only appear via desugared
-- sequencing; the last expr is the result.)
emitBlockTail : Prog -> Env -> Int -> List CStmt -> List String
emitBlockTail prog env arity [CSExpr ex] = emitRefTail prog env arity ex
emitBlockTail prog env arity ((CSExpr ex) :: rest) =
  emitRefExpr prog env 0 ex ++ ["drop"] ++ emitBlockTail prog env arity rest
emitBlockTail prog env arity ((CSLet recF pat ex) :: rest) =
  let (prefix, env2) = emitBlockBindingW prog env 0 recF pat ex
  prefix ++ emitBlockTail prog env2 arity rest
emitBlockTail prog env arity ((CSAssign x ex) :: rest) =
  emitRefExpr prog env 0 ex
    ++ ["local.set " ++ localTargetW prog env x]
    ++ emitBlockTail prog env arity rest
emitBlockTail prog env arity [] = emitRefTail prog env arity (CLit LUnit)
emitBlockTail prog _ _ _ = gapLP prog (if rawProgramW prog then
  "scalar-mode: unsupported block statement"
else
  "ref-mode: unsupported block statement in tail position")

-- a CDecision in tail position: each arm body is itself in tail position.  Reuse the
-- W3 decision machinery but route arm bodies through emitRefTail (so a tail call in
-- a match arm is a return_call).  The decision's result block is no longer needed —
-- each arm either return_calls or value+returns, so the function returns directly
-- from within the tower.  We emit the scrutinee stash + the tree with TAIL arm
-- emission.  `decLabel` is unused for tail arms (they `return`/`return_call`), but
-- the tree walker still threads it; we pass a dead label that is never branched to.
emitDecisionTail : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  CExpr ->
  List CArm ->
  CTree ->
  List String
emitDecisionTail prog env arity scrut arms tree =
  let st = emitRefExpr prog env 0 scrut
  let scrutL = scratchLocal 0
  let occ0 = ["local.get $" ++ scrutL]
  st
    ++ ["local.set $" ++ scrutL]
    ++ emitTreeTail prog env arity 1 occ0 [occ0] arms tree

-- the decision tree, with arm LEAVES emitted in tail position.  Structurally mirrors
-- emitTreeRef but: leaves → emitRefTail (return_call / value+return), and switches do
-- NOT need a result block (each path returns).  Reuses the same br_table tower shape
-- with the slot bodies tail-emitting their arms.
emitTreeTail : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List String ->
  List (List String) ->
  List CArm ->
  CTree ->
  List String
emitTreeTail prog env arity d root occs arms (CTFail fs) =
  wasmFailTrap (progEmit prog) fs
emitTreeTail prog env arity d root occs arms (CTLeaf i) =
  emitLeafTail prog env arity root arms i
emitTreeTail prog env arity d root occs arms (CTGuard i fail) =
  emitGuardArmTail prog env arity d root occs arms i fail
emitTreeTail prog env arity d root occs arms (CTDrop sub) =
  emitTreeTail prog env arity d root (tailList occs) arms sub
emitTreeTail prog env arity d root occs arms (CTSwitch branches dft) =
  emitSwitchTail prog env arity d root occs arms branches dft

-- Like emitLeafRef, for an arm body in TAIL POSITION (emitRefTail path).
emitLeafTail : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  List String ->
  List CArm ->
  Int ->
  List String
emitLeafTail prog env arity root arms i = match nthArm arms i
  Some (CArm pat _ body) =>
    let (binds, env2) = bindPatRef prog env pat root
    let bodyCode = emitRefTail prog env2 arity body
    binds ++ bodyCode
  None => gapLP prog "ref-mode: tail decision arm index out of range"

-- Like emitGuardArmRef, for guarded arms in tail position.
-- G6 (#379): same `patTestBind` re-match as emitGuardArmRef — see its note.  A `PRng`
-- arm reaches THIS site too (`f n = match n` is a tail match), so the range test has to
-- exist on both engines or the two disagree.
emitGuardArmTail : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List String ->
  List (List String) ->
  List CArm ->
  Int ->
  CTree ->
  List String
emitGuardArmTail prog env arity d root occs arms i fail = match nthArm arms i
  Some (CArm pat guards body) =>
    let gLabel = "$gt" ++ intToString d
    let (tests, binds, env2) = patTestBind prog pat root gLabel env
    -- #379: guards now thread the env (a CGBind binds names the body can see), so the
    -- body is emitted under env3, not env2.
    let (gcode, env3) = emitGuardChainRef prog env2 0 gLabel guards
    let armCode =
      ["block " ++ gLabel]
        ++ indent (tests ++ binds ++ gcode ++ emitRefTail prog env3 arity body)
        ++ ["end"]
    armCode ++ emitTreeTail prog env arity d root occs arms fail
  None => gapLP prog "ref-mode: tail guarded arm index out of range"

emitSwitchTail : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List String ->
  List (List String) ->
  List CArm ->
  List CTBranch ->
  CTree ->
  List String
emitSwitchTail prog env arity d root [] arms branches dft =
  emitTreeTail prog env arity d root [] arms dft
emitSwitchTail prog env arity d root (foc :: rest) arms [] dft =
  emitTreeTail prog env arity d root rest arms dft
emitSwitchTail prog env arity d root (foc :: rest) arms (branches@((CTBranch (HLit _) _) :: _)) dft =
  emitLitSwitchTail prog env arity d root foc rest arms branches dft 0
emitSwitchTail prog env arity d root (foc :: rest) arms ((CTBranch HUnit sub) :: _) dft =
  emitTreeTail prog env arity d root rest arms sub
emitSwitchTail prog env arity d root (foc :: rest) arms (branches@((CTBranch h _) :: _)) dft =
  match conHeadInfo h
    Some _ => emitConSwitchTail prog env arity d root foc rest arms branches dft
    None => gapLP prog "ref-mode: unsupported tail switch head"

-- constructor switch (tail): stash focus, br_table on the discriminant; each slot
-- tail-emits its arm (which return_calls / returns), so we need no result block.
emitConSwitchTail : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List String ->
  List String ->
  List (List String) ->
  List CArm ->
  List CTBranch ->
  CTree ->
  List String
emitConSwitchTail prog env arity d root foc rest arms branches dft =
  let ty = switchTypeName prog branches
  let nOrd = typeCtorCount prog ty
  let sv = scratchLocal d
  let svRead = ["local.get $" ++ sv]
  foc
    ++ ["local.set $" ++ sv]
    ++ emitBrTableTowerTail
      prog
      env
      arity
      (d + 1)
      root
      svRead
      rest
      arms
      (branchOrdMapW prog branches)
      dft
      ty
      d
      nOrd

-- the br_table tower in tail position: no `$swd` result block — each ordinal slot's
-- body tail-emits its arm (return_call / return), and the default subtree follows the
-- innermost `end`.  The table targets `$sw<sd>_k` slots; the default slot is the last
-- `end`'s fall-through into the default subtree.
emitBrTableTowerTail : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List String ->
  List String ->
  List (List String) ->
  List CArm ->
  OrdMap CTBranch ->
  CTree ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List String
emitBrTableTowerTail prog env arity d root svRead rest arms branches dft ty sd nOrd =
  let sfx = intToString sd
  let labels = map (k => "$swt\{sfx}_\{intToString k}") (rangeList 0 nOrd)
  let dftLabel = "$swdt" ++ sfx
  let tableInstr = "br_table \{joinWith " " labels} \{dftLabel}"
  let opens =
    ["block " ++ dftLabel]
      ++ map (k => "block $swt\{sfx}_\{intToString k}") (rangeList 0 nOrd)
  let pick = discrimReadOf svRead ty ++ [tableInstr]
  opens
    ++ pick
    ++ towerBodiesTail
      prog
      env
      arity
      d
      root
      svRead
      rest
      arms
      branches
      dft
      ty
      sd
      (nOrd - 1)

towerBodiesTail : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List String ->
  List String ->
  List (List String) ->
  List CArm ->
  OrdMap CTBranch ->
  CTree ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List String
towerBodiesTail prog env arity d root svRead rest arms branches dft ty sd k =
  if k < 0 then
    ["end"] ++ emitTreeTail prog env arity d root rest arms dft
  else
    ["end"]
      ++ emitOrdinalSlotTail
        prog
        env
        arity
        d
        root
        svRead
        rest
        arms
        branches
        ty
        sd
        k
      ++ towerBodiesTail
        prog
        env
        arity
        d
        root
        svRead
        rest
        arms
        branches
        dft
        ty
        sd
        (k - 1)

emitOrdinalSlotTail : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List String ->
  List String ->
  List (List String) ->
  List CArm ->
  OrdMap CTBranch ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List String
emitOrdinalSlotTail prog env arity d root svRead rest arms branches ty sd k =
  match branchForOrdinal branches k
    Some (CTBranch h sub) =>
      -- #712: key the field-extract cast off the CHead (headCtorStructName), not the
      -- bare ctor name — so a built-in `HCons` stays on the reserved `$C_Cons` even when
      -- a user ADT also declares a `Cons` (which resolves to `$CU_Cons`).
      let cs = headCtorStructName prog h
      let a = snd (conHeadInfoUnsafe prog h)
      let fieldOccs =
        map
          (i =>
            svRead
              ++ [
                "ref.cast (ref $" ++ cs ++ ")",
                "struct.get $\{cs} \{intToString (i + 1)}",
              ])
          (rangeList 0 a)
      emitTreeTail prog env arity d root (fieldOccs ++ rest) arms sub
    None => ["br $swdt" ++ intToString sd]

-- `idt` (trailing) is the chain's own INDENT depth — see emitLitSwitchRef (#381).
emitLitSwitchTail : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List String ->
  List String ->
  List (List String) ->
  List CArm ->
  List CTBranch ->
  CTree ->
  Int ->
  List String
emitLitSwitchTail prog env arity d root foc rest arms [] dft idt =
  indentBy idt (emitTreeTail prog env arity d root rest arms dft)
-- #759: unbox to i64 ($mdk_unbox_int handles i31 immediate OR $boxint) and compare at
-- full width, so a head |k| >= 2^30 neither overflows `i32.const` (module rejected) nor
-- ref.casts a boxed scrutinee to i31 (trap).
emitLitSwitchTail prog env arity d root foc rest arms ((CTBranch (HLit (LInt k)) sub) :: more) dft idt =
  indentBy
      idt
      (foc
        ++ [unboxIntW prog, "i64.const " ++ intToString k, "i64.eq"]
        ++ ["if"])
    ++ indentBy (idt + 1) (emitTreeTail prog env arity d root rest arms sub)
    ++ indentBy idt ["else"]
    ++ emitLitSwitchTail prog env arity d root foc rest arms more dft (idt + 1)
    ++ indentBy idt ["end", "unreachable"]
-- W6: Char-literal switch head — a Char is an i31 codepoint immediate (cf.
-- `PLit (LChar)`); compare the i31 against the codepoint constant.
emitLitSwitchTail prog env arity d root foc rest arms ((CTBranch (HLit (LChar c)) sub) :: more) dft idt =
  indentBy
      idt
      (foc
        ++ [
          "ref.cast (ref i31)",
          "i31.get_u",
          "i32.const "
            ++ intToString (charCode (arrayGetUnsafe 0 (stringToChars c))),
          "i32.eq",
        ]
        ++ ["if"])
    ++ indentBy (idt + 1) (emitTreeTail prog env arity d root rest arms sub)
    ++ indentBy idt ["else"]
    ++ emitLitSwitchTail prog env arity d root foc rest arms more dft (idt + 1)
    ++ indentBy idt ["end", "unreachable"]
-- W6: String-literal switch head — compare the focus $str against each literal via
-- `$mdk_str_compare` (returns the i31 1 on equal), reusing the `PLit (LString)` logic.
emitLitSwitchTail prog env arity d root foc rest arms ((CTBranch (HLit (LString s)) sub) :: more) dft idt =
  indentBy
      idt
      (foc
        ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)"]
        ++ emitLitRef prog (LString s)
        ++ [
          rtCallW prog "mdk_str_compare" 2,
          "ref.cast (ref i31)",
          "i31.get_u",
          "i32.const 1",
          "i32.eq",
        ]
        ++ ["if"])
    ++ indentBy (idt + 1) (emitTreeTail prog env arity d root rest arms sub)
    ++ indentBy idt ["else"]
    ++ emitLitSwitchTail prog env arity d root foc rest arms more dft (idt + 1)
    ++ indentBy idt ["end", "unreachable"]
emitLitSwitchTail prog _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ =
  gapLP prog "ref-mode: non-Int literal tail switch head"

-- ── §4 closure (CLam) lowering — lambda-lift + arity-in-struct ───────────────
-- A CLam is lambda-lifted to a top-level $codety function `$mdk_lamN`.  Its FREE
-- variables (names referenced in the body, minus the lambda's own params, that are
-- live in the enclosing env) are CAPTURED into the closure's $env array, in a fixed
-- order.  The lifted function reads its captures from `self`'s $env (cast to $clos)
-- and its params from the $args array.  At the USE site we build the $clos struct:
-- code = `ref.func $mdk_lamN`, arity = the lambda's param count, env = the captured
-- values emitted from the current env.  Arity lives IN THE STRUCT (§11) so apply
-- never consults a name-keyed table.
emitClosure : Prog -> Env -> Int -> List Pat -> CExpr -> List String
emitClosure prog env d pats body =
  let n = freshLamId (progEmit prog)
  let lamName = "$mdk_lam" ++ intToString n
  -- W2/cat2: a param may be a destructuring pattern (tuple/ctor); its BOUND vars
  -- (patVars) — not a single synthetic name — are what the body's free-var set
  -- subtracts, so the captures are computed over the real bound names.
  let boundVars = flatMap patVars pats
  let captured =
    filterList (c => envHas c env) (dedupKeep (freeVarsExpr boundVars body))
  let _ = noteFuncRef prog lamName
  let _ =
    addLifted
      prog
      lamName
      codeShapeW
      (emitLamDefine prog lamName pats captured (envRestrict captured env) body)
  -- build the closure struct at the use site: ref.func, arity, env array of captures.
  -- S-4: with NO captures every operand is constant, so hoist the struct to a module
  -- global (wConstClos) instead of rebuilding it on each evaluation of the `CLam`.
  match captured
    [] => wConstClos prog lamName (listLen pats)
    _ =>
      let capInstrs = flatMap (c => ["local.get $" ++ gname c]) captured
      [refFuncW prog lamName, "i32.const " ++ intToString (listLen pats)]
        ++ capInstrs
        ++ [
          "array.new_fixed $argarr " ++ intToString (listLen captured),
          "struct.new $clos",
        ]

-- the lifted lambda body.  Prologue: bind each captured var from self's $env (cast
-- self to $clos, get $env, array.get i, non-null) into its local; bind each param
-- from the $args array.  Then TAIL-emit the body.
emitLamDefine : Prog ->
  String ->
  List Pat ->
  List String ->
  Env ->
  CExpr ->
  List String
emitLamDefine prog lamName pats captured capEnv body =
  let arity = listLen pats
  -- each param i: load $args[i] into a synthetic local `$__lp<i>`, then bind its
  -- (possibly-destructuring) pattern against that local via bindPatRef (the same
  -- field-extraction machinery match-arm leaves / destructuring-lets use).
  let synthPs = map (i => "__lp" ++ intToString i) (rangeList 0 arity)
  let w7Outer = w7ScopeOpen (progEmit prog)
  let capPrologue = flatMap capLoadAt (zipIdx captured 0)
  let argLoads = flatMap argLoadAt (zipIdx synthPs 0)
  let (paramBinds, bodyEnv0) =
    bindParamPats
      prog
      (envExtendUnstamped synthPs capEnv)
      (zipPatsP pats synthPs)
  let bodyEnv = bodyEnv0
  let patBoundVars = flatMap patVars pats
  let bodyLocals =
    filterList
      (notIn (synthPs ++ captured ++ patBoundVars))
      (dedupKeep (collectExprLocals body))
  let scratch = scratchLocals (maxRefDepth body)
  let localLines =
    ["(local $__self_clos (ref $clos))"]
      ++ map
        (l => localDeclRef l)
        (synthPs ++ captured ++ patBoundVars ++ bodyLocals ++ scratch)
  let setup =
    ["local.get $self", "ref.cast (ref $clos)", "local.set $__self_clos"]
  -- A lifted lambda is an INDEPENDENT function: it must NOT inherit the enclosing
  -- fn's TMC loop context nor a dispatch-group context, so its body is emitted
  -- with `progInFn`.
  -- emitLamDefine can run while one of those is LIVE (a cons-tail clause body whose
  -- lead-field / recomputed-arg builds a closure is emitted under a live trmc context),
  -- and without clearing it the lambda body's tail leaves would emit `$__tmc_*` /
  -- `$tmcloop` references that this lambda never declares as locals → invalid wasm.
  let bodyLines = emitRefTail (progInFn prog) bodyEnv arity body
  let w7Decls =
    w7LocalDecls (w7ScopeClose (progEmit prog) w7Outer) (maxRefDepth body)
  [
      "  (func "
        ++ lamName
        ++ " (type $codety) (param $self (ref eq)) (param $args (ref $argarr)) (result (ref eq))",
    ]
    ++ map ("  " ++ _) (localLines ++ w7Decls)
    ++ indent (setup ++ capPrologue ++ argLoads ++ paramBinds ++ bodyLines)
    ++ ["  )"]

-- bind a list of (pattern, synthetic-local-name) lambda params: for each, run
-- bindPatRef against `local.get $<synth>` (the pattern is irrefutable — the type
-- proves the shape, like a destructuring let).  Threads the env left-to-right.
bindParamPats : Prog -> Env -> List (Pat, String) -> (List String, Env)
bindParamPats _ env [] = ([], env)
bindParamPats prog env ((p, a) :: rest) =
  let (binds, env2) = bindPatRef prog env p ["local.get $" ++ gname a]
  let (more, env3) = bindParamPats prog env2 rest
  (binds ++ more, env3)

-- zip patterns to synthetic param names (peer of zipPats but for synthetic params).
zipPatsP : List Pat -> List String -> List (Pat, String)
zipPatsP (p :: ps) (a :: bs) = (p, a) :: zipPatsP ps bs
zipPatsP _ _ = []

-- load captured var i: $__self_clos.$env[i] → its local.
capLoadAt : (String, Int) -> List String
capLoadAt (c, i) = [
  "local.get $__self_clos",
  "struct.get $clos $env",
  "i32.const " ++ intToString i,
  "array.get $argarr",
  "ref.as_non_null",
  "local.set $" ++ gname c,
]

-- load param i: $args[i] → its local.
argLoadAt : (String, Int) -> List String
argLoadAt (p, i) = [
  "local.get $args",
  "i32.const " ++ intToString i,
  "array.get $argarr",
  "ref.as_non_null",
  "local.set $" ++ gname p,
]

-- ── W9: CLetGroup (where / local letrec functions) ───────────────────────────
-- A `where`/`let`-group of (possibly mutually-recursive, multi-clause) LOCAL
-- functions, lambda-lifted to top-level functions.  Strategy (the wasm peer of
-- llvm_emit.emitKnotRun):
--   * groupCaps = the free vars across ALL bindings' clause bodies, minus every
--     binding's own params and minus the group's own names, kept to those visible
--     in the enclosing env.  This single capture set is shared by every member.
--   * each binding `name` is lifted to `$mdk_lgN_<name>` whose $env carries
--     groupCaps.  Its prologue (a) loads groupCaps from $env, (b) REBUILDS every
--     group member's closure (ref.func + arity + an $argarr of groupCaps) into a
--     local — so a member body referencing itself or a sibling resolves to a fresh
--     closure with the same captures (the knot is tied by reconstruction, no cyclic
--     heap value needed), (c) loads its own params from $args, then emits the
--     clause chain.
--   * the USE site (the group body) rebuilds the same closures into locals from the
--     enclosing env, then emits the body — so the body sees each group name bound.
-- A zero-binding group is just its body.
--
-- P1 — a NULLARY VALUE binding (`base = 10`, i.e. `CBind n [CClause [] rhs]`) is NOT a
-- local function and must NOT be lifted.  Lifting every member of the group
-- uniformly binds `base` in `where base = 10 …` to an arity-0 CLOSURE that is never
-- forced, and a sibling's `x + base` then runs $mdk_unbox_int over a `$clos` → the module
-- validates and traps `illegal cast` at instantiate (test/llvm_fixtures/where_sibling_ref).
-- llvm_emit's emitLetGroup has always had the dedicated nullary-value arm; ref-mode
-- didn't.  Fix: evaluate a value binding's rhs at the use site into its local, and hand
-- the value to the lifted members as an ordinary CAPTURE (it joins groupCaps, so each
-- member loads it from $env exactly like any enclosing free var).  Values are computed
-- before the closures because the closures capture them — so a value binding whose rhs
-- calls a sibling FUNCTION is the one shape this cannot tie, and it is rejected
-- precisely rather than miscompiled (llvm_emit rejects the mirror case in emitKnotRun).
-- #314: a block-statement function-`let` (`let go i = … go …`) — a single
-- self-recursive LOCAL function that the CBlock emitters (emitBlockTail /
-- emitBlockRef) would otherwise lower as a plain `CLam` capture, leaving the
-- self-call `go` unbound in the lifted body (build-fail; eval worked because it
-- binds the name first).  Reuse the W9 letgroup machinery for a ONE-member group:
-- lift `$mdk_lgN_go` (its prologue rebuilds `go`'s own closure into a local, so the
-- self-call resolves), then at the use site rebuild `go`'s closure into local `$go`.
-- Returns the use-site rebuild instrs; the caller binds `go` (`envBind`) for the rest
-- of the block.  Peer of the native emitter's `emitRecLam` route in emitBlock.
emitSelfRecLocalBind : Prog ->
  Env ->
  String ->
  BinderId ->
  List Pat ->
  CExpr ->
  List String
emitSelfRecLocalBind prog env x bid pats body =
  let gid = freshLamId (progEmit prog)
  let bind = CBind x [CClause pats body] noDeclLoc bid
  let groupCaps =
    filterList
      (c => envHas c env)
      (dedupKeep (filterList (notIn [x]) (freeVarsClauses [] bind)))
  let groupEnv = envBind x bid (envRestrict groupCaps env)
  let _ = emitLgLifted prog gid [x] groupCaps groupEnv [bind] bind
  -- one-member group: `useSiteRebuilds`'s later-sibling guard is vacuous here, so a
  -- capture-free `go` reaches the hoisted-global branch.  Self-reference is not a
  -- forward reference — the knot is tied inside the lifted prologue, not here.
  useSiteRebuilds prog gid groupCaps [bind]

-- A let-group: its members, then `body` emitted by `emitBody` with every member
-- bound (`emitLetWith`'s contract).
emitLetGroupWith : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  (Env -> CExpr -> List String) ->
  List CBind ->
  CExpr ->
  List String
emitLetGroupWith prog env d emitBody binds body =
  let gid = freshLamId (progEmit prog)
  let valBinds = filterList isLgValBind binds
  let fnBinds = filterList (b => not (isLgValBind b)) binds
  let valNames = map lgBindName valBinds
  let names = map lgBindName fnBinds
  let allParams = flatMap lgBindParams fnBinds
  let valFree = dedupKeep (flatMap (freeVarsClauses []) valBinds)
  if anyOfList names valFree then
    gapLP
      prog
      "wasm W9: unsupported let-group — a VALUE binding's right-hand side calls a sibling FUNCTION of the same group; the value must be computed before the group's closures are built (peer of the native emitter's knot-tying restriction)"
  else
    let freeCaps =
      filterList
        (c => envHas c env)
        (dedupKeep
          (filterList
            (notIn (names ++ valNames ++ allParams))
            (flatMap (freeVarsClauses []) binds)))
    -- the group's value bindings are shared by every member, so they ride along as caps.
    let groupCaps = freeCaps ++ valNames
    -- emit each lifted top-level fn (drained into the module like other lifted lams).
    let groupEnv = envBindGroups binds (envRestrict freeCaps env)
    let _ =
      forEachU
        (b => emitLgLifted prog gid names groupCaps groupEnv fnBinds b)
        fnBinds
    -- at the use site: compute the value bindings into their locals (each visible to the
    -- next), rebuild every FUNCTION member's closure, then emit the body with all bound.
    let valInit = emitLgValBinds prog env d valBinds
    let rebuilds = useSiteRebuilds prog gid groupCaps fnBinds
    valInit ++ rebuilds ++ emitBody (envBindGroups binds env) body

-- S-4: the USE-SITE closure rebuilds for a let-group.  A member whose group capture
-- set is EMPTY and which does not FORWARD-reference a later sibling builds a `$clos`
-- out of nothing but constants, so it reads one hoisted module global (wConstClos)
-- instead of rebuilding the struct on every entry to the enclosing function.
--
-- The forward-reference guard is the direct analogue of the LLVM emitter's routing
-- (`emitLetGroup` sends a binding that `refsLater` to `emitLetGroupKnot`, and only the
-- non-forward-referencing arm reaches the `emitGroupBind` hoist).  Self-recursion is
-- NOT a forward reference and stays eligible — the capture-free `where go … = … go …`
-- worker is exactly the shape this is for.  On THIS backend the guard is conservative
-- rather than load-bearing: `groupCaps` never contains a sibling's name (siblings are
-- subtracted when it is computed) and every `$clos` field is immutable, so the wasm
-- knot is tied by RECONSTRUCTION inside `emitLgLifted`'s prologue — which this never
-- touches — and not by patching the use-site struct.
useSiteRebuilds : Prog -> Int -> List String -> List CBind -> List String
useSiteRebuilds _ _ _ [] = []
useSiteRebuilds prog gid groupCaps (b :: rest) =
  let laterNames = map lgBindName rest
  let hoistable =
    listLen groupCaps == 0 && not (anyOfList laterNames (freeVarsClauses [] b))
  let here =
    if hoistable then
      constLgClosure prog gid b
    else
      rebuildLgClosure prog gid groupCaps b
  here ++ useSiteRebuilds prog gid groupCaps rest

-- S-4 (prologue half): the member-closure rebuilds a LIFTED member runs on every
-- entry, including a tail self-call's re-entry.  Its hoist condition is weaker than
-- the use site's: this materializes the group's ENTIRE member set before any body
-- line runs, so there is no later sibling to forward-reference — a member naming any
-- other member finds it in a local whichever order the rebuilds emitted in.  What is
-- left is the condition that makes a `$clos` constant at all, an empty `groupCaps`,
-- which is a property of the GROUP — so the group hoists whole or not at all.
liftedMemberRebuilds : Prog -> Int -> List String -> List CBind -> List String
liftedMemberRebuilds prog gid groupCaps binds =
  if listLen groupCaps == 0 then
    flatMap (b => constLgClosure prog gid b) binds
  else
    flatMap (b => rebuildLgClosure prog gid groupCaps b) binds

-- the hoisted-global form of rebuildLgClosure: same lifted code function, same arity,
-- an empty env — read from one module global and stored into the member's local.
constLgClosure : Prog -> Int -> CBind -> List String
constLgClosure prog gid (CBind name clauses _ _) =
  wConstClos
      prog
      "$mdk_lg\{intToString gid}_\{gname name}"
      (clauseArityOf clauses)
    ++ ["local.set $" ++ gname name]

-- P1: a CLetGroup member that is a nullary VALUE binding, not a local function.
isLgValBind : CBind -> Bool
isLgValBind (CBind _ [CClause [] _] _ _) = True
isLgValBind _ = False

-- P1: evaluate each value binding's rhs into its local, threading the bound names
-- through the env so a later value binding can reference an earlier one.
emitLgValBinds : Prog -> Env -> Int -> List CBind -> List String
emitLgValBinds _ _ _ [] = []
emitLgValBinds prog env d ((CBind name [CClause [] rhs] _ bid) :: rest) =
  emitRefExpr prog env d rhs
    ++ ["local.set $" ++ gname name]
    ++ emitLgValBinds prog (envBind name bid env) d rest
emitLgValBinds prog env d (_ :: rest) = emitLgValBinds prog env d rest

-- P1: does any name in `xs` occur in `ys`?
anyOfList : List String -> List String -> Bool
anyOfList xs ys = anyList (x => contains x ys) xs

-- params of a CLetGroup binding (the first clause's pattern arity → synthetic names).
lgBindParams : CBind -> List String
lgBindParams (CBind _ clauses _ _) = synthParams (clauseArityOf clauses)

-- the lifted member function `$mdk_lg<gid>_<name>`: $env = groupCaps; prologue loads
-- caps, rebuilds every member closure into its local, loads own params, emits clauses.
emitLgLifted : Prog ->
  Int ->
  List String ->
  List String ->
  Env ->
  List CBind ->
  CBind ->
  Unit
emitLgLifted prog gid names groupCaps groupEnv binds (CBind name clauses bindLoc _) =
  let memberProg =
    progForBinding
      ("lg:" ++ name)
      bindLoc
      (sitePackedW (progEmit prog) bindLoc)
      prog
  let lamName = "$mdk_lg\{intToString gid}_\{gname name}"
  let _ = noteFuncRef prog lamName
  let arity = clauseArityOf clauses
  -- synthetic names: this member also declares its group captures and sibling
  -- names as locals, so a source-named param could collide with either.
  let params = synthParams arity
  let w7Outer = w7ScopeOpen (progEmit prog)
  let capPrologue = flatMap capLoadAt (zipIdx groupCaps 0)
  let memberRebuilds = liftedMemberRebuilds prog gid groupCaps binds
  let argPrologue = flatMap argLoadAt (zipIdx params 0)
  -- a lifted letgroup member is an independent function: clear any live TMC /
  -- dispatch-group context so its body doesn't leak `$__tmc_*`/`$tmcloop` references
  -- (see emitLamDefine — same hazard when lifted under a live trmc context).
  let bodyLines =
    emitClausesRefEnv memberProg groupEnv name params arity clauses
  let memberLocals = names
  let bodyLocals =
    filterList
      (notIn (params ++ groupCaps ++ memberLocals))
      (dedupKeep (clauseLocals clauses))
  let scratch = scratchLocals (clausesMaxDepth clauses)
  let localLines =
    ["(local $__self_clos (ref $clos))"]
      ++ map (n => "(local $" ++ gname n ++ " (ref eq))") memberLocals
      ++ map
        (l => localDeclRef l)
        (params ++ groupCaps ++ bodyLocals ++ scratch)
      ++ w7LocalDecls
        (w7ScopeClose (progEmit prog) w7Outer)
        (clausesMaxDepth clauses)
  let setup =
    ["local.get $self", "ref.cast (ref $clos)", "local.set $__self_clos"]
  let def =
    [
        "  (func "
          ++ lamName
          ++ " (type $codety) (param $self (ref eq)) (param $args (ref $argarr)) (result (ref eq))",
      ]
      ++ map ("  " ++ _) localLines
      ++ indent
        (setup ++ capPrologue ++ memberRebuilds ++ argPrologue ++ bodyLines)
      ++ ["  )"]
  addLifted prog lamName codeShapeW def

-- rebuild ONE member's closure value (ref.func + arity + $argarr of groupCaps) and
-- bind it to its local `$<name>`.  Used BOTH at the use site and inside each lifted
-- member's prologue; groupCaps must be bound as locals in either context.
rebuildLgClosure : Prog -> Int -> List String -> CBind -> List String
rebuildLgClosure prog gid groupCaps (CBind name clauses _ _) =
  let lamName = "$mdk_lg\{intToString gid}_\{gname name}"
  let arity = clauseArityOf clauses
  let capInstrs = flatMap (c => ["local.get $" ++ gname c]) groupCaps
  [refFuncW prog lamName, "i32.const " ++ intToString arity]
    ++ capInstrs
    ++ [
      "array.new_fixed $argarr " ++ intToString (listLen groupCaps),
      "struct.new $clos",
      "local.set $" ++ gname name,
    ]

zipIdx : List String -> Int -> List (String, Int)
zipIdx [] _ = []
zipIdx (x :: xs) i = (x, i) :: zipIdx xs (i + 1)

-- free variables of a lambda body (names referenced, minus the bound params; we
-- also subtract names bound by inner let/lambda/match so only truly-free names
-- remain).  Returns names in first-seen order.
freeVarsExpr : List String -> CExpr -> List String
freeVarsExpr bound (CVar x _) = if contains x bound then [] else [x]
freeVarsExpr bound (CApp f args _) =
  freeVarsExpr bound f ++ flatMap (freeVarsExpr bound) args
-- A lambda param may be a DESTRUCTURING pattern (tuple/ctor) — e.g. a `do`-bind
-- with a tuple LHS `(a, b) <- m` desugars to `andThen m (\(a, b) => …)`.  Subtract
-- ALL its bound vars (patVars, like the CLet case), not `map patName` which only
-- accepts PVar/PWild and gaps on any real pattern.  (emitClosure/emitLamDefine
-- already destructure such params via bindPatRef; only this free-var walk lagged.)
freeVarsExpr bound (CLam pats b) =
  freeVarsExpr (flatMap patVars pats ++ bound) b
freeVarsExpr bound (CLit _) = []
freeVarsExpr bound (CBinPrim _ l r _ _) =
  freeVarsExpr bound l ++ freeVarsExpr bound r
freeVarsExpr bound (CUnOp _ x) = freeVarsExpr bound x
freeVarsExpr bound (CIf c t f) =
  freeVarsExpr bound c ++ freeVarsExpr bound t ++ freeVarsExpr bound f
freeVarsExpr bound (CLet _ pat e1 e2) =
  freeVarsExpr bound e1 ++ freeVarsExpr (patVars pat ++ bound) e2
freeVarsExpr bound (CBlock stmts) = freeVarsStmts bound stmts
freeVarsExpr bound (CDecision scrut arms _) =
  freeVarsExpr bound scrut ++ flatMap (freeVarsArm bound) arms
freeVarsExpr bound (CMatch scrut arms) =
  freeVarsExpr bound scrut ++ flatMap (freeVarsArm bound) arms
freeVarsExpr bound (CLetGroup binds b) =
  let names = map lgBindName binds
  let bound2 = names ++ bound
  flatMap (freeVarsClauses bound2) binds ++ freeVarsExpr bound2 b
-- compound value nodes: their sub-expressions can reference outer-bound vars
-- (e.g. a do-block's `pure (a, b, c)` lowers to CTuple — without this arm the
-- captured `a`/`b` are dropped and emit as unbound).  Each descends with the
-- SAME `bound` (these nodes introduce no binders).
freeVarsExpr bound (CTuple es) = flatMap (freeVarsExpr bound) es
freeVarsExpr bound (CList es) = flatMap (freeVarsExpr bound) es
freeVarsExpr bound (CArray es) = flatMap (freeVarsExpr bound) es
freeVarsExpr bound (CRecord _ fields) = flatMap (freeVarsField bound) fields
freeVarsExpr bound (CFieldAccess e _ _ _) = freeVarsExpr bound e
freeVarsExpr bound (CRecordUpdate _ e fields) =
  freeVarsExpr bound e ++ flatMap (freeVarsField bound) fields
freeVarsExpr bound (CVariantUpdate _ e fields) =
  freeVarsExpr bound e ++ flatMap (freeVarsField bound) fields
freeVarsExpr bound (CRangeList lo hi _) =
  freeVarsExpr bound lo ++ freeVarsExpr bound hi
freeVarsExpr bound (CRangeArray lo hi _) =
  freeVarsExpr bound lo ++ freeVarsExpr bound hi
freeVarsExpr bound (CIndex e i) = freeVarsExpr bound e ++ freeVarsExpr bound i
freeVarsExpr bound (CSlice e lo hi _) =
  freeVarsExpr bound e ++ freeVarsExpr bound lo ++ freeVarsExpr bound hi
