-- cat4/W5: a return-position method occurrence (CMethod) and a constrained-fn
-- occurrence (CDict) carry their dispatch Routes; a route's RDict/RDictFwd names a
-- dict PARAM that is read at the use site.  Without surfacing it here, a method/
-- constrained-fn call inside a lifted lambda (`clamp lo hi = min hi >> max lo`) or a
-- where-group closure (`minimum`/`maximum`'s `step`) drops the dict from the closure
-- capture set → "dict param '$dict_…' not in scope".  (These nodes carry no value
-- args of their own — args arrive via the surrounding CApp, already handled.)
freeVarsExpr bound (CMethod _ (MethodEvidence _ _ route implRoutes methRoutes)) =
  freeGivens bound (route :: implRoutes ++ methRoutes)
freeVarsExpr bound (CDict name routes) =
  (if contains name bound then [] else [name]) ++ freeGivens bound routes
freeVarsExpr bound _ = []

-- free vars of a CLetGroup binding's clauses (each clause's params are locally bound).
freeVarsClauses : List String -> CBind -> List String
freeVarsClauses bound (CBind _ clauses _ _) =
  flatMap (freeVarsClause bound) clauses

freeVarsClause : List String -> CClause -> List String
freeVarsClause bound (CClause pats body) =
  freeVarsExpr (flatMap patVars pats ++ bound) body

lgBindName : CBind -> String
lgBindName (CBind n _ _ _) = n

freeVarsStmts : List String -> List CStmt -> List String
freeVarsStmts _ [] = []
freeVarsStmts bound ((CSExpr e) :: rest) =
  freeVarsExpr bound e ++ freeVarsStmts bound rest
freeVarsStmts bound ((CSLet _ pat e) :: rest) =
  freeVarsExpr bound e ++ freeVarsStmts (patVars pat ++ bound) rest
freeVarsStmts bound (_ :: rest) = freeVarsStmts bound rest

freeVarsArm : List String -> CArm -> List String
freeVarsArm bound (CArm pat guards body) =
  let bound2 = patVars pat ++ bound
  flatMap (freeVarsGuard bound2) guards ++ freeVarsExpr bound2 body

freeVarsGuard : List String -> CGuard -> List String
freeVarsGuard bound (CGBool g) = freeVarsExpr bound g
freeVarsGuard bound (CGBind p e) = freeVarsExpr bound e

freeVarsField : List String -> CField -> List String
freeVarsField bound (CField _ _ e) = freeVarsExpr bound e

-- ── ADT construction (§3.4) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- A NULLARY ctor → an `i31ref` carrying its PER-TYPE dense ordinal (the same value
-- a payload ctor stores in struct field 0, so one discriminant read + one br_table
-- cover both reps within a match).  Two nullary ctors of DIFFERENT types could
-- share an i31 ordinal, but a well-typed match's scrutinee is one fixed type, so
-- only that type's ctors are ever compared — no cross-type aliasing.  The §3.4
-- structural-collapse caution is about STRUCTS (handled by the per-ctor struct type
-- + explicit i32 tag field), not i31 immediates.  A PAYLOAD ctor → `struct.new
-- $S_ctor` with the per-type dense ordinal as i32 field 0, then the (ref eq) fields.
emitCtorConstruct : Prog -> Env -> Int -> String -> List CExpr -> List String
emitCtorConstruct prog env d ctor args =
  let arity = ctorArity prog ctor
  if arity == 0 then
    ["i32.const " ++ intToString (ctorOrdinal prog ctor), "ref.i31"]
  else
    let tagField = ["i32.const " ++ intToString (ctorOrdinal prog ctor)]
    let argInstrs = flatMap (a => emitRefExpr prog env d a) args
    tagField ++ argInstrs ++ ["struct.new $" ++ ctorStructName ctor]

-- ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- W7 — collections (§3.3): List / Tuple / Array / Record / Ref, ranges, index/slice
-- ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

-- a tuple: a single-shape struct `$C_Tup<n>` (tag-0 field + n (ref eq) fields).
-- Reuses the W3 ctor construction shape (a leading i32 tag = ordinal 0) so the match
-- machinery (discrimReadOf → struct field-0) drives HTuple uniformly.
emitTupleRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> List CExpr -> List String
emitTupleRef prog env d es =
  let n = listLen es
  let argInstrs = flatMap (a => emitRefExpr prog env d a) es
  ["i32.const 0"]
    ++ argInstrs
    ++ ["struct.new $" ++ ctorStructName (tupleCtorName n)]

-- a list literal: a right-nested cons spine ending in the Nil i31.  Built
-- back-to-front so the emitted struct.news nest correctly (Cons head tail).
-- #712/S0: the `[]` terminator is the BUILT-IN list Nil — emit its reserved ordinal
-- i31 directly, not `emitCtorConstruct "Nil"` (whose `ctorOrdinal "Nil"` a coexisting
-- user `Nil` ctor would poison to the user's declaration-order ordinal).
-- Assembled LINEARLY.  A two-clause recursion emitting, per cons level,
-- `["i32.const 0"] ++ hd ++ tl ++ ["struct.new $C_Cons"]` right-associates the
-- `tl ++ ["struct.new $C_Cons"]`, COPYING the growing accumulated instruction list at
-- each of N levels — O(n²) instruction-cons allocation in list-literal width (#522;
-- the LLVM peer emitList/emitRtList prepends via `::` and is linear).  The emitted WAT
-- is BYTE-IDENTICAL: N leading `(i32.const 0, <head instrs>)` prefixes, then the
-- built-in Nil i31 terminator, then N `struct.new $C_Cons` closers — exactly the
-- flattening of the old right-nested `struct.new (Cons hd tl)` spine.  Each `flatMap`
-- chunk / `replicate` cell is constant-length, so total assembly is O(n).
emitListRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> List CExpr -> List String
emitListRef prog env d es =
  let prefixes = flatMap (x => ["i32.const 0"] ++ emitRefExpr prog env d x) es
  let nilTerm =
    ["i32.const " ++ intToString (syntheticCtorOrdinal "Nil"), "ref.i31"]
  let closers = replicate (listLen es) "struct.new $C_Cons"
  prefixes ++ nilTerm ++ closers

-- a range list [lo..hi] / [lo..=hi]: a back-to-front counted loop building the cons
-- spine in a scratch accumulator local.  The accumulator + counter reuse the
-- depth-keyed scratch locals ($__rl_acc<d> / $__rl_i<d>) declared in the header.
emitRangeListRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> CExpr -> CExpr -> Bool -> List String
-- The bounds unbox to i64 ($mdk_unbox_int), so a bound outside ±2^30 works, and
-- the count is raw i64 arithmetic on two 63-bit values: `hi + 1` at intMaxBound is
-- 2^62, which i64 holds, so `[lo..=intMaxBound]` neither traps nor comes out empty.
-- Each element `lo + i` lies in [lo, hi] and boxes through $mdk_box_int.
emitRangeListRef prog env d lo hi incl =
  let loI = emitRefExpr prog env d lo ++ [unboxIntW prog]
  let hiI = emitRefExpr prog env d hi ++ [unboxIntW prog]
  let sfx = intToString d
  let accL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__rlacc" sfx
  let iL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__rli" sfx
  let loL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__rllo" sfx
  -- count = (incl ? hi+1 : hi) - lo ; clamped at 0 by the loop guard.
  let adj = if incl then ["i64.const 1", "i64.add"] else []
  -- stash lo, init acc=Nil, i = count-1, loop i>=0: acc = Cons (lo+i) acc.
  loI
    ++ ["local.set " ++ loL]
    ++ ["i32.const 1", "ref.i31", "local.set " ++ accL]
    ++ hiI
    ++ adj
    ++ [
      "local.get " ++ loL,
      "i64.sub",
      "i64.const 1",
      "i64.sub",
      "local.set " ++ iL,
    ]
    ++ ["block $rld" ++ sfx, "loop $rll" ++ sfx]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ iL, "i64.const 0", "i64.lt_s", "br_if $rld" ++ sfx]
    ++ ["i32.const 0"]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ loL, "local.get " ++ iL, "i64.add", boxIntW prog]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ accL]
    ++ ["struct.new $C_Cons", "local.set " ++ accL]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ iL, "i64.const 1", "i64.sub", "local.set " ++ iL]
    ++ ["br $rll" ++ sfx, "end", "end"]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ accL]

-- an array literal: array.new_fixed over the emitted element values.
emitArrayCreateRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> List CExpr -> List String
emitArrayCreateRef prog env d es =
  let argInstrs = flatMap (a => emitRefExpr prog env d a) es
  argInstrs ++ ["array.new_fixed $arr " ++ intToString (listLen es)]

-- a range array [lo..hi] / [lo..=hi]: allocate `count` slots, fill with a counted
-- loop (peer to llvm_emit.emitRangeArray's alloca-counter loop).
emitRangeArrayRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> CExpr -> CExpr -> Bool -> List String
emitRangeArrayRef prog env d lo hi incl =
  let loI = emitRefExpr prog env d lo ++ [unboxIntW prog]
  let hiI = emitRefExpr prog env d hi ++ [unboxIntW prog]
  let sfx = intToString d
  let arrL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__raarr" sfx
  let iL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__rai" sfx
  let loL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__ralo" sfx
  let cntL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__racnt" sfx
  -- the bound and count arithmetic is i64, as in emitRangeListRef; the slot index
  -- stays i32, the width `array.new`/`array.set` take.
  let adj = if incl then ["i64.const 1", "i64.add"] else []
  loI
    ++ ["local.set " ++ loL]
    ++ hiI
    ++ adj
    ++ ["local.get " ++ loL, "i64.sub", "local.set " ++ cntL]
    -- clamp negative count to 0
    ++ [
      "local.get " ++ cntL,
      "i64.const 0",
      "i64.lt_s",
      "if",
      "i64.const 0",
      "local.set " ++ cntL,
      "end",
    ]
    -- a count past array.new's i32 length is clamped to the largest one, whose
    -- allocation fails, rather than wrapped to a small array.
    ++ [
      "local.get " ++ cntL,
      "i64.const 2147483647",
      "i64.gt_s",
      "if",
      "i64.const 2147483647",
      "local.set " ++ cntL,
      "end",
    ]
    ++ [
      "i32.const 0",
      "ref.i31",
      "local.get " ++ cntL,
      "i32.wrap_i64",
      "array.new $arr",
      "local.set " ++ arrL,
    ]
    ++ ["i32.const 0", "local.set " ++ iL]
    ++ ["block $rad" ++ sfx, "loop $ral" ++ sfx]
    ++ [
      "local.get " ++ iL,
      "i64.extend_i32_u",
      "local.get " ++ cntL,
      "i64.ge_s",
      "br_if $rad" ++ sfx,
    ]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ arrL, "ref.as_non_null", "local.get " ++ iL]
    ++ [
      "local.get " ++ loL,
      "local.get " ++ iL,
      "i64.extend_i32_u",
      "i64.add",
      boxIntW prog,
    ]
    ++ ["array.set $arr"]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ iL, "i32.const 1", "i32.add", "local.set " ++ iL]
    ++ ["br $ral" ++ sfx, "end", "end"]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ arrL, "ref.as_non_null"]

-- CIndex arr i: bounds-check (i<0 or i>=len → trap, matching native @mdk_oob), then
-- array.get.  The trap is `unreachable` (WasmGC has no host-trap call here; an OOB
-- access aborting the module mirrors the native abort).
emitIndexRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> CExpr -> CExpr -> List String
emitIndexRef prog env d a i =
  let sfx = intToString d
  let arrL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__ixarr" sfx
  let idxL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__ixi" sfx
  let arrI =
    emitRefExpr prog env d a ++ ["ref.cast (ref $arr)", "local.set " ++ arrL]
  let idxI =
    emitRefExpr prog env d i
      ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_s", "local.set " ++ idxL]
  arrI
    ++ idxI
    -- bounds: idx < 0 || idx >= len → B5 coded [E-INDEX-OOB] trap (peer of native
    -- @mdk_oob; message matches medaka_rt.c, sans the index value native also omits).
    ++ ["local.get " ++ idxL, "i32.const 0", "i32.lt_s"]
    ++ [
      "local.get " ++ idxL,
      "local.get " ++ arrL,
      "ref.as_non_null",
      "array.len",
      "i32.ge_s",
    ]
    ++ ["i32.or", "if"]
    ++ indent (wasmTrap (progEmit prog) "E-INDEX-OOB" "index out of bounds")
    ++ ["end"]
    ++ [
      "local.get " ++ arrL,
      "ref.as_non_null",
      "local.get " ++ idxL,
      "array.get $arr",
      "ref.as_non_null",
    ]

-- CSlice arr lo hi incl: bounds-check, then new array of (end-lo) slots, copy via
-- array.copy.  end = incl ? hi+1 : hi.
--
-- #550: this used to carry NO bounds check — the comment here read "an over-range copy
-- traps in-engine", which was true but is not the contract: the trap is a RAW ENGINE
-- trap, not the coded [E-SLICE-OOB] line `run` produces (sliceArray, eval.mdk).  So wasm
-- was memory-safe but diagnosed wrong, while the LLVM backend (which the comment claimed
-- to "mirror") had no check at all and read out of bounds.  Both are now guarded on the
-- same predicate: `lo < 0 || end > len || end - lo < 0`.  Guarding explicitly rather than
-- leaning on array.new/array.copy's own traps also keeps the two backends' ABORT
-- CONDITION identical instead of merely coincidentally-both-fatal.
--
-- Message parity, and its one REMAINING GAP: this trap line is static bytes (wasmTrap
-- streams them through $mdk_write_err_byte at emit time, no $str value and no data
-- segment), so wasm reports the CODE but not the `[lo..hi]` numbers that eval and
-- native's @mdk_slice_oob both print.
--
-- E-INDEX-OOB does not have this gap: #1787's wasmTrapNum
-- streams a runtime value through $mdk_write_err_int between two fixed byte runs, so
-- all three engines name the offending index.  The same treatment would work here (two
-- numbers instead of one); it is simply not done yet.
--
-- ⚠️ Do NOT read this gap as unobserved.  An earlier version of this comment claimed
-- "nothing compares stderr text across engines: diff_wasm*.sh diff stdout" — that has
-- been FALSE since #531, which made test/wasm/diff_wasm_modules.sh compare stdout,
-- stderr AND exit code (see its `diverges` reporting).  E-SLICE-OOB survives only
-- because no wasm module fixture trips an out-of-range slice; add one and this gate
-- goes red until the numbers match.  (diff_compiler_engines.sh does still classify an
-- interpreter `runtime error [E-` as n/a.)
-- The ABORT CONDITION — which is what soundness turns on — is identical on all three.
emitSliceRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  CExpr ->
  CExpr ->
  CExpr ->
  Bool ->
  List String
emitSliceRef prog env d a lo hi incl =
  let sfx = intToString d
  let srcL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__slsrc" sfx
  let dstL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__sldst" sfx
  let loL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__sllo" sfx
  let lenL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__sllen" sfx
  let arrI =
    emitRefExpr prog env d a ++ ["ref.cast (ref $arr)", "local.set " ++ srcL]
  let loI =
    emitRefExpr prog env d lo
      ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_s", "local.set " ++ loL]
  let hiI = emitRefExpr prog env d hi ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_s"]
  let adj = if incl then ["i32.const 1", "i32.add"] else []
  -- `end` is live on the stack after adj; stash it in lenL, guard, then turn it into the
  -- element count.  Ordering matters: the `end > len` compare needs `end`, and the
  -- `len < 0` compare needs `end - lo`, so the two uses are sequenced through lenL.
  let guardI =
    ["local.set " ++ lenL]
      -- lo < 0
      ++ ["local.get " ++ loL, "i32.const 0", "i32.lt_s"]
      -- end > array.len src
      ++ [
        "local.get " ++ lenL,
        "local.get " ++ srcL,
        "ref.as_non_null",
        "array.len",
        "i32.gt_s",
        "i32.or",
      ]
      -- (end - lo) < 0  (inverted range)
      ++ [
        "local.get " ++ lenL,
        "local.get " ++ loL,
        "i32.sub",
        "i32.const 0",
        "i32.lt_s",
        "i32.or",
      ]
      ++ ["if"]
      ++ indent (wasmTrap (progEmit prog) "E-SLICE-OOB" "slice out of bounds")
      ++ ["end"]
      ++ [
        "local.get " ++ lenL,
        "local.get " ++ loL,
        "i32.sub",
        "local.set " ++ lenL,
      ]
  arrI
    ++ loI
    ++ hiI
    ++ adj
    ++ guardI
    ++ [
      "i32.const 0",
      "ref.i31",
      "local.get " ++ lenL,
      "array.new $arr",
      "local.set " ++ dstL,
    ]
    -- array.copy dst dstoff src srcoff len
    ++ [
      "local.get " ++ dstL,
      "ref.as_non_null",
      "i32.const 0",
      "local.get " ++ srcL,
      "ref.as_non_null",
      "local.get " ++ loL,
      "local.get " ++ lenL,
      "array.copy $arr $arr",
    ]
    ++ ["local.get " ++ dstL, "ref.as_non_null"]

-- a named-field record construction: CRecord carries fields in DECLARED order
-- (lowering preserves it), so emit positionally — identical to a positional ctor
-- struct.new (the ctor IS a W3 user ctor with a $C_<name> struct already declared).
emitRecordRef : Prog -> Env -> Int -> String -> List CField -> List String
emitRecordRef prog env d name fields =
  let tagField = ["i32.const " ++ intToString (ctorOrdinal prog name)]
  let argInstrs = flatMap (f => emitRefExpr prog env d (cFieldExpr f)) fields
  tagField ++ argInstrs ++ ["struct.new $" ++ ctorStructName name]

-- field access `r.label`: cast to the record's ctor struct and struct.get the field
-- at index (1 + its declared ordinal), both stamped by `core_ir_lower`.  The label
-- `value` is always a `Ref` read (the typechecker refuses `.value` on a record),
-- whatever ordinal it carries, as in llvm_emit's `emitFieldAccess`.
emitFieldAccessRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  CExpr ->
  String ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  List String
emitFieldAccessRef prog env d ex label recName ord =
  if label == "value" then
    -- a $refbox read: cast to $refbox and read the mutable field at slot 0.
    emitRefExpr prog env d ex
      ++ ["ref.cast (ref $refbox)", "struct.get $refbox 0"]
  else if ord >= 0 then
    emitRefExpr prog env d ex
      ++ [
        "ref.cast (ref $" ++ ctorStructName recName ++ ")",
        "struct.get $\{ctorStructName recName} \{intToString (ord + 1)}",
      ]
  else
    gapLP
      prog
      ("ref-mode: CFieldAccess on unknown field '"
        ++ label
        ++ "' (no record ctor in the field-order table)")

-- functional update `{ base | f = v … }`: copy the base's struct, overriding the
-- fields at the stamped ordinals.
emitRecordUpdateRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  CExpr ->
  List CField ->
  List String
emitRecordUpdateRef prog env d recName base fields =
  emitUpdateCopy prog env d recName base fields

-- named-field variant update `Con { base | f = v … }`: same copy, ctor known.
emitVariantUpdateRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  CExpr ->
  List CField ->
  List String
emitVariantUpdateRef prog env d con base fields =
  emitUpdateCopy prog env d con base fields

-- the shared copy-with-overrides: stash the base into a scratch local, then build a
-- struct.new whose tag is the ctor ordinal and whose fields are, per ordinal, the
-- override expr (if present) or a struct.get of the stashed base.  The base local
-- stays live across the override exprs, so they are emitted one depth deeper: an
-- update nested in an override (`{ r | f = { r.f | g = v } }`) stashes its own base
-- in `$__rub<d+1>` instead of overwriting this one.
emitUpdateCopy : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  CExpr ->
  List CField ->
  List String
emitUpdateCopy prog env d ctor base fields =
  let sfx = intToString d
  let bL = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__rub" sfx
  let baseI =
    emitRefExpr prog env d base
      ++ ["ref.cast (ref $" ++ ctorStructName ctor ++ ")", "local.set " ++ bL]
  let tagField = ["i32.const " ++ intToString (ctorOrdinal prog ctor)]
  baseI
    ++ tagField
    ++ flatMap
      (idx => oneUpdateField prog env d ctor bL fields idx)
      (rangeList 0 (ctorArity prog ctor))
    ++ ["struct.new $" ++ ctorStructName ctor]

oneUpdateField : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  String ->
  List CField ->
  Int ->
  List String
oneUpdateField prog env d ctor bL fields idx = match findUpdateExpr idx fields
  Some ex => emitRefExpr prog env (d + 1) ex
  None => [
    "local.get " ++ bL,
    "ref.cast (ref $" ++ ctorStructName ctor ++ ")",
    "struct.get $\{ctorStructName ctor} \{intToString (idx + 1)}",
  ]

findUpdateExpr : Int -> List CField -> Option CExpr
findUpdateExpr _ [] = None
findUpdateExpr idx ((CField _ o ex) :: rest) =
  if o == idx then Some ex else findUpdateExpr idx rest

-- ── match lowering: CDecision → discriminant + br_table + field extraction ───
-- The scrutinee is a (ref eq).  The decision tree (CTree) is walked into a nest of
-- wasm blocks.  We mirror the LLVM emitter's structure: `root` is the whole
-- scrutinee value (kept for the leaf re-match that recovers bindings); each arm
-- body computes a (ref eq).  A CTSwitch on a constructor column reads the column's
-- discriminant (i31 nullary tag vs struct field-0 ordinal) and `br_table`s on the
-- dense per-type ordinal to the matching branch.
--
-- IMPLEMENTATION: a uniform result via a labelled block that all arms `br` out of
-- with their value.  Each arm stores its (ref eq) into a fresh result LOCAL and
-- branches to the shared end.  The tree's control flow is a tower of wasm `block`s.
-- We thread occurrence-values (the focus stack) as a list of "value-producing
-- instruction snippets" (each a List String that, executed, pushes that occurrence
-- onto the stack) — the LLVM emitter uses SSA register names; we use re-emittable
-- snippets (local.get of a stashed local), which keeps it stackless and simple.

-- CDecision at nesting depth `d`.  Stashes the scrutinee into scratch local
-- `$__rf<d>` (so the focus stack re-reads it), wraps the tree in a result block
-- `$dec<d>` that arm bodies `br` out of with their value, and recurses into the
-- tree at depth `d+1` (nested matches/switches get fresh, non-colliding locals +
-- labels).  `decLabel` is `$dec<d>` — the target every arm body branches to.
emitDecisionRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  CExpr ->
  List CArm ->
  CTree ->
  List String
emitDecisionRef prog env d scrut arms tree =
  let st = emitRefExpr prog env d scrut
  let scrutL = scratchLocal d
  let decLabel = "$dec" ++ intToString d
  let occ0 = ["local.get $" ++ scrutL]
  st
    ++ ["local.set $" ++ scrutL]
    ++ ["block " ++ decLabel ++ " (result (ref eq))"]
    ++ indent (emitTreeRef prog env (d + 1) decLabel occ0 [occ0] arms tree)
    ++ ["end"]

-- emit a CTree.  `d` = nesting depth (fresh locals/labels); `decLabel` = the
-- enclosing `$dec<n>` an arm body branches to; `root` = the scrutinee occurrence
-- snippet (for leaf re-match); `occs` = the live focus columns.  Every path leaves
-- exactly one (ref eq) for `decLabel`'s block to yield (via `br decLabel`), except
-- the default tail of a switch tower which falls through with the value on the stack.
emitTreeRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  List (List String) ->
  List CArm ->
  CTree ->
  List String
emitTreeRef prog env d decLabel root occs arms (CTFail fs) =
  wasmFailTrap (progEmit prog) fs
emitTreeRef prog env d decLabel root occs arms (CTLeaf i) =
  emitLeafRef prog env d decLabel root arms i
emitTreeRef prog env d decLabel root occs arms (CTGuard i fail) =
  emitGuardArmRef prog env d decLabel root occs arms i fail
emitTreeRef prog env d decLabel root occs arms (CTDrop sub) =
  emitTreeRef prog env d decLabel root (tailList occs) arms sub
emitTreeRef prog env d decLabel root occs arms (CTSwitch branches dft) =
  emitSwitchRef prog env d decLabel root occs arms branches dft

-- a leaf: re-match arm i's pattern against `root` to bind its PVars (loading struct
-- fields), then emit the body, then `br decLabel` with the value.
emitLeafRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  List CArm ->
  Int ->
  List String
emitLeafRef prog env d decLabel root arms i = match nthArm arms i
  Some (CArm pat _ body) =>
    let (binds, env2) = bindPatRef prog env pat root
    let bodyCode = emitRefExpr prog env2 d body
    binds ++ bodyCode ++ ["br " ++ decLabel]
  None => gapLP prog "ref-mode: decision arm index out of range"

-- a guarded arm: RE-MATCH the pattern, evaluate the guards; all-pass → body + br
-- decLabel; any fail → the `fail` subtree (resumes at the same column context).
-- Fall-through is a labelled block `$g<d>`: a failed guard `br_if $g<d>` skips the
-- body, then control falls into the fail subtree after the block's `end`.
-- G6 (#379): the re-match goes through `patTestBind` (test+bind against `gLabel`), not
-- `bindPatRef` (bind only) — a `PRng` arm canonicalizes to PWild in the matrix, so the
-- tree routes HERE unconditionally and this re-match must do the range comparison.
-- An irrefutable pattern emits NO test, so the plain-`if`-guard case is unchanged.
-- Mirrors llvm_emit's emitGuardedArm/`emitRefutArm`.  `root` is the scrutinee
-- `local.get` (occ0), which satisfies patTestBind's re-runnable-read contract.
emitGuardArmRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  List (List String) ->
  List CArm ->
  Int ->
  CTree ->
  List String
emitGuardArmRef prog env d decLabel root occs arms i fail = match nthArm arms i
  Some (CArm pat guards body) =>
    let gLabel = "$g" ++ intToString d
    let (tests, binds, env2) = patTestBind prog pat root gLabel env
    -- #379: guards now thread the env (a CGBind binds names the body can see), so the
    -- body is emitted under env3, not env2.
    let (gcode, env3) = emitGuardChainRef prog env2 d gLabel guards
    let armCode =
      ["block " ++ gLabel]
        ++ indent
          (tests
            ++ binds
            ++ gcode
            ++ emitRefExpr prog env3 d body
            ++ ["br " ++ decLabel])
        ++ ["end"]
    armCode ++ emitTreeRef prog env d decLabel root occs arms fail
  None => gapLP prog "ref-mode: guarded arm index out of range"

-- #379: the stash slot for a refutable pattern guard's right-hand side.  `patTestBind`
-- embeds its `occ` snippet once per test AND once per bind, so `occ` must be a cheap,
-- side-effect-free, re-runnable read — every other caller passes a `local.get`.  The
-- guard RHS must therefore be evaluated ONCE into a local.  The native peer just reuses
-- the SSA register `emitExpr` hands back (llvm_emit's `emitGuardChain`); wasm has no
-- free-mint temp, so the slot is declared like any other body local, via
-- `collectGuardLocals`.  ONE slot per function suffices: a stash is consumed
-- (tests ++ binds, into named locals) immediately after it is set, and a nested CGBind
-- inside the RHS finishes evaluating before the outer `local.set` — live ranges never
-- overlap, so no depth indexing is needed (unlike the `__rf<d>` scratch pool, which
-- `maxIndexAt` sizes by walking arm BODIES only, never their guards).
guardStashLocal : String
guardStashLocal = "__gbind"

-- emit a clause's guard chain left-to-right, THREADING the env: a `CGBind p <- e` binds
-- names that later guards AND the body can see -- which the old `flatMap` over a
-- FIXED env could not express.  A CGBool tests the unboxed i31 Bool; a
-- CGBind evaluates `e` into the stash and refutably matches `p` against it via
-- patTestBind (an irrefutable `p` emits no test and just binds; a refutable `Just x <- e`
-- tests the discriminant).  Either failure `br`s to gLabel, exiting the guard block and
-- landing in the fail subtree — the same fall-through the CGBool path always used.
-- Peer of the native emitter's `emitGuardChain`.  Returns (code, env').
emitGuardChainRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  List CGuard ->
  (List String, Env)
emitGuardChainRef _ env _ _ [] = ([], env)
emitGuardChainRef prog env d gLabel ((CGBool g) :: rest) =
  let unbox = ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_u", "i32.eqz", "br_if " ++ gLabel]
  let boolTest = emitRefExpr prog env d g ++ unbox
  let (more, env2) = emitGuardChainRef prog env d gLabel rest
  (boolTest ++ more, env2)
emitGuardChainRef prog env d gLabel ((CGBind p ex) :: rest) =
  let sv = gname guardStashLocal
  let rhs = emitRefExpr prog env d ex ++ ["local.set $" ++ sv]
  let (tests, binds, env2) = patTestBind prog p ["local.get $" ++ sv] gLabel env
  let (more, env3) = emitGuardChainRef prog env2 d gLabel rest
  (rhs ++ tests ++ binds ++ more, env3)

-- a CTSwitch on the focus column.  All heads in one switch are homogeneous.  ADT
-- heads → discriminant + br_table on the dense per-type ordinal.  Int-literal heads
-- → compare immediates.  HUnit is irrefutable (drop focus, descend).
emitSwitchRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  List (List String) ->
  List CArm ->
  List CTBranch ->
  CTree ->
  List String
emitSwitchRef prog env d decLabel root [] arms branches dft =
  emitTreeRef prog env d decLabel root [] arms dft
emitSwitchRef prog env d decLabel root (foc :: rest) arms [] dft =
  emitTreeRef prog env d decLabel root rest arms dft
emitSwitchRef prog env d decLabel root (foc :: rest) arms (branches@((CTBranch (HLit _) _) :: _)) dft =
  emitLitSwitchRef prog env d decLabel root foc rest arms branches dft 0
emitSwitchRef prog env d decLabel root (foc :: rest) arms ((CTBranch HUnit sub) :: _) dft =
  emitTreeRef prog env d decLabel root rest arms sub
emitSwitchRef prog env d decLabel root (foc :: rest) arms (branches@((CTBranch h _) :: _)) dft =
  match conHeadInfo h
    Some _ =>
      emitConSwitchRef prog env d decLabel root foc rest arms branches dft
    None =>
      gapLP
        prog
        "ref-mode: unsupported switch head (constructor / int-literal / unit only)"

-- the constructor switch (§3.4): stash the focus into scratch local `$__rf<d>`,
-- read its discriminant, and `br_table` on the dense per-type ordinal.  Recurses
-- into branch subtrees at depth d+1.
emitConSwitchRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  List String ->
  List (List String) ->
  List CArm ->
  List CTBranch ->
  CTree ->
  List String
emitConSwitchRef prog env d decLabel root foc rest arms branches dft =
  let ty = switchTypeName prog branches
  let nOrd = typeCtorCount prog ty
  let sv = scratchLocal d
  let svRead = ["local.get $" ++ sv]
  foc
    ++ ["local.set $" ++ sv]
    ++ emitBrTableTower
      prog
      env
      (d + 1)
      decLabel
      root
      svRead
      rest
      arms
      (branchOrdMapW prog branches)
      dft
      ty
      d
      nOrd

-- the discriminant: from a value that is EITHER an i31 nullary (its per-type ordinal,
-- set at construction) OR a payload struct (the per-type ordinal in field 0).
-- `ref.test (ref i31)` selects the rep; both yield the SAME dense ordinal.
discrimReadOf : List String -> String -> List String
discrimReadOf svRead ty =
  -- W9: Bool is always an i31 (0/1) — it has no $T_Bool root struct, so emit the i31
  -- read directly (the generic two-branch form would reference an undeclared type in
  -- its dead struct branch and fail wasm-tools validation).
  if ty == "Bool" then
    svRead ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_u"]
  else
    svRead
      ++ ["ref.test (ref i31)", "if (result i32)"]
      ++ indent (svRead ++ ["ref.cast (ref i31)", "i31.get_u"])
      ++ ["else"]
      ++ indent
        (svRead
          ++ [
            "ref.cast (ref $" ++ typeRootName ty ++ ")",
            "struct.get $" ++ typeRootName ty ++ " 0",
          ])
      ++ ["end"]

-- build the br_table tower (the standard switch idiom).  Labels are suffixed by the
-- SWITCH depth `sd` so nested switches don't collide.  Structure for nOrd cases:
--
--   block $swd<sd> (result (ref eq))
--     block $sw<sd>_{n-1} … block $sw<sd>_0
--       <discriminant i32>  br_table $sw<sd>_0 … $sw<sd>_{n-1} $swd<sd>
--     end           ;; end $sw<sd>_0 — fall through = ordinal 0 selected
--     <arm 0>  br decLabel
--     end           ;; end $sw<sd>_1
--     <arm 1>  br decLabel
--     …
--   end             ;; end $swd<sd>
--   <default subtree>          (falls through with its value on the stack)
emitBrTableTower : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  List String ->
  List (List String) ->
  List CArm ->
  OrdMap CTBranch ->
  CTree ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List String
emitBrTableTower prog env d decLabel root svRead rest arms branches dft ty sd nOrd =
  let sfx = intToString sd
  let labels = map (k => "$sw\{sfx}_\{intToString k}") (rangeList 0 nOrd)
  let tableInstr = "br_table \{joinWith " " labels} $swd\{sfx}"
  let opens =
    ["block $swd" ++ sfx]
      ++ map (k => "block $sw\{sfx}_\{intToString k}") (rangeList 0 nOrd)
  let pick = discrimReadOf svRead ty ++ [tableInstr]
  opens
    ++ pick
    ++ towerBodies
      prog
      env
      d
      decLabel
      root
      svRead
      rest
      arms
      branches
      dft
      ty
      sd
      (nOrd - 1)

-- emit, innermost-first (ordinal n-1 down to 0): `end` of $sw<sd>_k then ordinal k's
-- arm; finally `end` of $swd<sd> then the default subtree (yields the block value).
towerBodies : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  List String ->
  List (List String) ->
  List CArm ->
  OrdMap CTBranch ->
  CTree ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List String
towerBodies prog env d decLabel root svRead rest arms branches dft ty sd k =
  if k < 0 then
    ["end"] ++ emitTreeRef prog env d decLabel root rest arms dft
  else
    ["end"]
      ++ emitOrdinalSlot
        prog
        env
        d
        decLabel
        root
        svRead
        rest
        arms
        branches
        ty
        sd
        k
      ++ towerBodies
        prog
        env
        d
        decLabel
        root
        svRead
        rest
        arms
        branches
        dft
        ty
        sd
        (k - 1)

-- ordinal k's arm: the branch whose head has ordinal k.  Present → extract its
-- fields (ref.cast to the ctor struct + struct.get i+1) as new leading occurrences,
-- emit its subtree.  Absent → fall to $swd<sd> (the default).
emitOrdinalSlot : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  List String ->
  List (List String) ->
  List CArm ->
  OrdMap CTBranch ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List String
emitOrdinalSlot prog env d decLabel root svRead rest arms branches ty sd k =
  match branchForOrdinal branches k
    Some (CTBranch h sub) =>
      -- #712: key the field-extract cast off the CHead (headCtorStructName), not the
      -- bare ctor name — so a built-in `HCons` stays on the reserved `$C_Cons` even when
      -- a user ADT also declares a `Cons` (which resolves to `$CU_Cons`).
      let cs = headCtorStructName prog h
      let a = snd (conHeadInfoUnsafe prog h)
      let fieldOccs =
        map
          (i =>
            svRead
              ++ [
                "ref.cast (ref $" ++ cs ++ ")",
                "struct.get $\{cs} \{intToString (i + 1)}",
              ])
          (rangeList 0 a)
      emitTreeRef prog env d decLabel root (fieldOccs ++ rest) arms sub
    None => ["br $swd" ++ intToString sd]

-- the literal switch: compare the focus i31 Int against each branch's constant via
-- an if/else chain.  The focus is re-read per comparison through `foc`.
-- `idt` (trailing) is the chain's own INDENT depth — distinct from the switch depth
-- `d`.  Each level renders itself at `idt` and its arm at `idt + 1`, then hands the
-- else-chain `idt + 1`, instead of wrapping the recursion in `indent` and re-copying
-- every line below it once per level (#381).  Callers start the chain at 0.
emitLitSwitchRef : Prog ->
  Env ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  List String ->
  List (List String) ->
  List CArm ->
  List CTBranch ->
  CTree ->
  Int ->
  List String
emitLitSwitchRef prog env d decLabel root foc rest arms [] dft idt =
  indentBy idt (emitTreeRef prog env d decLabel root rest arms dft)
emitLitSwitchRef prog env d decLabel root foc rest arms ((CTBranch (HLit (LInt k)) sub) :: more) dft idt =
  -- W6 (validate fix): a NO-RESULT `if`.  Every decision-tree path is `br`-terminated
  -- (leaves `br decLabel`, CTFail → unreachable, the else-chain recurses to another
  -- br-terminated `if` or the br-terminated `dft`), so the `if` never falls through
  -- with a value.  A `(result (ref eq))` form leaves a PHANTOM `(ref eq)` on the stack
  -- when this switch is NESTED inside a con-tower slot — at the slot's untyped `end`
  -- that strands the value ("values remaining on stack at end of block").  No result
  -- type ⇒ nothing stranded.
  --
  -- …but a no-result `if` is REACHABLE-after: wasm types it `[] -> []` and does NOT
  -- propagate "both arms diverged", so control notionally falls out of `end` with an
  -- empty stack.  Under a `block $dec… (result (ref eq))` head (a value-position
  -- scrutinee, e.g. `main = match "if"`) that fall-out hits the block's end owing a
  -- `(ref eq)` and strands it the other way — "expected (ref eq) but nothing on
  -- stack", an INVALID module (#374).  Every path here really is `br`-terminated, so
  -- close with `unreachable`: the fall-out goes stack-polymorphic and validates under
  -- BOTH a result-typed head and an untyped con-tower slot.  This is exactly what the
  -- `emitLitSwitchTail` twin already does — the fix was ported to only one of the pair.
  -- #759: unbox to i64 ($mdk_unbox_int handles i31 immediate OR $boxint); see
  -- emitLitSwitchTail — the i31/i32 path truncated/trapped for |k| >= 2^30.
  indentBy
      idt
      (foc
        ++ [unboxIntW prog, "i64.const " ++ intToString k, "i64.eq"]
        ++ ["if"])
    ++ indentBy (idt + 1) (emitTreeRef prog env d decLabel root rest arms sub)
    ++ indentBy idt ["else"]
    ++ emitLitSwitchRef
      prog
      env
      d
      decLabel
      root
      foc
      rest
      arms
      more
      dft
      (idt + 1)
    ++ indentBy idt ["end", "unreachable"]
-- W6: Char-literal switch head — a Char is an i31 codepoint immediate (cf.
-- `PLit (LChar)`); compare the i31 against the codepoint constant.
emitLitSwitchRef prog env d decLabel root foc rest arms ((CTBranch (HLit (LChar c)) sub) :: more) dft idt =
  indentBy
      idt
      (foc
        ++ [
          "ref.cast (ref i31)",
          "i31.get_u",
          "i32.const "
            ++ intToString (charCode (arrayGetUnsafe 0 (stringToChars c))),
          "i32.eq",
        ]
        ++ ["if"])
    ++ indentBy (idt + 1) (emitTreeRef prog env d decLabel root rest arms sub)
    ++ indentBy idt ["else"]
    ++ emitLitSwitchRef
      prog
      env
      d
      decLabel
      root
      foc
      rest
      arms
      more
      dft
      (idt + 1)
    ++ indentBy idt ["end", "unreachable"]
-- W6: String-literal switch head — compare the focus $str against each literal via
-- `$mdk_str_compare` (returns the i31 1 on equal), reusing the `PLit (LString)` logic.
emitLitSwitchRef prog env d decLabel root foc rest arms ((CTBranch (HLit (LString s)) sub) :: more) dft idt =
  indentBy
      idt
      (foc
        ++ ["ref.cast (ref $str)"]
        ++ emitLitRef prog (LString s)
        ++ [
          rtCallW prog "mdk_str_compare" 2,
          "ref.cast (ref i31)",
          "i31.get_u",
          "i32.const 1",
          "i32.eq",
        ]
        ++ ["if"])
    ++ indentBy (idt + 1) (emitTreeRef prog env d decLabel root rest arms sub)
    ++ indentBy idt ["else"]
    ++ emitLitSwitchRef
      prog
      env
      d
      decLabel
      root
      foc
      rest
      arms
      more
      dft
      (idt + 1)
    ++ indentBy idt ["end", "unreachable"]
emitLitSwitchRef prog _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ =
  gapLP
    prog
    "ref-mode: non-Int literal switch head (Char/String literals are W6)"

-- ── pattern binding (leaf re-match) ──────────────────────────────────────────
-- bind a pattern's PVars against the value the snippet `v` produces, emitting struct
-- field extractions.  Returns (instructions that stash bound vars into their locals,
-- extended env).  Mirrors the LLVM bindPattern but stashes into named locals.
bindPatRef : Prog -> Env -> Pat -> List String -> (List String, Env)
bindPatRef prog env PWild v = ([], env)
bindPatRef prog env (PLit _) v = ([], env)
bindPatRef prog env (PVar x _ bid) v =
  (v ++ ["local.set $" ++ gname x], envBind x bid env)
bindPatRef prog env (PCon c args) v = bindConFields prog env c args v
-- W7: a cons cell — field 1 = head, field 2 = tail (struct $C_Cons).
bindPatRef prog env (PCons h t) v =
  let hSnip = v ++ ["ref.cast (ref $C_Cons)", "struct.get $C_Cons 1"]
  let tSnip = v ++ ["ref.cast (ref $C_Cons)", "struct.get $C_Cons 2"]
  let (hb, env2) = bindPatRef prog env h hSnip
  let (tb, env3) = bindPatRef prog env2 t tSnip
  (hb ++ tb, env3)
-- W7: a fixed-length list pattern — bind each element by descending the Cons spine.
bindPatRef prog env (PList ps) v = bindListPat prog env ps v
-- W7: a tuple pattern — field i+1 of the $C_Tup<n> struct.
bindPatRef prog env (PTuple ps) v =
  bindTupleFields prog env (tupleCtorName (listLen ps)) ps v 0
bindPatRef prog env (PAs x _ bid p) v =
  let setX = v ++ ["local.set $" ++ gname x]
  let (inner, env2) = bindPatRef prog (envBind x bid env) p v
  (setX ++ inner, env2)
bindPatRef prog env other v =
  gapL2P
    prog
    ("ref-mode: unsupported pattern in match arm (variable / wildcard / constructor / literal): "
      ++ ptag other)

-- bind a fixed-length list pattern `[p0, p1, …]`: p0 = head of v, the rest match the
-- tail recursively (descending Cons cells; the final empty list / Nil is irrefutable
-- here — the decision tree already proved the length).
bindListPat : Prog -> Env -> List Pat -> List String -> (List String, Env)
bindListPat _ env [] _ = ([], env)
bindListPat prog env (p :: ps) v =
  let hSnip = v ++ ["ref.cast (ref $C_Cons)", "struct.get $C_Cons 1"]
  let tSnip = v ++ ["ref.cast (ref $C_Cons)", "struct.get $C_Cons 2"]
  let (hb, env2) = bindPatRef prog env p hSnip
  let (tb, env3) = bindListPat prog env2 ps tSnip
  (hb ++ tb, env3)

-- bind a tuple pattern's fields: field i+1 of $C_Tup<n> (after the i32 tag).
bindTupleFields : Prog ->
  Env ->
  String ->
  List Pat ->
  List String ->
  Int ->
  (List String, Env)
bindTupleFields _ env _ [] _ _ = ([], env)
bindTupleFields prog env tc (p :: rest) v i =
  let fieldSnippet =
    v
      ++ [
        "ref.cast (ref $" ++ ctorStructName tc ++ ")",
        "struct.get $\{ctorStructName tc} \{intToString (i + 1)}",
      ]
  let (cur, env2) = bindPatRef prog env p fieldSnippet
  let (more, env3) = bindTupleFields prog env2 tc rest v (i + 1)
  (cur ++ more, env3)

-- bind a constructor pattern's fields: for each field i, extract via ref.cast +
-- struct.get (field i+1, after the i32 tag), then recurse into the sub-pattern.
bindConFields : Prog ->
  Env ->
  String ->
  List Pat ->
  List String ->
  (List String, Env)
bindConFields prog env c args v = bindConFieldsGo prog env c args v 0

bindConFieldsGo : Prog ->
  Env ->
  String ->
  List Pat ->
  List String ->
  Int ->
  (List String, Env)
bindConFieldsGo _ env _ [] _ _ = ([], env)
bindConFieldsGo prog env c (p :: rest) v i =
  let fieldSnippet =
    v
      ++ [
        "ref.cast (ref $" ++ ctorStructName c ++ ")",
        "struct.get $\{ctorStructName c} \{intToString (i + 1)}",
      ]
  let (cur, env2) = bindPatRef prog env p fieldSnippet
  let (more, env3) = bindConFieldsGo prog env2 c rest v (i + 1)
  (cur ++ more, env3)

-- ── helpers shared by both modes ─────────────────────────────────────────────

isFnBind : CBind -> Bool
isFnBind (CBind "main" _ _ _) = False
isFnBind b = not (isValBind b)

userFnBinds : List CBind -> List CBind
userFnBinds groups = filterList isFnBind groups

collectFnNames : List CBind -> List String
collectFnNames groups = map bindName (filterList isFnBind groups)

collectValNames : List CBind -> List String
collectValNames groups = map bindName (filterList isValBind groups)

bindName : CBind -> String
bindName (CBind n _ _ _) = n

findMain : WasmEmit -> List CBind -> Option CExpr
findMain _ [] = None
findMain _ ((CBind "main" [CClause [] body] _ _) :: _) = Some body
findMain emit ((CBind "main" _ _ _) :: _) =
  gapOptE emit "`main` must be a nullary value (main = ...)"
findMain emit (_ :: rest) = findMain emit rest

-- the let-bound locals inside a binding's (single, nullary) clause body.
collectBindLocals : CBind -> List String
collectBindLocals (CBind _ [CClause _ body] _ _) = collectExprLocals body
collectBindLocals _ = []

patName : WasmEmit -> String -> Pat -> String
patName _ _ (PVar x _ _) = x
patName _ _ PWild = "_"
patName emit binding _ =
  gapS
    emit
    ("only PVar/PWild parameters (pattern params are inner-match material) [in "
      ++ binding
      ++ "]")

-- ── local collection ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Wasm requires every local declared in the function header.  Walk the body for
-- every `let`-bound / block-let-bound PVar AND (W3) every PATTERN-bound var in a
-- CDecision arm (the leaf re-match binds them into locals).
collectExprLocals : CExpr -> List String
collectExprLocals (CLet _ (PVar x _ _) e1 e2) =
  x :: collectExprLocals e1 ++ collectExprLocals e2
collectExprLocals (CLet _ pat e1 e2) =
  patVars pat ++ (collectExprLocals e1 ++ collectExprLocals e2)
collectExprLocals (CBinPrim _ l r _ _) =
  collectExprLocals l ++ collectExprLocals r
collectExprLocals (CUnOp _ x) = collectExprLocals x
collectExprLocals (CIf c t f) =
  collectExprLocals c ++ collectExprLocals t ++ collectExprLocals f
collectExprLocals (app@(CApp f args _)) = match fileBoundW app
  Some (g, body, _) => collectExprLocals g ++ collectExprLocals body
  None => collectExprLocals f ++ flatMap collectExprLocals args
collectExprLocals (CTuple items) = flatMap collectExprLocals items
collectExprLocals (CList items) = flatMap collectExprLocals items
collectExprLocals (CArray items) = flatMap collectExprLocals items
collectExprLocals (CRecord _ fields) = flatMap collectFieldLocals fields
collectExprLocals (CFieldAccess base _ _ _) = collectExprLocals base
collectExprLocals (CRecordUpdate _ base fields) =
  collectExprLocals base ++ flatMap collectFieldLocals fields
collectExprLocals (CVariantUpdate _ base fields) =
  collectExprLocals base ++ flatMap collectFieldLocals fields
collectExprLocals (CRangeList lo hi _) =
  collectExprLocals lo ++ collectExprLocals hi
collectExprLocals (CRangeArray lo hi _) =
  collectExprLocals lo ++ collectExprLocals hi
collectExprLocals (CIndex base index) =
  collectExprLocals base ++ collectExprLocals index
collectExprLocals (CSlice base lo hi _) =
  collectExprLocals base ++ collectExprLocals lo ++ collectExprLocals hi
collectExprLocals (CBlock stmts) = flatMap collectStmtLocals stmts
collectExprLocals (CDecision scrut arms _) =
  collectExprLocals scrut ++ flatMap collectArmLocals arms
collectExprLocals (CMatch scrut arms) =
  collectExprLocals scrut ++ flatMap collectArmLocals arms
-- W9: a CLetGroup's member NAMES are bound as closure locals at the use site (the
-- enclosing fn must declare them); the bindings' own clause locals belong to the
-- LIFTED fns, not here, so only the group body's locals are collected here.
-- P1: a group's FUNCTION members are lambda-lifted (their bodies declare their own
-- locals in their own lifted fn), but a nullary VALUE member's rhs is emitted INLINE at
-- the use site — so its locals must be declared HERE, in the enclosing function.
collectExprLocals (CLetGroup binds body) =
  map lgBindName binds
    ++ flatMap collectLgValLocals binds
    ++ collectExprLocals body
-- a method dispatched on a projected super dictionary reads it through a local
collectExprLocals (CMethod _ (MethodEvidence _ _ (RProj r path) _ _)) =
  [projLocalName r path]
collectExprLocals _ = []

collectFieldLocals : CField -> List String
collectFieldLocals (CField _ _ value) = collectExprLocals value

-- P1: the inline-emitted locals of a group's nullary VALUE member (none for a function
-- member — that one is lifted).
collectLgValLocals : CBind -> List String
collectLgValLocals (CBind _ [CClause [] rhs] _ _) = collectExprLocals rhs
collectLgValLocals _ = []

collectStmtLocals : CStmt -> List String
collectStmtLocals (CSExpr ex) = collectExprLocals ex
collectStmtLocals (CSLet _ (PVar x _ _) ex) = x :: collectExprLocals ex
collectStmtLocals (CSLet _ pat ex) = patVars pat ++ collectExprLocals ex
collectStmtLocals (CSAssign _ ex) = collectExprLocals ex

-- ── W7 scratch-local declarations ────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The range/index/slice/record-update/array-extern/divisor-guard codegen uses
-- depth-keyed scratch locals ($__rli<d> etc.) with specific WAT types (i32 counters,
-- (ref $arr) array temps, (ref eq) accumulators).  Each site names its local through
-- `w7Local`, which records the name in `w7Used`, and a function declares exactly the
-- W7 locals its own body recorded.  A local is a stack slot in every frame of its
-- function on some engines (Firefox), so declaring every W7 local in every function
-- multiplied frame sizes and overflowed deep but legitimate recursion (#3882).
--
-- A function's emitter brackets the codegen of its body with `w7ScopeOpen` and
-- `w7ScopeClose`.  The pair saves and restores the enclosing function's set, because
-- a lifted lambda or let-group member is emitted while its parent's body is
-- being emitted.

-- the `$`-prefixed name of the W7 scratch local `stem` at depth suffix `sfx`, recorded
-- as referenced by the function being emitted.
w7Local : WasmEmit -> String -> String -> String
w7Local emit stem sfx =
  let name = stem ++ sfx
  let _ = setRef emit.w7Used (omInsert name () !emit.w7Used)
  "$" ++ name

-- start recording a new function's W7 locals; returns the enclosing function's set,
-- which `w7ScopeClose` restores.
w7ScopeOpen : WasmEmit -> OrdMap Unit
w7ScopeOpen emit =
  let outer = !emit.w7Used
  let _ = setRef emit.w7Used omEmpty
  outer

-- the W7 locals recorded since the matching `w7ScopeOpen`; restores `outer`.
w7ScopeClose : WasmEmit -> OrdMap Unit -> OrdMap Unit
w7ScopeClose emit outer =
  let used = !emit.w7Used
  let _ = setRef emit.w7Used outer
  used

-- The `(local …)` lines for the W7 locals in `used`, over depths 0..maxDepth (the
-- bound `maxRefDepth` already computes for $__rf<d>, which covers every W7 site),
-- in depth-major then `w7LocalKinds` order.
w7LocalDecls : OrdMap Unit -> Int -> List String
w7LocalDecls used maxDepth = match omKeys used
  [] => []
  _ => flatMap (d => w7LocalsAtDepth used d) (rangeList 0 (maxI maxDepth 1))

w7LocalsAtDepth : OrdMap Unit -> Int -> List String
w7LocalsAtDepth used d =
  let sfx = intToString d
  flatMap
    ((stem, ty) =>
      if omHasKey (stem ++ sfx) used then
        ["(local $\{stem}\{sfx} \{ty})"]
      else
        [])
    w7LocalKinds

-- the divisor-guard scratch local of a concrete `/`/`%` at depth `d`.
divrLocal : Prog -> Int -> String
divrLocal prog d = w7Local (progEmit prog) "__divr" (intToString d)

-- every W7 scratch local's name stem and WAT type, in declaration order.
w7LocalKinds : List (String, String)
w7LocalKinds = [
  ("__rlacc", "(ref eq)"),
  ("__rli", "i64"),
  ("__rllo", "i64"),
  ("__raarr", "(ref null $arr)"),
  ("__rai", "i32"),
  ("__ralo", "i64"),
  ("__racnt", "i64"),
  ("__ixarr", "(ref null $arr)"),
  ("__ixi", "i32"),
  ("__slsrc", "(ref null $arr)"),
  ("__sldst", "(ref null $arr)"),
  ("__sllo", "i32"),
  ("__sllen", "i32"),
  -- W10 array-intrinsic-extern scratch (loop counter, size, result array, list cursor,
  -- closure/init value) for arrayMake/arrayMakeWith/arrayFromList/arraySetUnsafe.
  ("__aexi", "i32"),
  ("__aexn", "i32"),
  ("__aexarr", "(ref null $arr)"),
  ("__aexlst", "(ref eq)"),
  ("__aexf", "(ref eq)"),
  ("__aexv", "(ref eq)"),
  -- stage-B: i64 bit accumulator for floatToBytes64/bytesToFloat64 reinterpret.
  ("__aexbits", "i64"),
  -- the record/variant update base (emitUpdateCopy).
  ("__rub", "(ref eq)"),
  -- B5: the i64 divisor-guard scratch for a concrete-Int `/`/`%`.
  ("__divr", "i64"),
]

-- an arm contributes its pattern's bound vars + its body's locals + guard locals.
collectArmLocals : CArm -> List String
collectArmLocals (CArm pat guards body) =
  patVars pat ++ flatMap collectGuardLocals guards ++ collectExprLocals body

collectGuardLocals : CGuard -> List String
collectGuardLocals (CGBool g) = collectExprLocals g
-- #379: `guardStashLocal` is the slot emitGuardChainRef evaluates the RHS into before
-- refutably matching `p` against it — declared here so it rides the normal body-local
-- path (dedupKeep collapses the repeats when a function has several such guards).
collectGuardLocals (CGBind p e) =
  guardStashLocal :: patVars p ++ collectExprLocals e

-- the variables a pattern binds (for local declaration).
patVars : Pat -> List String
patVars (PVar x _ _) = [x]
patVars PWild = []
patVars (PLit _) = []
patVars (PCon _ args) = flatMap patVars args
patVars (PTuple ps) = flatMap patVars ps
patVars (PCons h t) = patVars h ++ patVars t
patVars (PList ps) = flatMap patVars ps
patVars (PAs x _ _ p) = x :: patVars p
patVars _ = []

-- ── operator tables (both modes) ─────────────────────────────────────────────

-- Ref-mode Int arithmetic/comparison over the box/unbox seam (layer-17 §2.1):
-- i64 throughout, so values outside +/-2^30 no longer truncate.  Division/modulo are
-- i64 signed (i64.div_s/i64.rem_s) — matching native's truncated-toward-zero div and
-- sign-of-dividend rem (medaka_rt.c).
--
-- (The i32 peer `wasmBinOp` was removed with #305: its last two callers were the
-- ordering arms of emitValueCmpRef/emitValueCmpNumRef, which compared a 3-way
-- -1/0/1 against 0 — the derivation that could not express NaN's unorderedness.
-- Those now call the per-op IEEE $mdk_value_lt/le/gt/ge(_num) instead, and every
-- surviving caller was already on wasmBinOp64.)
wasmBinOp64 : WasmEmit -> String -> String
wasmBinOp64 _ "+" = "i64.add"
wasmBinOp64 _ "-" = "i64.sub"
wasmBinOp64 _ "*" = "i64.mul"
wasmBinOp64 _ "/" = "i64.div_s"
wasmBinOp64 _ "%" = "i64.rem_s"
wasmBinOp64 _ "==" = "i64.eq"
wasmBinOp64 _ "/=" = "i64.ne"
wasmBinOp64 _ "<" = "i64.lt_s"
wasmBinOp64 _ ">" = "i64.gt_s"
wasmBinOp64 _ "<=" = "i64.le_s"
wasmBinOp64 _ ">=" = "i64.ge_s"
wasmBinOp64 emit op =
  gapS emit ("unsupported i64 binary operator '" ++ op ++ "'")

binOpTy : String -> WTy
binOpTy op =
  if op == "++" then
    WStr
  else if contains op ["==", "/=", "<", ">", "<=", ">="] then
    WBool
  else
    WInt

-- ── ctor / type info (ref mode) ──────────────────────────────────────────────

isCtor : Prog -> String -> Bool
isCtor prog name =
  isSome (omLookup name (indexCtorAritiesW (progIndex prog)))
    || isReservedCtor name
    || isSyntheticCtor name

isReservedCtor : String -> Bool
isReservedCtor name = isSome (reservedCtorOrdinal name)

-- ── W7 synthetic ctors (List Cons/Nil, tuple Tup<n>) ─────────────────────────
-- These are not in the user ctor table; they share the W3 ctor machinery so the
-- match tower / construction / field-extract code stays uniform.  A tuple ctor is
-- "Tup<n>" (its own single-ctor synthetic type "$Tuple<n>").  List = Cons/Nil under
-- type "List".
isSyntheticCtor : String -> Bool
isSyntheticCtor name =
  name == "Cons"
    || name == "Nil"
    || name == "True"
    || name == "False"
    || isTupleCtorName name

tupleCtorName : Int -> String
tupleCtorName n = "Tup" ++ intToString n

isTupleCtorName : String -> Bool
isTupleCtorName name =
  startsWith "Tup" name && allDigitsFrom (stringToChars name) 3

-- the synthetic type a synthetic ctor belongs to.
syntheticCtorType : String -> String
syntheticCtorType "Cons" = "List"
syntheticCtorType "Nil" = "List"
-- W9: with the REAL prelude, `Bool` is a builtin (not a `data` decl), so its ctors
-- True/False are not in the ctor table.  Treat them as synthetic Bool ctors:
-- type "Bool", ordinals False=0/True=1, nullary, rep = i31 (same as emitVarRef's
-- True/False fast path and emitLitRef LBool), so discrimReadOf's i31 branch reads
-- the ordinal directly.
syntheticCtorType "True" = "Bool"
syntheticCtorType "False" = "Bool"
syntheticCtorType name = "$Tuple" ++ intToString (trailingIntOf name)

syntheticCtorOrdinal : String -> Int
syntheticCtorOrdinal "Cons" = 0
syntheticCtorOrdinal "Nil" = 1
syntheticCtorOrdinal "False" = 0
syntheticCtorOrdinal "True" = 1
syntheticCtorOrdinal _ = 0

syntheticCtorArity : String -> Int
syntheticCtorArity "Cons" = 2
syntheticCtorArity "Nil" = 0
syntheticCtorArity "True" = 0
syntheticCtorArity "False" = 0
syntheticCtorArity name = trailingIntOf name

-- typeName → its ctor list in DECLARATION order.  Walks the ctor→type table
-- REVERSED and PREPENDS, so each type's list comes out in forward declaration
-- order — the same order `ctorsOfTypeUser`'s filter+map produced, duplicates and
-- all.
typeCtorsOfW : List (String, String) ->
  OrdMap (List String) ->
  OrdMap (List String)
typeCtorsOfW [] m = m
typeCtorsOfW ((c, t) :: rest) m =
  typeCtorsOfW rest (omInsert t (c :: optionOr [] (omLookup t m)) m)

-- ctorName → dense per-type ordinal, for the USER path of `ctorOrdinal` only.
-- Reproduces that path's formula
--   orZeroIdx (indexOfL name (ctorsOfType prog (ctorTypeName prog name)))
-- exactly, but in O(ctors · log ctors) instead of O(ctors) per call:
--   * types are walked in DECLARATION order (`distinctTypeNames`);
--   * a ctor is indexed only under the type `ctorTypeName` would name for it (its
--     FIRST type, per `tym`) — so a name shared by two types still takes its
--     ordinal from the first one, as `lookupAssoc` + `indexOfL` did;
--   * the `omHasKey` guard keeps the FIRST index on a name repeated within one
--     type, matching `indexOfL`'s first-match.
-- A ctor absent from the map is not a user ctor, so `userCtorOrdinalW` returns None
-- and `ctorOrdinal` falls through to the reserved/synthetic ordinal (#712/S0).
ctorOrdsOfW : List String ->
  OrdMap String ->
  OrdMap (List String) ->
  OrdMap Int ->
  OrdMap Int
ctorOrdsOfW [] _ _ m = m
ctorOrdsOfW (ty :: rest) tym tcm m =
  ctorOrdsOfW rest tym tcm (indexCtorsW tym ty (ctorsOfTypeIxW tcm ty) 0 m)

indexCtorsW : OrdMap String ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  Int ->
  OrdMap Int ->
  OrdMap Int
indexCtorsW _ _ [] _ m = m
indexCtorsW tym ty (c :: cs) i m = indexCtorsW tym ty cs (i + 1) (if omHasKey
  c
  m then
  m
else if firstTyIsW tym c ty then
  omInsert c i m
else
  m)

firstTyIsW : OrdMap String -> String -> String -> Bool
firstTyIsW tym c ty = match omLookup c tym
  Some t => eqStr t ty
  None => False

-- the shared 5-branch ctor-list dispatch used by BOTH `ctorsOfTypeIxW` (memo-only,
-- called before the `Prog` exists) and `ctorsOfType` (Prog-based). Parameterized
-- over the fallback for a plain user type, so each caller supplies its own way to
-- resolve that case (a direct memo lookup vs `ctorsOfTypeUser`) while the
-- reserved/List/Bool/tuple branches — and their order — exist exactly once, so
-- the two can no longer drift apart.
ctorsOfTypeDispatchW : (String -> List String) -> String -> List String
ctorsOfTypeDispatchW userFallback ty =
  if isReservedType ty then
    reservedCtorsOfType ty
  else if ty == "List" then
    ["Cons", "Nil"]
  else if ty == "Bool" then
    ["False", "True"]
  else if isTupleType ty then
    [tupleCtorName (tupleTypeArity ty)]
  else
    userFallback ty

-- `ctorsOfType`'s dispatch, off the memo and without a `Prog` (the indices are built
-- before the Prog exists). Shares its branches with `ctorsOfType` via
-- `ctorsOfTypeDispatchW` — nothing left to keep in lockstep by hand.
ctorsOfTypeIxW : OrdMap (List String) -> String -> List String
ctorsOfTypeIxW tcm ty =
  ctorsOfTypeDispatchW (t => optionOr [] (omLookup t tcm)) ty

ctorArity : Prog -> String -> Int
ctorArity prog name = match omLookup name (indexCtorAritiesW (progIndex prog))
  Some a => a
  None =>
    if isSyntheticCtor name then
      syntheticCtorArity name
    else
      reservedCtorArity name

-- a ctor's owning type name (user types via the ctor→type map; reserved ctors map
-- to their fixed type names; W7 synthetic ctors to their synthetic types).
ctorTypeName : Prog -> String -> String
ctorTypeName prog name = match omLookup name (indexCtorTypesW (progIndex prog))
  Some ty => ty
  None =>
    if isSyntheticCtor name then
      syntheticCtorType name
    else
      reservedTypeOf prog name

-- the per-type dense ordinal of a ctor (0-based index in its type's declaration
-- order).  Reserved ctors have fixed ordinals.
--
-- #712/S0: a USER ctor is looked up in the ctor TABLE **before** the name-based
-- `syntheticCtorOrdinal` short-circuit — mirroring `ctorArity`/`ctorTypeName` (both
-- table-first) and native `llvm_emit.mdk`'s `ctorOrdinal`.  Taking the
-- synthetic short-circuit FIRST instead gives a user ctor named `Cons`/`Nil` the
-- built-in list ordinal (Cons=0/Nil=1) instead of its DECLARATION-ORDER index.  In a
-- ≥3-ctor ADT like `data T = Extra | Cons Int T | Nil` that collides the user `Cons`
-- (wrongly 0) with `Extra` (legitimately 0) → wasm `br_table` sent `Cons` to `Extra`'s
-- arm = SILENT wrong dispatch. The private ctor-ordinal index holds only USER ctors, so a genuine
-- built-in list ctor (absent) still falls through to `syntheticCtorOrdinal`; a user
-- ctor and the built-in list are told apart at CALL sites via the CHead / tail expr
-- (see `ordinalOfHead`, `emitWDispCell`, the TRMC `isBuiltinList` flag, `emitListRef`),
-- the same discipline the struct-id fix uses.
ctorOrdinal : Prog -> String -> Int
ctorOrdinal prog name =
  optionOr
    (syntheticCtorOrdinal name)
    (orElse (reservedCtorOrdinal name) (userCtorOrdinalW prog name))

-- the DECLARATION-ORDER ordinal of a name IFF it is a user-declared ctor (present in
-- the ctor table), else None so the caller falls back to a synthetic/reserved ordinal.
userCtorOrdinalW : Prog -> String -> Option Int
userCtorOrdinalW prog name = omLookup name (indexCtorOrdinalsW (progIndex prog))

-- the ordinal to discriminate a decision-tree switch HEAD against.  Built-in list
-- heads keep their reserved ordinal (Cons=0/Nil=1) regardless of a poisoning user
-- ctor of the same name; every other head keys off `ctorOrdinal` (a user `HCon
-- "Cons"` thus gets its declaration-order ordinal).  Distinguished by the CHead
-- (`HCons`/`HNil` vs `HCon`), the only signal that survives the bare-name ctor table.
ordinalOfHead : Prog -> CHead -> Int
ordinalOfHead _ HCons = syntheticCtorOrdinal "Cons"
ordinalOfHead _ HNil = syntheticCtorOrdinal "Nil"
ordinalOfHead prog h = ctorOrdinal prog (fstConHead prog h)

-- the declaration-ordered ctor list of a user type (the ctor→type map lists each
-- type's ctors consecutively in declaration order — filter to this type).
-- Bool's ctors are SYNTHETIC (registered via syntheticCtor* helpers, not in the
-- program's ctorTypes table), so `ctorsOfTypeUser` would return [] → a 0-slot
-- br_table tower → both arms dropped → fall-through `unreachable` if it weren't
-- special-cased in the shared dispatch below. A genuine `match <Bool> { True =>
-- …; False => … }` (a CDecision switch, not a lowered CIf) hits this.
-- Index-aligned to syntheticCtorOrdinal: False=0, True=1.
-- Shares its branches with `ctorsOfTypeIxW` via `ctorsOfTypeDispatchW` — nothing
-- left to keep in lockstep by hand.
ctorsOfType : Prog -> String -> List String
ctorsOfType prog ty = ctorsOfTypeDispatchW (ctorsOfTypeUser prog) ty

-- a synthetic tuple type name "$Tuple<n>" and its arity.
isTupleType : String -> Bool
isTupleType ty = startsWith "$Tuple" ty

tupleTypeArity : String -> Int
tupleTypeArity ty = trailingIntOf ty

ctorsOfTypeUser : Prog -> String -> List String
ctorsOfTypeUser prog ty =
  optionOr [] (omLookup ty (indexTypeCtorsW (progIndex prog)))

-- the number of ctors a type has (the br_table's slot count).
typeCtorCount : Prog -> String -> Int
typeCtorCount prog ty = listLen (ctorsOfType prog ty)

-- the type a switch's branches discriminate (all branches share one type — take the
-- first ADT head's ctor's owning type).
switchTypeName : Prog -> List CTBranch -> String
switchTypeName prog [] = gapSP prog "ref-mode: empty constructor switch"
-- #712: the built-in list heads discriminate type "List" (root `$T_List`) — pin
-- them off the CHead, NOT `ctorTypeName "Cons"`, which the bare-name ctor table
-- would (mis)route to a user type "T" the moment `data T = Cons … | Nil` exists.
switchTypeName _ ((CTBranch HCons _) :: _) = "List"
switchTypeName _ ((CTBranch HNil _) :: _) = "List"
switchTypeName prog ((CTBranch h _) :: rest) = match conHeadInfo h
  Some (c, _) => ctorTypeName prog c
  None => switchTypeName prog rest

-- ordinal → the branch that fills that br_table slot, built ONCE per switch (#381).
-- The tower walks every ordinal slot 0..n-1; re-scanning the whole
-- branch list per slot (`branchForOrdinal`) calling `ctorOrdinal` per branch is O(slots ×
-- branches) even with `ctorOrdinal` memoized.  Keyed by the ordinal rendered as a
-- string (`OrdMap` is String-keyed).  The `omHasKey` guard keeps the FIRST branch on
-- a duplicate ordinal, matching the old left-to-right `branchForOrdinal` scan.
branchOrdMapW : Prog -> List CTBranch -> OrdMap CTBranch
branchOrdMapW prog bs = branchOrdMapGoW prog bs omEmpty

branchOrdMapGoW : Prog -> List CTBranch -> OrdMap CTBranch -> OrdMap CTBranch
branchOrdMapGoW _ [] m = m
branchOrdMapGoW prog ((CTBranch h sub) :: rest) m = match conHeadInfo h
  Some _ =>
    -- #712/S0: key off the HEAD (ordinalOfHead), so a built-in `HCons`/`HNil` keeps
    -- its reserved ordinal while a user `HCon "Cons"` gets its declaration-order one.
    let k = intToString (ordinalOfHead prog h)
    branchOrdMapGoW prog rest (if omHasKey k m then
      m
    else
      omInsert k (CTBranch h sub) m)
  None => branchOrdMapGoW prog rest m

-- the branch whose head's ordinal is k (for the br_table slot).
branchForOrdinal : OrdMap CTBranch -> Int -> Option CTBranch
branchForOrdinal bmap k = omLookup (intToString k) bmap

-- the name + arity a constructor-LIKE head tests against.  W7 maps the built-in
-- heads to synthetic ctor names so the SAME ctor machinery (ordinal / struct /
-- field-extract) drives them: HCons → ("Cons", 2) / HNil → ("Nil", 0) (type "List",
-- exactly the LLVM names), HTuple n → the per-arity synthetic tuple ctor "Tup<n>".
conHeadInfo : CHead -> Option (String, Int)
conHeadInfo (HCon c a) = Some (c, a)
conHeadInfo HCons = Some ("Cons", 2)
conHeadInfo HNil = Some ("Nil", 0)
conHeadInfo (HTuple n) = Some (tupleCtorName n, n)
conHeadInfo _ = None

conHeadInfoUnsafe : Prog -> CHead -> (String, Int)
conHeadInfoUnsafe prog h = match conHeadInfo h
  Some p => p
  None =>
    gapSIntP
      prog
      "ref-mode: non-constructor head in a constructor switch (HCons/HNil/HTuple are W7)"

-- ── reserved ADTs (Option / Result / Ordering) ───────────────────────────────
-- The lowering names Ordering's ctors `Lt`/`Eq`/`Gt` (capitalized — see
-- llvm_emit.reservedTag).
isReservedType : String -> Bool
isReservedType ty = contains ty ["Option", "Result", "Ordering"]

reservedCtorsOfType : String -> List String
reservedCtorsOfType "Option" = ["Some", "None"]
reservedCtorsOfType "Result" = ["Ok", "Err"]
reservedCtorsOfType "Ordering" = ["Lt", "Eq", "Gt"]
reservedCtorsOfType _ = []

reservedTypeOf : Prog -> String -> String
reservedTypeOf prog name =
  if contains name ["Some", "None"] then
    "Option"
  else if contains name ["Ok", "Err"] then
    "Result"
  else if contains name ["Lt", "Eq", "Gt"] then
    "Ordering"
  else
    gapSP
      prog
      ("ref-mode: unknown constructor '"
        ++ name
        ++ "' (not in the ctor table, not reserved)")

reservedCtorOrdinal : String -> Option Int
reservedCtorOrdinal "Some" = Some 0
reservedCtorOrdinal "None" = Some 1
reservedCtorOrdinal "Ok" = Some 0
reservedCtorOrdinal "Err" = Some 1
reservedCtorOrdinal "Lt" = Some 0
reservedCtorOrdinal "Eq" = Some 1
reservedCtorOrdinal "Gt" = Some 2
reservedCtorOrdinal _ = None

reservedCtorArity : String -> Int
reservedCtorArity "Some" = 1
reservedCtorArity "Ok" = 1
reservedCtorArity "Err" = 1
reservedCtorArity _ = 0

-- ── WAT type-name mangling ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- a per-type root struct type name and a per-ctor struct type name.  Prefixed to
-- avoid colliding with the fixed $float / $boxint scaffolding.  The type word
-- carries its module id (`my prog.T`, `café.T`), which need not be a WAT
-- identifier, so it is spelled through `injectiveIdent`.
typeRootName : String -> String
typeRootName ty = "T_" ++ injectiveIdent ty

-- The per-ctor WasmGC struct type identifier.
--
-- #712: a USER constructor whose bare name coincides with a built-in list head
-- (`Cons`/`Nil` — the names the built-in list SYNTAX canonicalises to) would mint
-- the SAME id as the reserved built-in list cons cell (`$C_Cons`), so
-- `data T = Cons Int T | Nil` declares `$C_Cons` TWICE (once `(sub $T_List)` for the
-- built-in list, once `(sub $T_T)` for the user ctor) and wasm-tools rejects the
-- module with "duplicate type identifier".  `Cons`/`Nil` are NOT prelude `data`
-- ctors (they are pure list SYNTAX with no `data` decl), so resolve lets a user
-- reuse them.  Disambiguate the USER ctor with a `U` (user) prefix → `$CU_Cons`,
-- keeping the reserved built-in `$C_Cons` bare.  This mirrors, on the WasmGC side,
-- native's universal-ctor discipline (private_mangle.mdk): the reserved built-in id
-- stays fixed and the user-defined same-name ctor gets a collision-free key.  Native
-- needs no analogue — its LLVM value rep is a uniform boxed cell with no per-ctor
-- NOMINAL struct type, so the two never collide there.
--
-- The remap is keyed on the ctor NAME, so it fires for a USER `Cons`/`Nil` at EVERY
-- construct / match-field-extract / decl site uniformly (they all route through
-- here).  The built-in list's OWN generic paths — the decision-tree switch on an
-- `HCons` head and the TRMC `::`-spine loop — must NOT be remapped (they build the
-- reserved `$C_Cons`); they force the bare id via `headCtorStructName` / the
-- `isBuiltinList` flag rather than calling this with the bare name.
ctorStructName : String -> String
ctorStructName ctor
  | isBuiltinListHeadName ctor = "CU_" ++ ctor
  | otherwise = "C_" ++ ctor

-- the two ctor names the built-in list syntax canonicalises to.  A user ctor of
-- either name is remapped away from the reserved list type id (see ctorStructName).
isBuiltinListHeadName : String -> Bool
isBuiltinListHeadName name = name == "Cons" || name == "Nil"

-- the struct id to `ref.cast` / `struct.get` against for a decision-tree switch
-- HEAD.  The built-in list head `HCons` is the RESERVED `$C_Cons` cell (never the
-- user remap), regardless of whether a user ADT also declares a `Cons` ctor; every
-- other head keys off its ctor name via ctorStructName (so a user `HCon "Cons"`
-- correctly resolves to the remapped `$CU_Cons`).  This is what keeps the built-in
-- list's generic switch/field-extract on `$C_Cons` while the user ctor's is on
-- `$CU_Cons`, the two being distinguished by the CHead (`HCons` vs `HCon "Cons"`),
-- the only signal that survives once the bare-name ctor table maps `Cons` → the
-- user type.
headCtorStructName : Prog -> CHead -> String
headCtorStructName _ HCons = "C_Cons"
headCtorStructName _ HNil = "C_Nil"
headCtorStructName prog h = ctorStructName (fstConHead prog h)

fstConHead : Prog -> CHead -> String
fstConHead prog h = match conHeadInfo h
  Some (c, _) => c
  None =>
    gapSP
      prog
      "ref-mode: non-constructor head where a ctor struct id was needed"

-- ── distinct type names (declaration order) ──────────────────────────────────
-- the ctor→type map lists each type's ctors consecutively, so dedup-preserving-
-- order over the type column gives declaration order.
distinctTypeNames : List (String, String) -> List String
distinctTypeNames ctorTypes = dedupKeep (map sndPair ctorTypes)

-- ── scratch locals for match scrutinee/focus stashes ─────────────────────────
-- a CDecision/CTSwitch at nesting depth d stashes its value into `$__rf<d>`.  The
-- function header declares `$__rf0..$__rf<maxDepth-1>`.
scratchLocal : Int -> String
scratchLocal d = "__rf" ++ intToString d

scratchLocals : Int -> List String
scratchLocals n = map scratchLocal (rangeList 0 n)

-- the number of scratch locals an expression needs = (highest scratch index used
-- anywhere) + 1.  This MIRRORS the actual depth threading: emitDecisionRef at depth
-- d uses local d and recurses its tree at d+1; emitConSwitchRef at depth d uses
-- local d and recurses subtrees at d+1.  `maxIndexAt e d` = the highest local index
-- used when `e` is emitted at depth d (or d-1 if `e` uses no stash, meaning no
-- scratch beyond what the caller already accounts for).
maxRefDepth : CExpr -> Int
maxRefDepth e = maxIndexAt e 0 + 1

-- the highest scratch-local index used emitting `e` at depth `d`.  Returns d-1 as a
-- "nothing used here" sentinel (so `+1` gives d, i.e. no extra slot).
maxIndexAt : CExpr -> Int -> Int
maxIndexAt (CDecision scrut arms tree) d =
  let scrutI = maxIndexAt scrut d
  let treeI = maxIndexTree tree (d + 1)
  let armDepth = d + 1 + treeSwitchNesting tree
  let armsI = foldMaxI (map (a => maxIndexAt (armBody a) armDepth) arms)
  maxI d (maxI scrutI (maxI treeI armsI))
maxIndexAt (CMatch scrut arms) d =
  let scrutI = maxIndexAt scrut d
  let armsI = foldMaxI (map (a => maxIndexAt (armBody a) (d + 1)) arms)
  maxI d (maxI scrutI armsI)
maxIndexAt (CIf c t f) d =
  maxI (maxIndexAt c d) (maxI (maxIndexAt t d) (maxIndexAt f d))
maxIndexAt (CLet _ pat a b) d =
  maxI (letStashIndex pat a d) (maxI (maxIndexAt a d) (maxIndexAt b d))
-- a `/` or `%` stashes its divisor in `$__divr<d>` (emitDivZeroGuard), so like the
-- four nodes below it counts `d` even over leaf operands, or an Int or `U64`
-- division nested two matches deep names an undeclared `$__divr2`.
maxIndexAt (CBinPrim op a b _ _) d =
  let sub = maxI (maxIndexAt a d) (maxIndexAt b d)
  if op == "/" || op == "%" then maxI d sub else sub
maxIndexAt (CUnOp _ a) d = maxIndexAt a d
maxIndexAt (app@(CApp f args _)) d = match fileBoundW app
  Some (g, body, _) => maxI (maxIndexAt g d) (maxIndexAt body d)
  None => foldMaxI (maxIndexAt f d :: map (a => maxIndexAt a d) args)
maxIndexAt (CBlock stmts) d = foldMaxI (map (s => maxIndexAtStmt s d) stmts)
-- a let-group's BODY is emitted at this same depth `d` at the use site (its lifted
-- members carry their own scratch in their own functions); descend into the body so
-- the enclosing function declares enough `$__rf` slots (a match in the body uses them).
-- P1: a nullary VALUE member's rhs is emitted INLINE at the use site (function members
-- are lifted and size their own scratch), so its depth must be folded in here — else the
-- enclosing fn under-declares scratch locals for it.
maxIndexAt (CLetGroup binds body) d =
  foldMaxI (maxIndexAt body d :: map (b => maxIndexAtLgVal b d) binds)
-- compound value nodes emit their sub-expressions at depth `d` (no own stash slot);
-- descend so a scratch-using element (e.g. CIndex/CSlice/a nested match) is counted.
maxIndexAt (CTuple es) d = foldMaxI (map (x => maxIndexAt x d) es)
maxIndexAt (CList es) d = foldMaxI (map (x => maxIndexAt x d) es)
maxIndexAt (CArray es) d = foldMaxI (map (x => maxIndexAt x d) es)
maxIndexAt (CRecord _ fields) d =
  foldMaxI (map (x => maxIndexAt (cFieldExpr x) d) fields)
-- CRecordUpdate/CVariantUpdate stash the base in $__rub<d> at their own emit site
-- and emit their override exprs at d+1 (emitUpdateCopy).
maxIndexAt (CRecordUpdate _ b fields) d =
  maxI
    d
    (maxI
      (maxIndexAt b d)
      (foldMaxI (map (x => maxIndexAt (cFieldExpr x) (d + 1)) fields)))
maxIndexAt (CVariantUpdate _ b fields) d =
  maxI
    d
    (maxI
      (maxIndexAt b d)
      (foldMaxI (map (x => maxIndexAt (cFieldExpr x) (d + 1)) fields)))
maxIndexAt (CFieldAccess e1 _ _ _) d = maxIndexAt e1 d
-- These four nodes each allocate depth-`d` scratch locals ($__rl*/$__ra*/$__ix*/
-- $__sl* at suffix `d`) at their OWN emit site, so they must contribute `d` even
-- when their subexpressions are leaves (which report d-1).  Omitting the `maxI d`
-- undercounts by one — masked at depths 0/1 by the `maxI maxDepth 1` floor in
-- w7LocalDecls, but at depth >= 2 (e.g. an `arr[i]` nested inside two matches, as in
-- the sqlite lib) it left `$__ixarr2` undeclared → wasm-tools "unknown local".
maxIndexAt (CRangeList lo hi _) d =
  maxI d (maxI (maxIndexAt lo d) (maxIndexAt hi d))
maxIndexAt (CRangeArray lo hi _) d =
  maxI d (maxI (maxIndexAt lo d) (maxIndexAt hi d))
maxIndexAt (CIndex a i) d = maxI d (maxI (maxIndexAt a d) (maxIndexAt i d))
maxIndexAt (CSlice a lo hi _) d =
  maxI d (maxI (maxIndexAt a d) (maxI (maxIndexAt lo d) (maxIndexAt hi d)))
maxIndexAt _ d = d - 1

-- the deepest switch nesting in a tree (each CTSwitch increments the emit depth by
-- 1 for its subtrees; an arm body at a leaf is emitted at decision-depth + this).
-- A constructor switch emits its default subtree inside the same tower as its
-- branches, one level deeper (`emitBrTableTower` at d+1); a literal switch emits
-- both at its own depth, so counting the default one level deeper covers both.
treeSwitchNesting : CTree -> Int
treeSwitchNesting (CTFail _) = 0
treeSwitchNesting (CTLeaf _) = 0
treeSwitchNesting (CTGuard _ fail) = treeSwitchNesting fail
treeSwitchNesting (CTDrop sub) = treeSwitchNesting sub
treeSwitchNesting (CTSwitch branches dft) =
  let bd = foldMaxI (map (b => treeSwitchNesting (branchSub b)) branches)
  1 + maxI bd (treeSwitchNesting dft)

-- P1: scratch depth of a group's nullary VALUE member's inline-emitted rhs (a function
-- member contributes nothing here — it is lifted).
maxIndexAtLgVal : CBind -> Int -> Int
maxIndexAtLgVal (CBind _ [CClause [] rhs] _ _) d = maxIndexAt rhs d
maxIndexAtLgVal _ d = d - 1

maxIndexAtStmt : CStmt -> Int -> Int
maxIndexAtStmt (CSExpr e) d = maxIndexAt e d
maxIndexAtStmt (CSLet _ pat e) d = maxI (letStashIndex pat e d) (maxIndexAt e d)
maxIndexAtStmt (CSAssign _ e) d = maxIndexAt e d

-- the scratch-local index a let/block-let with `pat` against RHS `e` (emitted at
-- depth d) needs to stash its RHS, or d-1 (no stash) for a PVar/PWild bind which
-- needs no scratch.  An irrefutable destructure stashes the RHS one slot ABOVE
-- whatever the RHS itself uses, so the stash never collides with the RHS's own
-- scratch and is live only while the sub-patterns extract their fields.
letStashIndex : Pat -> CExpr -> Int -> Int
letStashIndex (PVar _ _ _) _ d = d - 1
letStashIndex PWild _ d = d - 1
letStashIndex _ e d = maxIndexAt e d + 1

-- the highest scratch index used emitting a decision tree at depth d (a CTSwitch
-- stashes the focus at index d and recurses subtrees, the default included, at d+1;
-- leaves/guards re-emit arm bodies via emitTreeRef at the same depth, accounted by the
-- arm walk above).
maxIndexTree : CTree -> Int -> Int
maxIndexTree (CTFail _) d = d - 1
maxIndexTree (CTLeaf _) d = d - 1
maxIndexTree (CTGuard _ fail) d = maxIndexTree fail d
maxIndexTree (CTDrop sub) d = maxIndexTree sub d
maxIndexTree (CTSwitch branches dft) d =
  let bd = foldMaxI (map (b => maxIndexTree (branchSub b) (d + 1)) branches)
  maxI d (maxI bd (maxIndexTree dft (d + 1)))

branchSub : CTBranch -> CTree
branchSub (CTBranch _ sub) = sub

foldMaxI : List Int -> Int
foldMaxI [] = 0
foldMaxI (x :: xs) = maxI x (foldMaxI xs)

-- ── small generic helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

-- W7 string helpers (no stdlib): trailing-integer parse over the char array.
-- Used only for the synthetic tuple ctor/type names ("Tup<n>" / "$Tuple<n>")
-- whose arity is recovered from the trailing decimal.
--
-- the integer formed by the trailing decimal digits of `s` (e.g. "Tup3" → 3,
-- "$Tuple12" → 12).  Walks from the first digit to the end.
trailingIntOf : String -> Int
trailingIntOf s =
  let cs = stringToChars s
  trailingIntGo cs (firstDigitIdx cs 0) 0

firstDigitIdx : Array Char -> Int -> Int
firstDigitIdx cs i =
  if i >= arrayLength cs then
    i
  else if isDigitCh (charCode (arrayGetUnsafe i cs)) then
    i
  else
    firstDigitIdx cs (i + 1)

trailingIntGo : Array Char -> Int -> Int -> Int
trailingIntGo cs i acc =
  if i >= arrayLength cs then
    acc
  else
    trailingIntGo cs (i + 1) (acc * 10 + (charCode (arrayGetUnsafe i cs) - 48))

isDigitCh : Int -> Bool
isDigitCh c = c >= 48 && c <= 57

-- True if every char from index `i` to the end is a decimal digit (and there is at
-- least one).  Used to confirm a "Tup<n>" synthetic tuple ctor name.
allDigitsFrom : Array Char -> Int -> Bool
allDigitsFrom cs i = if i >= arrayLength cs then False else allDigitsGo cs i

allDigitsGo : Array Char -> Int -> Bool
allDigitsGo cs i =
  if i >= arrayLength cs then
    True
  else if isDigitCh (charCode (arrayGetUnsafe i cs)) then
    allDigitsGo cs (i + 1)
  else
    False

indent : List String -> List String
indent lines = map ("    " ++ _) lines

-- `indent` applied `d` times, but in ONE pass (#381).  The if/else CHAIN emitters
-- (emitLitSwitch{Ref,Tail}, emitDispatchChain) nest their own recursion inside
-- `indent`, so the k-th arm's text would be re-mapped — and every line
